periods.intro: The history of the region now known as Silicon Valley begins with the lives of the Ohlone People, who have resided, and continue to reside, along the Peninsula, the South Bay, and the wider San Francisco Bay Region since time immemorial. As with histories such as Fred Glass’s *From Mission to Microchip* (2016) and David Pellow and Lisa Park’s *The Silicon Valley of Dreams* (2002), we invite scholars conducting research on the long history of Silicon Valley to consider materials collected by our colleagues in allied fields such as the University Archaeology Collections as well as records drawn from projects of the Stanford Historical Society such as the Native American Alumni Oral Histories.

links.name: Native American Alumni Oral Histories
links.holder: Stanford Historical Society, Oral History Program

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — General manufacturing

items.title: Jacquard loom patterns and samples, 1821
items.description: A unique book of patterns and descriptions created by an early user of the revolutionary Jaquard loom, identified as "Richaud" on the cover of the book. Illustrated with hand-drawn Jacquard loom patterns and fabric samples.

items.title: Visite de Msr le Duc d'Aumale a la Croix-Rousse, dans l'atelier de M. Carquillat : le 24 Août 1841
items.description: Picture shows the Duc d'Aumale full length and facing right, accompanied by four members of his entourage; to his right, Carquillat, also full length but facing slightly left, holds his well-known portrait of Joseph Marie Jacquard; another full length male figure stands to the right of Carquillat, gesturing at the portrait. The figures are standing in Carquillat's workshop in front of the loom which produced both the portrait of Jacquard and the item here described; a workman stands at the loom, body pointed away but looking over his shoulder at D'Aurnale and Carquillat.

sectors.name: Education and research — Science and mathematics

items.title: The landscape of the Palo Alto area in the early Spanish period: observations of the vegetation cover from original sources : typescript, 1988
items.description: Historical overview; a table of major events and participants arranged chronologically. Particular emphasis on botanically relevant events. Quoted observations from original sources.
items.era_note: [The whole of this 1988 typescript, a study of the area's vegetation drawn from original sources of the early Spanish period, concerns this period.]

sectors.name: Society and community — Local and California history

items.title: Juana Briones collection, circa 1960-2009
items.description: Oral histories, memoirs, research files, photographs, newsclippings, maps, publications, adobe house preservation work, etc. Juana Briones (1802-1899) was a businesswoman and landowner in the San Francisco Bay Area.
items.era_note: [About a third of the collection, research files, memoirs and publications on Juana Briones's life before 1846, concerns this period.]

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: Harwood family papers, 1722-1962
items.description: Over his lifetime, Andrew Allen Harwood (1802-1884), great grandson of Benjamin Franklin, kept letters and notes of interest and autographs in a collection known as ODDS & ENDS. Letters, notes, autographs, portraits, and other materials collected by the Harwood Family over a period of two hundred-fifty years. Much of the early materials, including Revolutionary War era materials, are navy and military service related.

sectors.name: Society and community — Religion, clubs and societies

items.title: Father Narciso Durán letters : San Jose, Calif. : ALS, 1806 July 28-June 8, 1827
items.description: Thirty-six letters from Father Durán, in his role as administrator of Mission San Jose, to the fathers who held the office of Procurador of the Missions of California, concerning standing orders for supplies to the mission, and related financial and administrative matters.

items.title: Mission Santa Clara padrón, 1839 December 31
items.description: 1839 census of Mission Santa Clara, recording baptisms, marriages, confessions, communions, and deaths at the mission for the year, and baptisms, marriages, and deaths since the mission's founding. Entered and signed, with manuscript notes by, Father Jesús María Vásquez del Mercado.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Foreign affairs and diplomacy

items.title: Cabinet noir coding and decoding tables, circa 1777-circa 1800
items.description: Coding and decoding tables for use of a late-18th-century "cabinet noir" or "Black Chamber," the secret cipher departments of the European courts of the early modern age. Content and provenance link this specimen with the Bavarian Electoran court.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Government and public administration

items.title: Agustin V. Zamorano letter : Santa Barbara, Calif., to the alcaldes of Santa Barbara, Monterrey, and San José Guadalupe, 1832 May 9
items.description: Zamorano's letter to the alcaldes of Santa Barbara, Monterey, and San José Guadalupe, requesting that they publish the attached manifesto informing the public of Zamorano's journey to Santa Barbara and his efforts to preserve peace in California.

items.title: Jose Maria Estudillo manuscript document
items.description: Jose was the founder of the Estudillo family in upper California. The dealer believes the document is addressed to the Alcalde of the Pueblo of San Jose regarding a dispute between Ranchero Don Ignacio Ortega and locksmith Raphael Romero.

items.title: Letter and administrative file concerning storm-related damage to the Presidio of San Francisco and proposals for its repair : ALS and ADS, 1805-1807
items.description: Leatherbound folio containing a letter from Josef de Iturrigaray, Viceroy of New Spain, to His Excellency Don José Antonio Cavallero, explaining an enclosed document containing testimony compiled by José de Arrillaga, governor of the Californias, describing damage to the Presidio caused by a storm in Dec. 1798-Jan. 1799, with recommendations for repairs and additional military personnel.

items.title: Letter, 1832 Aug. 14, to the Alcade of San J'ose de Guadelupe
items.description: Statesman, soldier, craftsman, and California's first printer.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — General manufacturing

items.title: Capital Soap Company, manufacturers of chemical, olive, family, toilet and bleaching soaps : also the famous Le Roi du Savons Soap, which washes without rubbing. : letter, 1863 October 5.
items.description: Handwritten letter addressed to H. French, Esq. introducing Mr. Charles Bernhardt as the agent for Santa Clara Co. regarding the sale of Roi du Savons soap and signed by Withington Williams. Verso of letterhead includes advertising inserts for Sacramento businesses.
items.era_note: [The letter is dated 1863 in its title, which places it in this period rather than on the catalogue's date of 1883.]

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Labor and professional organizations

items.title: Chinese Railroad Workers
items.description: The Chinese Railroad Workers in North America Project seeks to give a voice to the Chinese migrants whose labor on the Transcontinental Railroad helped to shape the physical and social landscape of the American West. The Chinese Railroad Workers Digital Materials Repository offers open access to materials that are selected for their qualities that they are difficult to retrieve, and rich for historical study.

items.title: Journal of the clipper ship Red Gauntlet, 1855-1856
items.description: Journal kept by ship's carpenter William F. Harden documenting the second voyage of the clipper ship Red Gauntlet under Captain Andrews, departing New York for San Francisco, Hawaii, and Canton on August 18, 1855. The journal records Chinese longshoremen strikes, confiscation of liquor, brutal punishments including floggings, the death of the Captain's youngest son, the death of the ship's cook after repeated beatings, forced prizefights between ship's boys for crew entertainment, and other harsh conditions aboard ship.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Networking and telecommunications

items.title: Sketch (reproduced) of New Westminster, British Columbia, and the terminal station of Collin's Overland Telegraph, 1865
The celebration in San Francisco : in commemoration of the successful laying of the Atlantic telegraphic cable, Monday, September 27th, 1858 ...
items.description: The broadsheet commemorates "the success of the most important undertaking of modern times." This sheet reflects that excitement with the vignettes, detailed descriptions of the celebrations and great enthusiasm for the memorable accomplishment.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Trade, merchandising and retail

items.title: Alfred Robinson papers, 1837-1859
items.description: Originally from Mass., Robinson first went to Calif. in 1829 as the representative for the hide-trading and shipping firm Bryant, Sturgis & Co. Primarily business correspondence to and from Robinson, in his role as a San Francisco merchant and as agent for the firm Howland & Aspinwall of New York, including: a letter book (Dec. 1848-June 1849) concerning prices of goods in San Francisco and suggesting cargoes to be sent to Calif. from the East coast; letters from Howland & Aspinwall in New York (1848-1849); and other business correspondence from various individuals and companies (1848-1849).

items.title: Jacob P. Leese papers
items.description: Consists of personal and business correspondence, indentures, legal documents, ship's papers, accounts, inventories, and maps, documenting the activities, business interests, and land holdings of early California merchant Jacob P. Leese, his wife Rosalia Vallejo de Leese, and his partner Thomas O. Larkin, between the years 1837 to 1862.

items.title: Letter from C. Curry Guns and Fancy Goods to Hardy & Kennedy regarding pistol order and firearms inventory, 1860 September 27.
items.description: Letter from Charles and Nathaniel Curry of C. Curry Guns and Fancy Goods, San Francisco, to William S. Hardy and Samuel S. Kennedy of Hardy & Kennedy Co., Forest Hill mining district, regarding an order of three pairs of large pistols with Damascus barrels and holsters.

items.title: William A. Leidesdorff collection, 1834-1857, 1928
items.description: A prominent merchant and landowner, Leidesdorff also served in a number of civic positions, including United States vice-consul to Mexico (appointed by Thomas Larkin in 1845) and treasurer of San Francisco. Leidesdorff's business correspondence and records document his transactions with many prominent early Californians, including Yerba Buena alcaldes Francisco Guerrero and George Hyde; Thomas Larkin; William Davis Merry Howard; Samuel Brannan; Stephen Smith; Nathan Spear; Henry Dalton; Concepcion Avila; and Henry Mellus.

items.title: William D.M. Howard papers, 1823-1878
items.description: Howard was a merchant and financier in San Francisco, California. Correspondence, invoices, and receipts from pioneer Calif. residents, merchants, and companies, reflecting Howard's extensive commercial activities through his firm, Mellus & Howard Company, including letters to and from business partner Henry D. Mellus, Francis Mellus at the Los Angeles branch of the firm, Abel Stearns, Henry F. Teschemacher, and Joseph P. Thompson.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Transportation and utilities

items.title: Leland Stanford letter to Butler Ives
items.description: At the time of the letter, Butler Ives was an assistant engineer with the Central Pacific Railroad. Handwritten letter, January 25, 1869, requesting more men at work "on our line at the point where the U.P. line strikes it east of Ogden," along with a photoprint copy of a stereocard showing Butler Ives on horseback in the mountains.

items.title: Notes about Henry Root and the California Central Railway, nd
items.description: Notes from Root's book, "Personal History and Reminiscences, 1845 to 1921." Also notes from the DAILY ALTA CALIFORNIA, 1860-1863.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work

items.title: Incoming correspondence, 1863-1864
items.description: Bulk of the letters are requests for purchasing the Fowler adding machine and the circulars advertising the product. Several letters are responses to the company's advertisement seeking agents throughout the United States to sell the machines.

items.title: Towne and Bacon Printers records, 1854-1875
items.description: Journals (1856-1870), daybooks (1854-1866), cashbooks (1855-1875), receipt books (1855-1865), petty accounts and ledgers (1855-1868), ledgers (1854-1868), and a payroll book (1865-1873) of Towne and Bacon Printers.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Mining and quarrying

items.title: New Almaden Mine records, 1845-1973
items.description: Correspondence, legal and financial documents, ledgers, reports, research notes, photographs, maps, plans, profiles, charts and artifacts relating to the operation of the New Almaden Mine and the Quicksilver Mining Co.

items.title: Reports on California mines : ms, 1860-1865
items.description: Reports and letters giving overviews of mines either purchased by or of interest to the firm of Adelberg & Raymond. Includes gold, silver, iron, quicksilver, and tin mines.

items.title: Stock certificate, 1869 August 21.
items.description: Stock certificate issued to C.G. Myrick for ten shares in the capital stock of the mining company. The mine location is White Pine District, Nevada.

items.title: Telegraphic mining code, c. 1860
items.description: Birdseye Creek was one of California's earliest hydraulic mining companies to use thir private telegraphic codes. Beginning in the 1870's there were several firms publishing cryptographic code books so that messages could be sent from the mining superintendent to the officers without divulging the content of the message.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Real estate and land development

items.title: California : legal documents, 1863-1867
items.description: Two documents (1864 and 1867) concern ownership of the Sanchez de Pacheco land grant, Rancho San Miguel. The 1863 document concerns the Savage Mining Company.

items.title: Map of the Santa Clara City Homestead Association
items.description: Shows owners, Quito Ranch line, proposed railroad from Alviso to Saratoga, Lawrence and Santa Clara depots, etc.

items.title: Mesa land case papers, 1853-1930
items.description: Copies of transcript of proceedings in case No. 238, Maria Antonia Mesa, claimant vs. The United States, defendent for the place named "Rinconada del Arroyo de San Francisquito," 1853 and 1861; and notes on Ranchos of Santa Clara, Santa Cruz and San Benito Counties from Capt. William M. Kerr Collection, San Diego Serra Museum.

items.title: Records of Stanford properties, 1861-1927
items.description: The collection consists of deeds and legal documents relating to property that was owned by Leland and Jane Stanford, or Stanford University. Leland and Jane Stanford owned over 100,000 acres throughout California . Of special interest are the deeds to the Stanford's three primary residences in Sacramento (1861), San Francisco (1875), and Palo Alto (1876).

items.title: Santa Clara County (Calif.) land grant plats, 1851, 1856, and 1863
items.description: The corner of Market Street and San Fernando Street in San Jose, with the division of the Mesa family land into six parcels, surrounded by Antonio Sunol and Brown & Co. land.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Surveying and mapping

items.title: City of San Jose / copied from the original map drawn by Pherman [i.e. Sherman] Day, civil engineer, 1850 : facsimile map.
Pulgas base : map, 1854
items.description: Shows coastal outline, hills, roads, vegetation, and settlement locations of Jones, Steinbergen, and Carr in the vicinity of Palo Alto. Includes a profile of the base line (length 6.53 miles) and a sketch showing the location of the base line in relation to the southern half of San Francisco Bay.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Transportation

items.title: Alfred A. Hart photographs, 1862-1869
items.description: Nonetheless, Hart is remembered for his work in visually documenting the construction of the western half of the first transcontinental railroad. Photographic series documenting construction of the Central Pacific Railroad, 1866-1869, presented both as an album and stereographs. Also includes mounted stereograph views of the Leland Stanford residence in Sacramento, 1862-1863.

items.title: E. G. Greenfield account book for wharfages collected from steamers, vessels, etc., and diary : Stockton, Calif., 1855-1861
items.description: Account book (1855 May 16-1856 May 12) and diary (1858 Jan. 1-1859 Nov. 12) kept by harbor master Elijah G. Greenfield recording wharfages collected from ships and daily events in Stockton, Calif.

items.title: Keepsakes issued to members of the Book Club of California in commemoration of the centennial of the transcontinental railroad, 1969
items.description: Includes 1. "The Hewes Receipt," by Ralph W. Hansen; and 2. "The 'Goat Island Grab'," by Ted Wurm (2 copies).
items.era_note: [Nearly all of these 1969 keepsakes, short histories of the transcontinental railroad's completion and the Goat Island dispute, concern this period.]

items.title: The Southern Pacific Railroad Company, plaintiff, vs. Calvin Martin et als, defendants : petition for the condemnation of lands to public use, 1868
items.description: Defendants include ca. 140 names, many of which are from early Santa Clara County families.

items.title: To the Honorable the Legislature of the State of California : the citizens of the City of San Francisco, in view of the great commercial interests so necessarily... Pilotage
items.description: A petition to the California state legislature from San Francisco citizens, calling on the government to reform the official pilotage system.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use

items.title: Manuscript letter copy book from Department of the Interior, General Land Office regarding claims of Central Pacific Railroad land, mineral title issues, conflicts, etc. for the Placer County, California region from the estate of W & P Nicholls, bankers, at Dutch Flat, 1862-1869
items.description: Based on the contents, the letters are primarily concerned with conflicting claims to land between the Central Pacific Railroad and American settlers in California. Many of the letters involve Joseph S. Wilson in his role as the General Land Commissioner.

sectors.name: Education and research — Schools, colleges and training

items.title: Journal of a schoolteacher
items.description: The journal is largely about his work at the Sacramento Seminary, then at the school of Mr. E. Crowell until he leaves Sacramento for Santa Clara when appointed to a post at he new Pacific College (later University of the Pacific). He writes of his enjoyment working with young students.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Art, music, literature and photography

items.title: Carleton E. Watkins photograph collection
items.description: Carleton E. Watkins was a 19th century photographer based in San Francisco who made his name documenting the rapid growth of the American West. This collection contains albumen prints taken throughout Watkins's career, between the years of 1856 and 1885. The bulk of photographs depict Yosemite Valley and Mariposa Grove between 1861 and 1881.

items.title: William Hubert Burgess letters and miscellany, 1851-1899
items.description: Burgess was an artist, silversmith, miner, and teacher. Consists of 13 letters and some incomplete letters to Burgess's mother in England; newspaper clippings and reminiscences of Burgess and the Burgess family; notebooks and writings belonging to or written by Burgess; and 29 pencil and ink sketches of California scenes.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Design and architecture

items.title: Samuel Charles Bugbee papers, 1861-1876
items.description: Architect Samuel Charles Bugbee helped plan the Stanford family home in Palo Alto, and perhaps also contributed to the San Francisco Conservatory of Flowers in the late 19th century. This collection consists of three sketchbooks and some loose drawings on onion skin paper. Most of the drawings are either portraits or sketches of interiors and exteriors.

sectors.name: Society and community — Local and California history

items.title: a Roy Page Ballard papers 1894
items.description: Notes and outlines for a history of the Stanford campus area originally prepared for a class assignment. Focusing on the pre-Palo Alto Stock Farm period, Ballard's subjects include early inhabitants, Spanish ownership, land grants and title deeds, and early residents such as Peter Coutts, George Gordon, Jose Pena, and Sandy Wilson.
items.era_note: [Most of these 1894 notes, on land grants, title deeds and early owners of the Stanford campus area before the Stock Farm, concern this period.]

items.title: California biography collection
items.description: Consists of ephemeral items relating to people widely known and relatively unknown in California. Contains mostly newspaper obituaries, but also includes: handwritten biographical documents, invitations, wedding announcements, family reunion newsletters, genealogy forms, family trees, memorials, political speeches, campaign material, correspondence, and newspaper and magazine clippings.

items.title: Californian and Western manuscripts collection, ca. 1760-1963
items.description: Small collections and miscellaneous single items pertaining to various periods, persons, and phases of California history (1760-1963). Includes letters, journals, diaries, reports, financial and legal documents, pictures and maps, some typescripts and photostats.

items.title: Juana Briones collection, circa 1960-2009
items.description: Oral histories, memoirs, research files, photographs, newsclippings, maps, publications, adobe house preservation work, etc. Juana Briones (1802-1899) was a businesswoman and landowner in the San Francisco Bay Area.
items.era_note: [About a third of the collection, research on Briones's adobe house and landholdings after the American conquest, concerns this period.]

items.title: Northern California newspaper clippings : mounted in one large album, 1854
Pacific Slope scrapbooks, 1819-1906
items.description: The first series of scrapbooks was created by mayor (and later governor) Washington Bartlett, containing articles pertaining to political and civic issues in San Francisco and California from 1855 to 1886, as well as some notes and memoranda chronicling his duties as mayor. Other scrapbooks were assembled by Mary Sheldon Barnes in the 1890s and include articles and other ephemera related to the American West, including material on Native Americans, Oregon territory, Alaska, Pacific and Asiatic relations, and the San Francisco Peninsula.

items.title: Paul Percy Parker collection of historical documents pertaining to Monterey County, California, 1782-1936
items.description: Paul Percy Parker was a newspaperman in California'a Salinas Valley. Correspondence, manuscripts of narratives and memoirs, official documents, and clippings dealing predominantly with the Monterey and Salinas Valley areas before 1900.

items.title: Reid W. Dennis collection of California lithographs, 1850-1908
items.description: This collection of prints, mostly lithographs (including chromolithographs and colored lithographs), as well as one engraving, primarily portray San Francisco city views, public buildings, and landscapes. Subjects also include San Jose, Stanford University, the U.S. Navy Yard at Mare Island, San Diego, and San Luis Rey.

items.title: William Wesley Boak pocket letter book to his wife Samantha
items.description: Thirty-seven page autograph signed filled-in Gregory's Express Pocket Letter Book, written by an Iowan gold seeker in California to his wife with an interesting detailed description of the mild climate and successful farming in the Santa Clara Valley, preceding its development as the world's leading fruit growing region in the early 20th century.

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: Andrew Smith Hallidie diary : ms, 1852 Jan.-May.
items.description: Diary of Hallidie's voyage with his father from Liverpool to San Francisco via New York and Panama aboard the ships Pacific, Brother Jonathan, and Brutus. Discusses everyday life aboard as well as engineering aspects of the ships, including propulsion equipment and functional problems during a storm.
items.era_note: [The whole diary, written between January and May 1852, concerns this period.]

items.title: California letters, 1852-1858
items.description: A. S. Gibbons was an itinerant Methodist preacher who spent one year teaching at Santa Clara College. Collection consists of letters from A. S. Gibbons and his wife, Sarah Cloud Gibbons, to her family in Virginia (1852-1857). The letters describe domestic problems and the temperance movement.

items.title: Chester Smith Lyman journals, 1845-1854
items.description: Consists of 14 journals kept by Chester Smith Lyman documenting his voyages from New York to Hawaii (1845-1846), from Hawaii to San Francisco (1847), and from San Francisco to Connecticut (1850), as well as his observations and experiences in Hawaii and California between the years 1846 and 1850.

items.title: Culver family papers, 1858-1915
items.description: Includes correspondence, diaries, and photographs. The Collection reflects J. O. Culver's experience as a lawyer, his service as an Army Paymaster and Post Office Inspector, his endeavors in small fruit culture, and his excursions into prospecting and mining. In general, the family letters and papers give a panorama of middle class society in New York, Wisconsin and Missouri, and Colorado and California, from 1860 to 1915, a familiar pattern in the United States of looking ever westward for opportunity.

items.title: Daingerfield family letters, 1850-1853
items.description: Letters of Leroy Daingerfield (miner and rancher) and William Daingerfield (lawyer and businessman) from California to their family in Harper's Ferry, Virginia. Letters are revealing of legal, mining, and business conditions of the time.

items.title: Daniel Jagger diary : ms, 1846-1860
items.description: Leatherbound diary, primarily documenting Jagger's overland journey with other members of his gold mining company from Warren, Ohio to Georgetown, El Dorado, County, Calif., Apr. 1849-Jan. 1850; along with smaller sections of entries at the front and back of the journal, recording an 1846 trip to Lake Superior and daily conditions in Woodside, San Mateo County, Calif.

items.title: Diary, March-April 1851
items.description: Littlefield writes about his experiences in California, giving details of selling lumber, traveling from Benicia to San Francisco by steamer, staying at the Temperance House, and telling of the many ships and their cargoes that he observes on San Francisco Bay.

items.title: H.S. Bradley ship's log : ms copy, 1849 Nov. 13-1850 May 7
items.description: Handwritten copy of a ship's log kept by Bradley, a passenger on the bark Orion, on a voyage from Boston to San Francisco via Rio de Janeiro and the island of Juan Fernandez. Entries record the weather, the ship's course and location, ships spoken, and significant shipboard events.

items.title: Hosmer correspondence, 1849-1853
items.description: Letters of Charles and Edward Hosmer, two brothers who left Avon, New York in 1849 for California. The letters describe Charles' overland trip by wagon train and Edward's trip around Cape Horn to California, their work in San Francisco and Edward's unsuccessful prospecting in the Feather River area.

items.title: Joseph G. Eastland diary and letters : ms and ALS, 1846-1853
items.description: The entries in Joseph Eastman's diary, dated May 1846 to May 1849, begin when Eastland was a 14-year-old from his home in Nashville, Tenn. and New Orleans, La. Eastman's letters to family members, dated 1846 to 1853, include several written from San Francisco, giving details about Thomas' business ventures in quartz mining and real estate, and about Joseph's employment with Donahue's Union Iron and Brass Foundry.

items.title: Leland Stanford papers, 1840-1909
items.description: Early in the 1860s, Stanford joined with three other Sacramento merchants--Charles Crocker, Mark Hopkins, and Collis P. Huntington--in the building of the Central Pacific Railroad. In 1885, Leland and Jane founded Leland Stanford Jr. University in memory of their son. Correspondence, telegrams; business, legal, financial, and official papers; speeches, journals, and newsclippings; and other materials relating to the construction of the Central Pacific Railroad, Stanford's political career, business and financial interests, and the founding and construction of Stanford University.

items.title: Letters (photocopies) to family, 1866
items.description: 3 letters were mailed from Green Oaks and describe episodes of her life on the Steele brothers' dairy; one was mailed from Aspinwall, the Atlantic port of Panama, before crossing by train to the Pacific.

items.title: Log of the extreme clipper ship Spitfire, 1854-1855
items.description: Manuscript logbook documenting the second voyage of the extreme clipper ship Spitfire under Captain John W. Arey, comprising approximately 9,000 words of daily entries. The voyage departed Boston in November 1854, arriving at San Francisco on March 21, 1855, after a passage of 118 days. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Logbook for the steamship Panama : ms, 1849 Feb. 18-May 6
items.description: Daily record of the ship's voyage from New York to Panama via the Straits of Magellan, under the command of Lt. David D. Porter, U.S. Navy. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Moses Schallenberger papers, 1847-1898
items.description: Moses Schallenberger was an early California pioneer. Correspondence and photographs (1847-1898) covering the period after the arrival of Schallenberger in California. Also included is an account, recorded by Mary Sheldon Barnes, of Schallenberger's overland journey to California from Missouri in 1844.

items.title: Richard J. Bush journal of the Collins Overland Telegraph expedition
items.description: An original unpublished manuscript journal of Collin's telegraph expedition departing San Francisco, CA on July 3, 1865 to Nikolayefsk-on-Amur, Russia. After Civil War service, Bush joined Perry Collins' Russian-American Telegraph Expedition (the Western Union Extension) to explore the proposed route to connect the United States with Europe by way of the Bering Strait.

sectors.name: Society and community — Religion, clubs and societies

items.title: Mission Santa Clara marriage records, 1846-1847
items.description: Undated manuscript translation of a portion of the Mission Santa Clara marriage register, beginning with record number 2873 (1846 Jan. 3) and ending with record number 3003 (1847 Dec. 11).

items.title: Record-Book. Rules, By-Laws & Proceedings of the Santa Cruz Cornet Band
items.description: A 43 page hand-written record book in a contemporary notebook. Includes minutes of the meetings from 1869 up to 1871.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Armed forces and military history

items.title: Calvin Brown letter to James T. Ames on Mare Island Navy Yard, 1861 May 30
items.description: Letter from U.S. Navy civil engineer Calvin Brown to arms manufacturer James T. Ames describing Brown's first impressions of the Mare Island Navy Yard, then under construction.

items.title: Edward Otho Cresap Ord letters, 1854-1885
items.description: Letters written by Ord to his wife during the period when Ord was on a survey of the Pacific Coast, including descriptions of the region, details of incidents and problems relating to the survey, Indian campaigns, and other matters relating to the West Coast. Also includes several letters pertaining to military matters.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Government and public administration

items.title: San Francisco town journal : ms, 1847-1848
items.description: First financial record of San Francisco, kept by the elected treasurer, William A. Leidesdorff. The journal contains eleven pages of entries, recording cash received and expended, and expenditures for goods and services, including payments made for the salary of Alcalde George Hyde, the first survey of San Francisco by Jasper O'Farrell, and construction of streets, wharves, and the first schoolhouse.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — General manufacturing

items.title: Cours de theorie pour le tissage professée par P. Audibert [two students' course books]
items.description: Two students' manuscript notebooks documenting the use of Jacquard's punched card silk weaving method in 1884 and 1885. These manuscripts appear to be students' handmade coursebooks (or year-long "final projects"?) created under the tutelage of P. Audibert, a professor at the school of weaving in Lyon (historically an important center of the weaving industry).

items.title: Framed portraits of Christian De Guigne (color photograph by Mushet Photography, Los Angeles, n.d.) and John Stauffer (oil painting by unknown artist, n.d.)
items.description: These portraits hung in the Stauffer Chemical Company San Francisco offices until their closure in 1987.

items.title: French Jacquard loom programming manual with textile samples, circa late 19th century
items.description: French manuscript documenting Jacquard loom programming methods and textile production, containing 94 textile samples with corresponding loom programming instructions and machine patterns. The manuscript represents either professional training documentation or proprietary trade information for the Lyon silk industry, demonstrating early programmable machine technology that prefigured computer punch card systems.

items.title: Joshua Hendy Machine Works Articles of Incorporation and minutes of the proceedings of the board of directors : ledger, 1882-1909
Les laboureurs: poème tiré de Jocelyn. Reproduit en caractères tissés avec license des propriétaires éditeurs
items.description: This is the first book woven entirely in silk using programmable punch cards (Jacquard loom method). At the time of its invention in 1801, the Jacquard Loom was the most complex programmable machine in existence for which thosands of punched cards were employed as automated weaving instructions to a mechanized loom.

items.title: Remillard Brick Company records, 1879-1921
items.description: Title papers, together with various bound ledgers of the Remillard Brick Company (San Francisco and Oakland, California) covering the period 1879 to 1921. Records of sales, purchases, jobs, inventory, employee records, etc.

items.title: White's Patent Rotary furnace : patent agreement, San Francisco, 1879
items.description: Concerns the various interests of parties involved with the ore-processing furnace, who are from either San Francisco or San Jose. John Howell is to be paid $1000. for the exclusive right of Rankin Brayton & Co. to manufacture the "Howell improved White furnace."

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Labor and professional organizations

items.title: [Wong Quon Sue ("Wah Chung") businessman and Chinese labor contractor for the Southern Pacific Railroad] [graphic]

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Networking and telecommunications

items.title: Letter to Ebon C. Ingersoll, Chairman Sub-Committee on Commerce on Cuba Telegraph, 1870 July 12.
items.description: Requests repeal of the monopoly claimed by Act of 1866.

items.title: Oakland Home Telephone Company records, 1893-1909
items.description: Business and legal documents and correspondence which deals with the creation and organization of the Oakland Home Telephone Company.

items.title: Telephone advertising card / Portsmouth Telephone Exchange

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Trade, merchandising and retail

items.title: Faxon Dean Atherton Papers
items.description: A native of Dedham, Massachusetts, Atherton first came to the Pacific coast around 1834 to work for a ship chandlery firm in Valparaiso, Chile. He settled in Valparaiso in 1840 and became a successful merchant dealing in hides and tallow, foodstuffs, and other commodities. The collection comprises business records and correspondence documenting Atherton's mercantile relationships and activities in Boston, California, Hawaii, and Valparaiso; correspondence, deeds, and other documents relating to Atherton's real estate investments in California, including Las Milpitas Ranch and Bolsa de San Cayetano Ranch in Monterey County, San Lorenzo Ranch in Alameda County, Los Putos Ranch in Solano County, and Valparaiso Park in San Mateo County; and legal documents and other papers concerning Atherton's estate after his death.

items.title: Menlo Park (Calif.) grocery store : day book, 1882
items.description: List of customers, their purchases and the prices paid for their supplies.

items.title: W.H. Taylor collection, 1837-1938
items.description: Collection consists of records of a general merchandise store in North Bloomfield, Nevada County, California (1862-1936), and bound records of various other mercantile and mining establishments in California (1837-1938). Included are legal documents, agreements, correspondence, general accounts, production records, and samples of various forms.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Transportation and utilities

items.title: American and Australian Line via New Zealand around the world : schedule, 18--.
items.description: Schedule, with fold out maps of the world, United States, New Zealand, and the British Isles. Schedule includes timetables for connecting transporation services: Atchison, Topeka & Santa Fe System; Chicago & Alton; Chicago & North-Western (the North-Western Line); Union Pacific; Oceanic S.S. Co. of San Francisco; and Oceanic S.S. Co. of New Zealand.

items.title: California Street Railroad Co. records, 1877-1904
items.description: Legal papers, accounting reports and other papers pertaining to the company.

items.title: James Otey Bradford papers, 1869-1919
items.description: The Bradford papers contain James Otey Bradford's correspondence from 1888-1919. Much of it is correspondence pertaining to his duties with the Wells, Fargo & Co. Correspondence (1888-1919); articles on early stagecoaching and its problems, and on the Pony Express; photographs of stagecoaches; and identification photographs of Wells Fargo employees.

items.title: Letcher railroad collection, 1860-1889
items.description: Correspondence and documents concerning the Southern Pacific Company and the Northern California operations of the Central Pacific Railroad. Topics include: accidents, brakes, employee problems, engines, engineers, rates pay, and train delays.

items.title: Letcher railroad collection, 1887-1889
items.description: Business correspondence of the Southern Pacific Railroad between December 1887 and May 1889. The letters include daily reports of the operations of the railroad, employee problems, maintenance, and purchases.

items.title: Lewis Tasheira's history : typescript copy, 1920 Dec. 13.
items.description: Mention of various railroad men and companies. Worked with Henry Root in Oakland, later C.P. Huntington and Leland Stanford in California and elsewhere. Covers the period 1864-1903.
items.era_note: [Most of this 1920 memoir, recollections of railroad work with C.P. Huntington and Leland Stanford, concerns this period.]

items.title: Manzanita Water Company records, 1883-1908
items.description: Since the early 1860s, The Manzanita Water Company distributed water for domestic, manufacturing, and irrigation purposes. Correspondence, journal, stock journal, bylaws, description of lands, water grants, legal documents and other papers pertaining to Leland Stanford's association with the Manzanita Water Company.

items.title: Mr. C.P. Huntington's reception : Palace Hotel, San Francisco : albumen print, 1888 May 1.
items.description: Fifty-three male portrait busts with Collis Potter Huntington in the center. Each attendee to the reception is identified by name. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Photographs of an early street car and Henry Casebolt, president, ca. 1872 and 1875 Feb.
items.description: The street car photo includes the driver, John McCord, and Henry Casebolt, president. The portrait of Henry Casebolt, president of the Sutter Street Railroad Company in 1872, was made by I.W. Taber.

items.title: Relations between the Central Pacific Railroad Company and the U.S. government : published pamphlet
items.description: I. The legal obligations and the manner in which they have been observed. II. The benefits promised and how they have been realized.

items.title: Reports, 1880-1881
items.description: Includes: 1. Extracts from the land agent's report, 1880; 2. The stock of the Central Pacific Railroad Company by Fisk & Hatch, 1880; and 3. Central Pacifc report to stock holders by Fisk & Hatch, 1881.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 1, Board of Directors records, 1867-1996
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 2, Operating and Maintenance Department records, 1889-1997
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 3, Mechanical Department records, 1909-1996
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 4, Accounting Department records, 1862-1988
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Venture capital and finance

items.title: Anthony Egl et als., plaintiffs, vs. The Central Pacific Railroad Company, defendants. Complaint. In the District Court of the Fourth Judicial District of the State of California, in and for the City and County of San Francisco : published pamphlet, 1876
items.description: Legal brief presented in the Fourth judicial district court of the State of California by plaintiffs Anthony Egl, Anthony Coolot and John R. Robinson vs. The Central Pacific Railroad Company. Defendants are Leland Stanford, Mark Hopkins and Collis Potter Huntington. The stockholders are claiming that they are being swindled out of their bonds in the company.

items.title: Donohoe Kelly & Co. records, 1863-1917
items.description: The Donohoe, Kelly Banking Company was a large private banking company formed in the second half of the nineteenth century, and flourishing until 1929 when it transferred its business to the Bank of America of California, later the Bank of America, National Trust and Savings Association. Represented in the collection are a variety of business papers including those documenting liquidation of Donohoe, Ralston and Company (1863-1867) when W. C. Ralston left the company, routine business papers regarding accounts and bank business, and volumes of cash books, collection journals, checks and deposits volumes, and balance sheets.

items.title: Stock and bond certificates : miscellaneous collection, 1875-1911
items.description: Several of the stock certificates were signed by Charles F. Crocker.

items.title: Stock report and California Street Journal, 1872 May 21.
items.description: Lists latest mining news, removals, morning sales, previous day's afternoon sales, stock brokers' cards, and lost or stolen shares.

items.title: William C. Ralston Correspondence, ca. 1870-1890
items.description: William Chapman Ralston, born 12 June 1826 in Ohio, was a banker and steamship owner. In 1864 he helped organize the Bank of California and served as its first president. Letters primarily to Ralston, dealing with William W. Cargill of the Oriental Bank Corporation of London and Charles de Long, U.S. Envoy and Minister to Japan.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work

items.title: Classification and Arrangement of the Stock of A.L. Bancroft & Company, No. 721 Market Street, San Francisco
items.description: Single-sided printed broadside, with one small woodcut, arranged as if an uncut eight-page pamphlet. Describes the arrangement of the books as well as "The Scope of the Business: Books, Stationery, Music & Musical Instruments, Printing, Lithography & Engravings, Binding and Blank Book Manufacturing, Publishing."

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company payroll book, 1883
items.description: Pacific Improvement Company payroll ledger, 1883. The ledger shows the actual rates of pay, which is difficult to locate elsewhere.

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company records, 1863-1967
items.description: Pacific Improvement Company was a large holding company in California, formed by C. P. Huntington, Leland Stanford, Mark Hopkins, and Charles Crocker. Contains business records of the Pacific Improvement Company and its subsidiaries. Business areas covered include land development, coal and iron mining, railroads, and hotels.

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company records, 1869-1931 (bulk 1883-1927)
items.description: The Pacific Improvement Company was a large holding company in California, formed during the days of C.P. Huntington, Leland Stanford, Mark Hopkins, and Charles Crocker. Contains business records of the Pacific Improvement Company and its subsidiaries. Contains materials related to the development of the Monterey Peninsula and to the general business areas of land development, coal and iron mining, railroads, and hotels.

items.title: Parke & Lacy business records, circa 1870-1901
items.description: 1 business ledger (labeled "day book," 7 original photographs, and related business documents).

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Farming, canning and food processing

items.title: Palo Alto Stock Farm photographs, 1880-1885
items.description: Charles Conklin Wooster, born in Albany, NY, in 1845, was a horse trainer and coachman for Leland Stanford from about 1870 until Stanford's death in 1893. Images in this collection include Stock Farm horses Electioneer and Lady Russel; Leland Stanford, Jr., with the horse Cheatano, 1882; trainers and grooms at the Stock Farm, 1881 and 1884; two trotters racing; and the Wooster home on campus.

items.title: Palo Alto Stock Farm Records, 1875-1913
items.description: The Palo Alto Stock Farm comprised the major farming properties of Senator Leland Stanford. Records of Leland Stanford's Santa Clara County property, the Palo Alto Stock Farm (devoted to the breeding and training of trotting horses) and his Tehama County property, the Vina Ranch (primarily a vineyard and winery with some horse breeding facilities.) Includes correspondence, letter books, auction catalogs, daily journals, stud records, farm records, breeding registers, time books, foal records, maps and employee records of the Palo Alto Stock Farm and winery, and clippings about the Stock Farm.

items.title: Steele Ranch records, 1855-1973
items.description: Compilation of ranch records from the Steele Ranches of San Mateo County, California. Includes financial papers, legal papers, photographs, maps, and miscellaneous background notes written by Mrs. Catherine Steele. The collection covers over 100 years of ranching in California.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Mining and quarrying

items.title: Adolph Sutro papers, 1869-1899
items.description: Sutro was the mining engineer who planned the Sutro Tunnel, which was constructed through Mount Davidson to reach the Comstock lode. Collection includes correspondence dealing with construction of the Sutro Tunnel (1869-1890); applications for employment on the Sutro Tunnel project (1873-1877) and in the Baths (1892-1895); personal bills (1869-1890); miscellaneous correspondence (1870-1895); miscellaneous papers and printed matter (1865-1889); and a safe book (1861-1899).

items.title: Asbury Harpending papers
items.description: Harpending gained notoriety, however, for his role in the swindle known as the Great Diamond Hoax (1872). Consists of correspondence, deeds, agreements, accounts, receipts, manuscript maps, and other papers reflecting Asbury Harpending's business and speculative activities in the Western United States, Kentucky, New York, and Latin America between the years 1862 and 1919. Deeds, accounts, receipts, and other financial records reflect Harpending's interests in numerous mining properties in the Western United States, Mexico, and Colombia.

items.title: Greystone Quarry papers
items.description: Greystone Quarry, formerly known as Goodrich Quarry, was the source for the sandstone used to build Stanford University in the 1880s and 1890s. Map, instructions, and photographs (with negatives) from a tour of Greystone Quarry led by Robert Butler and Rixford Snyder in April 1994; a clipping on the quarry, 1984; and a replica of the business card of Jacob Pfeiffer, proprietor of Goodrich Quarry.
items.era_note: [Most of the collection, a 1994 tour of and a clipping on the quarry that supplied Stanford's sandstone in the 1880s and 1890s, concerns this period.]

items.title: New Almaden Mine records, 1845-1973
items.description: Correspondence, legal and financial documents, ledgers, reports, research notes, photographs, maps, plans, profiles, charts and artifacts relating to the operation of the New Almaden Mine and the Quicksilver Mining Co.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Real estate and land development

items.title: Buildings of Fair Heirs in San Francisco [graphic]
items.description: This album documents approximately forty downtown San Francisco real estate holdings of the heirs of real estate, silver, and railroad magnate James Graham Fair. The album contains 39 gelatin silver prints (most approximately 6 x 8 inches, with two panoramic views, 3 ¾ x 11 inches), each mounted on card with a manuscript map locating the property.

items.title: Deed to Mary E. Daves for land in the Rancho Rinconada de los Gatos, Santa Clara County, Calif., 1877
Keep your eye on Palo Alto : real estate promotion, 1892
items.description: The brochure includes a Palo Alto map by H.W. Simkins, city clerk and editor of the Palo Alto Times, from which a large segment on Stanford University, its founders, and the environs of Palo Alto is reprinted.

items.title: Land sale document to Samuel Manning, 1870 Aug. 16.
items.description: Nine and one-half acres in Santa Clara County, Calif.

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company map collection
items.description: Over 300 blueprint maps mounted on 144 canvas-backed, bound sheets showing various towns and localities in the Western United States and depicting the real estate holdings of the Pacific Improvement Company from 1880-1920.

items.title: R.O. Holtzman letter to Herbert C. Nash
items.description: Herbert C. Nash (1860-1902) was private secretary to Leland Stanford, tutor to Leland Stanford Jr., and librarian at Stanford University. Letter from Holtzman, Washington, D.C., real estate agent, to Herbert C. Nash pertaining to the disposition of Leland Stanford's house and property in Washington.

items.title: Records of Stanford properties, 1861-1927
items.description: The collection consists of deeds and legal documents relating to property that was owned by Leland and Jane Stanford, or Stanford University. Leland and Jane Stanford owned over 100,000 acres throughout California . Of special interest are the deeds to the Stanford's three primary residences in Sacramento (1861), San Francisco (1875), and Palo Alto (1876).

items.title: Santa Clara County abstracts of title, 1889-1919
items.description: 8 abstracts of title, city of San Jose, 1889-1919; 1 abstract of title, city of Santa Clara, 1914; and 1 abstract of title, Solano County, 1910 (lacking title page).

items.title: Stanford ranches and lands records, 1838-1896
items.description: In 1876, Leland Stanford acquired 650 acres of the former Rancho San Francisquito with the intention of establishing a rural residence. Abstracts of titles and transcripts of titles to various property holdings of Leland Stanford, including the Palo Alto Stock Farm (Santa Clara Co.), the Vina Ranch (Tehama Co.), the Grindley Farm (Butler Co.), Mayfield Grange (Santa Clara Co.), the Gwinn Ranch (Contra Costa Co.), and San Francisco properties.

items.title: Stanford University map collection, 1853-1998
items.description: The maps in this collection pertain to the University campus, to other lands owned by Jane and Leland Stanford or the University, and to adjacent communities.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Transportation

items.title: A few of the first steamship pioneers living in 1874, surrounding the old ship, and William H. Webb : photographs, ca. 1875
items.description: Included in the photo of pioneers is a photo of the "California."

items.title: George E. Tillitson collection on railroads, 1880-1940
items.description: Collection contains outlines of corporate histories of railroads in the United States and Canada including some streetcar lines and electric interurban lines. Includes dates of incorporation, lists of points served, lists of mileage, time schedules, maps of lines, and lists or reports of accidents.

items.title: I.W. Taber photographs
items.description: Taber was a noted commercial photographer whose studio was based in San Francisco beginning in 1871. 33 mounted prints by Isaiah West Taber (1830-1912) documenting California mountain scenery and the Southern Pacific Railroad.

items.title: Life of Cable Ropes : notebook containing data on the San Francisco cable railroads, 1884-1888
Mayfield Road proposed changes papers
items.description: Consists of two documents: notice to Santa Clara Supervisors relative to planting trees along Mayfield Road (undated but initiated by Leland Stanford) and "field notes of proposed change of road from Mayfield to Searsville" by J. G. McMillan, November 1887.

items.title: Railroad passes issued by and to C.H. Redington, 1873-1924
items.description: Redington received passes from many railroad companies, both before and after his retirement as Assistant Treasurer for the Southern Pacific Company.

items.title: Railroad timetables and other printed ephemera, 1838-1946
items.description: Includes timetables for the New England states (The Pathfinder Railway Guide, (1849-1854 & 1896), the west coast (The Pacific Rail Road Guide, 1869, Standwell's Pacific Coast Railroad Guide and Business Directory, 1869, and Union and Central Pacific Rail Road Line via Omaha or Kansas City to San Francisco, 1883), and the Southern Pacific Railroad, 1880-1884 and 1946.

items.title: Timothy Hopkins transportation collection, 1816-1942
items.description: Correspondence, records, logs, clipping books, timetables, tickets and legal documents pertaining to early railroading in England, India, and the United States. Topics include the construction of the Central Pacific railroad, shipping and aviation.

items.title: William Birelie Hyde papers, 1861-1896
items.description: California surveyor and engineer. Worked for both the Central Pacific and Southern Pacific railroads; later for the San Francisco Water Works Company. Correspondence, notebooks, maps, etc. relating to railroad and engineering ventures in California and the West, 1864-1879.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Water and public works

items.title: John G. McMillan papers, 1887
items.description: Map, estimates of water flow, and letter to Leland Stanford relating to proposed pipeline extending from a proposed dam on Corte Madera Creek to a proposed dam on San Francisquito Creek, 1887.

items.title: Niles Dam collection
items.description: Niles Dam on Alameda Creek was built in 1887 by the Spring Valley Water Company, at the same site where Jose de Jesus Vallejo had build a dam for his grist mill in 1841. This collection consists of the Niles Dam Historic American Engineering Report in three sections – the report, the figures, and the measured drawings.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use

items.title: Angelo F. Semino papers, 1856-1986
items.description: Angelo F. Semino received his a.b. in mechanical engineering from Stanford in 1922. Land deeds for property in Mountain View, California (the Mayfield Mall), together with a 79 page typescript about its history. Original typed reports, copies, reprints, and manuscript notes on heat exchanges in the petroleum industry.

items.title: View of the widening of Kearny Street and construction of the Mechanics' Hotel in San Francisco : photographic print
items.description: Large crowd of men and one woman is gathered in front of the three-story brick Mechanics' Hotel on Kearny Street near Broadway. The hotel has been elevated on wooden supports to widen the street.

sectors.name: Education and research — Campus and student life

items.title: Geological Club of Stanford University minute book
items.description: The Geological Club at Stanford University was founded in 1892, and was later reorganized into a geological society in 1899 and included both students and alumni. Minute book of the Geological Club of Stanford University.

sectors.name: Education and research — Engineering

items.title: J.C.L. Fish notes for the drafting room
items.description: J. C. L. (John Charles Lounsbury) Fish (1870-1962) was a Professor of Civil Engineering, Emeritus, at the School of Engineering, Stanford University. One plane projection with applications to mapping, location and earthwork.

items.title: John Richards, "Works administration: lectures before the student of the Leland Stanford Junior University"
items.description: John Richards was a lecturer in mechanical engineering at Stanford University, 1895-96. Contains ten lectures on shop management; topics include expense, plant implements and processes, plant design, employees, measurements, machine tools, invention, cooperation, and selling the product.

items.title: L.M. Hoskins, the theory of hydraulic motors lecture notes
items.description: Hoskins was professor of applied mathematics at Stanford University from 1892 until his retirement in 1925. Notebook of Hoskins' mimeographed lectures kept by Thomas Henry Pomeroy, with some problem solutions done by Pomeroy, a member of the Stanford class of 1895.

sectors.name: Education and research — Schools, colleges and training

items.title: George A. Merrill letters, 1885-1908
items.description: Letters from Horace Davis, A.S. Hallidie, David Starr Jordan, and L.A. Buchanan, largely pertaining to the Lick School of Mechanical Arts, of which Merrill was principal.

items.title: Stanford University, School of Education, records
items.description: In October 1892, the Department of Education at Stanford University established a kindergarten on campus to serve in part as a laboratory for advanced students of the education department. These records from the School of Education at Stanford University consist of kindergarten records including drawings and short stories by the children, 1892-93; class reading under Clara Vostrovsky; stories, correspondence and notes, 1893-1894 ; and a scrapbook of child studies and learning definitions from schools across the United States, 1891.

sectors.name: Education and research — Science and mathematics

items.title: John Casper Branner papers, 1882-1921
items.description: The first professor to be named at the new Stanford University in 1891, Branner served as professor of geology at Stanford as well as executive head of the Geology Department. Personal papers of John Casper Branner including correspondence, manuscripts, field notebooks, photographs from field work, line drawings of geological formations, scrapbooks of photographs of the effects of the 1906 earthquake, report of the commission investigating the Panama Canal, slides, genealogies of the Baker and Branner families, and books and articles by Branner, many annotated.

items.title: William Russel Dudley papers, 1838-1937 (inclusive), 1864-1912 (bulk)
items.description: Once at Stanford, his work focused on California flora, with a special interest in the study of trees; he was instrumental in the establishment of the Big Basin Redwoods State Park. Papers include field notes, a diary, manuscripts, articles and reprints, maps, and correspondence; most of the field notes relate to California, with occasional later annotations by other botanists.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford history and ceremonial life

items.title: Andrew Putnam Hill photograph album, 1887-circa 1895
items.description: Formerly a student of art, Andrew Putnam Hill became a professional photographer in 1889, opening a studio in San Jose, California with his partner, Sydney J. Yard. The images in this album primarily document the Palo Alto residence of Jane and Leland Stanford, the Palo Alto Stock Farm horses, and Stanford University.

items.title: Andrew Putnam Hill Photograph collection, 1890-1895
items.description: Mounted albumen prints, commercially produced by Hill and his two studios, Hill & Yard and Hill & Watkins, of the newly established Stanford University and of the activity of the Palo Alto Stock Farm, upon which the University had been built.

items.title: Andrew Putnam Hill photographs
items.description: This collection consists of mounted albumen prints commercially produced by A. P. Hill and his two studios, Hill and Yard and Hill and Watkins. Subjects include views of the Stanford University campus, interior and exterior shots of major buildings, events such as the university's opening day and the funeral of Leland Stanford, student groups, and the Palo Alto Stock Farm and horses.

items.title: Archibald J. Treat papers, 1883-1961 (inclusive), 1883-1941 (bulk)
items.description: During the construction of Stanford University, Treat took photographs of the work in progress that were regularly sent to Leland Stanford to keep him informed. These papers pertain largely to Treat's association with Leland Stanford and the history of the University and include correspondence, a notebook (largely in shorthand), his typescript reminiscences, and two letters by his daughter pertaining to her father.

items.title: David Starr Jordan Papers
items.description: Jordan was a naturalist-first a botanist and secondly and of greater significance an ichthyologist. The collection consists primarily of Jordan's voluminous correspondence (62.25 linear ft.) relating to professional and university matters, but also contains other types of material such as writings (published and unpublished), clippings, journals and diaries, scrapbooks, financial papers, biographical and genealogical information, and photographs. He developed the idea of a junior college and was responsible for developing Stanford University into an intellectually competitive university rather than the technical training school envisioned by the founders.

items.title: David Starr Jordan papers, 1861-1981
items.description: In the Spring of 1891, Leland Stanford offered Jordan the presidency of the university established in memory of the late son of Leland Stanford and Jane Lathrop Stanford. The collection consists primarily of Jordan's correspondence relating to professional and university matters, and also contains writings (published and unpublished), clippings, journals and diaries, scrapbooks, financial papers, biographical and genealogical information, and photographs. Materials in the collection reflect Jordan's embrace of and advocacy for eugenics, including his leadership in 19th and 20th century eugenics organizations.

items.title: George Mann Richardson letter to Firstall
items.description: Professor of Organic Chemistry at Stanford University (1891-1902). Letter recounting the first year at Stanford University, in particular difficulties from the lack of equipment, the success of the football team in its first game against Berkeley, and a hiking trip Richardson and his wife took from Stanford to Pescadero.

items.title: George T. Clark papers, 1862-1935
items.description: Clark was Stanford University Librarian, 1907-1928 (emeritus 1928 until his death in 1940) and co-founder and first president of the California Library Association. These papers relate primarily to Clark's research on the life of Leland Stanford and include correspondence, 1924-1935, historical documents, 1862-1893, clippings, photographs, and two notebooks, 1928-1930,for his comprehensive biography of Senator Leland Stanford, published by the Stanford University Press in 1931.

items.title: Grant founding and endowing the Leland Stanford Junior University
items.description: Founding of the University was accomplished by a Grant of Endowment by Jane and Leland Stanford, dated November 1885. Manuscript on parchment, bound with blue leather and ribbon at the top with a manuscript decorative monogram cover signed by Carl Eisenschimel. Includes deeds of land from various counties.

items.title: Henry Z. Osborne papers
items.description: Henry Zenas Osborne (1848-1923) was owner/editor of the Los Angeles Evening Express (1884-1897), gold miner, and California state representative from 1917 until his death in 1923. These papers consist of a letter from Leland Stanford (on U.S. Senate letterhead), 1892; a telegram from Jane L. Stanford, March 1896, thanking Osborne for his loyalty to Leland Stanford; a letter from David Starr Jordan about the Dept. of Mining at Stanford, 1899, with a mention of the success of Herbert C. Hoover (an early graduate of the Dept.); and a letter from John C. Branner, 1921, commenting on an article by Osborne and his opinion on Japan.

items.title: Palo Alto Times, Special Memorial Edition, March 24, 1905
items.description: In 1885, Jane and Leland Stanford founded the Leland Stanford Junior University, in memory of their son. Memorial edition published after the death and funeral of Jane L. Stanford.

items.title: President Benjamin Harrison's tour to the Pacific Coast : photographs and ephemera, 1891-1987
items.description: Collections largely consists of photographs taken during the tour, some of which are arranged in an album; subjects include the visit to Stanford University, San Francisco, Monterey, Sacramento, Salem (Oregon), the Presidential train and its crew, the Presidential party, and crowd scenes at various depots. The pioneer railroad builder had invite d the President to his ranch in Palo Alto to discuss a professorship at the newly built Stanford University and to participate in the dedication of that institution.

items.title: Stanford Alumni Association, alumni reminiscences
items.description: Correspondence between Jack W. Shoup, secretary of the Alumni Association, and alumni concerning memories of Senator and Mrs. Stanford (1955-1956), which included attending parties at the Stanford home, Mr. Stanford observing work on Encina Hall, Mrs. Stanford observing work on Memorial Church, Mrs. Stanford visiting Roble Hall, their attendance at Sunday Chapel on campus, and Mrs. Stanford's funeral.
items.era_note: [Most of the collection, alumni memories of Senator and Mrs. Stanford, concerns this period.]

items.title: Stanford Historical Photograph collection, 1887-circa 1996
items.description: The Stanford Photograph Collection contains over 16,000 images of Stanford scenes including photographs of and relating to the Stanford family, views of the campus and individual buildings, photographs of students and student life activities, and photographs of faculty and administrative staff.

items.title: Stanford University biographical files collection, circa 1891-2011
items.description: The collection contains biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford University.

items.title: Stanford University glass plate negatives, circa 1890-1900
items.description: Eighty glass plate negatives of Stanford images, circa 1890-1900. Subjects include construction, students, faculty, the museum, and the campus.

items.title: Stanford University Photographs, circa 1880s-1906
items.description: Loose and mounted photographs of Greystone Quarry and quarry workers, Stanford campus buildings, Stanford students.

items.title: The search for Jane's cold cream jar [electronic resource]; an archaeological adventure at the Stanfords' Palo Alto home
items.description: The Search for Jane's cold Cream Jar is an interactive CD containing images and information about the history, artifacts, and archaeology of the Stanfords' Palo Alto home.
items.era_note: [Most of this 2003 CD, on the history, artifacts and archaeology of the Stanfords' Palo Alto home, concerns this period.]

items.title: Thomas Welton Stanford Library time capsule collection, 1886-1898
items.description: Collection consists of the items placed in the time capsule by Jane L. Stanford and interred at the cornerstone laying of the library on November 2, 1898. Included are university circulars and registers, entrance exams, commencement programs, photograph of T. W. Stanford, letter by Jane L. Stanford, Bible, crucifix, newspapers of the day, and coins.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford University

items.title: Jane Lathrop Stanford papers, 1860-1983
items.description: In 1885, Jane and Leland Stanford founded the Leland Stanford Junior University, in memory of their son. The papers of Jane L. Stanford pertain largely to the founding and administration of Stanford University, along with her personal and social affairs; included in the papers are correspondence, business records, legal and financial papers, speeches, news clippings, and biographical materials.

items.title: Samuel Franklin Leib papers, 1881-1920
items.description: The collection consists of four major components: Stanford correspondence pertaining to Judge Leib's association with the Stanford family and his responsibilities as a member of the first Board of Trustees of Stanford University (1891-1923); personal correspondence (1885-1910); correspondence pertaining to Leib's fruit and other farm interest (1883-1919); and legal and business correspondence pertaining to his San Jose law practice and local business interests (1881-1920), including cases resulting from the failure of the Savings Bank of San Diego County.

items.title: Stanford University, Vice President for Business Affairs, records
items.description: The collection includes minutes, reports, correspondence, leases, proposals, and other records pertaining to financial and business aspects of the administration of Stanford University. Among the subjects covered by the records are property matters, land development, building projects on campus, academic departments and professional schools, faculty and student housing, the hospital and medical center, SLAC, shopping center, industrial park, Jasper Ridge, relations with Palo Alto, roads, and water.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Art, music, literature and photography

items.title: Angle of repose collection, 1875-1934
items.description: Notes and research materials for Wallace Stegner's Pulitzer Prize winning novel, Angle of Repose , which was based on the life of American author and illustrator Mary Hallock Foote.

items.title: Animal locomotion : an electro-photographic investigation of consecutive phases of animal movements. 1872-1885
Canciones : collection of Mexican folksongs, 1883-1885
items.description: Probably collected by a Californian, possibly Mary Sheldon Barnes or someone in her history class, because the clippings come from San Francisco and San Jose newspapers.

items.title: Carleton E. Watkins photograph collection
items.description: Carleton E. Watkins was a 19th century photographer based in San Francisco who made his name documenting the rapid growth of the American West. This collection contains albumen prints taken throughout Watkins's career, between the years of 1856 and 1885. The bulk of photographs depict Yosemite Valley and Mariposa Grove between 1861 and 1881.

items.title: Eadweard Muybridge photograph collection
items.description: Muybridge worked closely with Senator Leland Stanford on experiments to record horses in motion, trying first to answer the question of whether or not all four feet are off the ground during the trot. This collection includes original Muybridge glass plate negatives and prints, as well as modern day copy prints of his photographs.

items.title: Eadweard Muybridge photograph collection
items.description: This collection by Eadweard Muybridge encompasses stereographic cards, gelatin silver prints, mammoth plates, an 1877 panorama of San Francisco, and Muybridge's motion studies plates.

items.title: Isaiah West Taber photograph collection
items.description: Isaiah West Taber (1830-1912) was an American daguerreotypist, ambrotypist, and photographer. Includes cabinet cards, cartes de visite, and mounted albumen prints taken by Isaiah West Taber. Images are of California scenes, early railroad construction in the Sierra Nevada (California and Nevada) and commercial studio portraiture.

items.title: Leland Stanford : lithograph, 1875
items.description: Portrait print mounted in a folder. Auradou mentions that Henry Steinegger engraved the image about 1875, and that it is rare that a protrait of this size should be engraved on stone.

items.title: Mary Hallock Foote papers, 1863-1924 (inclusive), 1868-1916 (bulk)
items.description: Stories based on the Leadville characters, especially her first novel, The Led-Horse Claim (1883), established Foote's reputation as a Western writer. Correspondence with Helena Gilder, spanning their friendship of fifty years (1868-1916), and with other friends, family, and business associates. The papers include correspondence, literary manuscripts, and artwork.

items.title: Pauline Lane papers, 1878-1897
items.description: Pauline Lane (d. 1902) was the wife of Levi Cooper Lane, president of Cooper Medical College in San Francisco. Primarily ordinal writings by Pauline Lane, translations of foreign works into English, and books of poems.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Design and architecture

items.title: Archibald J. Treat photograph collection
items.description: Photographs documenting construction of Leland Stanford Junior University, used as progress reports and sent to university founder Senator Leland Stanford for his approval. Views include the Stanford quadrangle, museum, mausoleum and Encina Hall, and some group shots of the construction workers.

items.title: Palo Alto ranch employee time records
items.description: Time record notebook for employees on Palo Alto Ranch, maintained by J. C. Conway. Includes records for named employees and the hours spent on specific Quad construction jobs during March 1892.

items.title: Stanford Historical Society, Historic Houses III : research and production materials, 1972-2004 (inclusive), 1999-2004 (bulk)
items.description: Research and production materials for the book, HISTORIC HOUSES III: SAN JUAN NEIGHBORHOOD, STANFORD UNIVERSITY, published by the Stanford Historical Society in 2005. Includes Byron Feig's original watercolor painting used on the cover and his original pencil drawings of each house; and copies of architectural drawings for several of the houses featured in the book.
items.era_note: [Much of this material, research and drawings on the historic faculty houses of Stanford's San Juan neighborhood, concerns this period.]

items.title: Stanford University, Museum, Committee for Art, Stanford portfolio records, 1970-1980
items.description: Research files of Hametia Fielder King relating to the design and construction of the Stanford Museum of Art, used by the Museum docent program for their "Stanford Portfolio." Materials include notes and correspondence of Mrs. King, photocopied historic sources, and contemporary brochures, articles, and clippings.
items.era_note: [Most of the collection, research files on the design and construction of the Stanford museum building, concerns this period.]

items.title: Stanford University, Operations and Maintenance, Maps and Records, architectural drawings, 1889-1994 [microform].
items.description: Microfiche copies of architectural drawings of buildings on the Stanford University campus; and photocopy of the department's "vault inventory" of drawings, most of which are included in these copies. There are also some copies of drawings for the Hanna House, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.

items.title: Views of Thurlow Lodge by Carleton Watkins: photograph album, circa 1874
items.description: The album contains original albumen prints of the mansion and grounds of Milton S. Latham in Menlo Park, California. This album, with images approximately 14 x 17 inches, was originally presented to David Farquharson, architect of Thurlow Lodge.

sectors.name: Arts and culture

items.title: [California Winery Exhibition 1894] [graphic]
items.description: Pair of large original photographs (27 x 33 cm) by Taber of the California Winery’s exhibition at the Midwinter Fair (1894). The photos show the building’s ornate entrance (with the entrance designed to appear as a wine barrel) as well as the decorative Tasting Room, with many tables (and bottles) but sans visiteurs.

items.title: Stanford family library, 1795-1902 (inclusive), 1834-1897 (bulk)
