items.description: A sampling of the books contained in the libraries of Jane Lathrop Stanford, Leland Stanford, and their son, Leland Stanford, Jr. Included are Bibles, religious publications, children's stories, a number of adventure series for boys, history books, travel essays, tourist guides, and novels. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Society and community — Local and California history

items.title: "The Sky Lark"
items.description: Volume 1, issue 1, of a one-page advertiser issued in Mayfield, CA, Oct. 21, 1876. Includes short notice that Peter Coutts was building a brick tower near his home.

items.title: Britton and Rey, Lithographers. Artotypes : Artistic homes of California, published in San Francisco Newsletter and Advertiser
items.description: This collection includes artotype images of private homes, public buildings, businesses, and other images of San Francisco and the Bay area from 1887 to 1902. The artotypes were published along with the San Francisco Newsletter, and are dated accordingly.

items.title: California biography collection
items.description: Consists of ephemeral items relating to people widely known and relatively unknown in California. Contains mostly newspaper obituaries, but also includes: handwritten biographical documents, invitations, wedding announcements, family reunion newsletters, genealogy forms, family trees, memorials, political speeches, campaign material, correspondence, and newspaper and magazine clippings.

items.title: California photographs : album, 1885-1899
items.description: Annotated photograph album of California landscape and topographical views. The prints include 19th century views of Palo Alto, Stanford University, San Francisco, Monterey; and in Southern California, Pasadena, Los Angeles, Riverside and Redlands.

items.title: California photographs, circa 1882-1940
items.description: 49 photographs. Includes Sierras, boats, Golden Gate Bridge under construction, one unidentified portrait, Pacific Coast Amateur photography association meeting 1889 photographing a solar eclipse, Higuera House in Warm Springs (Fremont) in 1882, interior views.

items.title: Carleton Watkins stereoview and cabinet photographs
items.description: Photographs by or published by Carleton E. Watkins in the form of cabinet cards or stereographs. All but one depict California scenes, including the railroad ferry Solano , Spring Valley Water Works projects in the San Francisco Bay Area, and views of Santa Monica, Monterey and Yosemite.

items.title: Eadweard Muybridge photographs, ca. 1870-1890
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Harry C. Peterson lantern slides, 1892-1917
items.description: Named the Director and Curator of the Stanford University Museum in 1899, he remained there until 1918, adding collections to the Museum and writing historical papers. Consists of lantern slides and photographs circa 1892-1917.

items.title: Illustrated newspapers reporting news from Santa Clara County, 1897-1900
items.description: Articles describe leading business establishments and institutions in Santa Clara County and its cities. Includes many illustrations and several pages of advertisements.

items.title: Katherine E. Doyle collection of photographs
items.description: Collection contains one print and 22 glass plate negatives, the latter depicting the grounds and interior of a large estate, probably the Doyle residence known as Ringwood in Menlo Park. The mounted albumen print is captioned "Western Union Telegraph Company at Hotel Del Monte, Nov. 8, 1897," and is credited to C.W.J. Johnson.

items.title: Main street, Palo Alto (Calif.) : photograph, ca.1898
items.description: View of University Avenue. Printed on wall of building on the left is "Mail pouch tobacco."

items.title: Mary Sheldon Barnes collection of Pacific Slope materials, 1769-1898
items.description: Letters, reminiscences, interviews, and term papers written for and collected by Mary Sheldon Barnes and her students in Stanford's Pacific Slope history class. Includes manuscripts of William B. Ide and others on the Bear Flag Revolt; a letter by Jessie Fremont; and other materials pertaining to California mining and early life in the Pacific states.

items.title: Newspaper devoted to the interests of the California pioneers, 1897, vol. XII, no.6.
items.description: Articles of interest to settlers and pioneers of California including mining news, obituaries, local observances, biographies and illustrations.

items.title: Pacific Slope scrapbooks, 1819-1906
items.description: The first series of scrapbooks was created by mayor (and later governor) Washington Bartlett, containing articles pertaining to political and civic issues in San Francisco and California from 1855 to 1886, as well as some notes and memoranda chronicling his duties as mayor. Other scrapbooks were assembled by Mary Sheldon Barnes in the 1890s and include articles and other ephemera related to the American West, including material on Native Americans, Oregon territory, Alaska, Pacific and Asiatic relations, and the San Francisco Peninsula.

items.title: Peter Coutts' Story papers
items.description: Jean-Baptiste Paulin Caperon (better known in California as Peter Coutts), was a successful French businessman, book collector and editor of the republican, anti-royalist paper, LA LIBERTE. In 1875 Caperon, now known as Peter Coutts, purchased 1,400 acres just north of Mayfield and named it Rancho Matadero. Collection consists mostly of clippings and published articles, with two unpublished papers: Geoffrey Bilson, "Peter Coutts - 'The Frenchman'" and Regina Kriss, "The influence and effects of French politics (1848-1880) on the life of Stanford's Frenchman, Peter Coutts," 1965.
items.era_note: [Most of the collection, articles and papers on Peter Coutts, who owned Rancho Matadero from 1875 to 1880, concerns this period.]

items.title: Reid W. Dennis collection of California lithographs, 1850-1908
items.description: This collection of prints, mostly lithographs (including chromolithographs and colored lithographs), as well as one engraving, primarily portray San Francisco city views, public buildings, and landscapes. Subjects also include San Jose, Stanford University, the U.S. Navy Yard at Mare Island, San Diego, and San Luis Rey.

items.title: The eastern editors visit to Vacaville : photographs, 1892 May 21st.
items.description: The photographs depict two scenes along Main Street with a railroad, parade of horse-drawn carts and several buildings, one displaying the American flag. Vacaville was hosting eastern newspaper editors in order to promote their town and orchard industry.

sectors.name: Society and community — Medicine and public health

items.title: Agnews State Asylum photograph album, 1890-1906
items.description: Consists of photo albumn with 62 photos and an additional 18 loose photos. Depicts Agnews State Asylum in Santa Clara, California. The images depict residents, staff, grounds, and the interior of the asylum including: offices, kitchen, dining room, workshops, the pharmacy, and other areas.

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: A camping party in California, 1887
items.description: A transcript of "A Camping Trip to California" undertaken by four friends: Charles Wheeler and his soon-to-be-bride Lily Marsh, and James de Fremery (driver and photographer of the expedition) and his wife Wilhelmina Suermondt de Fremery over two weeks in the summer of 1887. This is a bound typescript of the account originally written by Wilhelmina de Fremery to share her adventure with her family in Holland.
items.era_note: [Nearly all of this 1960 typescript is an account of a two-week camping trip made in the summer of 1887.]

items.title: Alice G. Lathrop photograph album, circa 1870-circa 1880
items.description: Photographs, mostly cabinet cards, and one tintype of unidentified friends and family members, taken by San Francisco photographers.

items.title: Amy White photograph album of the American West
items.description: Photo album from the early 1870s commemorating a trip to California with prints by Carleton Watkins, Alfred Hart, Eadweard Muybridge, and others. While there is little known documentation about its creation or provenance beyond the inscription "Amy White, from her brother Howard. Christmas 1871," evidence suggests this scrapbook was compiled to commemorate a trip (probably by Amy, and possibly with her brother) through the western United States on the Central Pacific Railroad, traveling through Utah, Nevada, the Sierras and Yosemite, San Francisco and the peninsula, Napa, Mendocino, and southern Oregon.

items.title: Anderson family papers, 1848-1963
items.description: The family settled on the East Coast, later moving West; the Andersons contributed to society in the fields of theology, education and literature. Personal and business letters, literary and scientific manuscripts, official and legal documents, and clippings comprising a history of Edward Coffin Anderson (1821-1890); his sons, Melville Best Anderson (1851-1933) and Edward Playfair Anderson (1856-1951); and grandsons, Malcolm Playfair Anderson (1878-1949) and Robert Van Vleck Anderson (1884-1949); together with general material on the Anderson, Best, Playfair, Gurnee, and Van Vleck families.

items.title: Charles A. Gunnison journals, 1881-1887
items.description: Personal diaries of author and poet Charles Andrew Gunnison capturing his daily life in San Francisco, friendship with Timothy Hopkins, and travels in Europe and Asia. The journals include newspaper clippings of his poems and articles printed in the San Francisco Evening Bulletin and Sacramento Record Union.

items.title: Culver family papers, 1858-1915
items.description: Includes correspondence, diaries, and photographs. The Collection reflects J. O. Culver's experience as a lawyer, his service as an Army Paymaster and Post Office Inspector, his endeavors in small fruit culture, and his excursions into prospecting and mining. In general, the family letters and papers give a panorama of middle class society in New York, Wisconsin and Missouri, and Colorado and California, from 1860 to 1915, a familiar pattern in the United States of looking ever westward for opportunity.

items.title: Diario borrador : Notebook of accounts and special events, 1860-1890
items.description: Includes a list of deaths, prices of supplies, verses of songs, a recipe for "cleansing the teeth" (the only item in English), notes of departures for family members (to Sulphur Banks, Lake County; Guadalupe, Los Angeles, Idria, etc.), and on the last page of writing, an account of the trip from Tepic to Mazatlán to San Francisco to San Jose to Hacienda de Nueva Almaden.

items.title: Ellen Coit Elliott papers, 1891-1942
items.description: Ellen Coit Elliott, wife of Orrin Leslie Elliott, Stanford University's first registrar, was the author of several books of poetry and an autobiography, IT HAPPENED THIS WAY; AMERICAN SCENE. These papers consist of photocopies of a diary, 1891 to 1893, and of her letters to her husband written from Pacific Grove, 1898 to 1904; as well as a typescript poem and a copy of her book UNICORNS BROWSING AT DAWN (1942).

items.title: Emil Fischer papers, 1865-1984
items.description: Emil Fischer (October 9, 1852 – July 15, 1919) was a German chemist who won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Family albums, glass negatives, album of (52) loose vintage photographs; personal letters, scientific publications, documents, clippings, and miscellaneous items. The materials document the lives of Emil Fischer, Hermann Otto Laurenz Fischer and Agnes Fischer Peterson.

items.title: Frank Shay, "A lifetime in California, 1860-1939" typescript
items.description: Growing up in California, Shay served in a wide variety of positions throughout his life, including special reporter for Sacramento and Virginia City newspapers, accountant and telegrapher for the Sutro Tunnel Company, and, after completing his law degree at Hastings Law College, attorney for the Southern Pacific Company and personal counsel for railroad president Leland Stanford. Autobiography, annotated by the author.

items.title: Handmade keepsake commemorating the golden wedding anniversary of Mary Kellogg Crittenden and Timothy Hopkins
items.description: Timothy Hopkins became a protégé of Senator Leland Stanford, a treasurer of the Central Pacific Railroad, a Director of the Southern Pacific Railroad and of the Wells Fargo Bank. This keepsake, presumably made for the family and in all likelihood unique, contains the following original documents (in order of inclusion): individual cabinet photographs of the Mary and Timothy; the engraved wedding invitation; the engraved "At Home" invitation to the reception at the Windsor Hotel; press clippings from three different newspapers containing accounts of the wedding and the reception in New York; a photograph of the bride in her wedding dress; two press clippings describing the reception held in San Francisco; and a final press clipping describing a "German" or "Cotillon" entertainment given at the Hopkins mansion in February 1882.
items.era_note: [Nearly all of this keepsake, photographs, invitations and press accounts of the couple's 1882 wedding, concerns this period.]

items.title: Isabella Cass diary, 1884-1885
items.description: Diary written during her visit to the Hopkins estate, Sherwood Hall, in Menlo Park, California, with a few entries during her return trip to Massachusetts. Other people mentioned include Jane and Leland Stanford, Mr. and Mrs. Edward C. Burrage, and James C. Flood.

items.title: Leland Stanford papers, 1840-1909
items.description: Early in the 1860s, Stanford joined with three other Sacramento merchants--Charles Crocker, Mark Hopkins, and Collis P. Huntington--in the building of the Central Pacific Railroad. In 1885, Leland and Jane founded Leland Stanford Jr. University in memory of their son. Correspondence, telegrams; business, legal, financial, and official papers; speeches, journals, and newsclippings; and other materials relating to the construction of the Central Pacific Railroad, Stanford's political career, business and financial interests, and the founding and construction of Stanford University.

items.title: Leland Stanford photograph album, 1868-1882
items.description: Images in the album are largely of Leland Stanford Jr., from the age of 3 months to 14 years; others include one image of Leland Jr. with Jane Stanford, which has been hand colored, and several images of Leland Stanford Sr.

items.title: Leland Stanford, Jr. papers, 1871-1893
items.description: Leland Stanford, Jr., the only child of Senator and Mrs. Leland Stanford, was born in Sacramento, California on May 14, 1868. Correspondence, journal, notebooks, drawings, personality studies and school work of Leland Jr., and condolences to Senator and Mrs. Stanford regarding the death of their son.

items.title: Stanford family greeting card collection, 1880-1883
items.description: Collection contains 29 greeting cards, 1880-1883 and undated; photographic reproductions of several cards; and a clipping about the collection, 1982. Several cards were sent by Wilson Taylor, a friend of Leland Stanford Jr., to Stanford family members for Christmas 1882.

items.title: Stanford family photograph collection, circa 1860-1905
items.description: Primarily studio portraits (mounted albumen prints) of Senator Leland Stanford, Jane Lathrop Stanford, Leland Stanford Jr., Gertrude Stanford, and Elizabeth Stanford. There are also a few images taken by Leland Stanford, Jr.

items.title: Stanford family scrapbooks. 1865-1894
items.description: Family scrapbooks, compiled for the Stanford family. Subjects cover a wide range of family activities including railroad affairs, the Palo Alto Stock Farm, the Vina Ranch, the University, the United States Senate, politics, personal affairs of the Stanford's, and horses.

items.title: Student cross country travel : photograph albums, ca. 1893
items.description: Two uncaptioned photo albums and some loose prints chronicling the travels and university studies of a student or group of students. Apparently setting out from the east coast on his way to Stanford, the photographer includes photos of Harvard University, New England, the grave markers of famous writers, Yellowstone Park, Native Americans, soldiers and military posts, rodeos, farming & mining operations, river boats, Mt. Shasta, and the San Francisco Bay Area. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Society and community — Race, ethnicity and immigration

items.title: [Cabinet card of an unidentified Chinese American man].
Certificates of residence for Chinese laborers, 1894-1897
items.description: Under the provisions of the 1892 Geary Act, which amended the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882, all Chinese in the United States were required to apply for, obtain, and carry a government-issued certificate of residence proving their legal presence in the United States. Collection consists of 17 certificates of residence for Chinese laborers in California, dated from 1894 to 1897.

items.title: Dennis J. Oliver and family diaries, 1848-1898
items.description: Dennis had several partners during the following years and was burned out twice, but he prospered by providing the paints, oils, glass, etc. needed by the growing city. Diaries of Dennis J. Oliver, his wife, Bridget, and their children: Joseph, Anna Maria, and Minnie. Oliver was involved in the founding of the Hibernian Society and the Irish Emigrant Society.

items.title: Walter and Emma Fong collection, 1889-2001 (inclusive), 1889-1928 (bulk)
items.description: Walter Ngon Fong (1866-1906) and Emma Fong Kuno nee Howse (1873-1948) met at Stanford University and were married in Colorado, as interracial marriage was prohibited under California Law. Photographs, manuscript materials, and printed materials related to the lives of Walter Ngon Fong (1866-1906, widely reported to be the first Chinese student to graduate from Stanford [class of 1896, A.B.]) and his wife, Emma Howse Fong.

sectors.name: Society and community — Religion, clubs and societies

items.title: Essays on spiritualism written for THE SARATOGA SENTINEL, 1878-1888
items.description: Newspaper clippings and one manuscript written by King, together with published responses primarily by William H. Tiffany bound in a scrapbook kept by King. New York medical doctor, a spiritualist.

items.title: Membership documents for the National Society of the Daughters of the American Revolution, 1896
items.description: One document appoints her an approved member of the national society by virtue of her descent from William Russell, who "with unfailing loyalty rendered material aid to the cause of American Independence as a Brigadier General during the Revolutionary War." The other document appoints Mrs. Leib as Chapter Regent of the Daughters of the American Revlution in the City of San Jose, California.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Government and public administration

items.title: 1893 Santa Clara County, CA Index Poll Tax List & Sheriff's Register of Actions; 1895 Santa Clara County, CA Sheriff's Register of Actions #9
items.description: Collection consists of 2 volumes: 1893 Santa Clara County, CA Index Poll Tax List & Sheriff's Register of Actions; 1895 Santa Clara County, CA Sheriff's Register of Actions #9.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Politics and elections

items.title: Searsville precinct (San Mateo County, Calif.) : Great Register, 1896-1899
items.description: Voting register, listing occupation, age, height (and other physical characteristics), country of birth, town of residence, ability to read and write, and if departed, destination.

sectors.name: Ideas and intellectual history

items.title: [Nine pamphlets from the pen of C. E. Pickett presented to Leland Stanford by the author]
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Advertising and marketing

items.title: Contract for painted bulletin or wall display, 1922
items.description: The correspondence and contract are with the Merchants' Association of San Jose. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Crate, can, and bottle label collection, circa 1920s-1940s
items.description: The collection documents the intersecting agriculture, food processing, and marketing industries, particularly in California, with large holdings of labels for beverages, canned foods, and fruits, especially apples, pears, and citrus fruits. Comprises thousands of crate, can, and bottle labels, the bulk of which were designed and created between the 1920s and 1940s by San Francisco and Los Angeles lithography companies.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Aerospace and defence

items.title: [Chinese-American pilot Wallace S. Chinn in Redwood City, California] [graphic].
items.description: A picture apparently taken at the airfield at Redwood City, California, in operation from 1915 until the 1930s as site of a School of Aviation then owned by World War I flying ace Walter Varney, an aviation pioneer who later founded a company that evolved into United Airlines. Photograph inscribed "Sincerely Yours, Wallace S. Chinn. 7-13-20".

items.title: Alfred S. Niles and Joseph S. Newell, Airplane Structures, typescript, circa 1928
items.description: Collection contains corrected typescripts of chapters 1 through 15, list of figures, illustrations, and index. Alfred S. Niles was professor of aeronautic engineering at Stanford University from 1927 until his retirement in 1959. In 1929 the first edition of Airplane Structures by Alfred S. Niles and Joseph S. Newell was published by John Wiley & Sons.

items.title: David Richard David papers, ca. 1934-1945
items.description: Davis was closely associated with aircraft development through the early part of the 20th century. Included are Davis's original papers and photographs for the innovative airfoil he theorized, designed, uniquely tested and finally patented. Known as the Davis Wing, it bettered performance by 20% and was used by Consolidated in production of their PBY-5 Catalina and Liberator B-24's - outstanding long-range bombers during WW II.

items.title: Irmgard Flugge-Lotz, Collector, Technical reports and papers, 1929-1984 (inclusive), 1929-1945 (bulk)
items.description: Irmgard Flugge-Lotz was professor of engineering at Stanford from 1949 until her retirement in 1968. These reports and papers on aerodynamics are primarily in German, with a few in French, Italian, and English; research facilities represented include Aeodynamische Versuchsanstalt in Gottingen and Deutsche Versuchsanstalt fur Luftfahrt in Berlin-Aldershof.

items.title: Leonard Eugene Root papers, 1923-1983
items.description: As the first Director of the Development and Planning Department, he proposed the creation of the Missile Systems Division to develop ballistic missiles and satellites. In 1961, he was named President of Lockheed Missiles and Space Company, and in 1969, he became Group Vice President of Lockheed Aircraft Corporation. The Leonard Eugene Root papers document his personal life and career in the aerospace industry from the 1940s to the 1960s, and includes correspondence, notebooks, business files, publications, memorabilia.

items.title: Letters patent, 1938-1939
items.description: These are patents for foil for passage through a fluid (Great Britain, 9 May 1938) and improvements in fluid foil (France, 21 Apr. 1939). [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Nicholas J. Hoff papers, 1903-1997 (inclusive), 1940-1997 (bulk)
items.description: Nicholas J. Hoff was a professor emeritus of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University at the time of his death in 1997. Collection includes articles and papers by Hoff on aircraft structures and other matters, 1944-1981; diplomas, awards and other biographical materials, 1928-1997; and materials he collected on the history of aviation including articles, reports, and photographs, 1903-1958.

items.title: William Frederick Durand papers, 1876-1979
items.description: Although his early research was in marine engineering, Durand was best known for his contributions to the science of aeronautics, specifically the development of the first variable pitch propeller. Papers include correspondence, manuscripts, typescripts, research notes, reports, reprints, clippings, photographs, and memorabilia pertaining to his research in engineering and aeronautics and professional matters; a copy of his published autobiography; and biographical and scientific writings by others relating to Durand.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Computer hardware

items.title: Moore School of Electrical Engineering, Bell Telephone Laboratories, RCA Research and Engineering : RADIO-CRAFT archive, 1937-1938
items.description: An archive of six original photographs, fifteen letters, four scientific papers, one typescript of a article for RADIO-CRAFT and one news clipping, all related to three early electro-mechanical equation solving analog computers.--vendor.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Construction and civil engineering practice

items.title: Guy F. Atkinson Company records, ca. 1921-1961
items.description: The Guy F. Atkinson Company is a construction and engineering firm founded in 1926 that specializes in civil projects such as dams, tunnels, and roadbuilding. The records contain materials related to the construction business (estimates, contracts, agreements, indexes of jobs, calculations, budgets, business correspondence, summary sheets, overheads, as well as individual projects' files), legal and financial papers, along with industrial publications, various leaflets, catalogs, clippings, photos, and scrapbooks.

items.title: Palmer and McBryde papers, 1921-1927
items.description: Construction firm, San Francisco. Correspondence, contracts, bills and estimates relating to Palmer and McBryde's construction of the Stanford Stadium (1921) and reconstruction of the stadium stands (1925, 1927).

items.title: Snyder Company records, 1912-1929
items.description: Records include specifications and calculations, estimates, correspondence, engineering drawings, charts, reports, and photographs pertaining to banks, schools, factories, and other commercial buildings. San Francisco buildings include Children's Hospital, Gallileo High School, Horticultural Building at the Panama-Pacific International Exposition, City Hall, and California Academy of Sciences.

items.title: William Bruce McMillan papers, 1905-2014 1920-1946 (bulk)
items.description: This collection contains materials related to the life and work of noted civil engineer William McMillan, who received his Bachelors and Engineers' degrees from Stanford University in 1911 and 1912. Incluided are biographical materials, news clippings, correspondence, and technical reports related to McMillan's engineering career.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Electronics industry (national and international)

items.title: Billy Malone, "The Early History of the Magnavox Company"
items.description: One of the founders of the Magnavox Company was Edwin S. Pridham, who graduated from Stanford University in May 1909 with an a.b. in physics. Other subjects covered in this history include the company's research in Napa, California, the invention of the loudspeaker, anti-noise systems used by the military, and the company's facility in Oakland, California.
items.era_note: [Most of this history, on the founding of the Magnavox Company in 1911 and its early work, concerns this period.]

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — General manufacturing

items.title: Cours supérieur de tissage. École de la Salle
items.description: An exceptional technical handbook written in a student's neat calligraphic hand for textile-weaving courses, taught in Lyon at the École de la Salles by professors Brocard and Granger. The volume is richly decorated with a numerous drawings and 137 original fabric samples.

items.title: Eloesser-Heynemann Co. records, 1860-1972
items.description: Comprises correspondence, news clippings, business documents, and ephemera related to the history of Eloesser-Heynemann Co., an early clothing manufacturing company founded in San Francisco. The company was a competitor of Levi Strauss & Co., and known for its denim and workwear, and its trademark logo, "Can't Bust 'Em."

items.title: General Cable Corporation and Hoover Dam photo album
items.description: This collections consists of approximately 282 black and white photographs depicting the General Cable Corporation factory(ies) used to manufacture the power transmission lines for the Hoover Dam. The images also include the Hoover Dam under construction, Lake Mead, transmission lines to Los Angeles and a Southwestern Portland Cement Factory plant.

items.title: George P. Hurst collection of Risdon Iron Works and Union Iron Works records, circa 1890-1980
items.description: From 1897 to 1911 the Risdon Iron Works designed and built 63 gold dredges, many of which were shipped to mining fields in other parts of the world. Collection of photographs, catalogs, notebooks, blueprints, and other records from the Risdon Iron Works and Union Iron Works in San Francisco, California, particularly concerning the manufacture of dredges and mining machinery.

items.title: Gladding, McBean and Company account book
items.description: Gladding, McBean and Company is a California firm that manufactures clay roofing tiles. Photocopy of contract book with brief entries on building, location, owner, architect, material, and amount; included are entries pertaining to buildings on the Stanford University campus.

items.title: Ralph Harrison Sherry papers, 1907-1953
items.description: Sherry earned his a.b. in chemistry at Stanford University, 1904, and his M.A. in 1905; he was a metallurgical engineer. Papers consist primarily of charts, drawings, illustrations, and photographs used in his book STEEL TREATING PRACTICE, published in 1929.

items.title: Stauffer Chemical Company records, 1881-1987
items.description: The Stauffer Chemical Company was founded in 1885 in San Francisco by two European immigrants, John Stauffer, Sr. and Christian de Guigne. The company mainly produced herbicides for corn and rice. The materials include minutes books, financial statements, correspondence, and photographs.

items.title: Welton J. Crook, "Linotype metal. Part I, Preliminary study, experimental alloys, methods of manufacture" typescript
items.description: He joined the Stanford faculty in the Department of Mining and Metallurgy in 1921. Includes bibliographical references and photographs.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Labor and professional organizations

items.title: [Workers at Hickmott Canning Company in Oakland, California]
items.description: Occupational photograph showing male and female workers at Hickmott Canning Company, in which some affectionately hold hands and/or have their arms draped around each other's shoulders.

items.title: C. Lyn Fox papers pertaining to the Longshoremen's strike and the Pacific Coast maritime strike, 1934-1937
items.description: C. Lyn Fox was assistant to Thomas G. Plant, the President of the Waterfront Employer's Union, and wrote news memoranda for the president, 1935-1936.

items.title: Eric Hakon Thomsen papers, 1936-1941
items.description: Correspondence with John Steinbeck, 1936-1940, including 3 cards, 4 letters, and 1 telegram from Steinbeck to Thomsen, 2 letters from Carol Steinbeck to Thomsen, and carbons of 2 letters from Thomsen to Steinbeck. Included is one file about the John Steinbeck Committee, a short-lived California farm labor advocacy society, 1939, and references to the Associated Farmers.

items.title: Herbert Gregory Prichard diary recording labor strife and the shipbuilding industry in the San Francisco Bay Area, 1918-1919
items.description: The diary records first-hand observation and eyewitness accounts of the coal strikes and ensuing violence that occurred in the San Francisco Bay Area in the early 1900's.

items.title: International Longshoremen's Association Local 38-79 member Arthur Otto Tallaksen records, 1918-1948
items.description: Arthur Otto Tallaksen was a Norwegian longshoremen. The materials document Tallaksen's involvement with the International Longshoremen's Association, the International Longshore and Warehouse Union, Norsk Matros- og Fyrbøter-Union [Norwegian Seafarers' Union], and the United States Coast Guard.

items.title: Letter from Guernsey Frazer as Executive Secretary, Associated Farmers of California, San Francisco, to John T. Mills, Taylor Bates & Co., 48 Wall Street, New York
items.description: Frazer charged that "Madame Secretary Perkins" - Franklin Roosevelt's Secretary of Labor Frances Perkins, the first woman appointed to a presidential Cabinet post - had "deliberately overruled the uniform line of court decisions to protect Communists, radicals, 'pinks' and similar vermin" by refusing to deport "obnoxious" and "troublesome" Red agitators who were trying to organize migratory farm worker unions in California's central valley. The Associated Farmers group had just been formed by "big growers" of the California Farm Bureau Federation and State Chamber of Commerce to prevent this "serious menace to the welfare of the state ... threatening the existence of the state's vast agricultural industry."

items.title: Operating force, Travers and Sakata, 1933 [graphic]
items.description: Documentary photographic portrait of the workforce for a California grower at the end of the season, with 61 women and 74 men-all Caucasian-and in the center, Kyusaburo [Harry] Sakata, a Japanese immigrant who was the co-owner of the operation.

items.title: Oral history interview with Gallagher on the I.W.W. and Tom Mooney by Willa Klug Baum
items.era_note: [Most of this 1955 interview, on the I.W.W. and the Tom Mooney case, concerns this period.]

items.title: Papers pertaining to the Mooney case, 1916-1933
items.description: Manuscripts, typescripts, notes, press releases, pamphlets, newspaper clippings, and ephemera related to the Mooney case, likely created or collected by San Francisco Chronicle political editor Earl C. Behrens. Pro-Mooney pamphlets and ephemera were published by the International Workers' Defense League and the Tom Mooney Molders Defense Committee.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Magnetic recording and data storage

items.title: Bell Labs Early Stereo Collection
items.description: Bell Labs had been involved with developing improved sound recording and reproduction since 1915, and was willing to record Stokowski and the orchestra among other test subjects, and so in in 1931 and 1932, one hundred experimental high fidelity, long playing, and stereophonic recordings of the Philadelphia Orchestra were produced. Master dubs on open reel tape, commercially released LP pressings, and a metal part for the Bell Telephone Laboratoriesalbums titled "Early Hi-Fi Wide Range and Stereo Recordings Made by Bell Telephone Laboratories in the 1930s - Leopold Stokowski Conducts the Philadelphia Orchestra, 1931-1932."
items.era_note: [Most of the collection, a 1979 reissue of Bell Labs' experimental high-fidelity and stereo recordings of 1931 and 1932, concerns this period.]

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Networking and telecommunications

items.title: 600-foot tower design for Federal Telegraph Co. : blueprints and typescript, 1912
[New England Telephone and Telegraph Company infrastructure photograph album] [graphic]
items.description: A photograph album consiting of more than one hundred 7 1/2 x 11 inch photographs each mounted on linen. The photographs offer a view into the state-of-the-art in telephone/telegraph cabling and outside plant as well as how that infrastructure was used to justify rates in 1925.

items.title: Guglielmo Marconi postcards, 1912-1913
items.description: Collection consists of 5 Guglielmo Marconi postcards from Italy. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Laying the first Pacific cable : diaries of cable engineer Henry Clifford on the ships Colonia and Anglia, 1902-1903
items.description: The diaries begin with joining the Anglia at Greenwich on January 7, 1902, and from there on there is a daily record of the voyage to Brisbane where the first leg - from Southport to Norfolk Island - begins. In April 1903 Clifford joined the Colonia laying the cable from Manila to Honolulu via Guam and Midway. In addition to the diary entries there are many clippings about the cable and ships, lists of expenses, and other notes including a diagram of the faults in the cable on the Anglia.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Radio, vacuum tubes and microwave

items.title: Baird Television : sales brochure, 1939
items.description: Describes and illustrateds different models, and describes why Baird televisions are better than the competitors. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Baird Television Limited reports and brochures, 1931-1939
items.description: "Report Of The Directors", "Statement Of Accounts "and other information provided to the shareholders. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Clippings about Elwell and his work, 1912-1934
items.description: Includes articles and illustrations about radio stations designed and built by Elwell, the Elwell mast, the Elwell Poulsen Arcs, and the continuous Wave Radio Station.

items.title: Cyril Frank Elwell papers, 1930-1961
items.description: Cyril Frank Elwell (1884 – 1963) was an American inventor and pioneer in the development of radio-telegraphy and long-distance communication. Contains several versions of Elwell's autobiography, including one written under a pseudonym and correspondence with possible ghost writers, especially R. B. Stone. Also includes engineering papers, clippings, biographical materials, correspondence, and photographs.

items.title: DeForest Radio Telephone Companies, 1907-1920 : typescript, 1977
items.description: Mayes has an interest in the history of radio tube development.

items.title: Federal telegraph company : photographs
items.description: Early 20th century photographs depict the first Poulsen arc from Denmark; a wireless telephone station; generators and cabinets; interior and exterior views of various telegraph stations in the United States, Ireland and England; and construction sites for new stations.

items.title: Herbert B. Van Etten papers, 1912-1947
items.description: Notebook with diagrams and explanations of the development of the audion amplifier and oscillator, indexed, 1912. Record of patent infringement lawsuits, ca. 1933, with published record of notebook contents. Newsclips from The Palo Alto Times, 1947, re the significance of the electronic discoveries made in Palo Alto.

items.title: His Master's Voice Television : sales brochure, 1937
Karl R. Spangenberg papers, 1935-1961
items.description: Karl Spangenberg (1910-1964) served as a Professor of Electrical Engineering at Stanford. This collection contains correspondence, teaching materials, subject files, and research notes of Karl R. Spangenberg relating to his work as an electircal engineer specilizing in vacuum tubes at Stanford.

items.title: Lester L. Libby papers, ca. 1936-1984
items.description: The Lester L. Libby papers consist of files created and maintained by Lester Louis Libby (1916-2002) pertaining to his work in the technical field of sound engineering and the application of microwave frequency technologies in various industries including radio, television, and early electronics from the 1930s to the 1970s. Materials include Libby's resarch notebooks, work papers, diagrams and schematics, articles he authored, and patents received.

items.title: Oral history transcription, 21 Jan. 1974
items.description: The interview by Arthur L. Norberg covers high school and first jobs (1-8), interest in amateur radio (8-18), Heintz and Kaufman, Inc. (18-44), Eitel McCullough, Inc. (44-96), and appendices (including copies of photographs).
items.era_note: [More than half of this 1974 interview, on early jobs, amateur radio, Heintz and Kaufman and early Eitel-McCullough, concerns this period.]

items.title: Osram Valves : The Baird Televisor [diagram]
items.description: Diagram of the first successful "television" transmitter exhibited at South Kensington Museum.

items.title: Ralph M. Hare photograph album and typescript documenting life at a wireless station in the Farallon Islands, 1910-1974, bulk 1918-1919
items.description: The collection consists of a photograph album and a typescript by Ralph M. Hare, a United States Navy wireless operator at the Farallon Island Wireless Station from 1918-1919. The typescript is primarily about the equipment used at the wireless station.

items.title: RCA's Farnsworth Patent File, 1930 : a collection of documents and manuscripts
items.description: A single file folder with thirteen documents created between 21 April and 7 July 1930. The file deals with a crucially important moment in the history of television technology, Vladimir Zworykin's evaluation of Philo Farnsworth's competing system of "electronic" television, followed by RCA's decision to devote the bulk of its resources to electronic rather than mechanical television development. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Russell and Sigurd Varian papers, 1892-1988
items.description: Russsell and Sigurd Varian were co-inventors, with William W. Hansen, of the klystron and rhumbatron and co-founders of Varian Associates. Joined by his brother, Sigurd, a pilot with Pan American Airlines, he began work on microwave technology as a research assistant with Professor William Hansen. In addition to original research notebooks and correspondence regarding the klystron, the collection includes materials on numerous other inventions and ideas from Russell's work for Philo Farnsworth and Humble Oil as well as the brothers' years at Stanford and at Varian Associates.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Trade, merchandising and retail

items.title: Account for M.J.H. Meyer, Menlo Park, 1916 Apr. 25
items.description: Foodstuffs, probably only for one household for a few days. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Alaska Commercial Company records, 1868-1940
items.description: The Company established stations in Alaska at Nome, Kodiak, Sunrise, Eagle City, Circle City, St. Michael, Unga, Unalaska and others, and in Dawson in Canada, as well as various other Canadian stations. Includes general accounts dating between 1888 and 1940, financial reports of Unalaska, annual financial reports and lists of stockholders of Alaska Commercial Company. Also included are stock certificates, stock journals, private and general ledgers, fur book, fur average record, and a Yukon Saw Mill ledger.

items.title: Duff & Doyle General Store ledger, 1900-1901 : manuscript
items.description: Ledger of the historic Duff & Doyle General Store, located in Menlo Park, California contains the food, liquor, sundries and supplies for 74 accounts. Listed also are all manner of purchases such as bread, salt, eggs, and more obscure fare such as scythe stones, sulphur and overalls, among others.

items.title: Guest registry, 1901-1905
items.description: Guest book with A-Z tabs where guest have penned the names, addresses, and sometimes phone numbers. There is a pencil notation "Occidental Hotel, P.A.Calif" on the free fly.

items.title: Schwabacher company records, 1894-1944
items.description: The Schwabacher Company records in this collection include records of several of the enterprises in Seattle, the Stockton Milling Company in Stockton, California, and of Schwabacher Bros. of San Francisco. Collection includes miscellaneous reports and letters concerning the Seattle enterprises (1910 and 1921-1923); accountant's reports and balance sheets for each of the four Seattle companies represented (1910-1933); minute book and cash book, as well as sundry agreements and correspondence for the Stockton Milling Company (1894-1920); and checkbooks and a trial balance for Schwabacher Bros. in San Francisco (1906-1944). [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: W.H. Taylor collection, 1837-1938
items.description: Collection consists of records of a general merchandise store in North Bloomfield, Nevada County, California (1862-1936), and bound records of various other mercantile and mining establishments in California (1837-1938). Included are legal documents, agreements, correspondence, general accounts, production records, and samples of various forms.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Transportation and utilities

items.title: [Feather River Power Project photograph album] [graphic]
items.description: This photo album contains photos that show the construction/maintenance of Big Bend PowerHouse, built by the Great Western Power Company on North Fork of the Feather River in California in 1915-1917. Included are 70 photos, including views of worker's dormitory, later used as a military camp.

items.title: Advertising card, ca. 1910
items.description: Includes a photograph of Lick Observatory on the top of Mt. Hamilton, as well as a schedule and fare information.

items.title: Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company : collection of pamphlets and other materials, circa 1892-1946
items.description: Includes pamphlets, typecript decisions of legal proceedings (many involving the Ferryboatmen's Union of California), tariff rate schedules, and other material.

items.title: First general deed of trust from the United Railroads of San Francisco to the Union Trust Company of San Francisco : pamphlet, 1902
items.description: "Four per cent. Sinking fund gold bonds, $35,275,000. Coupons payable 1st of April and 1st of October. Bonds dated June 7th, 1902 Due April 1st, 1927."

items.title: Pacific Car Demurrage Bureau records, 1901-1946
items.description: The Pacific Car Demurrage Bureau also called the Pacific Car Service Bureau seems to have been a sort of collection agency for the different west coast railroad companies. Collection contains business records including: receipted vouchers, payrolls, register of vouchers, cashbooks, time books, journals, and ledgers.

items.title: Pacific Car Service Bureau payroll papers and bills, 1904 June
items.description: Among other lists and information, the papers include a list of the railroads serviced by the company at this time, and the number of cars reported for each.

items.title: Paul Shoup papers, 1928-1946
items.description: Business and personal correspondence, business, legal and financial papers, bills and acts of Congress, governmental documents, political campaign material, minutes of meetings, texts of articles and printed materials covering the period of Shoup's presidency (1929-32) and vice chairmanship (1932-38) of the Southern Pacific Company and his interest and involvement with development and oil companies, notably the Tide Water Oil Group.

items.title: San Francisco-Oakland terminal railways : organizational charts, 1915-1920
items.description: The San Francisco-Oakland Terminal Railways formed in 1912 from a merger of the San Francisco & San Jose Consolidated Railway and the Oakland Traction Co. Three of the organization charts provide names of the board of directors and heads of various departments.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records, 1862-1997
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 1, Board of Directors records, 1867-1996
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 2, Operating and Maintenance Department records, 1889-1997
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 3, Mechanical Department records, 1909-1996
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 4, Accounting Department records, 1862-1988
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 5, Office of the Secretary records, 1904-1983
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 6, Legal Department records, 1905-1979
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: The road of a thousand wonders; the coast line - Shasta route of the Southern Pacific Company from Los Angeles through San Francisco, to Portland : tourist promotional brochure
Uncle John's Stables advertising card
items.description: Advertising card for livery stable in Palo Alto, Calif., with train schedule to San Francisco and descriptive text on Stanford University.

items.title: United Railroads of San Francisco records, 1866-1951
items.description: The United Railroads of San Francisco, as well as the Market Street Railway Company and the Municipal Railway Co., were all aggregations of smaller street railway lines that provided urban transportation for San Francisco. Business and legal papers, financial papers, record books, stock records, statistics, ledgers, clippings, and other records.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Venture capital and finance

items.title: Donohoe Kelly & Co. records, 1863-1917
items.description: The Donohoe, Kelly Banking Company was a large private banking company formed in the second half of the nineteenth century, and flourishing until 1929 when it transferred its business to the Bank of America of California, later the Bank of America, National Trust and Savings Association. Represented in the collection are a variety of business papers including those documenting liquidation of Donohoe, Ralston and Company (1863-1867) when W. C. Ralston left the company, routine business papers regarding accounts and bank business, and volumes of cash books, collection journals, checks and deposits volumes, and balance sheets.

items.title: Francis V. Keesling diaries and reprints, 1906-1953
items.description: Francis V. Keesling Sr. was a prolific figure in the Bay Area. He was a Stanford alumnus and had a hand in politics, legal affairs, and life insurance work. The collection contains Francis V. Keesling Sr.'s diaries from 1906 to 1953 and the reprints he collected.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work

items.title: H.K. Hathaway papers, 1907-1929
items.description: Business records of H. King Hathaway, who was a consulting engineer associated with the Schlage Lock Company in San Francisco and the Tabor Manufacturing Company of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Collection consists of reports and correspondence concerning the reorganization of various companies, mainly in the East and New England, but in several cases in San Francisco, for which Hathaway worked as a consultant.

items.title: James Deitrick papers, 1900-1918
items.description: James Deitrick (1864-circa 1932) was a businessman and speculator with interests around the world, including Russia, Asia, Mexico, and Nicaragua. The collections contains correspondence, legal and financial papers, extracts, notes, lists, printed material, and maps covering the period from 1900 to 1918, primarily 1914 to 1917.

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company records, 1863-1967
items.description: Pacific Improvement Company was a large holding company in California, formed by C. P. Huntington, Leland Stanford, Mark Hopkins, and Charles Crocker. Contains business records of the Pacific Improvement Company and its subsidiaries. Business areas covered include land development, coal and iron mining, railroads, and hotels.

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company records, 1869-1931 (bulk 1883-1927)
items.description: The Pacific Improvement Company was a large holding company in California, formed during the days of C.P. Huntington, Leland Stanford, Mark Hopkins, and Charles Crocker. Contains business records of the Pacific Improvement Company and its subsidiaries. Contains materials related to the development of the Monterey Peninsula and to the general business areas of land development, coal and iron mining, railroads, and hotels.

items.title: Samuel Morse papers, 1911-1982
items.description: He became associated with the Crockers and after making a success of the Crocker-Hoffman Land and Water Company, which he managed, he was subsequently offered a position managing the Pacific Improvement Company in 1915. Contains personal correspondence of Samuel Morse, correspondence of the Pacific Improvement Company relating to liquidation of the company, and a report (12 v.) prepared for the Pacific Improvement Company in 1916, titled, "Iron, Steel, Coal & Coke on the Pacific Coast."

items.title: Western Highway Historical Collection, 1888-1960
items.description: Photographs, dealer catalogs, and specification sheets concerning trucks, mostly from the 1920s and 30s, and trucking company ephemera from the early 1950s. This collection was created in 1960 with the cooperation of the Western Highway Institute, primarily to preserve the records and pictures of the early days of highway transportation west of the Rocky Mountains.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Environment and conservation

items.title: Are the lands in the Big Basin worth one hundred dollars per acre? The result of a personal visit to a most marvelous forest of redwood, that pointed gigantic fingers to heaven before Moses crossed the Red Sea : newsclipping, 1902 July 30.
items.description: Testimony is presented as to the land's value as a park and the value of the timber alone. Letters are printed from several readers.

items.title: Big Basin : photograph album, 1900
items.description: Photographs taken by Hill of Sequoia sempervirens and its habitat in Big Basin, including Waddell Creek, and Mt. Ben Lomond. Represented are the founding members of the Sempervirens Club among whom are Hill, W.W. Richards, R.S. Kooser, Carrie Stevens Walter, Mrs. S.A. Jones, J.F. Coope, J.Q. Packard, H.L. Middleton, Charles Wesley Reed and their guide, Andy Baldwin, and cook, Thomas Croon.

items.title: California State Redwood Park (Santa Cruz County) : photograph by [Andrew P. Hill], circa 1905
items.description: Shown is a group of five deer being offerred food by an unidentified man. In the background are redwood trees and an automobile and structure.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Farming, canning and food processing

items.title: A Sanitary survey of the canning industry of San Jose
items.description: Includes forms used by the California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Industrial Welfare. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.title: Betty Chase collection related to the Wilcox Fruit Company, 1870s-1960s.
items.description: Ms. Chase's family owned the company and its pear orchards from the 1870s to the late 1960s. The collection includes photos, legal papers, family memorabilia, letters, materials related to the State Fair, including booklets from 1927, 1928 and 1929, as well as photos of the company booth and display cards, and other documentation.

items.title: California Bean Growers Warehouse Corporation records, 1918-1947
items.description: From paragraph (i) of the Articles of Incorporation, "The primary purpose for the organization of this corporation is to pack, process, clean, store and warehouse the beans delivered to it by the California Bean Growers' Association, a California cooperative marketing association..." The first series consists of minute books, bylaws, legal papers, correspondence, leases, and account books of the Corporation (1922-1947). The second series includes minute books, bylaws, administrative material, and account books which document the California Bean Growers' Association (1918-1929).

items.title: Charles Wooster papers
items.description: Charles Conklin Wooster; born in Albany, NY, in 1845; horse trainer and coachman for Leland Stanford from about 1870 until Stanford's death in 1893; continued to work for Jane Stanford, and after her death in 1905, for the University; died in 1935. Photographs of Wooster with family members, horses, and his marriage certificate. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Frank Y. Chuck papers, 1912-2020
items.description: Frank Y. Chuck (1900-1994) was a research chemist who patented a technique for the dehydration of milk and the stabilization of whey products through crystallization so they would dissolve easily in liquid, a process that allowed milk products to be shipped overseas during wartime and is still used today in the production of household items such as instant hot cocoa mix and powdered milk. Included are photographs, academic transcripts, diplomas, domestic and international patents, professional papers, notebooks, correspondence, and an oral history interview transcript.

items.title: Henry Kingwell photo album of life as a California Agricultural Commissioner, 1921-1953
items.description: Henry Kingwell, a resident of Colusa, California, served for decades as Glenn County's Agricultural Commissioner until his retirement in 1951. Photographs include 38 photographs (8x10 or 4x5) showing displays of fruits and horticultural products at the Glenn County Fair, 1921-1931. Many other photographs of agricultural topics (e.g., apricot drying) and photos of meetings of other California Agricultural Commissioners.

items.title: Report on Lands of the Rio Tierra Investment Company on Mariposa Island
items.description: Detailed description by a professional appraiser of lands along the eastern bank of the San Joaquin River and as part of the Sand Slough field (whih was frequently irrigated or flooded). A report on agricultural land in California's Central Valley before the introduction of state and federal irrigation projects.

items.title: Sales album documenting the use of Kayso, or powdered calcium caseinate, to increase the coverage and effectiveness of pesticides, and fungicides following World War I, circa 1922
items.description: Small sales album documenting the use of Kayso, or powdered calcium caseinate, to increase the coverage and effectiveness of pesticides and fungicides following World War I. The album was issued by the California Central Creameries, Inc., circa 1922, to promote the value of using their calcium caseinate powder as an effective additive to pesticide and insecticide sprays for orchard farming.

items.title: Steele Ranch records, 1855-1973
items.description: Compilation of ranch records from the Steele Ranches of San Mateo County, California. Includes financial papers, legal papers, photographs, maps, and miscellaneous background notes written by Mrs. Catherine Steele. The collection covers over 100 years of ranching in California.

items.title: Zalba-Hollister Bakery records, 1907-1925
items.description: Business records of an early-20th century Basque bakery in Hollister, California. They catered to the local Basques, performing services such as finding them employment in the mines and loaning them money.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Mining and quarrying

items.title: 20 Mule Team borax : advertising brochures, ca. 1900
items.description: Includes a history of Pacific Coast Borax Company. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Curt Schuette collection of the New Almaden Corporation records, 1928-1944
items.description: Schuette was the general manager of the mining operation at New Almaden Mines from 1940 to 1945, when it was owned by the New Almaden Corporation. General and personal correspondence to and from the general manager,1943-1944, and business statements related to New Almaden Corporation.

items.title: Daniel Cowan Jackling papers, 1911-1956
items.description: Daniel Cowan Jackling (1869-1956) was a mining engineer who established several mining companies in the Western United States. Primarily correspondence, together with ledgers pertaining to Jackling's finances, photographs, annual reports, and clippings.

items.title: James Macdonald Hyde papers
items.description: James MacDonald Hyde, a mining engineer, earned his A.B. in geology at Stanford University in May 1901. These papers consist of three patents for mining apparatus, 1912-1919; three maps of the Sullivan Mine (Congress Junction, Arizona); photographs of Hyde's machinery, 1912-1916 and undated; letters of reference for Hyde, 1900-1907, including two by professor John Maxson Stillman and vice-president John Casper Branner; and Hyde's diploma, 1901.

items.title: Mayflower Gravel Mining Company letter copy book, 1908-1914 : manuscript
items.description: Manuscript letter copy book comprising 292 copies of letters, dated 21 October 1908 to 22 April 1914. Includes business correspondence from the Secretary of the company to other members of the company, and people who are doing work for them (surveyors, attorneys, etc.), or individuals they need to deal with in the course of doing business (tax collectors, assessors, recorders, and more).

items.title: New Almaden Mine records, 1845-1973
items.description: Correspondence, legal and financial documents, ledgers, reports, research notes, photographs, maps, plans, profiles, charts and artifacts relating to the operation of the New Almaden Mine and the Quicksilver Mining Co.

items.title: Stanford University, Office of Maps and Central Records, records
items.description: The Colusa Sandstone Company was a San Francisco based company and one of the largest suppliers of sandstone from the Colusa Sandstone Co. Quarry (aka the Knowles Quarry or Brownstone Quarry)for Stanford Univesrity after the 1906 earthquake. Colusa Sandstone Company employee record books listing employees involved in reconstruction following the 1906 earthquake.

items.title: The Page Mill Road basalt quarry
items.description: Submitted to the Department of Geology. Student Report--Stanford University, 1939.

items.title: Western mining documents, maps, and photographs, circa 1900-1941
items.description: Materials include a variety of documents related to mining operations (primarily in California and Nevada, though with some documents related to Colorado and British Columbia), including plans, printed matter, reports on properties, agreements, financials, maps, several reports on tungsten, blueprints, photographs, and negatives.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Petroleum and natural gas

items.title: Angelo F. Semino papers, 1919-1937
items.description: Semino received his A.B. in mechanical engineering from Stanford University in 1922. Student notes from Stanford's early mechanical engineering and electrical engineering classes, 1919-21; typescript articles, charts, reports, and reprints (by Semino and others) largely pertaining to research done for Shell Oil Company of California, 1922-32; manuscript of THE OIL HEAT EXCHANGER by Semino and F.L. Kallum, 1925; and correspondence, 1934-37.

items.title: Earl E. Brabb collection of Chevron oil well logs
items.description: Logs contain information for an estimated 6,000 oil test wells in California from an area extending from Eureka to the Salton Sea.

items.title: Robert B. Moran collection, 1850-1968
items.description: Robert Moran has been recognized as an early pioneer in the fields of petroleum geology and petroleum engineering and was one of a handful of geologists who gathered in 1924 to assist in the formation of the Pacific Section of the American Association of Petroleum Geologists. Collection includes reports, maps, correspondence, cross sections, logs, notes, printed material, production data, and other miscellaneous material relating to the professional career of Robert Moran.

items.title: Scrapbook about Oscar Sutro, circa 1935
items.description: An archival scrapbook pertaining to the life of Oscar Sutro, Vice-President and counsel of Standard Oil Company of California. The archive was likely created at the time of his death (1935) by a member of his family and contains newspaper clippings, pamphlets and typescripts of addresses of Mr. Sutro, handwritten correspondence, ephemera, a printed funeral address, and a 29 page biography.

items.title: The Chevron Oil Well File
items.description: This collection contains information from approximately 5,000 oil wells in California from an area extending from Eureka to the Salton Sea.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Real estate and land development

items.title: "Down the Peninsula" properties : Redwood Highlands, Oak Knoll Manor and Menlo Oaks
items.description: With a large map of the property in question on one side, 8 photographs of available domiciles on the other, with a pictorial representation of suburban bliss. Scarce brochure extolling the virtues or property on the San Francisco Peninsula, "Homes of the rich who had the world to choose from have always been here. Lately, people of moderate means are beginning to share the wonderful climate, easy accessibility from San Francisco, fine transportation, country comforts with city convenience..."

items.title: Abstract of title, 1916, to property in Palo Alto
Menlo Heights, Calif. : promotional leaflet, ca. 1900
items.description: Promotional leaflet from the Carnall-Hopkins Company advertising building lots available in Menlo Heights, adjacent to Stanford University land, now a part of Menlo Park, California.

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company map collection
items.description: Over 300 blueprint maps mounted on 144 canvas-backed, bound sheets showing various towns and localities in the Western United States and depicting the real estate holdings of the Pacific Improvement Company from 1880-1920.

items.title: Stanford University map collection, 1853-1998
items.description: The maps in this collection pertain to the University campus, to other lands owned by Jane and Leland Stanford or the University, and to adjacent communities.

items.title: Stanford University, Office of the General Counsel, records
items.description: The Office of the General Counsel (OGC) is responsible for addressing all of the legal issues arising out of the activities of Stanford University, Stanford Hospital and Clinics and Lucile Salter Packard Children's Hospital at Stanford. Records from the legal office pertain to real estate matters, including the Stanford Shopping Center, other leases, and gift deeds.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Surveying and mapping

items.title: [Field notebooks from the 1905 field season, San Jose quadrangle]
[Field notebooks from the 1905-06 field season, Mt. Hamilton and San Jose quadrangles]
[Field notebooks from the 1906 field season, Mt. Hamilton and Pleasanton quadrangles]
[Field notebooks from the 1917 field season, San Jose, Santa Cruz, and Tesla quadrangles]
[Field notebooks from the 1918 field season, Palo Alto, San Jose, and Santa Cruz quadrangles]
items.description: Also includes "Data and Computations of Stanford Triangulation System," by unknown author (Noname text).

items.title: [Field notebooks from the 1919 field season, Pleasanton and Tesla quadrangles]
[Field reports from the 1919 field season, Pleasanton and Tesla quadrangles]
California : Mt. Hamilton sheet
items.description: "Stanford Geological Survey Summer 1923" written in ink at top.

items.title: California : San Jose quadrangle
items.description: "Stanford Geological Survey Summer 1923" and "8/25/23" written in ink at top.

items.title: Fifty vara survey, 1909
items.description: Shows "the position of street monuments, monument line ties, and street and monument ties. Prepared by direction of the Board of Supervisors under resolution No. 1764 (new series), October 12 1908. Marsden Manson, City Engineer, and Charles H. Holcomb, Asst. City Engineer." [From the title page map].

items.title: Greystone area geology and topography
items.description: Five versions of the same map. Covers quarry area, source of sandstone for Stanford University buildings. Accompanied by field notebooks.

items.title: Hollister, Quien Sabe, Gonzales, San Benito 15' quadrangles
Map of the Ormondale Ranch : situated in San Mateo County, California
items.description: Property is adjacent of Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve. Relief shown by contours (interval 10 ft.) and spot heights. General vegetation, with actual acreage amounts shown, and percentages in various tracts.

items.title: Quarry area geology and topography
items.description: Three versions of the same map. Covers Greystone and Greystone Quarry areas, source of sandstone for Stanford University buildings.

items.title: San Francisquito and Corte Madera Creeks (Santa Clara County) : surveys and notes, ca. 1900
items.description: Includes, among others, lands belonging to Spring Valley Water Company, Manzanita Water Company, Leland Stanford, W.A. Newell, Morris Doyle, and Cornelius O'Conner.

items.title: The areal geology of the Livermore region
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Topography : California, Morgan Hill quadrangle
items.description: "Reconnaissance" and "Stanford Geological Survey 1923" written in pen at top.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Transportation

items.title: Bridges : miscellaneous pamphlet collection originally part of the Hopkins Transportation Collection, 1928-1951
items.description: Includes pamphlets produced about various bridges and bridge engineers.

items.title: Charles D. Marx Correspondence Regarding Bridges
items.description: Charles D. Marx was professor of civil engineering at Stanford University from its founding in 1891 to his retirement in 1923. Collection pertains to the construction of a bridge from San Francisco to Oakland.

items.title: Collection of photographs related to the construction of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge
items.description: This collection consists of photographic materials showing the construction of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge, in California. The materials include 11 albums containing approximately 1,050 gelatin silver prints (1934-1936) showing various aspects of bridge construction and a separate group of 52 photographs and 142 real photo postcards depicting views of the bridge and tunnel construction from both the banks of the San Francisco Bay and the bridge span itself (1933-1936).

items.title: Construction of the Golden Gate Bridge : photograph album, 1938-1939
items.description: The photographs were probably taken by a construction worker.

items.title: Farallon Islands photographic negatives
items.description: Early 20th century negatives from the lighthouse station on the Farallon islands off the coast of San Francisco, California. Collection contains 53 glass plate and 8 film negatives, along with some empty sleeves.

items.title: George E. Tillitson collection on railroads, 1880-1940
items.description: Collection contains outlines of corporate histories of railroads in the United States and Canada including some streetcar lines and electric interurban lines. Includes dates of incorporation, lists of points served, lists of mileage, time schedules, maps of lines, and lists or reports of accidents.

items.title: Golden Gate Bridge : daily calendar and related material, 1919-1962
items.description: Binder "Golden Gate Bridge & Highway District, Daily Calendar, Francis V. Keesling, 1929-1937." Binder "Rapid Transit over Golden Gate Bridge, report of Joseph B. Strauss, Chief Engineer, 1934."

items.title: Golden Gate Bridge : photographs, publications, and clippings, 1930-1992
items.description: Includes the book THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE, report of the Chief Engineer to the Board of Directors of the Golden Gate Bridge and Highway District, California, 1937. Other pamphlets include information on the Bay Bridge as well as the Golden Gate, and there are newsclippings and magazine articles that also have photographs.

items.title: Golden Gate Bridge photographs
items.description: Photographic documentation by Standard Oil Company of California of the building of The Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco (Calif.).

items.title: Hopkins transportation collection photographs, 1870-1964 (bulk 1877-1943)
items.description: Photograph collection containing various accessions of original and copy prints depicting railroads, street cars, airplanes, automobiles, and other forms of transportation. Material was formerly part of the Hopkins Transportation Library.

items.title: James Reed papers, 1907-1941
items.description: He resigned from the Navy in 1920 and managed various California corporations until his appointment as general manager of the Golden Gate Bridge and Highway District in 1933. The collection consists of reports and correspondence concerning the construction of the Golden Gate Bridge and some material dealing with Reed's earlier activities, such as his association with the Celite Company in Los Angeles, Public Works and management activities in Philadelphia, and involvement in a project on the Isthmus of Tehuantepec.

items.title: Joseph Strauss bridge plans, 1905-1935
items.description: Joseph Baermann Strauss (1870-1938) was an American structural engineer who revolutionized the design of bascule bridges. Original bridge plans and construction drafts. Four different bridge types are represented: Strauss direct lift bridge, Strauss trunnion draw span, Strauss trunnion bascule bridge, and Strauss vertical lift bridge.

items.title: Randolph Brandt collection of photographs
items.description: Approximately 60 prints collected by Randolph Brandt depicting transportation and other subjects in California, especially railroads and street cars. Brandt, whose father was an investor in the Ocean Shore Railroad, contributed many images to books and magazines on the history of railroads and the San Francisco Bay Area.

items.title: San Francisco Bay Bridge Collection, 1933-1939
items.description: The progress reports contain numerous photogrpahs, and some maps and drawings.

items.title: Santa Clara Valley Interurbans, An Oral History by One who Remembers it Well
items.description: Rixford Snyder was a professor of history at Stanford University. Photocopies of photographs, illustrations, and articles with additional text by Snyder, concerning the Peninsular Railway, the electric trolley that ran between San Jose and Palo Alto, California, passing through Stanford University.

items.title: Ted Huggins photographs of the Golden Gate Bridge
items.description: Theodore (or Ted) Huggins, was a public relations executive at Standard Oil Company of California and an amateur photographer who convinced his superiors to let him document the building of the Golden Gate Bridge. Comprises black and white prints taken by Ted Huggins of the Golden Gate Bridge, with an emphasis on construction during all phases, from groundbreaking to opening day in May 1937.

items.title: The Golden Gate Bridge leading to Marin County and the redwood empire : photoengraving, nd.
items.description: View of Golden Gate Bridge spanning the bay, direction towards Marin County.

items.title: University Avenue Underpass Project records
items.description: The University Avenue Underpass Project is the reprinting of a series of photographs taken in 1939 and 1941, before and after the construction of the underpass that connects downtown Palo Alto and Stanford University. Collection includes sets 29, 35, and 81, along with a text page explaining the project.

items.title: Waldemar F. Dietrich Mountain railroad electrification in California report
