items.description: Waldemar Fenn Dietrich earned his A.B. in geology at Stanford University in 1913 and his engineer's degree in 1914; he was professor of mining engineering at Stanford, 1916-30. Report on the feasibility of certain railroad electrifications as a future means of fuel oil conservation, submitted to D. M. Folsom, Federal Oil Director for the Pacific Coast.

items.title: William Gardiner transportation collection, 1869-1951
items.description: Collection of photographs and research material concerning railroads, street cars and other public transportation in and around Oakland and Berkeley, California from historian, collector and local railway employee William Everard Gardiner (1869-1949).

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Water and public works

items.title: [Topography of part of southern Santa Clara County, Calif [cartographic material] : from Edenvale to Rucker along Coyote River].
items.description: Shows Southern Pacific Railroad tracks, proposed dam, waterways, Bay Cities Water Company, Spring Valley Water Company. Canals with directional arrows, land divisions, roads.

items.title: A report on the underground water supply of Stanford University and vicinity
items.description: Cecil C. Killingsworth and Cooper Hyde were graduate students studying geology at Stanford during the 1930s. A report on the underground water supply of Stanford University and its vicinity from 1932.

items.title: Boulder Dam (aka Hoover Dam) : film of construction, ca. 1936
items.description: Titled "The Construction of the Boulder Dam, 1931-1936," this film was sponsored by the Six Companies, edited by Dowling & Brownell, Hollywood. The film is in black & white and has intertitles and no soundtrack.

items.title: Charles David Marx papers, 1873-1942
items.description: He came to Stanford in 1891 as Professor of Civil Engineering and taught here until his retirement in 1923. Correspondence, reports, research notes, manuscripts, drawings, financial records, clippings, minutes, reprints, and photographs largely pertaining to engineering projects, most of which concern dams and water systems in California; other subjects include his years as student and lecturer at Cornell University, his civic work, and other professional activities.

items.title: Electrolysis Survey on Treasure Island, 1939 June 16.
items.description: Report "Requested by Mr. Charles H. Lee, Chief of Division of Water Supply and Sanitation." Describes Treasure Island's soil, the various systems on the island (such as water, gas, and sanitary), and describes the results of "tests made to determine the amount of electrical protection necessary to stop [...] leaks which were developing."

items.title: Electrolysis Tests on Treasure Island, 1939 June 5.
items.description: Report "Requested by Mr. Charles H. Lee, Chief of Division of Water Supply and Sanitation" on electrical protection installed on Treasure Island's underground pipes. Describes the method of testing and the results.

items.title: Feather River power project : reports, photographs, maps, 1904-1906
items.description: Report, correspondence, photographs (94), and maps (27 with index), relating to a project undertaken for the Western Power Company of Los Angeles (later known as the Great Western Power Company) on the feasibility of creating a large reservoir at Big Meadows, on the North Fork of the Feather River (Plumas County, California), and creating a hydraulic power plant at Big Bend (on the North Fork) in order to deliver electric power to San Francisco and other places in northern California.

items.title: Felt Lake Dam photographs, 1929
items.description: The materials consist of photographs documenting the construction of the Felt Lake Dam.

items.title: Joseph W. Gross research collection pertaining to water supply/control and flooding in California, 1890-1940
items.description: An extensive collection pertaining to California water projects including printed research material, correspondence, official reports, maps, and over 2,600 captioned photographs He had a long career specializing as a "municipal and reclamation" engineer. This specialization had him working on all aspects of irrigation projects for specific water districts to consulting on flood control, especially relating to the Yuba, American, and Sacramento Rivers.

items.title: Mill creek flood control project : photograph collection, 1939-1942
items.description: 44 cardboard sheets mounted with 138 black and white photographs. Images include personnel, work crews, equipment, aerial views, a few accidents, and site shots, some showing multiple shots of work progression at a specific location.

items.title: Report on a Coast Stream Water Supply for the Palo Alto Water District
items.description: Preliminary report showing the feasibility of a coast stream water supply for the Palo Alto Water Disctrict.

items.title: Santa Clara Valley Water District Map and Drawing Collection
items.description: The Santa Clara Valley Water District Map and Drawing Collection are materials owned and selected for digitization by the Santa Clara Valley Water District. The materials are related to water resources management in Santa Clara County, California dating in the early 1900s.

items.title: Santa Clara Valley water supply photographs, 1935-1938
items.description: The photographs depict the building of California dams.

items.title: Spring Valley Water Company records, 1905-1920
items.description: Legal papers documenting the agreements between the Spring Valley Water Company and Stanford University regarding Searsville Dam and Resevoir, 1919; and recordbook of measurements of the depth of Searsville Lake and amount of rainfall, 1905-1913, with some notes pertaining to pipes, water flow, and effect of the 1906 earthquake.

items.title: William W. Helbush collection of water project records
items.description: William W. Helbush (circa 1895-1965) served as an engineer for the San Francisco Department of Public Works. The collection contains project records, including reports, contracts, notes, specifications, plans, blueprints, and site photographs, as well as administrative records, financial records, and reference material related to the design and construction of various water projects, most notably the Hetch Hetchy water supply project, the enlargement of O'Shaughnessy Dam, and the Richmond-Sunset sewage treatment plant and reservoir for the San Francisco Water Department.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use

items.title: Toichi Domoto papers, ca. 1860-1996
items.description: Japanese American Toichi Domoto (1902-2001) was a noted horticulturist who began in his family's Domoto Brothers Nursery and later founded his own nursery in Hayward, California. The collection contains family and business correspondence, legal advice concerning the Alien Land Law of 1913, early nursery business records, early nursery catalogs (from the Yokohama nursery, the Domoto Bros. nursery, and Toichi Domoto's nursery), photographs of the Domoto family and early nursery business, class notes and subject files.

sectors.name: Education and research — Applied physics

items.title: David Locke Webster papers, 1914-1976
items.description: He remained Professor of Physics at Stanford until 1954, when he retired. The papers of David Locke Webster document his career as a professor and physicist and include course material from physics classes taught at Stanford (1946-1954); notes and notebooks from his earlier teaching career at Harvard, Michigan and M.I.T.; correspondence and subject files on Army research projects; budget material for the Stanford physics department (1924-1943); reprints of articles; research data; photographs of apparatus used in experiments; manuscripts; correspondence (1939-70) regarding Webster's interests (e.g. Klystron Tube, compton effect); research notebooks (1916-1970); correspondence relating to the Physics Department during the 1940's; glass plates for printing graphs; photographs; maps.

sectors.name: Education and research — Campus and student life

items.title: Bernice C. Rowell photographs
items.description: Grandmother grew up in Fresno and attended Stanford in the 1900 to 1905 time frame. The first eighteen pictures provide a gallery of Stanford in the fall of 1900.

items.title: Florence Grace Savage photographs, circa 1904-1907
items.description: Florence Mary Grace graduated from Stanford University in 1906 with an A.B. in math; while a student she was a member of the women's basketball team. Photographs of Stanford students and campus scenes including Memorial Church, quad views, campus entrance gates, Roble Hall, the Stanford Mausoleum, campus roads, reservoir on the former Peter Coutts estate, Encina Hall residents, football team, women's basketball team, student excursions off-campus, and Prof. Fernando Sanford.

items.title: Georgina Rolph scrapbook of her junior year, 1920-1921
items.description: A single scrapbook including mementos from Georgina Rolph's junior year at Castilleja Girls School such as concert programs, notes from friends, photographs, drawings, and more.

items.title: Myron Carlos Burr papers and memorabilia
items.description: Myron C. Burr earned his A.B. in civil engineering at Stanford University in May 1907. Included are photographs, correspondence, clippings, typescripts of short articles, memorabilia from student days at Stanford University, and a scrapbook. Subjects of the campus photographs include the Quad, Memorial Church, Encina dormitory rooms, club members on the porch of the Entre Nous eating club, athletics, and the laying of the last keystone in the outer Quad arcades.

items.title: Robert Jerome Snyder photographs, 1928
items.description: Collection consists of two scrapbook pages of photographs and one illustration of football players, Coach Thornhill, and the construction of the Big Game bonfire, with one image of Herbert Hoover and family in front of the Hoover home on campus; and four images of the large hangar at Moffett Field, undated.

items.title: Student photograph album, 1889-circa 1930 (inclusive), 1905-1906 (bulk)
items.description: Album, possibly kept by John Stephens Martin, with photographs of athletic players and games (football and baseball), dormitory rooms, and groups of male students, ca. 1905-1906; most of the athletic uniforms have a "B" or "Belmont" on them, probably representing the Belmont School in Belmnont, Calif. There are several photographs of Stanford football players and of Stanford campus buildings before and after the 1906 earthquake.

sectors.name: Education and research — Engineering

items.title: Frank George Baum, "The Transformer" galleys
items.description: Baum earned his engineering degree at Stanford University in 1898; he was assistant professor of electrical engineering at Stanford from 1898 to 1903. Galleys (incomplete) from his book, THE ALTERNATING CURRENT TRANSFORMER, with his corrections and annotations.

items.title: Frederick Emmons Terman papers, 1901-1978
items.description: The papers of Frederick Emmons Terman, dating from 1920 to 1978, document all phases of his long and influential career as an educator, electronics engineer, administrator, and author. The collection consists of nearly 200 boxes of correspondence, memoranda, minutes, reports, speeches and miscellaneous materials accumulated by Dr. Terman and his staff throughout his professional life.

items.title: Harris J. Ryan papers, 1908-1934
items.description: Harris J. Ryan was a professor of electrical engineering at Stanford (1905-1931; emeritus, 1931-1934), head of the Department of Electrical Engineering and first director of the Ryan High Voltage Laboratory. Collection includes syllabi and notes on alternators, synchronous motors, transformers, transmission lines and other topics, 1899-1917; correspondence regarding a lecture tour of Japan, 1930-32; Harris' articles and publications, 1911-31; articles and clippings on the Ryan high voltage lab; guest book from the Ryan High Voltage Lab, 1920-1931; and biographical information and bibliographies.

items.title: Principles of Electrical Engineering : 32 weekly parts
items.description: Experiments designed to illustrate fundamental points of electrical science.

items.title: Report on the proposed Electrical Engineering Laboratory of Sibley College, Cornell University, 1904-1905
Stephen Timoshenko papers, 1907-1996 (inclusive), 1921-1970 (bulk)
items.description: Stephen Prokofievitch Timoshenko, a world-renowned authority on theoretical and applied mechanics, was educated at the Munich Polytechnic Institute and at the University of Gottingen. Correspondence, manuscripts, typescripts, galleys, notes, reprints, photographs, passports, awards, and other items; some materials are in Russian or German.

sectors.name: Education and research — Library, archival and information services

items.title: Herbert Hoover letter to Frank A. Golder, 1924
items.description: Hoover, Stanford University Trustee, founded the Hoover War Library at Stanford in 1919. Letter from Hoover to Frank A. Golder, director of the Hoover War Library, indicating the forwarding of documents relating to the history of the Library.

sectors.name: Education and research — Schools, colleges and training

items.title: Castilleja School, 1907-1940
items.description: Located in Palo Alto, California. Founded in 1907 by Mary Ishbel Lockey (a Stanford alumna) to offer girls a comprehensive, college preparatory education, taking its name from the first girl's school in Palo Alto known as Castilleja Hall.

items.title: College of Notre Dame (later: Notre Dame de Namur University), 1890-1976
items.description: Located in San Jose, then Belmont, California. Founded in 1851 as the Academy of Notre Dame. Chartered in 1868 as the College of Notre Dame.

items.title: Margarita Espinosa notes on Adelante Villa, 1987-1993
items.description: Photocopy of undated notes by Espinosa on Adelante Villa, a preparatory school for girls founded by Lucy Fletcher and Eleanor Brooks Pearson and first located at Stanford.
items.era_note: [Most of these notes, a later history of the early Adelante Villa school and of Castilleja School, concern this period.]

items.title: Palo Alto Military Academy (formerly: Manzanita Hall), 1893-1932
items.description: Located in Palo Alto, California. Founded in 1893 as Manzanita Hall. Became Palo Alto Military Academy in 1919. Closed in 1972.

items.title: San Jose State University (formerly: California State University, San Jose; formerly: San Jose State College; formerly: California State Teachers College at San Jose; formerly: California State Normal School), 1875-1982
items.description: Established in 1857 as the Minns' Evening Normal School. Became California State Normal School in 1862 and the California State Teachers College at San Jose in 1921.

items.title: St. Joseph's College (California)
items.description: Located in Mountain View, California. Opened in 1924. Closed in 1991.

items.title: University of the Pacific (formerly: College of the Pacific, formerly: University of the Pacific), 1873-1978
items.description: First located in Santa Clara, California. Chartered in 1851 as California Wesleyan College, soon changed to University of the Pacific.

sectors.name: Education and research — Science and mathematics

items.title: Bailey Willis papers, circa 1900-1962
items.description: He made geological research trips to China and Argentina, before coming to Stanford University in 1915 to succeed John C. Branner as head of the Department of Geology. Collection includes diagrams from Appalachian structures labeled "Experiments in Folding"; a pamphlet "Bailey Willis Speaks"; two typescript papers on geology, 1944 and undated; report on the San Andreas Fault Valley, ca. 1933; report of the Golden Gate Bridge & Highway District regarding Willis' criticism of the bridge foundation and his comment on the report, 1934-35; biographical materials, 1949-62; and a manuscript poem by Willis, 1939.

items.title: Charles Stacy French papers, 1935-1989
items.description: French, plant physiologist, was director of the Dept. of Plant Biology of the Carnegie Institution, located on the Stanford University campus, from 1947 until his retirement in 1973. Papers include correspondence, articles, speeches, manuscripts, lab notes, charts, and computer printouts pertaining largely to his research interests in the photosynthesis of purple bacteria, spectroscopy of plant pigments, and the construction of spectroscopic equipment.

items.title: Frank W. Weymouth papers, 1900-1965
items.description: He rose through the various ranks to professorship in 1931 and becdame head of the Department of Physiology in 1938. Correspondence, research notes, poetry and prose manuscripts, lectures and research papers. Subjects include animal and human physiology and other related topics.

items.title: Geological map; San Juan Bautist Hills, 3 miles south of San Jose, California : hand-drawn and colored map, 1901, Jan..
George James Peirce papers, 1905-1926
items.description: He taught at Indiana University before coming to Stanford University in 1897 as assistant professor of botany. Peirce's papers are primarily incoming and outgoing correspondence pertaining to his professional interests (research, publications, teaching positions) and his administrative duties at Stanford.

items.title: George Polya papers, 1884-1985
items.description: Hungarian mathematician George Pólya was educated at the University of Budapest and the University of Paris, and taught at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich from 1914 to 1940. Papers relate to Pólya's research and teaching in mathematics and include professional and personal correspondence with mathematicians worldwide, 1910-1984; course materials including lecture notes; mathematical research notebooks dating from 1917 to 1960; manuscripts including those from his published works Complex Variables , How to Solve It , Mathematical Discovery , and Mathematics and Plausible Reasoning ; ephemera; reprints; and photographs.

items.title: John Casper Branner papers, 1882-1921
items.description: The first professor to be named at the new Stanford University in 1891, Branner served as professor of geology at Stanford as well as executive head of the Geology Department. Personal papers of John Casper Branner including correspondence, manuscripts, field notebooks, photographs from field work, line drawings of geological formations, scrapbooks of photographs of the effects of the 1906 earthquake, report of the commission investigating the Panama Canal, slides, genealogies of the Baker and Branner families, and books and articles by Branner, many annotated.

items.title: John Casper Branner Photographs of San Francisco Earthquake, 1906
items.description: The first professor to be named at the new Stanford University in 1891, Branner served as professor of geology at Stanford as well as executive head of the Geology Department. Photographic prints belonging to John Casper Branner documenting geological changes and property damage after the 1906 earthquake. Likely images from surveying group led by Branner, who was a member of the California State Earthquake Investigation Commission.

items.title: John George Herriot papers, 1937-1992
items.description: He served as the first director of the Stanford Computation Center, 1953-61, taught the first programming course at Stanford in 1955, and helped found the computer science department at Stanford in 1965. These papers document his career as a mathematician and include his notes taken while a student at Brown University, 1937-41, and his master's and doctoral theses, 1940-41; research files (notes, computations, articles, computer printouts, some correspondence, and other materials) on Fourier series, Schlicht functions, spline theory, and other topics, 1940-83; memos, minutes, correspondence, and other records pertaining to Stanford's Dept. of Computer Sciences and the Stanford Computation Center, 1946-92; correspondence, notes, and reports pertaining to his Fulbright year, 1962-63; and bibliographic and biographical materials.

items.title: Pierre Van Rysselberghe papers, 1932-1973
items.description: Pierre van Rysselberghe, a chemist and chemical engineer, earned his masters (1928) and doctorate (1929) at Stanford University. He taught at the University of Oregon and at Stanford. Papers include correspondence, class materials, articles and reprints, lab notes, and other materials pertaining to his research and his teaching career.

items.title: San Francisco Earthquake Photographs
items.description: Artificial collection of photographs chronicling the after-effects of the San Francisco Earthquake and Fire of 1906. The core of the collection consists of images from the California State Earthquake Investigation Commission expeditions led by John Caspar Branner, many of which were published as figures in their reports.

items.title: Sidney Dean Townley papers, circa 1827-1939
items.description: Astronomer. In addition to practical astronomy, his research interests included asteroids, comets and variable stars, latitude measurements, and seismology. Personal and professional correspondence, manuscripts, research notes including astronomical observations and geological measurements, articles, lectures, personal diaries, family genealogy, and a collection of family photographs including glass plate negatives and a glass plate negative format camera.

items.title: Species Lupinorum and related correspondence, 1922-1953
items.description: "A series of papers reviewing the genus Lupinus... issued in dated signatures..."

items.title: Syllabus for the courses in field geology
items.description: Cyrus F. Tolman was a professor of economic geology at Stanford University These mimeographed syllabi are for Geology 4 and 5, the summer courses on field and topographic geology.

items.title: The Berkeley Hills : a detail of coast range geology / original typewritten copy, 1902
Thomas Jefferson Jackson See papers, 1891-1970
items.description: Thomas Jefferson Jackson See, born 19 February 1866 in Missouri, was an astronomer and mathematician who established laws of the Formation of the Solar System and founded the science of cosmogony. Consists of original drafts and copies of scientific papers.

items.title: William Russel Dudley papers, 1838-1937 (inclusive), 1864-1912 (bulk)
items.description: Once at Stanford, his work focused on California flora, with a special interest in the study of trees; he was instrumental in the establishment of the Big Basin Redwoods State Park. Papers include field notes, a diary, manuscripts, articles and reprints, maps, and correspondence; most of the field notes relate to California, with occasional later annotations by other botanists.

sectors.name: Education and research — Social sciences and humanities

items.title: Doris H. Linder papers, 1900-2008
items.description: Linder was Professor of History at the College of San Mateo for over forty years, teaching world history and women's studies courses. Doris Linder's papers includes research and teaching files and notes, drafts and correspondence related to her published research, travel and country files, family and personal correspondence and ephemera, slides, and published material.

items.title: Ephraim Douglass Adams papers, 1730-1974 (inclusive), 1900-1931 (bulk)
items.description: Professor Adams taught European history for his first six years at Stanford, but in 1908, with the reorganization of the department, he took over recent American history, and especially British-American relations. Professor Adams directed the acquisition of materials throughout Europe after the war; these papers formed the original collections in the new Hoover War Library (later renamed the Hoover Institution on War, Revolution, and Peace). Personal and professional correspondence, drafts, manuscripts and research notes for various publications, and other papers.

items.title: Eric Hutchinson papers, 1891-1982 (inclusive), 1954-1982 (bulk)
items.description: Although Hutchinson's professional field was chemistry, these papers pertain to his interest in history. They primarily relate to his research (done in the late 1960s) on scientific research in England prior to World War II and includes notes on the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, the Chemistry Research Board, National Physical Laboratory, Physics Research Board, and the Radio Research Board and his typescript paper "The Radio Research Board and the Early History of Radio Direction Finding."
items.era_note: [Most of these papers, research notes on British scientific research and radio direction finding before the Second World War, concern this period.]

items.title: Henry Rushton Fairclough papers, 1886-1937
items.description: Henry Rushton Fairclough (1862-1938) was a classical philologist from Ontario, Canada. Fairclough came to Stanford in 1893 as an associate professor in Classics, teaching Latin, Greek, and Classical Literature. Correspondence with family and associates including Melville Best Anderson, John Casper Branner, Herbert and Lou Henry Hoover, David Starr Jordan, Chester H. Rowell, Benjamin Ide Wheeler, and Ray Lyman Wilbur. Also includes diaries, notes, photographs, newsclippings, pamphlets, published works, medals, and memorabilia.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford history and ceremonial life

items.title: Bacon family papers, 1896-1970. (inclusive)
items.description: Papers related to mathematics professor Harold M. Bacon '28, MA '29, PhD '33, and his wife, Rosamond '30, MA '32, their son Charles R. Bacon, and their cousins Orrin and Harriet Dunn. Materials are related to the Dunn (Bacon) House, and Stanford history, inluding Jane Stanford and Herbert Hoover.

items.title: Charles Anderson Gauld papers
items.description: Gauld, who earned his A.B. in history at Stanford in 1932, was a lecturer at Stanford and assistant editor of HISPANIC AMERICAN REPORT. These papers pertain largely to Stanford anecdotes and history and include his typescript articles on George E. Crothers and Jane Stanford; letters from George E. Crothers, 1956, regarding vandalism to the Angel of Grief statue and the rebuilding of San Francisco after the 1906 earthquake; and his letter to Herbert Hoover requesting a few words on Crothers and a copy of Hoover's reply, 1956.
items.era_note: [Most of these papers, articles on George E. Crothers and Jane Stanford and letters recalling the 1906 earthquake, concern this period.]

items.title: David Starr Jordan Papers
items.description: Jordan was a naturalist-first a botanist and secondly and of greater significance an ichthyologist. The collection consists primarily of Jordan's voluminous correspondence (62.25 linear ft.) relating to professional and university matters, but also contains other types of material such as writings (published and unpublished), clippings, journals and diaries, scrapbooks, financial papers, biographical and genealogical information, and photographs. He developed the idea of a junior college and was responsible for developing Stanford University into an intellectually competitive university rather than the technical training school envisioned by the founders.

items.title: David Starr Jordan papers, 1861-1981
items.description: In the Spring of 1891, Leland Stanford offered Jordan the presidency of the university established in memory of the late son of Leland Stanford and Jane Lathrop Stanford. The collection consists primarily of Jordan's correspondence relating to professional and university matters, and also contains writings (published and unpublished), clippings, journals and diaries, scrapbooks, financial papers, biographical and genealogical information, and photographs. Materials in the collection reflect Jordan's embrace of and advocacy for eugenics, including his leadership in 19th and 20th century eugenics organizations.

items.title: Elinor Cogswell papers, circa 1896-1976
items.description: Elinor Cogswell received her A.B. in English at Stanford in 1916, her M.A. in 1917; she was a journalist with the PALO ALTO TIMES and served as editor from 1938 to 1954. Correspondence, manuscripts, articles, photograph album and photographs, diploma, memorabilia, and diaries (1912-1916, 1931) largely pertaining to her association with Stanford University.

items.title: Francis Albert Smith papers
items.description: Francis Albert Smith earned three degrees in chemistry at Stanford University: AB 1922, AM 1923, and Ph.D 1926. Collection includes two appointment letters from Ray Lyman Wilbur, 1922-23; 3 letters from Edward C. Franklin, 1923-32; fundraising letter from Herbert Hoover re the Stanford Re-investment Fund ca. 1940; letter and menu for Sigma Xi President's Dinner, 1924; booklet on Palo Alto, ca. 1930; and photographs of a Stanford chemistry lab and the cactus garden on campus.

items.title: Frederick Emmons Terman, 1900-1982: some recollections : typescript, 1982
items.description: Reminiscence regarding Frederick E. Terman as chairman of the Dept. of Electrical Engineering at Stanford University presented in a talk to the Stanford faculty women's club, 1982.

items.title: Nancy Mason, "A Part of his Childhood Belongs to Peter Coutts; A Reminiscence of Wendell Fletcher" typescript
items.description: Fletcher lived on campus in the Tower House with his family from 1910 to 1918. This two page typescript details Fletcher's experiences growing up on campus including playing with John D. McGIlvray's kittens and participating in Professor Terman's study on intelligence in children, and includes descriptions of the Tower House.
items.era_note: [Most of this reminiscence, on Wendell Fletcher's childhood on campus from 1910 to 1918, concerns this period.]

items.title: Palo Alto Times, Special Memorial Edition, March 24, 1905
items.description: In 1885, Jane and Leland Stanford founded the Leland Stanford Junior University, in memory of their son. Memorial edition published after the death and funeral of Jane L. Stanford.

items.title: Stanford Historical Photograph collection, 1887-circa 1996
items.description: The Stanford Photograph Collection contains over 16,000 images of Stanford scenes including photographs of and relating to the Stanford family, views of the campus and individual buildings, photographs of students and student life activities, and photographs of faculty and administrative staff.

items.title: Stanford University biographical files collection, circa 1891-2011
items.description: The collection contains biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford University.

items.title: Stanford University deeds, 1901
items.description: Two copies of the deed of grant and one copy of the deed of gift, issued by Jane Lathrop Stanford via the Board of Trustees in 1901. Parchment and ink, tied with red ribbons and sealed with red sealing wax, each copy is signed by Jane Stanford and other university officials.

items.title: The Stanford years, being an excerpt from "memoranda," the unpublished autobiography of Theodore J. Hoover:
items.description: Head, Department of Mining and Metallurgy (1919- ) and founding dean of the School of Engineering (1925-1936). Manuscript (typescript) excerpt from "Memoranda," the unpublished autobiography of Theodore J. Hoover. As most of the papers of Dean Hoover were lost in a fire, this manuscript provides valuable insight into the world of an early Stanford student, professor, and administrator (1897-1936).

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford University

items.title: George E. Crothers papers, 1905-1957
items.description: Of primary interest are Crothers' writings on his alma mater, Stanford University, which he served as attorney for Jane Stanford, as member of the university 's Board of Trustees, and as part-donor of two graduate dormitories. Correspondence (1905-1957), speeches, articles, legal documents, photographs, newsclippings and scrapbooks.

items.title: Harry C. Peterson papers, 1879-1936
items.description: Peterson, born in Iowa in 1876, was curator of the Stanford Museum from 1900-1917; after leaving Stanford, he directed the Sutter's Fort Museum in Sacramento. Collection includes administrative and personal correspondence, 1888-1936; reports, statistics, acquisition records, exhibit captions, and publications of the Stanford Museum, 1894-1917; glass slides of Stanford images probably used to illustrate talks; and research materials compiled by Peterson on the Gold Spike (ceremonial spike used to connect the Union Pacific and Central Pacific Railroads), Stanford history, and Peter Coutts, including an original letter by Coutts, 1879.

items.title: Herbert Hoover letter to Timothy Hopkins, 1913
items.description: Herbert Hoover was elected to Stanford University's Board of Trustees in 1912. Letter from H.C. Hoover to Timothy Hopkins, President of the Board of Trustees, July 30, 1913, regarding the location of athletic fields on the Stanford campus.

items.title: Horace Davis papers, 1865-1915
items.description: He was president of the Sperry Flour Company for 40 years. Jane and Leland Stanford appointed him to the original Board of Trustees for Stanford University in 1885; he served on the Board until his death in 1916. The bulk of the papers concern Stanford University, its Board of Trustees, and the problems it faced; subjects include salaries, tuition and fees, faculty retirements, student discipline, the 1906 earthquake, and the organization of the Board.

items.title: Jane Lathrop Stanford papers, 1860-1983
items.description: In 1885, Jane and Leland Stanford founded the Leland Stanford Junior University, in memory of their son. The papers of Jane L. Stanford pertain largely to the founding and administration of Stanford University, along with her personal and social affairs; included in the papers are correspondence, business records, legal and financial papers, speeches, news clippings, and biographical materials.

items.title: Leland Stanford Junior Memorial Scholarship legal documents
items.description: Trust agreement and Terms and Agreements for the Scholarship; the latter document relates family history concerning the origins of the scholarship and the original source of its funds.

items.title: Leland Whitman Cutler papers, 1909-1941
items.description: Leland Whitman Cutler was President of the Board of Trustees of Stanford University (1942-1954) and insurance businessman. These papers are chiefly correspondence and working papers of the Board of Trustees. Included are reports and programs on future expansion of the University, papers of the Graduate School of Business and its Industrial Relations Division, the Lower Division, and the Department of Education.

items.title: Ray Lyman Wilbur, president of Stanford University, papers, 1914-1951
items.description: He served as lecturer and professor of physiology and of medicine (1897-1903), Dean of the Cooper Medical College (Stanford) (1911-1916), third President of Stanford University (1916-1943), Chancellor of Stanford University, and Secretary of the Interior (September 1929-1933) under President Hoover. Administrative files from the president's office. Included is correspondence relating to administrative, financial, and educational affairs at Stanford, particularly as relates to departments and schools, athletics, organizations, buildings, clubs, individuals, and the Stanford Medical School.

items.title: Samuel Franklin Leib papers, 1881-1920
items.description: The collection consists of four major components: Stanford correspondence pertaining to Judge Leib's association with the Stanford family and his responsibilities as a member of the first Board of Trustees of Stanford University (1891-1923); personal correspondence (1885-1910); correspondence pertaining to Leib's fruit and other farm interest (1883-1919); and legal and business correspondence pertaining to his San Jose law practice and local business interests (1881-1920), including cases resulting from the failure of the Savings Bank of San Diego County.

items.title: Stanford University, Board of Trustees, records
items.description: The Board administers the invested funds, sets the annual budget, and determines policies for the operation and control of the University. Records of the Trustees pertaining to legal issues, financial affairs, investments, academic departments, student housing, gifts received, real estate, campus development, and other administrative concerns.

items.title: Stanford University, Business Office, Cooper Medical College correspondence
items.description: Correspondence, financial statements, and reports relating to absorption of the Cooper Medical College and Lane Hospital, San Francisco, by Stanford University. Correspondents include Timothy Hopkins, David Starr Jordan, J. M. Stillman, and Ray Lyman Wilbur.

items.title: Stanford University, Controller's Office, records, 1891-1998
items.description: The bound volumes in the collection (ledgers, journals, day books, and cash books) pertain to university finances, the Palo Alto Stock Farm, the Vina Ranch, Durham Ranch, and Lane Hospital (San Francisco). Additional accessions contain historical salary rolls and account ledgers.

items.title: Stanford University, Faculty Senate, records, 1891-2026(inclusive)
items.description: The Academic Council was organized by the Stanford University faculty in 1904 and currently consists of members of the Professoriate and certain officers of the academic administration as specified by the Articles of Organization. In 1968 the Academic Council created the Senate of the Academic Council, composed of representatives elected from the Council. They include minutes, memoranda, correspondence, reports, election records, agendas and supporting documents, rosters, memorial resolutions on deceased members, and audiotapes of meetings.

items.title: Stanford University, Office of the President, records
items.description: These records include letters from the President to the Board of Trustees, 1902-1948; budget records, 1906-1960; departmental appointment records, 1901-1909; salary rolls and letters of appointment, 1901-1924; contracts and agreements largely between Jane Stanford and David Starr Jordan, 1893-1902, regarding faculty salaries and university fees, budget matters, and the ground lease for University land; and reports of committee actions, 1898-1910. Presidents represented in these records are: David Starr Jordan (1891-1913), John Casper Branner (1913-1915), Ray Lyman Wilbur (1915-1943), and Donald B. Tresidder (1943-1948).

items.title: Stanford University, School of Engineering, Dean's Office records, 1915-1998 (inclusive), 1925-1955 (bulk)
items.description: In 1925, the formerly independent engineering departments were organized into the School of Engineering with Theodore Jesse Hoover as Dean. The collection consists of general office files from the School of Engineering Dean's Office. Included are subject files regarding school and departmental affairs as well as interests of the individual deans; files regarding teaching appointments of non-tenured assistants, lecturers, instructors, assistant professors and visiting faculty; annual budget files (1925-1960) and annual reports to the President (1945-1964) regarding school and departmental activites, goals, faculty achievement and funding.

items.title: Stanford University, School of Engineering, requisitions, 1926-1946
items.description: Requisitions from the Dept. of Civil Engineering, 1926-40, the Dept. of Electrical Engineering, 1926-40, Ryan High Voltage Laboratory, 1930-40, Dept. of Mechanical Engineering, 1926-46, Guggenheim Aeronautic Laboratory, 1927-44, and the Dept. of Mining Engineering, 1936-40.

items.title: Stanford University, Vice President for Business Affairs, records
items.description: The collection includes minutes, reports, correspondence, leases, proposals, and other records pertaining to financial and business aspects of the administration of Stanford University. Among the subjects covered by the records are property matters, land development, building projects on campus, academic departments and professional schools, faculty and student housing, the hospital and medical center, SLAC, shopping center, industrial park, Jasper Ridge, relations with Palo Alto, roads, and water.

sectors.name: Education and research

items.title: Correspondence concerning Dr. William Duane
items.description: Webster was professor of physics at Stanford University, 1920-1954, and emeritus professor, 1954-1976. Correspondence, 1970, between Webster, Albert A. Bartlett, physics professor at the University of Colorado, and George W. Wheelwright, III, concerning Dr. William Duane's years in the Physics department at Harvard University; also includes a clipping about Duane's career, 1954.
items.era_note: [Most of this correspondence, letters recalling William Duane's years in the Harvard physics department, concerns this period.]

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Art, music, literature and photography

items.title: Ansel Adams photograph collection
items.description: Widely known as a photographer of natural landscapes, most especially for his images of the Sierra Nevada and Yosemity Valley, Adams was also an environmental perservationist. Contains 26 black and white photographic prints taken by Ansel Easton Adams. Photographs include nature and landscape scenes; portraits; and city scenes of San Francisco.

items.title: Arthur L. Dahl papers, 1900-1970
items.description: Arthur L. Dahl held various positions in the United States Civil Service, among them personal secretary to Gifford Pinchot, who was then National Forester. However, the great majority of the collection is lists and copies of articles that Dahl had published in various magazines and other periodicals between 1910 and 1937. Writing was a profitable hobby, at which he spent his spare hours from his business career.

items.title: Bruce Bliven papers, 1906-1985
items.description: Upon Herbert Croly's demise, Bliven succeeded as editor of New Republic. Continuing his freelance literary career, Bliven completed several works, including Five Million Words Later, his autobiography, and A Mirror for Greatness a biography of six famous Americans. Correspondence, notes, printed materials, photographs, and clippings covering Bliven's journalistic and literary careers.

items.title: Chester W. Barker sheet music collection, 1891-1973
items.description: Sheet music collected by Stanford alumnus Chester Barker. Based on their music store stamps, Barker purchased this music in and around Palo Alto for the most part, and many were probably used in local theatrical productions. This collection contains approximately 70 items dating from 1891-1973, the majority of which are from musicals.

items.title: Clarence Urmy papers, 1878-1936
items.description: Urmy was the first native poet of California. Includes correspondence concerning Urmy's work, letters to and from his sister Mabel (Urmy) Seares, manuscript and printed verse by Urmy, biographical material, photographs, and other material.

items.title: Frank Ernest Hill papers, 1905-1969
items.description: Frank Ernest Hill, son of photographer Andrew Putnam Hill (1853- 1922), born 29 August 1888 in San Jose, California, was a newspaperman, college professor, aviator, poet, and author. Collection includes typescripts, with some corrections in pencil ("Geoffrey Chaucer," WINGED HORSE ANTHOLOGY revision, FATHER WAS PRESIDENT, and unpublished poems), correspondence dating chiefly from the 1960's and pertaining to negotiations for the publication of articles and books, and miscellaneous unpublished works by Hill.

items.title: George H. McMurry papers, ca. 1890-1970
items.description: George H. McMurry (1898-1975) was a writer and journalist who studied with Wallace Stegner at Stanford and later worked for Stanford Libraries. Collection contains material related to McMurry's writing career and studies at Stanford; biographical research & writing about author and illustrator Mary Hallock Foote (1847-1938) as well as other California historical topics; and correspondence and printed material related to the McMurry family and missionary work.

items.title: John W. Metcalf papers, c. 1880-1940
items.description: John W. Metcalf (1856-1926) was a composer, musician and music instructor. He wrote 126 songs and ballads, the most famous of which was "Absent."

items.title: Mary Hallock Foote papers, 1863-1924 (inclusive), 1868-1916 (bulk)
items.description: Stories based on the Leadville characters, especially her first novel, The Led-Horse Claim (1883), established Foote's reputation as a Western writer. Correspondence with Helena Gilder, spanning their friendship of fifty years (1868-1916), and with other friends, family, and business associates. The papers include correspondence, literary manuscripts, and artwork.

items.title: Sheet music : miscellaneous collection, ca 1890-1950
items.description: Includes some early San Francisco and San Jose imprints. Also includes professional copies specifically for broadcast only.

items.title: Theodore Wores papers, 1880-1999
items.description: The Theodore Wores Collection contains material especially pertinent to the painter's career in art. Includes correspondence, written works, clippings, articles, catalogs, and books, and reproductions by glass negative and print of his works.

items.title: Tillie Olsen papers, 1930-1990
items.description: Tell Me A Riddle was originally published in 1962, and its title novella received the O. Henry Award as the best American story of 1961. The collection includes personal and professional correspondence, literary manuscripts by American author Tillie Olsen and others, material on the Longshoremen's Strike and the Socialist Party from during the mid-1930s, teaching material and student work, clippings, pamphlets, book reviews, awards, etc.

items.title: Walter R. Miles research concerning Eadweard Muybridge, 1881-1939
items.description: Walter R. Miles, a professor of experimental psychology at Stanford University in the 1920s and 30s, engaged in research on photographer Eadweard Muybridge, particularly the animal motion studies conducted with Leland Stanford. Collection contains Miles' correspondence about Muybridge, material about the Semi-Centenial Celebration of the studies at Stanford, ephemera and published articles about Muybridge, material about motion pictures and the didactic value of Hollywood film, and photographs and negatives used by Miles in his articles and publications about Muybridge.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Design and architecture

items.title: "Frank Lloyd Wright's Hanna House" [videorecording]
items.description: Paul Turner, professor of art and specialist in architectural history from the 18th to 20th centuries, delves into the fascinating history of Stanford's Hanna House, with special focus on its architect, Frank Lloyd Wright.

items.title: An architect grows up in Palo Alto; memoirs of Birge M. Clark, F.A.I.A. : typescript, 1982
items.description: After his service as a balloon observer during World War I, he returned to Palo Alto and began his practice as an architect.
items.era_note: [Most of this 1982 memoir recalls Birge Clark's youth in Palo Alto and the start of his architectural practice in these years.]

items.title: Architecture of Stanford University, 1886-1937
items.description: Primarily original correspondence concerning the early stages of planning, construction and landscaping of Stanford University, 1886-1906. The construction of Memorial Church, the Library (1906), the Gymnasium (1906), the Museum, and parts of the Quadrangle are featured.

items.title: Arthur Brown papers, 1910-1961
items.description: Arthur Brown, Jr. and John Bakewell, Jr. formed their San Francisco architectural firm, Bakewell and Brown, in 1906. These papers of Arthur Brown, Jr. include correspondence, professional papers, clippings, and architectural drawings, pertaining to Hoover Tower and other buildings designed for Stanford University.

items.title: Birge M. Clark architectural drawings, 1909-1954
items.description: Collection contains architectural drawings by Birge M. Clark, his brother David B. Clark, and other partners Walter Stromquist, David F. Potter and Joseph Ehrlich, with a few drawings by his father A. B. Clark. Projects were mostly located in Palo Alto, Stanford, and other communities on the Peninsula and included residences, schools, businesses, and city offices.

items.title: Birge M. Clark architectural records and personal papers, 1919-1990
items.description: After his service as a balloon observer during World War I, he returned to Palo Alto and began his practice as an architect. He designed many homes and businesses in Palo Alto, including the Post Office, the Community Center, and the Hewlett-Packard plant. Series 1, Office Files, contains chronological correspondence files, 1921-1979; project files containing correspondence, contracts, financial documents, notes, small-scale drawings, memoranda, and other materials, 1924-1990; and files on administrative matters, articles and talks on Palo Alto's architectural history, and other professional activities.

items.title: Charles Edward Hodges papers, 1891-1929
items.description: Charles E. Hodges was appointed Resident Architect by Leland and Jane Stanford in 1891, a position he held until his resignation in June of 1906. Papers concern his architectural work at Stanford University. Included are carbon copies of his letters to Jane Stanford, March to August 1901; typescript description of the frieze on the Memorial Arch; two souvenir booklets of the University, 1902-06; photographs of campus buildings and construction, 1891-1901.

items.title: Charles Edward Hodges photograph albums, circa 1898-1905
items.description: Collection contains two photograph albums belonging to Charles E. Hodges, resident draftsman and later architect at Stanford University.

items.title: Hanna house collection, 1900-1995 (inclusive)
items.description: In 1935, Paul and Jean Hanna commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design their home to be built on the Stanford University campus. Correspondence, blueprints, drawings, photographs, and other records relating to the planning, design and construction of the campus home of Professor and Mrs. Paul R. Hanna. The collection focuses on the Hanna's work with architect Frank Lloyd Wright extending from the initial planning of the house through later renovations.

items.title: Hanna House collection, 1935-1982 [microform]
items.description: In 1935, Paul and Jean Hanna commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design their home to be built on the Stanford University campus. Correspondence, blueprints, drawings, photographs, and other records relating to the planning, design and construction of the campus home of Professor and Mrs. Paul R. Hanna. The collection focuses on the Hanna's work with architect Frank Lloyd Wright extending from the initial planning of the house through later renovations.

items.title: Henry C. Collins architectural files and drawings, 1928-1938
items.description: Collection includes correspondence, financial documents, lists of fixtures and hardware, photographs, and architectural drawings for homes built on the Stanford campus for Ida Stauf, Maurice L. Huggins, William Leonard Schwartz, and Arthur Martin Cathcart.

items.title: Lee Emerson Bassett house records
items.description: Lee Emerson Bassett, professor of Speech and Drama at Stanford University from 1900 to 1938, built his home on campus at 740 Santa Ynez Street. Included in this collection are specifications by the architect, A. W. Smith; bills and one letter from Leon S. Bean, general contractor, 1909; an accounting for the cost of the house; a clipping about this house and one being constructed for Prof. A. B. Clark, 1909; a photograph of the house, with the Bassetts and their son David on the steps, ca. 1911; and two letters from Lucile Bassett (Mrs. David L. Bassett) with information on Prof. Bassett and his wife, 1981.

items.title: Lou Henry Hoover House Papers, 1917-1960 (inclusive), 1917-1949 (bulk)
items.description: Both A. B. Clark and Birge Clark served as advising architects to Herbert and Lou Henry Hoover for their house on the Stanford campus. These papers consist primarily of correspondence between the Hoovers, Professor Clark, and Mr. Clark regarding planning and construction of the Lou Henry Hoover house; and sketches and specifications for the house.

items.title: Oral history, 1982
items.description: San Francisco architect and nephew of Frank Lloyd Wright. Interview conducted by Paul R. Hanna, Jean S. Hanna, and Roxanne Nilan.
items.era_note: [Most of this 1982 interview with a nephew of Frank Lloyd Wright, conducted by Paul and Jean Hanna, looks back on these years.]

items.title: Panama-Pacific international exposition, 1913-1915
items.description: Typescript report of the Division of Works about the building of the Exposition and architectural plans. Includes photographs, blueprints, maps, graphs, tables, and an appendix by Markwart, assistant director of Works and chief of construction.

items.title: Stanford Historical Society, Historic Houses III : research and production materials, 1972-2004 (inclusive), 1999-2004 (bulk)
items.description: Research and production materials for the book, HISTORIC HOUSES III: SAN JUAN NEIGHBORHOOD, STANFORD UNIVERSITY, published by the Stanford Historical Society in 2005. Includes Byron Feig's original watercolor painting used on the cover and his original pencil drawings of each house; and copies of architectural drawings for several of the houses featured in the book.
items.era_note: [Much of this material, research and drawings on the historic faculty houses of Stanford's San Juan neighborhood, concerns this period.]

items.title: Stanford University quad construction records
items.description: Contracts between Jane Stanford and Nels Peterson for work on construction of the Quad (1901); bills and receipts for materials used and work completed (1901-1903).

items.title: Stanford University, Commission of Engineers, records, 1906-1908
items.description: The Commission of Engineers was charged with directing the restoration of the university's buildings after the earthquake of April 1906. Includes correspondence, the Commission's daily journals, photographs, negatives, and estimates of repairs.

items.title: Stanford University, Hospital, specifications
items.description: Construction specifications, largely for power plant equipment for Stanford University Hospital at its San Francisco location; firms represented include Hunter and Hudson Consulting Engineers, Otis Elevator Company, and Bakewell and Brown Architects.

items.title: Stanford University, Operations and Maintenance, Maps and Records, architectural drawings, 1889-1994 [microform].
items.description: Microfiche copies of architectural drawings of buildings on the Stanford University campus; and photocopy of the department's "vault inventory" of drawings, most of which are included in these copies. There are also some copies of drawings for the Hanna House, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.

items.title: The autobiography of an architect
items.description: Includes a one-page letter from Mrs. Dorothy Feltham, Secretary to Mr. J.H. Clark, explaining the memoir.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Film, radio and television

items.title: Daniel Berman letters, 1929-1941
items.description: A gifted child who went on to study spectral intensity physics at Stanford, later following friends to Hollywood during its early heyday period. Still later, from Hollywood, he writes of his involvement with The Motion Picture Academy of Arts and Sciences, his work with Ty Cowan (Associate Producer at Columbia Pictures) and Harry Engwight, and discusses the movies being made, much on Edward G. Robinson's work, contracts, and controversy; he gives much news of the studio, its projects, gossip about its people, his work.

items.title: Exactus Photo Film Corporation records, 1914-1918
items.description: Correspondence, work reports, inventories, financial papers, legal and official documents, American Consular Service reports on overseas film distribution, descriptions and illustrations for patent applications, scenarios, promotional brochures, miscellaneous printed articles, photographs of an educational film enterprise founded by T. K. Peters and D. Lever, with the assistance of the Stanford faculty and other California educators.

items.title: Rapport sur le Tirage de Developpement des Films Sonores : Rapport de Monsieur Conrard sur l'étude du film parlant & sonore en Amérique
items.description: This report on the filming and developing of sound film, using the RCA Movietone and Vitaphone processes, presents the technical specifications and methods for producing sound cinema, complete with schematic diagrams and darkroom chemistry for successful production of a "talkie."

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Press, journalism and broadcasting

items.title: Crosley Corporation press release and photographs, 1939 June 16.
items.description: The press release discusses the use of six carrier pigeons to speed 32 photographs of the Cincinnati Reds - Pittsburgh Pirates baseball game to its studio four miles away for immediate transmission on the WLW-W8XUJ facsimile radio news broadcast.

items.title: Frank Kester papers and photographs
items.description: The Frank Kester papers and photographs provide a detailed account of the life of a reporter and nature lover. Included are chapters of his autobiography, short stories, poetry and photographs that document many of his travels.

items.title: Roy Pryor Collection
items.description: The Roy Pryor Collection consists of off-air recordings of local and network radio in Menlo Park, California between 1937 and 1949. There are a few entertainment programs (including the Standard Symphony Hour and Bell Telephone Hour) and sportscasts in the collection, as well as some Stanford-related content, but the majority of recordings feature news and commentary by announcers Raymond Gram Swing, H. V. Kaltenborn, Fulton Lewis, Jr., Walter Winchell, Dorothy Thompson, Gabriel Heatter, Wythe Williams, and Upton Close.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Sport and recreation

items.title: Bay Area highschools' track meet results : newsarticles, 1910 and 1913
International Sweepstakes : Greater San Francisco Speedway. San Carlos on the Peninsula. San Francisco, Cal., Dec. 11, 1921
items.description: Photograph showing the contestants and associated folk at the Greater San Francisco Speedway in San Carlos, CA, on race day for the speedway's inaugural event.

sectors.name: Arts and culture

items.title: James Ladd Delkin papers, 1918-1954
items.description: Local printer who published mainly San Francisco and vicinity guides and histories. Examples of his books and pamphlets, as well as wood and metal printers blocks, original illustrations, and a bit of personal material.

items.title: Panama-Pacific International Exposition : guide books and postcards, 1915
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Panama-Pacific International Exposition photographs, 1915
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: San Jose, CA : album of theater clippings, ca. 1910
items.description: Includes several articles by Clarence Urmy and Walter Anthony, and includes such groups as the The Whitney Opera Company and the Savoy, Victory, and Columbia theaters.

items.title: Stanford University Press archival book copies, 1900-2013
items.description: The Stanford University Press was established as an independent printing operation at Stanford University in 1892. It publishes scholarly monographs, textbooks, and professional reference works. The collection consists of archival copies of books published by Stanford University Press.

sectors.name: Society and community — Activism and advocacy

items.title: Alice Park collection of papers relating to the American League to Abolish Capital Punishment, 1914-1940
items.description: She was active in many socially progressive organizations.

items.title: Alice Park papers, 1920-1936
items.description: Alice Park was an American pacifist, a feminist and a socialist. Correspondence, pamphlets, newsclippings and flyers pertaining to the subject of birth control and planned parenthood.

items.title: American Civil Liberties Union of Northern California records, 1900-2000 bulk 1934-2000
items.description: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) is a non-profit organization committed to the defense, preservation, and extension of civil liberties in the United States. Comprising correspondence, minutes, policy statements, reports, court transcripts, attorney notes, scrapbooks, newspaper clippings, pamphlets, and other printed material created or collected by the ACLU-NC, these records document the establishment and activities of the northern California branch and its wide-ranging efforts to protect and extend individual liberties in California.

items.title: Big Basin : article and clippings removed from A.P. Hill's photograph album, 1901-1954
Guido H. Marx papers, 1893-1949
items.description: He became professor of machine design in 1908; he retired in 1936 with the rank of Professor Emeritus. Prof. Marx was also actively involved in many political and social issues. Correspondence, speeches, typed autobiography, reprints, press releases, minutes, pamphlets, clippings, and reports, 1898-1949, pertaining to his academic career at Stanford and his political interests which included repeal of criminal syndicalism laws, labor unions, the Sacco-Vanzetti case, cooperatives, and control of public utilities.

items.title: Simplified spelling collection, 1916-1920
items.description: Collection contains papers from the movement for simplified spelling in the American Institute of Mining Engineers lead by W. H. Shockley, with letters to and from him and other members of the A.I.M.E., typescript arguments for simplified spelling, membership lists of A.I.M.E., and miscellaneous memoranda.

sectors.name: Society and community — Local and California history

items.title: A Woodside reminiscence: as told by Grizzly Ryder
items.description: "A Woodside Reminiscence: as told by Grizzly Ryder," by Cutler L. Bonestell, is a recounting of a 1914 conversation between Cutler L. Bonestell and Grizzly Ryder on how he survived an attack by a grizzly bear near what is now called Bear Creek, near Woodside, CA.

items.title: California biography collection
items.description: Consists of ephemeral items relating to people widely known and relatively unknown in California. Contains mostly newspaper obituaries, but also includes: handwritten biographical documents, invitations, wedding announcements, family reunion newsletters, genealogy forms, family trees, memorials, political speeches, campaign material, correspondence, and newspaper and magazine clippings.

items.title: California history : scrapbook and miscellaneous pamphlets, 1857-1955
items.description: The scrapbook consists primarily of clippings about Santa Clara County history, as well as Monterey, Stanford, and Yosemite.

items.title: California photographs, circa 1900-1950
items.description: Three boxes of photo prints and lithographs depicting various locations in California.

items.title: Carnegie (Calif.) : typescripts about the Corral Hollow site, 1961
items.description: Includes several pieces: 1. Carnegie; historical landmark in Corral Hollow (11 p.).
items.era_note: [The typescripts, written in 1961, are histories of the Tesla and Carnegie pottery works and town in Corral Hollow, 1892-1912.]

items.title: Carnegie : typescripts about the Corral Hollow (California) site, 1961
items.description: Includes several pieces: 1. Carnegie; historical landmark in Corral Hollow (11 pp.), by Earle E. Williams. 2. Tesla, Pottery and Carnegie in Corral Hollow, 1892-1912 (17 pp.), by Mrs. Josephine Leary, of Stockton, Calif. 3. Notes about California registered historical landmarks No. 740 and 755 (including the home of Edward B. Carrell).
items.era_note: [The typescripts, written in 1961, are histories of the Tesla and Carnegie pottery works and town in Corral Hollow, 1892-1912.]

items.title: General Subjects photography collection
items.description: Contains photographs and picture postcards depicting scenes of California places, people, activities, and cultural resources, mainly from the 1870s to the 1980s.

items.title: Harry C. Peterson lantern slides, 1892-1917
items.description: Named the Director and Curator of the Stanford University Museum in 1899, he remained there until 1918, adding collections to the Museum and writing historical papers. Consists of lantern slides and photographs circa 1892-1917.

items.title: Harry C. Peterson papers, ca. 1880-1944
items.description: The inveterate historian spent his entire adult life in one position after another related to history, particularly California Gold Rush Days. Correspondence, notes, memorabilia, typescripts. Included is material pertaining to Stanford University and Sutters Fort.

items.title: Henry A. Holden stereograph collection, 1911
items.description: Henry Ambrose Holden attended Stanford University between 1911 and his death in 1914. Views taken by Holden and published by Underwood and Underwood as a boxed set. Subjects include Stanford University buildings and a student race on Lake Lagunita; homes in Palo Alto; Greek Theatre and the Faculty Club House at UC Berkeley; two bird's eye views of San Francisco and various animals in Golden Gate Park; redwood groves near Santa Cruz; and Point Lobos, Cypress Point, and other images of Monterey County.

items.title: John C. Beckett collection of Stanford and Palo Alto dance cards, 1931-1939
items.description: Collection includes invitations and dance cards to Stanford events, including the Jolly-Up; dances at the Palo Alto High School; private dance parties in Palo Alto and nearby locations, including one at the Duveneck's Hidden Villa Ranch; and dances at other schools.

items.title: Joseph Collier, My holiday in California : photograph album, 1901-1941 (inclusive), 1901 (bulk)
items.description: Joseph Collier (1836-1910) was a Scotland-born photographer. Leather bound album of 151 original photographs, including approximately 60 images of Stanford University. Other images include San Francisco buildings, views of San Francisco Bay, Golden Gate Park, and the McGilvray Raymond Mine Company facilities.

items.title: Mayfield, Calif. promotional leaflet
items.description: Mayfield was a municipality adjacent to Stanford University; it is now part of Palo Alto. Promotional leaflet with map detailing the advantages of Mayfield; two copies.

items.title: Rosebrook family glass plate negatives of Palo Alto and Stanford University, c.1890-1920
items.description: George was a carpenter and contractor who moved to Palo Alto in 1892; Margaret Rosebrook was active in local civic matters including suffrage, temperance, and the church. Collection of over 300 plate negatives, most depicting The Rosebrook family and other families and their residences in Palo Alto, Stanford University, and various locations the Western United States. Some images of the 1906 San Francisco earthquake are present as well.

items.title: Santa Clara County, Fiesta de las rosas records, 1926-1932
items.description: Includes some administrative material including financial records, files, and correspondence, as well as programs and newsclippings.

items.title: Ted Huggins photographs of San Francisco and other California locations
items.description: Contains images of San Francisco, including the Golden Gate Bridge, Treasure Island and the Golden Gate International Exposition, the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge, various ships, various locations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Northern California.

items.title: [Collection of drug prescriptions], 1880-1937
items.description: Collection of hand-written drug prescriptions from various physicians to various pharmacies. Many are on forms from I.D. Holden, druggist (sometimes apothecary or Holden's Drug Store), in Stockton, California, but others are from Palo Alto, San Francisco, Mayfield, and Niles.

items.description: Includes ordinances by the City Council of the City of San Jose and forms used by the City of San Jose Health Dept. and the California Dept. of Public Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.description: Includes forms used by San Jose Health Dept., the San Jose Building Dept., the California State Board of Health, and the California Dept. of Public Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.description: Includes forms from the Santa Clara County Dept. of Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.description: Includes ordinances from the Board of Supervisors of Santa Clara County; report, ordinances and charter from the City of Santa Clara; and forms used by the California Bureau of Child Hygiene and the Santa Clara Public Schools; and bulletins, reports and forms from the California Dept. of Public Health and the Santa Clara County Health Dept. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.title: American Social Hygiene Association minutes
items.description: Includes minutes of the Executive Committee, Planning Committee of the Western States Division, and the Administrative Committee; Stanford and Palo Alto people represented include Ray Lyman Wilbur, Thomas A. Storey, and Dr. Russel V. Lee.

items.title: Children's Hospital at Stanford records, 1917-1977
items.description: Originally the Stanford Convalescent Home, established on the Stanford campus in 1919 for needy children with long term illness, this privately supported organization changed its name to the Children's Hospital at Stanford in 1970. These records were collected by Ruth Spande Atwood, first superintentdent and administrator of the Stanford Convalescent Home (1923-1961), and include correspondence, memoranda, reports, clippings and photographs.

items.title: Clelia Duel Mosher papers, 1886-1940
items.description: Interested particularly in women's health, she carried out her research and writing interests both as a physician and faculty member in the Department of Physical Hygiene, the linear ancestor of Stanford's Department of Athletics, Physical Education and Recreation. The collection includes writings, diaries, biographical and genealogical material, Mosher's survey of collegiate women regarding their sexual practices and attitudes, publications, and a sketch entitled,"Clelia Duel Mosher--The Questioner."

items.title: Contagious disease reporting requirement : broadside, 1906
items.description: Notice issued by Dr. James W. Ward, President, San Francisco Health Commission, requesting all persons having knowldege of contagious disease to report to headquarters of the Board of Health. Broadside refers to the San Francisco earthquake and fire of 1906.

items.title: Esther Bridgman Clark papers, 1891-ca. 1980 (bulk 1914-1968)
items.description: She began her pediatric practice in Palo Alto in 1927 and was a founding partner of the Palo Alto Medical Clinic. The bulk of the collection is Clark's notes, papers, exams, and lab books from Palo Alto Union High School, 1914-17, Stanford University, 1918-21, and Stanford University Medical School, 1921-25, including records of her research on guinea pig ovaries. Other items include correspondence, notes, speeches, charts, and other records from her medical practice, 1923-68; medical pamphlets and handbooks; reprints; personal correspondence, and photographs.

items.title: Harold K. Faber papers, 1895-1979
items.description: A founder of the Childrens Hospital at Stanford, Harold K. Faber was a professor of Pediatrics known for his polio research. Collection includes plans for the H.K. Faber Library; personal family papers and photos; the minutes of the Stanford Convalescent Home Auxiliary, 1933-1935; newsclippings of the Menlo Park Circus <1928>, a fund-raising event sponsored by the Auxiliary.

items.title: Health survey of Palo Alto, California
items.description: Includes ordinances from the City of Palo Alto, forms and reports used by the Palo Alto Health Dept. and forms used by the California Dept. of Public Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.description: Includes ordinances from the City of Palo Alto and forms used by the Palo Alto Health Dept., the California State Board of Health and the California Dept. of Public Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.description: Includes ordinances from the City of Palo Alto and forms used by the Palo Alto Health Dept., the Palo Alto Schools, the California Bureau of Milk and Dairy Foods Control, and the California Dept. of Public Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.title: Health survey of the City of Stockton
items.description: Includes forms used by the San Joaquin Local Health District, the California Dept. of Public Health and the California Bureau of Milk and Dairy Foods Control. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.title: Leo L. Stanley scrapbooks and papers, 1849-1974 (bulk 1928-1965)
items.description: In 1913, Stanley accepted the position of Chief Medical Officer at the prison, a position he held until his retirement in 1951. Comprises scrapbooks, correspondence, writings, publications, and other materials created or collected by Dr. Leo Leonidas Stanley documenting his personal research and professional work as a prison doctor, ship's physician, and medical experimenter (1913-1974).

items.title: Leo Leonidas Stanley papers, 1916-1950
items.description: Chiefly diaries entitled Events of the Day from period of professional work as the Resident Physician of the Medical Department of the California State Prison at San Quentin. These narrative accounts are supplemented by annual reports of the prison hospital, minutes of prison committees, articles and speeches by L.L. Stanley, correspondence, criminal and medical case histories, notes on effects of coffee on sleep and whey experiments, black and white photoprints and collected clippings and articles.

items.title: Maison de Santé de la Société Française de Bienfaisance Mutuelle logbook, 1903-1908
items.description: The French Hospital was founded in 1851 by La Société Française de Bienfaisance Mutuelle (The French Mutual Benevolent Society) to serve French-Americans in the San Francisco Bay Area Logbook for the French Hospital in San Francisco, with entries spanning the years 1903 to 1908. Each entry contains information about a patient, such as name, nationality, date of entry, doctor, and diagnosis.

items.title: Maison de Santé de la Société Française de Bienfaisance Mutuelle logbook
items.description: The French Hospital was founded as La Societe Francaise de Bienfaisance Mutuelle on December 28, 1851. It was established by the French Benevolent Society to serve French-Americans in the San Francisco Bay Area and was the first private hospital in San Francisco. Logbook for the French Hospital in San Francisco, with patient entries spanning 1903 to 1908.

items.title: Palo Alto, California, a sanitary survey of the city
items.description: Includes ordinances from the City of Palo Alto; forms used by the Palo Alto Health Dept. and the California Bureau of Milk and Dairy Foods Control; and forms and bulletins from the California Dept. of Public Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.title: Peninsula Hospital, Incorporated, records
items.description: The hospital established by Peninsula Hospital, Incorporated, was Palo Alto's second hospital; the first was opened by the Students Guild of Leland Stanford Junior University during the typhoid epidemic of 1902-03. Includes list of original stockholders, 1908; petition by property owners and residents objecting to location of the hospital in block 54, 1908; deeds and other legal documents relating to property in lot 26, 1909-1913; and an agreement with the Students Guild of Leland Stanford Junior University regarding care of its members at the hospital, 1913.

items.title: Public health report of Palo Alto, California
items.description: Includes ordinances from the City of Palo Alto and forms used by the Palo Alto Health Dept. and the California Dept. of Public Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.description: Includes a pamphlet entitled: Let us increase milk consumption / E.P. Bernard and A Wealth of good water / San Jose Water Works. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.description: Includes forms from the Town of Santa Clara Board of Trustees, Santa Clara County Health Dept., the California Division of Animal Industry, and the California Dept. of Public Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.description: Includes an annual report from the Santa Clara County Hospital, forms and bulletins from the Santa Clara County Dept. of Health, and forms used by the Santa Clara School Dept., the Santa Clara County Sanatorium, and the California Dept. of Public Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.title: Sanitary survey of the Town of Santa Clara
items.description: Includes forms used by the City of San Jose Health Department and the California State Board of Health. Submitted to Stanford University, Dept. of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

items.title: Stanford University, Hospital, monthly reports, 1914-1940
items.description: At the time of these reports the Stanford University Hospital (also known as Lane Hospital) was located in San Francisco. In addition to a census of patients, these typescript reports cover the nursing school, medical supplies, dietary kitchens, operating room, housekeeping, engineering services, clinics, social service department, and medical departments such as obstetrics, anesthesiology, radiology, and physical therapy.

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: Anderson family papers, 1848-1963
items.description: The family settled on the East Coast, later moving West; the Andersons contributed to society in the fields of theology, education and literature. Personal and business letters, literary and scientific manuscripts, official and legal documents, and clippings comprising a history of Edward Coffin Anderson (1821-1890); his sons, Melville Best Anderson (1851-1933) and Edward Playfair Anderson (1856-1951); and grandsons, Malcolm Playfair Anderson (1878-1949) and Robert Van Vleck Anderson (1884-1949); together with general material on the Anderson, Best, Playfair, Gurnee, and Van Vleck families.
