items.title: Archive of Takeo Shikamura and Hatsu Shikamura
items.description: Collection of Takeo Shikamura’s papers and photo albums, Hatsu (Helen) Yamamoto's and her family’s papers, photos albums, journals.

items.title: Brasch family papers, 1891-1920
items.description: Collection consists primarily of letters written by the children of Otto and Caroline Brasch to their brother Frederick E. Brasch. The letters date from 1891 to 1920 and originate from San Jose, Santa Clara, San Francisco, and Hawaii.

items.title: Charles J. Sullivan papers, 1918-1921
items.description: These letters were written to his fiancée Rowena Gray, in Chowchilla, CA, while Sullivan was at Stanford and training for the military, 1918, and then working in Los Angeles, June-August 1919, and Salinas, 1919-21. His letters generally talked about his work, his social activities, family affairs, and their relationship.

items.title: Christian K. Binkley, a Biographical Sketch : typescript, 1977-1983
items.description: Biography of Christian K. Binkley [1870-1938], Stanford class of 1899, by his son Charles, briefly discussing his public school teaching career, his attempts at farming in Santa Clara County, and his poetry and writing.
items.era_note: [Most of this typescript, a biography of a Stanford graduate of 1899 who taught school and farmed in Santa Clara County, concerns this period.]

items.title: Culver family papers, 1858-1915
items.description: Includes correspondence, diaries, and photographs. The Collection reflects J. O. Culver's experience as a lawyer, his service as an Army Paymaster and Post Office Inspector, his endeavors in small fruit culture, and his excursions into prospecting and mining. In general, the family letters and papers give a panorama of middle class society in New York, Wisconsin and Missouri, and Colorado and California, from 1860 to 1915, a familiar pattern in the United States of looking ever westward for opportunity.

items.title: David Locke Webster, "Reminiscences of a Rolling Stone"
items.description: David Locke Webster, professor of physics (1920-1954; emeritus, 1954-1977) and chairman of the Physics Department at Stanford (1920-1942), was born in Boston November 6, 1888. Subjects covered in this autobiography include sailing experiences, airplane testing during World War I, life at Stanford from the 1920s to the 1950s, experiences working on rockets during World War II, and his experiences as a pilot.
items.era_note: [About half of this autobiography, on airplane testing in the First World War and Stanford life from the 1920s, concerns this period.]

items.title: Diary of William Harrison Hanns
items.description: A manuscript diary of William Harrison Hanns, future newspaper editor, Indian trader, and I.W.W. supporter, born in Arlington Heights, Illinois, kept while living in Palo Alto and Los Angeles, California, and while in Gallup, New Mexico from 1906-1909.

items.title: Ernesto Galarza photographs, 1900-1972
items.description: Includes photostatic pictures of Ernesto Galarza's mother, Henrietta Galarza, ca. 1900, sisters Nora and Henrietta and younger brother, ca. 1905, and pictures as an adult in 1959, 1965, and 1972.

items.title: Farris Family Papers, 1908-1976
items.description: Correspondence, photographs, diaries, and ephemera.

items.title: Gilbert Russell Jones photograph album, 1894-1935
items.description: Gilbert R. Jones attended Stanford University during 1906 and 1907; his career included teaching shop at University High School in Oakland, CA. The majority of the photographs in the album are unidentified; subjects include camping trips and other outdoor excursions, Stanford University scenes, ships and boats, Robert Fowler and his biplane, bridge and trestle construction, irrigation set-ups, scenic landscapes, and family and friends.

items.title: Helen Stanford Canfield papers, 1913-1945
items.description: Daughter of Josiah Winslow Stanford, Jr., and grand-niece of Leland Stanford. Correspondence, memorabilia, newsclippings, photographs, and albums, belonging to Helen Stanford Canfield and her husband David Canfield.

items.title: Journal and letters
items.description: Consists of: 1) bound manuscript with t.p.: A.B. Saroyan, 114 King Street, New-York, Nov. 24th '905, Journey from Erzeroum to New-York City : second part, from Trabizond to Marseille; 2) letter dated 1906; 3) letter dated Campbell, Cal. Mar. 26, 11; 4) envelope stamped Jun. 24 1971 with William Saroyan's handwritten message: Campbell Mar 1911, handwritten letter in Armenian from Peprov.

items.title: Leo L. Stanley diaries, 1918-1968
items.description: He spent most of his life as Chief Physician and Surgeon at the California State Prison at San Quentin. He did take time out to travel, however, usually as the ship's doctor on large luxury cruises. Diaries are written in the form of a daily log and include photographs, menus, passenger lists, ship's newspapers, maps, programs, trip literature, newspaper articles, and some correspondence. Also included are some case histories of various men he had known in prison.

items.title: Martin E. Johnson photograph album, 1926-1950
items.description: The photos are of Martin's friends on board ship, family members, vacations on land, ports of call in Panama, Europe, San Francisco, etc. Mr. Martin was a merchant seaman, probably of Swedish descent, with family apparently in the Seattle area.

items.title: Meyer family papers, 1850-1971
items.description: A native Californian, J. Henry Meyer was a successful San Francisco businessman. Series I includes memorial resolutions, correspondence, and documents pertaining to Meyer family properties and business interests such as deeds, abstracts of title, and stock certificates. Series II consists of drawings of the Meyer/Buck estate.

items.title: Mildred Crew Brooke: an unfinished manuscript of reminiscences and some extracts from her diary
items.description: Mildred Crew Brooke Hoover (1872-1940) was a California history writer who published "Historic Spots in California" in 1932. Privately printed memoir with an introduction, interpolations, and epilogue by her husband Theodore J. Hoover, engineering professor at Stanford University and brother of Herbert Hoover.
items.era_note: [Most of the collection, her reminiscences and diary extracts and wedding invitations of 1925 and 1926, concerns this period.]

items.title: Minna Stillman diary
items.description: Minna Stillman earned an A.B. in mathematics at Stanford in 1903; she was a document librarian in the Stanford University library. Diary includes entries from a European trip, 1898-99, and an account of the 1906 earthquake, primarily its impact at Stanford University.

items.title: Misselwitz and Crawford family papers, 1870-1968
items.description: This collection concerns two American families, related by marriage, who chose not to remain in their native Kansas, but sought opportunity wherever it took them. Primarily photographs, some correspondence, ephemera, and rock samples. The Crawford portion of the collection contains many photographs of Ottawa, Kansas, Los Angeles and other parts of California, Idaho, Alaska, and Japan and China.

items.title: Mrs. Sanford's scrapbook calendar
items.description: Scrapbook containing a page for each week of the year created by various friends of a woman, Mrs. Sanford, of Palo Alto, in convalesence. Pages feature poems, photographs and cyanotypes, drawings and watercolors, letters, graphs and postcards contributed by different people.

items.title: Newcomer family papers, 1850-1972
items.description: Dr. H. Sidney Newcomer worked in applied optics as it related to the motion picture industry during the 1950s, an important period in the evolution of this technology. Collection contains diaries and journals, letters, lecture notes reflecting pre-World War I mathematics and optics education at the University of Wisconsin, scientific reprints, patents, and photographs. A diary or record book of Sidney's life from birth to age 24, kept by his mother, together with other of her papers.

items.title: Ray Lyman Wilbur personal papers, 1829-1949 (inclusive) 1875-1949 (bulk)
items.description: He served as lecturer and professor of physiology and of medicine (1897-1903), Dean of the Cooper Medical College (Stanford) (1911-1916), third President of Stanford University (1916-1943), Chancellor of Stanford, and Secretary of the Interior (September 1929-1933) under President Hoover. Includes correspondence; scrapbooks; publications; speeches and trip notes; rough draft of Wilbur's "Memoirs"; R.L. Wilbur's will; honorary degrees; letters from Mrs. R.L. Wilbur to her children; and files on associations with which Wilbur was involved, friends and associates, clubs to which he belonged, conferences, and issues such as environmental protection, civil defense during World Wars I and II, prohibition, and anti-vivisection. Papers also include Wilbur family correspondence (1829-1949).

items.title: Rosemary Benet Dawson collection of material relating to Kathleen Norris and the Norris Ranch, circa 1887-1955
items.description: Collection consists of materials created and compiled by Rosemary Benet Dawson and relating to Kathleen Norris and the Norris Ranch-"La Estancia" in Los Gatos. Includes copious notes regarding the history of the Norris ranch "La Estancia" in Los Gatos, and Rosemary Dawson's reminiscences on spending summers there as a child; also contains correspondence: 2 letters dating from 1887 to the Thompson family, one from Kathleen Norris to her future husband CiGi Norris roughly 3 months before their marriage, one describing the funeral of a friend Billie Hermann, one talking of CiGi as he was dying, a variety of to/from personal news and thoughts to Rosemary Dawson and 2 "aunts" Cora and Jane Rowan and several letters from the Benets (her father, William, and her aunt Laura /"Lolly") to Rosemary Benet Dawson.

items.title: Samuel Franklin Leib photograph album, circa 1900
items.description: Lawyer and one of the original trustees of Stanford University. Photographs of Leib's home and gardens in San Jose; also includes four views of Stanford University and one view from Mount Hamilton.

items.title: Shafter Family scrapbook, 1910-1914
items.description: Included are a mix of clippings, primarily about Shafter family members and their friends, and the Pacific Grove, San Jose, and Marin County areas. There are also wedding announcements and theatre reviews and programs, including programs for the Cort and Columbia theatres and the Pacific Musical Society.

items.title: Stanford family papers, 1833-1964
items.description: Josiah and Leland Stanford remained in California and became successful businessmen, and Thomas Welton Stanford continued on to a successful career in Australia. The Stanford family papers include letters, telegrams, newsclippings, photographs and photograph albums, genealogical notes, legal and financial papers, pamphlets, and printed materials of Josiah Stanford (1817-1890) and his wife Helen Allyne Barker Stanford (1831-1909), Josiah Winslow Stanford (1864-1937) and his wife Alice Herrick Stanford (1858-1940), Charles Stanford (1819-1885), Asa Philips Stanford (1821-1903), DeWitt Clinton Stanford (1826-1864), Thomas Welton Stanford (1832-1918), Welton Stanford (1849-1922), and Welton Stanford, Jr (1878-1947).

items.title: Steinerson family photograph album, circa 1890-circa 1905
items.description: Images in this album include family portraits, houses, parades, cars, trains, the Monterey mission, Clermont (Iowa), San Francisco scenes, Stanford University buildings, and the Troy Laundry wagon (San Jose, Calif.). There are also several images of preparations for and the flight of a hang glider assisted by a hot-air balloon.

items.title: Thomas M. Williams papers
items.description: He was one of Palo Alto's first physicians, establishing his practice there in 1904; he continued a close affiliation with Stanford, serving on its Board of Athletic Control from 1916 to 1928. Correspondence, notes, clippings, photographs, and memorabilia pertaining to Williams' affiliation with Stanford University and Palo Alto Hospital, including syllabi and notes from classes, 1895-96; his World War I service in Scotland; and his family.

items.title: Timothy Hopkins papers, 1804-1942 (inclusive), 1870-1935 (bulk)
items.description: Timothy Hopkins was a businessman, member of the original Stanford University Board of Trustees (1885-1937), and served as president of the board (1908-1914). Collection includes correspondence (1804-1805, 1885-1935), daybook (1889-1928), newsclippings, and miscellaneous publications regarding the Hopkins family (1885-1935).

sectors.name: Society and community — Natural disasters

items.title: George E. Monson earthquake photograph album, 1906
items.description: Photographs, attributed to F.T. Moshiba, of campus buildings damaged by the 1906 earthquake, including Memorial Arch, the Library, Memorial Church, Encina Hall, and the quad buildings. Also includes eight views of damaged cathedrals in San Francisco.

items.title: Ralph Allen Hopkins photograph album and memorabilia, 1905-1958 (inclusive), 1905-1906 (bulk)
items.description: Ralph Allen Hopkins earned his bachelor's degree in electrical engineering at Stanford in 1907; he had a career with Westinghouse, which awarded him the Order of Merit when he retired in 1949. Collection contains a photograph album with images of Stanford and San Francisco after the 1906 earthquake; portrait of the Electrical Engineering Society at Stanford, 1907, of which Hopkins was the secretary; Senior Week Program for the class of 1907; and a 1958 pamphlet by Laurence M. Klauber "Two Days in San Francisco Year - 1906" which contains his letters about the 1906 earthquake.

items.title: Rebuilding downtown San Francisco after the earthquake and two portraits : photographic prints, ca.1906
items.description: Construction site and on verso two portrait prints, one of a child seated in a tree, the other of a woman seated on a bench.

items.title: San Francisco Earthquake and Fire collection, 1906-1979
items.description: The collection includes eyewitness accounts of the 1906 earthquake at Stanford; and eyewitness account of earthquake damage to the Stanford and Hopkins houses in San Francisco by Ah Wing, employee of the Stanford family (in Chinese with an English translation). Also included are magazine and newspaper accounts of the earthquake and its aftermath; and a 1908 map of San Francisco showing reconstruction of the city.

items.title: Ted Erlin photographs, circa 1906
items.description: The materials consist of photographs documenting the aftermath of the 1906 earthquake in San Francisco and at Stanford University.

items.title: The earthquake story of Stanford University : photograph albums, 1906-1964
items.description: Photographs taken by Carl Breer on the Stanford University campus and in San Francisco shortly after the April 1906 earthquake, accompanied by text written in 1963-64. Volume one depicts destruction on the Stanford campus, including Memorial Church, Memorial Arch, Encina Hall, the new Library and Gymnasium buildings, and the Aggasiz statue.

sectors.name: Society and community — Race, ethnicity and immigration

items.title: Early ephemera of Japanese-Americans in Pasadena and Menlo Park California, 1906-1923
items.description: Frank Kurananga opened a successful Japanese art and curio business in Pasadena in 1903, soon expanding into a lavish restaurant and tea room. Collection includes photograph postcard and 2 autographed letters. From a young farmer about the new Japanese-American Methodist Episcopal Church in Mountain View, built with support from wealthy local lumber man Earl Minton in what was then a rural town of "orchards and ranches, horses and buggies on dirt roads."

items.title: Kato Family photography collection
items.description: More than 1200 black and white photographs documenting the Kato family. The photographs include studio photographs, weddings, funerals, Boy Scouts, Stanford versus University of California Big Game, army training, road trips and other events. Also includes photographs of the Heart Mountain Relocation Center.

items.title: Kenneth Kann papers and oral histories relating to the Petaluma (CA) Jewish chicken ranchers and egg farmers and the life of Joe Rapoport, circa 1970-1995
items.description: While at Berkeley, Kann began writing a popular history of the Petaluma Jewish chicken ranching community with support from the California Historical Society and the National Endowment for the Humanities. The collection contains interview tapes and transcripts used as research for author Kenneth Kann's two books about the Jewish community in Petaluma, California, during the twentieth century.
items.era_note: [About a third of the interviews, on Joe Rapoport's youth, emigration and 1930s labor organizing and on the first Jewish settlers in Petaluma, concern this period.]

items.title: Survey of Race Relations records, 1924-1927
items.description: Report, correspondence, interview transcripts, questionnaires, and printed matter, relating to the social and economic status of Chinese, Japanese, other Asian, Mexican, and other minority residents of the Pacific Coast of the United States and Canada, and to race relations on the Pacific Coast.

sectors.name: Society and community — Religion, clubs and societies

items.title: Augustus Taber Murray papers, 1900-1940
items.description: Augustus Taber Murray was a professor of classical literature at Stanford (1892-1932; emeritus, 1932-1940) and member of the Society of Friends. Contents include manuscript lectures and sermons, notes and newsclippings about Professor Murray, and correspondence with Herbert Hoover regarding Murray's Service as Head of the Quaker congregation in Washington, D.C. during Hoover's administration.

items.title: College Park Association of Friends records [photocopy], 1889-1936
items.description: Joel Bean (1825-1914) was a Quaker minister and school teacher and a founder in 1889 of the College Park Association of Friends. Collection includes records from the semi-annual meetings of the Association, 1889-1936; minutes of the Board of Trustees 1899-1927 (transcribed by Tom M. King, 2000); articles of incorporation and by-laws; notes on the original source; and typescripts of poetry found in Joel Bean's diaries.

items.title: Dedication ceremonies, Odd Fellows Home, Los Gatos, California : panorama photograph, 1912 May 15.
items.description: Photo depicts Odd Fellows in parade uniform and a large group of people and dignitaries in front of the new Spanish-style Odd Fellows Home. The building still stand at 14500 Fruitvale Avenue, Saratoga, and is the center-piece for the Saratoga Retirement, still owned by the Odd Fellows.

items.title: Rev. David Charles Gardner collection, 1902-1949
items.description: Dr. David Charles Gardner was chaplain at Stanford University from 1902 until his retirement in 1936; he also taught Biblical history and literature and served on the board of the Stanford Home for Convalescent Children. Materials pertaining to Gardner include notes for a talk "Memories of Stanford"; typescript of his address at the dedication of Memorial Church, 1903; typescript article on the Bible, n.d.; appeal letter by Gardner laying out the idea of a convalescent home for children, 1919; letter from John C. Branner regarding the evils of smoking, 1902; typescript copies of articles on Gardner's retirement, 1936; and typescript copies of remarks at Gardner's memorial service, 1949.

sectors.name: Society and community

items.title: Annual outing of the International Business Machines Corporation at Roton Point Park, Sohar Walk, Conn., 1929 June 12.
Daughters of the American Revolution blacklist controversy papers, 1928
items.description: Pamphlets, newsclippings, articles and correspondence relating to the 1928 alleged D.A.R. blacklist of men and women accused of being communists, socialists and liberals and/or pacifists who would not be welcome as speakers before D.A.R. members. Inclusion of Stanford President David Starr Jordan on this list prompted the Palo Alto Chapter of the D.A.R. to resign its membership in the national organization.

items.title: Palo Alto Shelter records, 1931-1947
items.description: Captain and Mrs. (Mary Belle) J.W. Glover administered the Palo Alto Shelter as well as helping at the San Francisco Shelter. Letters, photographs and newsclippings dealing with both the Palo Alto and San Francisco Shelters.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Armed forces and military history

items.title: Correspondence of army ambulance driver Lloyd Litchfield, 1916-1919
items.description: Reuben Lloyd Litchfield was a native of San Francisco who enlisted in the U.S. Army there 12 Dec 1917. Before that, he had served for six months in Section XIV of the American Field Ambulance Service, comprised of students of Leland Stanford Junior University, which left for France on 17 Mar 1917. Consists of 44 letters with envelopes plus 3 postcards, the bulk (33 letters) written in 1917. The letters are addressed to his future wife, Miss Alice Gillis of San Francisco.

items.title: Thomas family papers, 1895-1968
items.description: Most of the collection is devoted to the Thomas's stay in the Philippine Islands, 1900-1905, during Jerome Thomas's service as a U. S. Army surgeon, immediately after the Spanish-American War. Correspondence from the Thomases while resident in the Philippines, 1900-1905; sketches, photographs, maps, newsclippings, and diaries. It also reveals aspects of military operations in the Philippines during this period.

items.title: W. F. Henry photograph of Mare Island (California) explosion, 1901 June 5
items.description: On June 5, 1901, about three-hundred pounds of black powder stored at the Mare Island Naval Ammunition Depot exploded.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Foreign affairs and diplomacy

items.title: Goodwill tour of President-elect Hoover to Latin American republics : photograph album, 1928-1929
items.description: Includes good quality photos of the U.S.S. Maryland, the travelling party of President-elect Hoover and his family, newsmen and photographers, including Merl LaVoy, stops at Honduras and El Salvador, the trans-Andean train journey from Los Andes, Chile, to Mendoza, Argentina, en route to Bueno Aires, and the King Neptune ceremonies at the crossing of the equator.

items.title: Herbert Hoover off the record talks typescripts
items.description: Herbert Hoover, President of the United States, 1929-1933, earned his A.B. in geology at Stanford University in May 1895. "Off-the-Record talk to Stanford University faculty," April 11, 1938, is 29 pages long and covers the political and economic conditions in Western Europe focusing on Germany and the Nazis, with questions from the faculty and Hoover's answers.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Government and public administration

items.title: Chester Francis Noble scrapbook, 1899-1939 (inclusive), 1910-1939 (bulk)
items.description: Chester Francis Noble was appointed Chief of Police of the City of Palo Alto in January 1910, a position he held through June of 1924. Scrapbook contains clippings on crime and law enforcement activities in Palo Alto and other local communities, 1910-16, with a few items on Noble's career, 1910 and 1924, and his obituary, 1939.

items.title: Hopkins transportation collection, 1868-1936 (inclusive), 1912-1936 (bulk)
items.description: Working papers for applications to and hearings before the California Railroad Commission or the Interstate Commerce Commission. Includes reports, histories, statistics, and maps giving background on a number of the smaller California railroads.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Law and legal practice

items.title: Frank B. Yoakum diaries, 1932-1990
items.description: Founding partner in the Los Angeles law firm of Iverson, Yoakum, Papiano and Hatch where he worked until he was 84.

items.title: James Roy Welch papers, 1895-1935
items.description: Legal papers relating to Judge James Roy Welch's term as City Attorney of San Jose (1894-1897) and later as a Superior Court Judge in Santa Clara County. Also includes a small amount of personal papers and photographs, largely about mining interests and automobiles.

items.title: Lamson murder case collection, 1933-1992
items.description: Allene Thorpe Lamson, wife of Stanford Press employee David Lamson, was found dead in her campus home on Memorial Day 1933. David Lamson was charged with her murder, tried and convicted, but was granted a new trial; all charges against him were dropped in April 1936. Collection includes clippings about the murder of Allene Thorpe Lamson and the trials of David Lamson, 1933-1992; photocopy of the testimony of police chief H. A. Zink; original typescript of D. L. Webster's "Notes on Investigation of the Physical Evidence in the Lamson Bathroom," with accompanying photographs, 1934; three notebooks kept during the trials, partially using shorthand (no author noted); copy of Russell and Winters' book THE CASE OF DAVID LAMSON (1934); photographs of the house the Lamsons lived in, taken in 1992; and miscellaneous materials on David and Allene Lamson copied from various Stanford publications.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Politics and elections

items.title: Francis V. Keesling papers, 1906-1957
items.description: Keesling Sr. was a "regular" Republican, one of the few whose papers are extant, and greatly opposed to Hiram Johnson and the Progressives. This collection includes a wide variety of records related to the political activities, civic work, life insurance career, and personal papers accrued by Francis V. Keesling Sr.

items.title: Herbert C. Jones papers, 1903-1954
items.description: Senator Jones served as State Senator for twenty-two years, 1913 through 1934. Correspondence, documents, pamphlets, clippings and photographs pertaining to Jones' work in the California Senate and including a considerable amount of material on legislative actions during the time he was active.

items.title: Herbert C. Jones papers, 1921-1944
items.description: Lawyer and state legislator (1913-1934) from San Jose, California. Business correspondence, initiatives and referendums, legislation, scrapbooks, maps, newsclippings, and other papers, relating to Jones' career in the California State Senate and to State political activity after his term of office.

items.title: James Carson Needham papers, 1893-1936
items.description: In 1899, he was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives and remained in that body until he was defeated for re-election in 1913. Correspondence, papers, speeches, and photographs relating to Needham's congressional career, his connections with the Newman Oil Company in the 1920's, and the Covered Wagon Babies Club (of which Needham was a founder).

items.title: James Rolph, Jr. papers, 1904-1934, bulk 1911-1930
items.description: The James Rolph, Jr. papers include material from his five consecutive terms as San Francisco mayor from 1912-1931. The bulk of the collection consists of routine mayoral correspondence, including requests for letters of reference, permits, licenses, appointments, and employment as well as correspondence with city departments, state and federal agencies.

items.title: Karl Hama : Assemblyman 22nd District - Vote Communist
items.description: Rare small poster from the 1934 campaign by the Japanese-American labor leader and activist, Karl "Hama" Yoneda. Yoneda was a longtime member of the Communist party and an active labor organizer, who helped to found the International Longshoremans' and Warehouse Union.

sectors.name: Ideas and intellectual history

items.title: Government in reverse : a typescript by F.W. Becker, after 1937
items.description: Original carbon typescript of this essay, apparently unpublished, against New Deal "fifth columnists" in the approaching war with the Axis powers.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Aerospace and defence

items.title: [Launching of the S.S. Millen Griffith [graphic] : photo album]
items.description: A souvenir of the launching of a World War II Liberty Ship at the Richmond Yards, presented to Miss Eugenia, who was official sponsor of the Launch. This unique assemblage includes: one page describing the ancient rite of Launching; a formal presentation letter from the Shipyard's Asst Manager; a brief biography of Millen Griffith, with a flag ribbon attached; and 20 original caption photographs of the Launching (8.5 x 11 in.), with many photographs showing the young Eugenia, accompanied by, apparently family members, and an older sister Alice who was her Matron of Honor.

items.title: Bachem-Natter rocketry photographs, 1944-1945
items.description: A series of pictures made for display which show the first unmanned and first manned lift-offs, as well as many details of the interior, guiding mechanisms, assisting rockets, parachute boxes, and construction plant.

items.title: Barbara Boyd scrapbooks and related material. 1940s
items.description: Barbara Boyd's personal scrapbook, primarily about the launching of the USS Missoula, contains newspaper clippings, invitations, ribbons, flyers, song sheets, programs, photographs, a list of VIP guests, a small metal ship, a Standard Stations hat, and other materials. There is also a deconstructed scrapbook with 46 programs from ship launches from the Permanente Metals shipyards in Richmond, California. The photo album was presented to Barbara Boyd, one of the 12 Harmonettes.

items.title: Charles Froesch papers, 1906-2023 (inclusive) 1906-1982 (bulk)
items.description: This collection consists of manuscript, printed, and photographic materials created by and related to aeronautical engineer Charles Froesch (1896-1982), and his career in the aviation industry.

items.title: Correspondence, 1954-1958
items.description: 1. Josef Stemmer correspondence with Alfred Fritz, 1955-1956, two letters, with an IAF (International Astronautical Federation) bulletin, 1955. 3. ARRAT (Arbeitskreis für Raketentechnik) letters to Alfred Fritz, 1956-1958, 4 letters and plans.

items.title: Deutsches Raketen- und Raumfahrt Museum e. V. records, 1942-1969
items.description: The museum was intended to gather and display technical and literary materials (both historical and contemporary) relevent to studies in astronautics. The collection primarily conains correspondence conducted worldwide concerning the planned museum. The collection is of value to those interested in the reception and development of post-war German research in space-travel.

items.title: Elise Higgins photograph album, scrapbook, and letters, 1942-1943
items.description: The materials consist of: A commemorative album titled "Launching of the U.S.S. General William M. Black, July 23, 1943" assembled for Mrs. Decatur S. Higgins, the sponsor of the troop ship (as selected by Kaiser); a scrapbook titled "Elise M. Farley/ August 5, 1942" commemorating the engagement and subsequest wedding (on Sept. 24, 1942) of Elise Marie Farley to USN Lieut. Decatur Sawyer Higgins.

items.title: Elliott Reid papers, 1924-1966
items.description: Professor of aeronautics at Stanford (1929-1965). The papers of Elliot G. Reid, dating from 1924 to 1966, document his research interests in aeronautics and his professional career at Stanford University. Included in the papers are correspondence, research notes and drawings, reports, articles, product specifications, commercial publications, and photographs.

items.title: Howard Seifert papers
items.description: Howard S. Seifert (1911-1977), an authority on rocket propulsion of space vehicles, was professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford from 1960 to 1976. Papers include correspondence, photographs, newsclippings, notes, memoranda, reports, reprints, proposals, and class materials (notes, problems, exams, and reference sources).

items.title: Joseph D. Cusick collection of Lockheed Missiles & Space Co. and the U.S. Air Force Satellite Test Center records, 1962-1991
items.description: History, policies, organization, personnel, and technical trainingmaterials collected by Joseph D. Cusick during employment by Lockheed Missiles & Space Co. (LMSC) from August 1962 to May 1968 and the U.S. Air Force, at the Air Force Satellite Test Center [Satellite Operations Center] Onizuka Air Force Base, Sunnyvale, CA), from May 1962 through May 1991.

items.title: Leonard Eugene Root papers, 1923-1983
items.description: As the first Director of the Development and Planning Department, he proposed the creation of the Missile Systems Division to develop ballistic missiles and satellites. In 1961, he was named President of Lockheed Missiles and Space Company, and in 1969, he became Group Vice President of Lockheed Aircraft Corporation. The Leonard Eugene Root papers document his personal life and career in the aerospace industry from the 1940s to the 1960s, and includes correspondence, notebooks, business files, publications, memorabilia.

items.title: Letter, 1956 March 25, to Wernher von Braun
items.description: Asks for materials for the museum displays. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Maurice Garbell papers, circa 1934-1960
items.description: After the war he established his own office in San Francisco as a consulting engineer, specializing in issues pertaining to aviation such as air traffic control, noise mitigation, and landing aids. The papers of aeronautical engineer and pilot Maurice Garbell consist of articles, reports and other writing, photographs, personal corresondence, memorabilia, and other material.

items.title: Nadaner Studio photographs of activities at the Richmond, California, Shipyard, 1944-1945
items.description: Group of 31 original 8x10 photographs taken at the Richmond Shipyards by Nadaner Studio (presumably under contract for Kaiser), documenting a few events, including: 12 photographs of the Christening of "Gunner's Knot," on April 30, 1945, with James Cagney as master-of-ceremonies, joined by his co-star, actress Sylvia Sydney (as guest of honor); 12 photographs documenting two performances at the shipyards, one Cuban-themed and one Hawaiian-themed; 9 miscellaneous photos, some of workers at the shipyard, some views of a ship at sea, views of the SF Bay, and a photo of comedian Joe E. Brown at the christening of the U.S.S. Faribault [edited from dealer information]. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Nicholas J. Hoff papers, 1903-1997 (inclusive), 1940-1997 (bulk)
items.description: Nicholas J. Hoff was a professor emeritus of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University at the time of his death in 1997. Collection includes articles and papers by Hoff on aircraft structures and other matters, 1944-1981; diplomas, awards and other biographical materials, 1928-1997; and materials he collected on the history of aviation including articles, reports, and photographs, 1903-1958.

items.title: Permanente Metals Corp. Yard Two decal, circa 1941-1945
items.description: The Permanente Metals Corporation managed the Richmond Shipyards in Richmond, California. A decal for Yard Two of the Richmond Ship Yards. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Photographs of building the Richmond Shipyards, 1942-1944
items.description: Collection of 29 original captioned 8x10 photographs showing various phases in the construction of the Richmond Shipyards No. 3A [10 photos] and No. 4 [17 photos] + an untitled photograph showing a broader view of the Yards. The photographs show the rapid evolution of the formerly undeveloped section of the East Bay that was speedily turned into one of the largest and most productive shipyards for the construction of liberty ships, cargo ships, frigates, and other vessels for the War effort.

items.title: Preliminary design of an experimental world-circling spaceship, 1946 May 2.
items.description: This report presents an engineering analysis of the possibilities of designing a man-made satellite. The question of power plants, structural weights, multiple stages, optimum design values, trajectories, stability, and landing are considered in detail. The results are used to furnish designs for two proposed vehicles.

items.title: Report on certain phases of war research in Germany, 1947 Jan.
items.description: Summary report based on interrogation of Germany's top rocket scientists at Peenemunde.

items.title: Space Tracking and Data Acquisition Network (STADAN) and Manned Space Flight Newtwork (MSFN) : poster, 1963
items.description: Minitrack and data acquisition dish characteristics for stations around the world.

items.title: The christening of the Liberty ship S.S. Edwin C. Musick, Richmond, California, Feb. 11, 1944 : album
items.description: Album commemorates the launching of the Liberty ship, SS. Edwin C. Musick. Photographs depict the ship; Capt. Edwin C. Musick.

items.title: The Grapevine : newspaper
items.description: This edition (vol. X, No.23) contains articles about the Mare Island shipyard dealing with safety issues, better tool performance and training activities. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Thule Air Base collection, circa 1961
items.description: Collection of nine large, bordered black and white photographs and a booklet from Thule Air Force Base, Greenland, circa 1961.

items.title: Warum Raumfahrt? : Stuttgarter Luftfahrtgesprach in Stuttgart-Flughafen, 1959 Sept. 3.
items.description: Director, Development Operations Division, Army Ballistic Missile Agency, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama.

items.title: William Francis Whitmore papers, 1945-1991
items.description: William Francis Whitmore was a mathematician in the field of oceanography and a scientist and consultant with Lockheed Missiles and Space Company. This collection contains papers relating to William Francis Whitmore's work at Lockheed Missile and Space Company and as a consultant to the United States Navy.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Artificial intelligence

items.title: Arthur Lee Samuel collection, 1953-1992 (inclusive), 1990-1992 (bulk)
items.description: Samuel was on staff at the Bell Telephone Laboratories and at IBM in Poughkeepsie prior to joining the computer science faculty at Stanford in 1966. Collection is largely biographical and includes photographs, his C.V., biographies and obituaries, and Samuel's annotated copy of LEES' GUIDE TO THE GAME OF DRAUGHTS, 1953. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Charles Rosen papers, 1957-1985
items.description: Charles Rosen was an American scientist and pioneering researcher and developer in the field of artificial intelligence and robotics. Five linear feet of material (1957-1985) including, professional papers and presentations given by Rosen; newspaper clippings and articles; correspondence, contract reports, grant proposals and memoranda pertaining to the robotics and Artificial Intelligence Center at Stanford Research Institute; and business planning documents for the Machine Intelligence Corporation.

items.title: Donald A. Waterman papers, 1961-1987
items.description: Computer scientist; first Ph.D. from Stanford University in Artificial Intelligence. Course notes and research material, largely from 1961 through 1974, in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Psychology, and other subjects.

items.title: Edward A. Feigenbaum papers, 1950-2007 (inclusive)
items.description: Feigenbaum is a leading national figure in artificial intelligence and has developed computer resources for interactive research between medical and scientific collaborators on a national and global scale. Collection primarily concerns his work in artificial intelligence at Stanford University and includes administrative files, correspondence, project files, trip files, proposals, reports, reprints, Artificial Intelligence Lab memos, audio tapes, video tapes, and files on computer programs, mainly DENDRAL, MOLGEN, EPAM, and SUMEX.

items.title: Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Records
items.description: The materials consist of SAIL Dump And Restore Technique (DART) backup files, 1972-1990; digital copies of 16 mm films created from 1963-1980; handbooks; log books; manuals; and photographs and videos from the 35th SAIL reunion held in 2009.

items.title: Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory records, 1963-2009
items.description: The materials consist of SAIL Dump And Restore Technique (DART) backup files, 1972-1990; digital copies of 16 mm films created from 1963-1980; handbooks; log books; manuals; and photographs and videos from the 35th SAIL reunion held in 2009. The Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (also known as Stanford AI Lab or SAIL) is the artificial intelligence (AI) research laboratory of Stanford University.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Computer hardware

items.title: Computers behind the Iron Curtain, 1965-1966
items.description: This album is of the Buerotechnica Leipzig Fair of 1965 (or 1966). In addition to Ascota machines, Büromaschinenwerk Sömmenda is represented in the album (the leading manufacturer of computers in East Germany).

items.title: David S. Maynard collection of one chord keyset from Douglas Engelbart's Augmentation Research Lab, circa 1968
items.description: In addition to inventing the computer mouse, Doug Engelbart and his research team at SRI adapted a five-key "keyset" for typing and entering commands with the left hand while pointing and clicking with the mouse.

items.title: Edward J. McCluskey papers
items.description: In 1966, he joined Stanford University, where he is Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, as well as Director of the Center for Reliable Computing. His Stanford research focuses on logic testing, synthesis, design for testability, and fault-tolerant computing. The materials consist of subject files, teaching files, chronological files, and compter files.

items.title: Final report ER 54-56 : sequence counter (modification of serial punch), 1956 Oct. 12. Engineering Research Division of U.S. Army Biological Warfare Laboratories
items.description: According to the report's summary, "The sequence counter was developed to establish Remington Rand numerical codes for the automatic punching of pre-selected sequential runs of numbers into each of a deck of Remington Rand punch cards at a rate of 100 cards per minute.

items.title: John Gruber archive, 1944-1980
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Joseph Dela Rutledge papers, 1951-1958
items.description: While at Reminton Rand, Rutledge was one of the engineers responsible for the development of UNIVAC. Materials consist of 66 documents of Joseph Dela Rutledge's papers related largely to his work at the Eckhert-Mauchly Computer Corporation and Remington Rand Corporation.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Computing (general)

items.title: Alan Kay, "Mice, Windows, and the Great Comet" [videorecording]
items.description: Lecture about computer sciences in the 1960's and trends in computer engineering. The MacFest is a conference of speakers, seminars, and product demonstrations pertaining to the Macintosh computer, sponsored by the Stanford Macintosh Users' Group.
items.era_note: [About half of this lecture, on computer science in the 1960s, concerns this period.]

items.title: Augmentation; Collective-IQ and Communication tool : DVD, copy DVD, and booklet, 2005
items.description: Interview with Douglas Engelbart on January 7, 2005, developer of the computer mouse and the first hypertext system.
items.era_note: [Most of this 2005 interview with Douglas Engelbart concerns his augmentation research of these years, which produced the computer mouse and the first hypertext system.]

items.title: Douglas C. Engelbart papers, 1953-2005
items.description: This collection documents that activities of Douglas C. Engelbart, a computer scientist whose pioneering work in the 1950s and 1960s (first at SRI International, later at Tymshare, Inc.) led to the development of the interactive personal computer. Professional papers, including correspondence, research proposals, technical reports, notes, journals, and computer disks, as well as audiovisual material on a variety of media.

items.title: George and Alexandra Forsythe papers, 1938-1979
items.description: He founded the Stanford Computer Science Department, one of the first such departments in the nation, on January 1, 1965. While George was developing Computer Science education at the college level, Sandra was also actively pioneering this area at the high school level and continues to pursue this activity. Professional correspondence, notes for lectures and publications, committee records and publications, materials relating to the Forsythes' writings in the field of computer science and materials relating to Alexandra Forsythe's interest in secondary school instruction of computer science.

items.title: Introduction to digital computer coding and logic : mimeograph
items.description: Course documents for MIT's course number 6.535 on computer coding and logic in the fall of 1952. A simplified version of Jay W. Forrester's Whirlwind I was used as a teaching aid in this course.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Computer Science, records, 1962-2007
items.description: The Department of Computer Science was established in 1965. Reports and memoranda concerning departmental rap sessions, 1968-69; memoranda, reports, diagrams, papers, and other materials, 1976-1981, pertaining to development of the SUN workstation, a network-based personal computer system designed at Stanford University; report on the Department, 1970; listing of personnel (staff, faculty, and students), 1971; files of Carolyn Tajnai, Director of the Stanford Computer Form, pertaining to Silicon Valley history and F. E. Terman, 1963-2007; class materials (syllabi, handouts, exams), 1962-84; reports on research in the department, 1967-69; Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Operating Notes, numbers 1-70 (incomplete set); "The Future of Computer Science at Stanford," by Forsythe, Herriot, and Miller, Feb. 1967; and Robert Floyd "Notes toward a revised formula ALGOL," 1966.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Computer Science, technical reports
items.description: Collection contains 972 PDF technical reports by various authors from within the Stanford Computer Science Department.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Construction and civil engineering practice

items.title: Guy F. Atkinson Company records, ca. 1921-1961
items.description: The Guy F. Atkinson Company is a construction and engineering firm founded in 1926 that specializes in civil projects such as dams, tunnels, and roadbuilding. The records contain materials related to the construction business (estimates, contracts, agreements, indexes of jobs, calculations, budgets, business correspondence, summary sheets, overheads, as well as individual projects' files), legal and financial papers, along with industrial publications, various leaflets, catalogs, clippings, photos, and scrapbooks.

items.title: Harold W. Burke papers, 1945-1985
items.description: Harold W. Burke was an engineering geologist, with particular interest in structural geology, limestone problems, and small hydroelectrics. He did field work around the world in evaluation of foundation problems, particularly for dams and tunnels. Correspondence, reports, subject files, unpublished research, computer data files, bibliography, photographs, and maps.

items.title: John Kiely papers, circa 1945-1977
items.description: Project management files, personal project files, and correspondence documenting John Kiely's years as Vice-President of Bechtel Corporation's Power Division, mostly in the late 1940s-early 50s. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Electronics industry (national and international)

items.title: Ted Nelson collection of technology ephemera, 1950s-1990s.
items.description: Catalogs and other promotional material, mostly concerning electronics, mostly from the 1960s and 70s. Ted Nelson, often referred to as the "father of hypertext," has a long history in the field of computing. This collection primarily contains mailed promotional material in the form of catalogs and advertisements, much of which was requested by Nelson via reader service cards in trade magazines from the 1960s through the early 1990s.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — General manufacturing

items.title: History of Industrial Engineers, Inc. typescript
items.description: Typescript history (written between 1953 and 1974) of the engineering company founded in 1933 by four Stanford alumni: F. L. Kallam, Gregory H. Lifur, William L. Rifenberick, and Angelo F. Semino. The company developed and produced machinery for the petroleum refining industry; it was dissolved in 1972.

items.title: Joseph D. Eisenstadt collection of Ran Battery Company documents, ca. 1930-1989
items.description: Joseph D. Eisenstadt (later Ardon) founded Ran, the Palestine and Israeli Battery company which was the predecessor of the Israeli electronics and military communications equipment firm Tadiran. Included are technical documents, correspondence, and graphic and advertising materials.

items.title: Ralph Heintz prints, tracings, and sketches, undated
items.description: Ralph M. Heintz was chemical engineer and a physical chemist. He was a leading figure in early electronics and radio engineering. He then started the firm Heintz & Kaufman which produced transmitting and vacuum tubes for radios as well as completed radio sets primarily for airplanes and ships. Prints, tracings, and sketches of technical equipment such as compressors and generators.

items.title: Stauffer Chemical Company records, 1881-1987
items.description: The Stauffer Chemical Company was founded in 1885 in San Francisco by two European immigrants, John Stauffer, Sr. and Christian de Guigne. The company mainly produced herbicides for corn and rice. The materials include minutes books, financial statements, correspondence, and photographs.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Labor and professional organizations

items.title: Anne Draper papers, 1938-1973
items.description: Correspondence, articles, statements, reports, newsletters, newsclippings, notes, photographs and posters, primarily concerned with agricultural labor organizations and issues in California. The Anne Draper Papers reflect Draper's work as a trade union organizer, writer, and champion of the rights of farm workers.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- Cesar Chavez East Coast & Canada Tour 1969
items.description: In the fall of 1969, Cesar Chavez toured the East Coast of the United States and Canada to build support for a national boycott of non-union harvested grapes and other produce. Chavez met with boycott staff, donors, politicians, and organized labor leaders, accompanied by four guards led by organizer Mack Lyons, his personal assistant Juanita Brown, nurse Marion Moses, and documentary photographer Bob Fitch.

items.title: Bracero Oral History interviews
items.description: Includes thumb drive and several documents and photographs in connection with Ornelas Bracero Oral History Project. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]
items.era_note: [The oral histories, recorded around 2017, concern the Bracero farm labor program of these years.]

items.title: Charles Batom papers, 1944-1975
items.description: Mr. Batom was an African American union member and a member of civil rights organizations. Includes union items (Cannery Workers Union No. 750, Teamsters, Oakland; ILWU Local 6, the Oakland Warehouse local of the longshore union; Construciton and General Laborers' Union Local 304, Oakland; and Retired Railroad Employee's Club); civil rights items (2 membership cards in the NAACP, 1963 & 1974); fraternal organization items (a membership card in Good Hope Lodge #29, Prince Hall Order, Oakland, and the Prince Hall "Masonic Digest," 1964); and two business cards.

items.title: Ernesto Galarza papers, 1936-1993
items.description: Correspondence, reports, minutes, legal documents, notes, newsletters, press releases, newsclippings, statistical information, questionnaires and photographs documenting Galarza's career as a labor organizer, scholar, Research Director in the National Agricultural Workers Union (1947-1960), and nationally prominent Mexican American activist. The Galarza Papers are particularly rich in information about Mexican and Mexican American farm workers in California from 1948 to 1960.

items.title: Frank Bardacke papers, 1960-1990
items.description: Frank Bardacke is a historian, author, educator, trade unionist, and political activist. Contains manuscript drafts of his book "Trampling Out The Vintage," United Farm Worker administrative material, research files, correspondence, and recordings of interviews and UFW meetings.

items.title: Fred Ross papers, 1920-2003
items.description: Fred W. Ross, Sr. was a pioneer community and labor organizer who fought racial prejudice and championed the rights of the working poor. His papers include correspondence, memoranda, subject files, press clippings, drafts, unpublished writing, photographs, and audio recordings.

items.title: James L. Vizzard papers, 1942-1983
items.description: Correspondence, reports, legislative testimony, speeches, articles, minutes, agendas, newsclippings, oral history tape and transcript, and photographs, documenting Vizzard's career as a lobbyist and worker on behalf of rural poor, migrants and braceros. As the Washington representative for the National Catholic Rural Life Conference (and later for the United Farm Workers), Vizzard was instrumental in influencing legislation aimed at improving the lot of the largely unorganized agricultural labor force.

items.title: Joan London papers, 1962-1970
items.description: Joan London (1901-1971) was the librarian for the California Labor Federation from the 1940s until her retirement in 1962. Correspondence, book draft, newsletters and statements, and newsclippings and publications relating to the agricultural labor movement in California.

items.title: Marion Moses, M.D., papers
items.description: The Dr. Marion Moses, M.D., papers consist of her career spanning fifty years as a nurse, physician, and advocate for farmworkers with the United Farm Workers Union (UFW). The collection consists of her many years of work with the UFW, meeting notes, correspondence with Cesar Chavez, Eliseo Medina, Jessica Govea, Marshal Ganz among many more UFW founders and organizers.

items.title: Nosotros venceremos : digital videodisc (dvd, 11 minutes)and portfolio of 24 photographs, 1960-2004
items.description: The film, in Spanish, is "made from still photographs as an organizing tool for the United Farm Workers. The film-maker combines his photogrpahs with the sounds of the movement: from the march to Sacramento, through Cesar's fast, to the union label on a grape box."

items.title: Original broadsides and circulars relating to the 1966 Farmworkers Peregrinacion from Delano to Sacramento, 1966
items.description: These pieces document one of the seminal events in Mexican-American political history. The 1966 Peregrinacion, a 350-mile pilgrimage from the vineyards of Delano to the State Capitol in Sacramento, was for Chicano farmworkers what the Selma-to-Montgomery March had been for Southern African Americans a year earlier.

items.title: Spiders in the house and workers in the field : Video interview transcript, 1971 Mar. 1.
items.description: Galarza discusses Mexican American labor history, leading up to Joseph DiGiorgio and the DiGiorgio Fruit Corporation and the union organizing and strike attempts in 1949-1950. He discusses the bracero program, illegal immigration of Mexicans, and the political maneuvering to break the strike.
items.era_note: [Most of this 1971 interview, Galarza's account of the 1949-1950 DiGiorgio strike and the bracero program, concerns this period.]

items.title: Viva la causa! : Songs and sound from the Delano strike, por los huelguistas del Delano y el Teatro Campesino
items.description: The recording recounts the farm workers' 300 mile pilgrimage from Delano to Sacramento, California, in March, 1966. Live recordings of song and spoken word performances. All but two are original songs from the strike written by Valdes, Lira or Cantu.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Magnetic recording and data storage

items.title: Alex Maxey papers, circa 1950s
items.description: Collection consits of Maxey’s lab book of mechanical drawings, patent applications, large-scale drawings, and photographs from his time working for AMPEX. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Ampex Collection Addenda
items.description: This is a group of small collections, assembled from various donors, related to the history of the Ampex Corporation and its role in the development of sound recording on tape and stereophonic sound.

items.title: Ampex Corporation historical videotapes
items.description: Video recordings produced or used by Ampex. Five reels of 1960s-70s video tape recordings, all labeled "Ampex Training Department." Most were produced by Ampex themselves.

items.title: Ampex Corporation records, ca. 1944-2005 (bulk 1944-1999)
items.description: Primarily known for their mass storage systems, instrumentation/data recorders, helical scan tape drives, robotic storage libraries, post-production switchers, digital special effects, tape cartridges, and system components. Artifacts (including audio and video recording devices, recordings, and memorabilia) formerly comprising the Ampex Museum collection; approximately 25,000 photographs (including negatives and prints) and related indexes; documents in hard copy or microfilm form (including manuals, memos, sales materials, public relations materials, articles, drawings, engineering notes, specifications, and manuscripts); and other miscellaneous material relating to the history of the Ampex Corporation and the recording industry.

items.title: Crosby-Mullin B-42 (pre-Ampex video machine) slides and ephemera, circa 1985
items.description: This collection consists of a single carousel of slides documenting videorecording equipment developed at Bing Crosby Enterprises (BCE) under Jack Mullin's direction as well as notes and ephemera.
items.era_note: [The slides, taken around 1985, document the video recording equipment built at Bing Crosby Enterprises before the Ampex video machine.]

items.title: Florence James collection of Alexander M. Poniatoff and Ampex Corporation papers, 1964-1978
items.description: Included in box 1 is a biography of Poniatoff (probably an autobiography), circa 1978, written when Mr. Poniatoff was 86 years old. There are also original photographs, excerpts from the Ampex Monitor, and some correspondence. Box 2 contains the tape recorder.

items.title: Fred Pfost papers, 1952-2018
items.description: Born near Boise, Idaho, Fred Pfost (1928-2023) was an American engineer and the last surviving member of the pioneering 1956 Ampex video tape recorder development team which included Ray Dolby, Charles Ginsburg, Alex Maxey, Charles Anderson, and Shelby Henderson. Fred Pfost's correspondence, lab reports, testing notes, and assorted materials--including two tape head assemblies--regarding his work on tape head design for Ampex Corporation's video tape recorder project in the 1950s-60s.

items.title: James Arthur Miller papers, 1912-1971
items.description: James Arthur Miller (1891-1971) was an inventor, engineer and businessman best known for his 1930s audio recording system Millertape. The papers of sound recording engineer James Arthur Miller (1891-1971) include correspondence, press, reports & articles, patents, as well as equipment, prototypes, and personal ephemera.

items.title: Neal Kyser McNaughten papers, 1951-2001
items.description: Neal Kyser McNaughten served as Ampex's Vice President for Professional Products from 1957 to 1962. The papers include copies of corporate memos, personal correspondence, photographs, and other documents related to Neal Kyser McNaughten's career at Ampex. Also, in a small envelope, there is a 1954 prototype video head wheel.

items.title: Philip Rice papers, 1953-1981
items.description: Philip Rice was an American physicist with a particular interest in vision, ultrasound, optics, and electronics. Correspondence, research proposals, and product notes and descriptions (including diagrams and photographs) pertaining to Rice's major innovations in the video/electronics field, 1953-1981. Specific topics and products include electrostatic printing/imaging systems, photographic discs, the electrophotographic process, the development of the first optical videodisc, and a videodisc-based document storage and retrieval system.

items.title: Ray Dolby papers, circa 1940s - 2000s
items.description: Ray Milton Dolby was an American engineer whose inventions and company, Dolby Laboratories, have had a profound effect on the storage, transmission, and reproduction of audio and video. Materials in the collection include Dolby's schoolwork, circuit drawings and engineering schematics for work both at Ampex and Dolby Laboratories, research notes and calculations, patents, correspondence, ephemera from Ampex and from the early years of Dolby Laboratories, and photographs.

items.title: Richard Hess Mullin-Palmer Tape Restoration Project Collection
items.description: The Richard Hess Collection chronicles the early history of tape recording in the United States. The tapes were assembled and reformatted by engineer and researcher Richard L. Hess from 2003 to 2008. Entertainer Bing Crosby was an enthusiastic early adopter, and this collection is largely recordings used in the production of his radio programs.

items.title: The Joe Roizen film archive [videorecording], ca. 1955-1975
items.description: Joe Roizen was a television and broadcasting technologist, author, and consultant. These DVDs contain selected film clips that were used by Roizen as part of technology demonstrations for Ampex Corporation, Telegen, and several other corporate and governmental bodies. They represent a sampling of television broadcasting during the late 1950s through the 1970s. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Tom Rose collection documenting the electronics industry, 1964 - 1988
items.description: Tom Rose worked as a Design Engineer at Dynasonic Systems of Dallas, Texas. The collection includes product catalogs, brochures, flyers, and handouts from electronics firms throughout the United States, as well as from U.S. subsidiaries of international electronics firms. The majority of the materials document electronic sound and data recording technology.

items.title: William Slatkin papers, circa 1940-2019
items.description: Materials related to the history of Ampex Corporation. Includes documents, photocopies, audio recordings of interviews with former Ampex executives and engineers, and a set of Ampex annual reports. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Networking and telecommunications

items.title: Donald MacQuivey papers, circa 1950-1990
items.description: Donald R. MacQuivey (1913-1993) was an engineer and policy analyst in the field of telecommunications. MacQuivey's work largely centered on radio frequency allocation and management, as well as satellite communication and its implementation. The professional papers of Donald MacQuivey consists primarily of correspondence, memoranda, and reports kept by Macquivey in the course of his work.

items.title: The Lenkurt Demodulator, 1961-1976
items.description: General telephone and electronics: video, voice and data transmission systems. The Lenkurt Demodulator is circulated monthly to technicians, engineers, and managers employed by companies of government agencies who use and operate communications systems, and to educational institutions.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Radio, vacuum tubes and microwave

items.title: 10th anniversary celebration of founding : cassette audio tape, 1958 Nov. 2.
items.description: The tape begins with comments by Russel Varian. Numerous speakers follow. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: CPI/Eimac (Communication & Power Industries, Eimac Division) media collection and files, circa 1944-1990
items.description: The Communication Products Industry (CPI), Eimac Division media collection includes photographic media, motion film, and sound recordings produced from the mid-1940s to late 1980s by Eitel-McCullough Incorporated (Eimac), an early innovator in the development and application of high frequency vacuum tubes and radar technology founded in San Bruno, California in 1934.

items.title: Don Preist papers, circa 1934-2002
items.description: The Don Preist papers include 32 containers of print and photographic materials dating back to the 1930s, and document Preist's life and his involvement with innovative research and development for transmitter tubes and klystron beams while he was a lead engineer with the Eimac and Varian companies. The collection includes technical reports and drawings; inter-office memos; research notes and calculations; correspondence; and photographs.

items.title: Edward Ginzton papers, circa 1937-1992
items.description: Co-founder of Varian Associates and a pioneer in microwave tube technology and linear accelerator development. Papers regarding Ginzton's activities at Stanford University, with Varian Associates, and on national committees and local organizations. Includes correspondence, manuscripts, memoranda, journals, publications, technical reports, manufacturing reports, oral history materials, and photographs.

items.title: Eimac Historical artifacts, ca. 1950-1980
items.description: Eitel-McCullough Inc. ("Eimac") was a company based in San Bruno, California and an early innovator of radio transmitter tubes. Diode cuff links and tie clasp, together with a lighter with the Eimac logo.

items.title: Eimac News, 1942-1961
items.description: Publication of the Eimac company featuring employees, events, and engineering activities at their San Bruno, California and Salt Lake City, Utah plants. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Ervin J. Nalos papers, 1939-1993
items.description: Dr. Nalos' research has been in electron physics and electronics, high power microwave devices and electromagnetic scattering. Technical information on electron tube research and early GE Microwave Lab (Stanford) reports including original data on the first derivative tube at S and X-band; also lecture and lab notes, some correspondence, photos and objects relating to electron tubes.

items.title: Jack McCullough interview by Robert Herdman and Jack Strother, 25 Nov. 1997
items.description: Co-founder of Eitel-McCullough Inc. (EIMAC), now a division of Varian Associates. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]
items.era_note: [Most of this 1997 interview, with a co-founder of Eitel-McCullough, looks back on the firm in these years.]

items.title: John Paul (J.P.) Smith papers, circa 1927-1970
items.description: John Paul (frequently referred to as J.P.) Smith worked on the early development of television at Radio Corporation of America (RCA). His collection consists primarily of his reseach papers and schematics, but also includes patents, notes, diagrams, instructions, graphs, articles, reprints, photographic prints and slides.

items.title: Karl R. Spangenberg papers, 1935-1961
items.description: Karl Spangenberg (1910-1964) served as a Professor of Electrical Engineering at Stanford. This collection contains correspondence, teaching materials, subject files, and research notes of Karl R. Spangenberg relating to his work as an electircal engineer specilizing in vacuum tubes at Stanford.

items.title: Lester L. Libby papers, ca. 1936-1984
items.description: The Lester L. Libby papers consist of files created and maintained by Lester Louis Libby (1916-2002) pertaining to his work in the technical field of sound engineering and the application of microwave frequency technologies in various industries including radio, television, and early electronics from the 1930s to the 1970s. Materials include Libby's resarch notebooks, work papers, diagrams and schematics, articles he authored, and patents received.

items.title: Marvin Chodorow papers, 1929-1993 (inclusive), 1943-1974 (bulk)
items.description: He served as Chair of the Department of Applied Physics from 1962-69 and Director of the Edward L. Ginzton Laboratory, 1959-78. Collection largely pertains to his research in linear accelerators, klystrons, and microwaves; professional activities; classes he taught at Stanford; and administrative duties at Stanford.

items.title: Oswald G. Villard papers, 1932-1998 (inclusive), 1958-1998 (bulk)
items.description: Oswald Garrison Villard Jr. (1916-2004), a leader in electromagnetic theory and experimental methods, earned his engineer's degree in 1943 and his Ph.D. in 1949 at Stanford, studying with Dr. F. E. Terman. The papers include correspondence, articles and research papers, memoranda, reports, research files, contracts, minutes, and other materials, 1958-1998. The collection also includes instruction manuals and a log for radio station W6YX, 1932-1933 (club station at Stanford).

items.title: Pert-o-graph (Program evaluation and review technique) : time estimate computer, 1962
items.description: A time estimate computer with resource cost scale. Scales include expected time, pessimistic time, most likely time, optimistic time, and on the reverse, the resources cost. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Rudolf Kompfner papers, 1937-1981
items.description: Professor of Applied Physics at Stanford University and world renowned communications scientist, Rudolf Kompfner came to Stanford in 1973 after a distinguished career at Bell Telephone Laboratories, Oxford University, and with British government research. His invention of the traveling wave tube during this time is credited with making future satellite communications practicable. The collection concentrates primarily on Professor Kompfner's research interests while at Bell Laboratories, Stanford University and Oxford University. Included are general correspondence files, diaries (1937-1941), notebooks and notes (1937-1977), articles and reports (1937-1980), awards, and drawings.

items.title: Russell and Sigurd Varian papers, 1892-1988
items.description: Russsell and Sigurd Varian were co-inventors, with William W. Hansen, of the klystron and rhumbatron and co-founders of Varian Associates. Joined by his brother, Sigurd, a pilot with Pan American Airlines, he began work on microwave technology as a research assistant with Professor William Hansen. In addition to original research notebooks and correspondence regarding the klystron, the collection includes materials on numerous other inventions and ideas from Russell's work for Philo Farnsworth and Humble Oil as well as the brothers' years at Stanford and at Varian Associates.

items.title: Russell Harrison Varian notebook, 1898-1960
items.description: Biographical material about Russell Varian, and articles and speeches written by him. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Physics, correspondence, 1937-1949
items.description: Correspondence and news clippings regarding the Klystron Tube Research Project, 1937-1945; correspondence between department chairman Paul Kirkpatrick and Stanford President Donald B. Tresidder regarding budget and faculty matters, 1943-1947; and statements of William W. Hansen and Robert L. Wathen, 1944, regarding the physics department and research on microwave devices, with a statement by David L. Webster on Hansen's memo, 1949.

items.title: Stanford University, W.W. Hansen Laboratories, klystron reports and patents, 1936-1949
items.description: Brothers Sigurd and Russell Varian worked in collaboration with Prof. William W. Hansen beginning in 1937 to invent and perfect the Klystron, a device for generating high-power microwaves. Reports generated at the Sperry Gyroscope Company on various aspects of the Klystron, 1945-1947; photocopy of the Wave Guide Handbook, 1944-1945, prepared by the Radiation Laboratory at Massachusetts Institute of Technology; paper by V.F. Kovalenko on the history of microwave electron-beam tubes, 1940; and printed patents for the various elements of the Klystron, 1936-1949.

items.title: Sterling McNees papers, undated
items.description: The addendum contains a Report on RRL Project A500 (Tuba) from the Radio Research Laboratory, Harvard University along with research materials about Project A500. There is also newsletters from the Varian Association and the Collins Radio Company, Eimac photographs, Eimac runs of code, and Sterling McNees diploma from Allegheny College.

items.title: The story of EIMAC and the remarkable men who made it : photocopied typescript, 1966
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]
items.era_note: [This history of EIMAC, a typescript of 1966 by its title, concerns the company's first decades, most of them in this period.]

items.title: U.S. Patent #2,558,021, 1951 June 26.
items.description: Includes early petitions, correspondence, and final patent for thermionic vacuum tubes and circuits, which was invented by Russell Varian and David Packard, and assigned to the Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University in 1951 for 17 years.

items.title: William Webster Hansen papers, 1925-1945
items.description: William Webster Hansen was Professor of Physics and Director of the Microwave Laboratory at Stanford University, 1929-1949. Hansen's professional and research papers include correspondence, manuscripts, research notebooks, lecture notes, patents, unpublished studies and notes on various experiments and scientific developments such as radar, the rhumbatron, the klystron, radiation, and microwave mechanics.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Semiconductors

items.title: "The Legacy of Shockley Semiconductor" [videorecording]
items.description: Videorecording of the roundtable discussion held on September 27, 2005, moderated by Leslie Berlin, featuring Gordon Moore, Jay Last, Julius Blank, all co-founders of Fairchild Semiconductor, and James F. Gibbons, professor of electrical engineering at Stanford.
items.era_note: [Most of this recording, a discussion by Fairchild Semiconductor co-founders of their years at Shockley Semiconductor, concerns this period.]

items.title: Armen Sahagun papers, 1954-1965
items.description: The Armen Sahagun papers consist of material related to the development of semiconductor technology during the 1950s-60s. Included are two binders of engineering data, price lists, and other reports from American Micro Devices, a semiconductor manufacturing company founded in Minnesota in 1961.

items.title: Bruce E. Deal collection of Fairchild Semiconductor publications, 1958-1987
items.description: Dr. Deal's work involved studies of silicon thermal oxidation and passivation for semiconductor device and circuit applications, and he also directed activities in all phases of semiconductor materials process, device, and design technology. Collection of technical papers and publications from the Fairchild Semiconductor Corporation, Research and Development Laboratory assembled by Bruce E. Deal, a chemist research staff member for the company.

items.title: Christophe Lécuyer research material on the history of Silicon Valley, 1999-2003
items.description: Academic research files and recorded interviews created by Christophe Lécuyer, a published historian of Silicon Valley high tech industries. He has written books on Fairchild Semiconductor and the history of Silicon Valley. The bulk of materials within the collection is comprised of research notes, photocopied resource materials, presentations, and academic works by Lécuyer.
items.era_note: [Most of this collection, research files and interviews on the early electronics and semiconductor firms of the valley, concerns this period.]

items.title: Fairchild Camera and Instrument 35 mm slides, 1960-1970
items.description: Includes early pictures of researchers and projects, including a progression of chips from the early transistor to the latest 4500.

items.title: Fairchild Semiconductor 50th anniversary [videorecording]
items.description: On October 4, 2007, Julius Blank, Jay Last, Gordon Moore, and Arthur Rock--three Fairchild Semiconductor founders and the venture capitalist who backed them -- discussed the firm's early years and its significance in a panel discussion moderated by Leslie Berlin of the Silicon Valley Archives at Stanford University.
items.era_note: [This 2007 panel discussion is about the founding and early years of Fairchild Semiconductor, which fall in this period.]

items.title: Fairchild Semiconductor Corporation: files of Steve Allen, photographer, circa 1960-1985
items.description: The Steve Allen photographs of Fairchild Semiconductor contains photographs of professional photographer Steve Allen, a Fairchild Semiconductor and National Semiconductor Corporation employee from 1966 through about 1997. The collection documents executive employees, sales force, fabrication facilities, and products of Fairchild Semiconductor.

items.title: Fairchild Semiconductor technical reports and progress reports, 1965-1987
Fairchild Semiconductor, 1957-1977 : booklet of reproduced historical documents, ca. 1978
items.description: Includes important letters, telegrams, photographs, newsclippings, etc.

items.title: Fairchild, The Fairchild chronicles [videorecording]
items.description: Tells the story of the company that invented the integrated circuit, describing the events that spawned the first generation of Silicon Valley technology companies. It covers the period from Fairchild's founding in 1957 to the purchase of the company by National Semiconductor in 1986.
items.era_note: [Most of this documentary, interviews on Fairchild's founding in 1957 and the invention of the integrated circuit, concerns this period.]

items.title: Gerald Pearson papers, 1934-1987
items.description: Co-inventor of the solar cell, Pearson held a total of 34 U.S. patents relating to thermistors, transistors, silicon power diodes, and solar cells.
