Correspondence, 1961-1982, research notebooks on optical properties of solids and other subjects, technical reports prepared during his tenure at Bell Telephone Laboratories, reprints, photographs and slides, legal papers relating to patents, transcript of an oral history interview, memorabilia, and other miscellaneous items.

items.title: Gordon Moore Fairchild Semiconductor patent notebooks, 1957-1968
items.description: Gordon Earle Moore (1929- ), was co-founder of Intel Corporation and progenitor of "Moore's Law." Digital surrogates of the original notebooks held by the Computer History Museum. Gordon Moore kept notes on projects at Fairchild Semiconductor in these notebooks.

items.title: Interview with Victor Grinich by Christophe Lécuyer : typscript, 1996
items.description: Victor Grinich (November 24, 1924 - November 5, 2000) was a pioneer in the semiconductor industry. He worked at the seminal Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory of Beckman Instruments, and then left with other disgruntled members to create the influential Fairchild Semiconductor corporation.
items.era_note: [Most of this 1996 interview, on Grinich's work at Shockley Semiconductor and the founding of Fairchild Semiconductor, concerns this period.]

items.title: Interviews conducted for research on THE INTEGRATED CIRCUIT; a case study of product innovation in the electronics industry, 1965
items.description: References to Fairchild Semiconductor are numerous.

items.title: Jay T. Last papers, 1940-2012
items.description: The collection contains materials from Jay T. Last, one of the "traitorous eight" who quit Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory in 1957 to establish Fairchild Semiconductor. In addition to materials from Last's time at Shockley and Fairchild, there is an assortment of articles, papers, and memorabilia about the history of the semiconductor industry and the lasting impact of Fairchild Semiconductor and its founders in the establishment of Silicon Valley.

items.title: Jean Hoerni papers, 1950-2000
items.description: The collection contains materials from Jean A. Hoerni, one of the "traitorous eight" that quit Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory in 1957 to establish Fairchild Semiconductor. The collection includes correspondence between Hoerni and various semiconductor laboratories, including Shockley, as he searched for a position during the mid-1950s; handwritten notes from his time at Shockley and Fairchild; and copies of Hoerni's publications throughout his education and career.

items.title: Letters from William Shockley to Julius Blank, 1956 March 18 and 19.
items.description: An employment offer with terms, together with a follow-up letter asking Blank to discuss the offer with his supervisor at Western Electric so that there be no suggestion of "indirect methods." [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Photographs of integrated circuits, etc., ca. 1964-1995
items.description: Primarily manufacturing images relating to the work of Robert C. Hall at Fairchild Semiconductor; also some failure analysis photos. There are also some historical reports from the 1960s relating to the work of G. Tripp and J.H. Friedrich.

items.title: Podfather : Robert Noyce and the rise of Silicon Valley
items.description: The epic story of silicon chip inventor Robert Noyce, godfather of today's digital world. Recalls the heady days of Silicon Valley's seminal start-ups and tells how Noyce also founded Intel, the company responsible for more than 80% of the microprocessors in personal computers.
items.era_note: [About half of this 2010 documentary, on Robert Noyce and the early Silicon Valley start-ups, concerns this period.]

items.title: Proposal for custom integrated circuit organization : photocopy of typescript by Jean A. Hoerni, circa 1966-1967
items.description: Hoerni's summary of this paper states, "the new organization will be geared to provide not only diffusion and epitaxial capabilities, but also sputtering and die-electric isolation techniques in order to achieve greatest flexibility in custom circuits fabrication." He discusses the market and the forecast for custom vs. standard integrated circuits.

items.title: Raytheon Semiconductor files kept to monitor the electronics industry, 1965-1986
items.description: Raytheon's Semiconductor Division was established in Mountain View, California in 1968 by its parent company, Raytheon Company of Lexington, Massachusetts, which, in 1990, was described as "one of the largest and most diversified electronics companies in the United States." The collection consists of files that Raytheon's Semiconductor Division kept to monitor both the progress of their competitors and trends in the electronics industry.

items.title: Research material about Robert Noyce, ca. 1970-2005
items.description: The collection documents the research phase of Berlin's biography of Robert Noyce, entitled THE MAN BEHIND THE MICROCHIP. The collection consists of photographs, transcripts and audiotapes of interviews, speeches given by Noyce and others, and background research on the history of the micro-chip industry and the growth of Silicon Valley.
items.era_note: [About a third of this research, on Noyce's early career and the founding of Fairchild Semiconductor, concerns this period.]

items.title: Robert H. Norman microcomputing materials
items.description: 1. Photo of first MOS/LSI chip -- 2. Mock-up of 2000 Gae computer fabricated using Micrologic in TO-18 cans (which were not used) -- 3a. Color print of an actual Victor EC-3900 Logic Board with 28 LSI-ICs of 23 types. Included is a report by Fry Associates to Pyle National Board, "Evaluation of General Micro Electronics business proposal, including market, personnel, and Arthur Anderson analysis of proposed financial plan.

items.title: The 30th anniversary of the integrated circuit; thirty who made a difference : a history of the integrated circuit, 1988
items.era_note: [More than half of this 1988 history, on the invention of the integrated circuit and the people who built the first chips, concerns this period.]

items.title: The Fairchild Chronicles : DVD, 2005
items.description: The is the story of the pioneering semiconductor company from it's founding in 1957 to it's sale to National Semiconductor in 1986. The story is told in the words of those who were there.
items.era_note: [Most of this documentary, interviews on Fairchild's founding in 1957 and the invention of the integrated circuit, concerns this period.]

items.title: Victor Grinich papers and photographs, 1942-1985
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: William Bradford Shockley papers, 1860-2002 (inclusive), 1940-1988 (bulk)
items.description: Professor of engineering at Stanford (1958-1975; emeritus 1975-1989). Shockley was co-recipient of the Nobel Prize in physics, 1956. Professional and personal papers relating to Professor Shockley's controversial interests in environment and genetic influences on intelligence; research on transistors and electronics; and science education. Also includes extensive family materials including diaries and correspondence.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Silicon Valley technology industry as a whole

items.title: Austin Randall collection of photographic negatives, circa 1955-2000
items.description: Black and white negatives related to Silicon Valley corporate culture. Images depict primarily electronic equipment, though people and buildings (including a number by developer Joseph Eichler) are also represented in the collection. Companies represented include Hewlett-Packard, Beckman Instruments, Varian, Wiltron, and Applied Biosystems.

items.title: Bernard M. Oliver oral history interview
items.description: In 1950 He joined the Hewlett-Packard company as director of research. Transcript of an interview conducted by Arthur L. Norberg covering Oliver's early life, his education, and work experiences at Bell Laboratories and Hewlett-Packard.
items.era_note: [Most of this interview, on Oliver's work at Bell Laboratories from 1939 and at Hewlett-Packard from 1950, concerns this period.]

items.title: Frederick E. Terman biographical collection, 1948-1997
items.description: Frederick Emmons Terman (1900-1982) was an American electrical engineer known for his contributions to electronics research and anti-radar technology. Collection consists of photocopies of biographical materials including drafts of the memorial resolution on Terman, newspaper articles and obituaries, list of his patents, speeches and a few articles by Terman, text of remarks from a dinner in honor of Terman in 1977, and several published articles on Terman and Silicon Valley.

items.title: HP Memory Project Collection
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Stanford University, Development Office, Hewlett Packard project video recordings, 1995
items.description: Source tapes used in the production of FOUNDERS OF THE FUTURE, a video project honoring William Hewlett and David Packard and their contributions to Stanford University, and several copies of the final edited version. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]
items.era_note: [About half of these recordings, interviews and historical photographs on the careers of Hewlett and Packard and their ties to Stanford, concern this period.]

items.title: Vernon Russell Anderson papers, 1953-2000
items.description: Papers include class notes, files, and records relating to the Vidar Corporation and Silicon Graphics. In addition to the bound memoir covering Anderson's life, there is a 14-page review written by Anderson about his engineering career.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Software

items.title: Ned Chapin papers, 1960-2008
items.description: Dr. Ned Chapin was a leader in the field of Computer Science, particularly the discipline of Software Maintenance, from its infancy. This collection primarily consists of conference materials, manuscripts, minicartridges, floppy disks, publications, and computer printouts relating to the courses and system development primarily created by Chapin during his tenure at Stanford University.

items.title: Robert W. Floyd papers, 1960-1995
items.description: Robert W. Floyd joined the Stanford faculty in 1968 as an associate professor of computer science. His most important scientific achievement was pioneering systematic methods of program verification. These papers include his Stanford course files, 1976-94; correspondence, 1968-95, including that with Donald Knuth, 1963-1987; research and subject files; reprints and manuscripts; computer printouts; and note cards.

items.title: Ted Nelson papers, 1950s-2019
items.description: Theodor Holm "Ted" Nelson is an information technology pioneer and systems humanist. Nelson founded Project Xanadu in 1960, a global hypertext system designed to permanently connect different types of documents, display visible connections between documents, and include a simplified copyright system.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Transportation and utilities

items.title: Southern Pacific Company public relations collection, 1900, 1959-1972
items.description: Typescripts generated by the Southern Pacific public relations office concerning historical material, the Southern Pacific Pipe Lines, Inc., and the Southern Pacific Transportation Company. Also included is a bibliography, a photocopy of a speech by C.P. Huntington, May 1900, and two publications.

items.title: Southern Pacific Company: drawings and maps
items.description: The collection includes 78 maps produced by Southern Pacific Railroad of lines, sidings, stations, and rail yards in California, primarily in the San Francisco Bay Area but also including the Santa Barbara region.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records, 1862-1997
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 1, Board of Directors records, 1867-1996
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 2, Operating and Maintenance Department records, 1889-1997
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 3, Mechanical Department records, 1909-1996
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 4, Accounting Department records, 1862-1988
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 5, Office of the Secretary records, 1904-1983
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 6, Legal Department records, 1905-1979
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 7, Real Estate Department records, 1954-1970
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Transportation Company records, 1936-1954
items.description: Collection includes Southern Pacific dispatcher's daily train sheets and correspondence, a memorandum and a map regarding the sheets. The sheets are a sampling from three stations (Los Angeles, Beaumont, and Mexicali, Baja).

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work

items.title: Alan Bagley papers, 1950-2003
items.description: Alan Bagley was a longtime Hewlett-Packard engineer and manager. Communications, technical notes, in-house publications, newspaper clippings, organizational charts, catalogs, training manuals, and other materials related to the career of Alan Bagley, primarily at Hewlett-Packard.

items.title: Arthur Hyatt papers, 1959-1992
items.description: American computer scientist. Correspondence, printed matter and miscellany, relating to Soviet-American aerial cooperation during World War II and to the postwar computer industry in the Soviet Union.

items.title: International Measurement and Instrument Show : photographs, 1961
items.description: Images, which are identified by Pettit, include the fairgrounds where the show was held, company exhibits, and various electronic instruments.

items.title: Laurence W. "Bill" Lane, Jr. papers, circa 1953-2010
items.description: The papers include speeches, personal correspondence, and correspondence and documents relating to Lane Publishing Co., producers of Sunset Magazine, books, and films. Laurence William Lane Jr. often known as Bill Lane (November 7, 1919 - July 31, 2010) was an American magazine publisher and philanthropist. The Lane family owned and published Sunset Magazine.

items.title: Martin Packard papers, c. 1946-1990
items.description: In the late 1940s and early 50s, physicist Martin Packard made significant contributions to the emerging field of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) technology at Stanford University. Packard was later employed by Varian Associates, where he became head of the analytical instrumentation department, Corporate Vice President, and finally Assistant to Board Chairman Edward Ginzton. The collection is largely from his time at Varian, consisting of correspondence and memoranda, subject files maintained as Varian's reference library, and files related to Varian's corporate history.

items.title: National Company's cesium beam primary frequency standards : black and white photographic prints, ca. 1960
items.description: Grant joined National Company in 1954, becoming their vice-president of engineering. Mr. Grant has 11 patents in atomic beam frequency standards, radar circuits, mircrowave components, and laser technology.

items.title: Pacific Improvement Company records, 1863-1967
items.description: Pacific Improvement Company was a large holding company in California, formed by C. P. Huntington, Leland Stanford, Mark Hopkins, and Charles Crocker. Contains business records of the Pacific Improvement Company and its subsidiaries. Business areas covered include land development, coal and iron mining, railroads, and hotels.

items.title: Project Plowshare reports, 1960-1975
items.description: Project Plowshare, which originated at the Lawrence Radiation Laboratory of the University of California, Livermore, in 1956, was concerned with the peaceful uses of nuclear explosions in excavations and other engineering projects. Collection consists largely of reports and studies from various projects and experiments, with some memoranda, press releases, articles, clippings, and brochures.

items.title: Samuel Morse papers, 1911-1982
items.description: He became associated with the Crockers and after making a success of the Crocker-Hoffman Land and Water Company, which he managed, he was subsequently offered a position managing the Pacific Improvement Company in 1915. Contains personal correspondence of Samuel Morse, correspondence of the Pacific Improvement Company relating to liquidation of the company, and a report (12 v.) prepared for the Pacific Improvement Company in 1916, titled, "Iron, Steel, Coal & Coke on the Pacific Coast."

items.title: Selket Corporation records, circa 1967-1997
items.description: Materials include company documents, drawings, printed material, product development plans, and artifacts, as well as reference materials used by Rojo to set up and run his company.

items.title: Thomas J. Carr papers, circa 1940s-1990s
items.description: This archive documents military, computing and space history.

items.title: William P. Wreden, Books & Manuscripts archive, 1936-1993
items.description: Correspondence, financial records, catalogue checking copies, orders, appraisals, account books, jeweler's inventory books, flyers, publications, scrapbook, and photographs.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Environment and conservation

items.title: Philip Albert Leighton, "Man and air in California" address
items.description: Professor of chemistry at Stanford University and chairman of the board of Metronics Associates, Inc. Text of address presented at the Statewide Conference on Man in California, 1980s, held in Sacramento, January 27, 1964. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: San Mateo County Resource Conservation District records, 1935-2008
items.description: The San Mateo County Resource Conservation District (formerly known as the San Mateo County Soil Conservation District) is a non-regulatory public benefit district to help protect, conserve, and restore natural resources through information, education, and technical assistance programs. The records of the San Mateo County Resource Conservation District span the history of the organization and include administrative and financial files, meeting minutes, reports, maps, and other material.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Farming, canning and food processing

items.title: All the answers about walnuts [graphic] : photograph album
items.description: Story told in photographs of the shelling and cleaning procedure of getting walnuts from shell to can, each with a typed caption mounted below the photograph.

items.title: Home, W.S. Wilcox, 1950, Below [graphic].
items.description: A 2017 scan of a 1950 photograph of an orchard owned by W.S. Wilcox that once stood where the Intel building is now in the Santa Clara Valley.

items.title: Land capability, land use adjustment and conservation farming of the Stanford University agricultural lands : report, 1949
items.description: Report of land conditions on the agricultural lands requested of the Soil Conservation Service of the U.S. Department of Agriculture by the University; includes photographs, charts, and a partial map.

items.title: Steele Ranch records, 1855-1973
items.description: Compilation of ranch records from the Steele Ranches of San Mateo County, California. Includes financial papers, legal papers, photographs, maps, and miscellaneous background notes written by Mrs. Catherine Steele. The collection covers over 100 years of ranching in California.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Mining and quarrying

items.title: Benjamin M. Page, "Mineral Resources on Stanford Land, A Preliminary Report"
items.description: Typescript report on mineral, water, and oil resources on Stanford land by Benjamin M. Page, Stanley N. Davis, Frank W. Atchley, L. Trowbridge Grose, John W. Harbaugh, and Charles F. Park, Jr.; with related correspondence of Park and university president J. E. Wallace Sterling.

items.title: Calvin Charles Enderlin engineering reports on mining and metallurgy, 1947
items.description: The materials consist of engineering reports on mining and metallurgy.

items.title: Charles Frederick Park papers, 1950-1987
items.description: Professor of geology (1946-1969; emeritus, 1969-); and Dean of the School of Earth Sciences (1950-1965). Collection largely consists of correspondence with professional colleagues and correspondence which covers Park's activities in national and international geological organizations (especially the Society of Economic Geologists and the International Association of the Genesis of Ore Deposits), mineral explorations, work as a mining consultant, and the School of Earth Sciences at Stanford.

items.title: Daniel Cowan Jackling papers, 1911-1956
items.description: Daniel Cowan Jackling (1869-1956) was a mining engineer who established several mining companies in the Western United States. Primarily correspondence, together with ledgers pertaining to Jackling's finances, photographs, annual reports, and clippings.

items.title: New Almaden Mine records, 1845-1973
items.description: Correspondence, legal and financial documents, ledgers, reports, research notes, photographs, maps, plans, profiles, charts and artifacts relating to the operation of the New Almaden Mine and the Quicksilver Mining Co.

items.title: Robert B. Hoy papers, 1949-1980
items.description: Robert B. Hoy graduated from Lafayette College (Pennsylvania) in 1937 and pursued a career as a geologist, working with the New Jersey Zinc Company, Stanford Research Institute, and AMAX Exploration, Inc. Collection includes manuscripts, project files, reports, correspondence, and subject files related to his career.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Petroleum and natural gas

items.title: Earl E. Brabb collection of Chevron oil well logs
items.description: Logs contain information for an estimated 6,000 oil test wells in California from an area extending from Eureka to the Salton Sea.

items.title: Richard Sterling Finnie papers, 1950-1967
items.description: The Richard Finnie Collection contains films, audio recordings, and photographs by Richard Sterling Finnie (1906-1987), a documentary filmmaker, photographer, ethnographer, and historian. As a producer for Bechtel's industrial film division, Finnie made over 60 promotional films touting Bechtel's pipeline and other development projects around the world, including such titles as Oil Across Sumatra , More Power to Korea , Exploring Libya , and Bechtel in Europe . Photographs, films, and audio recordings relating to Bechtel Corporation's development projects, especially pipe line construction, all by company historian and film producer Richard Finnie.

items.title: Robert B. Moran collection, 1850-1968
items.description: Robert Moran has been recognized as an early pioneer in the fields of petroleum geology and petroleum engineering and was one of a handful of geologists who gathered in 1924 to assist in the formation of the Pacific Section of the American Association of Petroleum Geologists. Collection includes reports, maps, correspondence, cross sections, logs, notes, printed material, production data, and other miscellaneous material relating to the professional career of Robert Moran.

items.title: Theodore L. Lenzen papers, circa 1920s-1960s
items.description: The photo albums were created by Theodore Lenzen, a Standard Oil executive who worked in a number of locations including Richmond, California, Alaska, Saudia Arabia, Indonesia, and Bahrain. This collection consists 15 photo albums, which include some correspondence and documents.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Real estate and land development

items.title: Andrew Doty : an interview conducted by Susan Schofield : transcript, 2007
items.description: Oral history interview conducted in June 2007 pertaining to his 30-year career in community relations and public affairs at Stanford. Topics include San Hill Road, Peter Coutts housing development, SLAC power line, commercial development of Stanford lands, and relations with Palo Alto and Santa Clara County.
items.era_note: [About half of this 2007 interview, on disputes such as the SLAC power line and Sand Hill Road, concerns this period.]

items.title: Archive of the Japanese Cultural and Trade Center, Japantown, San Francisco, 1961-1954
items.description: Collection consists of project booklets and related materials for the Japanese Cultural and Trade Center in San Francisco. There are also news clippings and correspondence from National-Braemar, Inc. to the San Francisco Redevelopment Agency.

items.title: Frenchman's Hill development lottery
items.description: List of the lottery picks for prospective lessees when Frenchman's Hill was to be developed, circa 1965. The 'prospective lessee's' was handed out to attendees at the drawing for lots in Frenchman's Hill.

items.title: Harry L. Sanders planning documents, 1940-1970
items.description: Harry L. Sanders came to Stanford in 1956 as associate director of planning. This collection includes reports, proposals, agenda, minutes, transcripts of public hearings, and other documents pertaining to development in San Francisco, especially Diamond Heights and the Western Addition, 1948-54; and reports, booklets, and brochures pertaining to planning in general, 1940-70.

items.title: Land use and planning documents, San Mateo and Santa Clara Counties, 1958-1995
items.description: Crowder served as Palo Alto City Planner from 1972-1982 and was on the Portola Valley Planning Commission from 1974-1982. The collection consists primarily of reports and other publications regarding land use in California, particularly in San Mateo and Santa Clara Counties, 1958-1980.

items.title: Pacific Heights Company, Westview, San Mateo County, California : typescript
items.description: A business proposal with supporting documents tipped in. The proposal itself is brief (3 pages) and a bit opaque as to purpose but it concerns development of the Westview Tract (aka Pacific Highlands, one of the neighborhoods that became Pacifica when the city was incorporated in 1957). The proposal is followed by several attachments, including a VA Master Certificate of Reasonable Value, an FHA Subdivision Report, an FHA Description of Materials, two blueprint reproductions, three tract maps of Pacific Hightlands and a brochure promoting the Westview home (a 1-1/2 story home with 4 bedrooms, two baths and a single car garage).

items.title: Stanford Lands Clippings and Ephemera collection, 1950-1967
items.description: Photocopied clippings pertaining to land development at Stanford University. Subjects include flood control, freeways, housing, the industrial park, Stanford Linear Accelerator Center, the Stanford Shopping Center, the Stanford Barn (the old winery), the medical center, the Veterans Administration Hospital, and related events in Menlo Park and Palo Alto.

items.title: Stanford University faculty housing photographs, 1891-2000 (inclusive), 1961-2000 (bulk)
items.description: Photographs of individual houses and housing complexes on the Stanford University campus; includes images taken during the construction of homes in the Frenchmen's Hill subdivision, 1967-69,and of the Stanford West Apartments, 2000.

items.title: Stanford University map collection, 1853-1998
items.description: The maps in this collection pertain to the University campus, to other lands owned by Jane and Leland Stanford or the University, and to adjacent communities.

items.title: Stanford University, Office of the General Counsel, records
items.description: The Office of the General Counsel (OGC) is responsible for addressing all of the legal issues arising out of the activities of Stanford University, Stanford Hospital and Clinics and Lucile Salter Packard Children's Hospital at Stanford. Records from the legal office pertain to real estate matters, including the Stanford Shopping Center, other leases, and gift deeds.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Surveying and mapping

items.title: Hatfield aerial survey of Palo Alto High School : photoprint, 1947
Hatfield Aerial Surveys photographs, 1947-1979
items.description: This collection consists of aerial photographs of the Stanford University campus and lands taken by Hatfield Aerial Surveys, a firm owned by Adrian R. Hatfield. Of notes are images of areas of the campus now the site of the Stanford Shopping Center, the Medical Center, the industrial park, and faculty housing developments.

items.title: James Crossen oral history, 2001
items.description: From 1953 to his retirement in 1985, James Crossen worked with the U.S. Geological Survey, primarily making topographic maps in the seven western states and Hawaii.
items.era_note: [Most of this 2001 oral history concerns James Crossen's Geological Survey mapping work and the Apollo lunar project of the 1950s and 1960s.]

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Transportation

items.title: Captain John L. Lee correspondence, 1943-1944, 1946
items.description: Materials consist ofthe incoming and outgoing correspondence John L. Lee, most of it related to the operation of the tanker SS Umatilla by San Francisco-based Pacific Tankers Inc. between April 17, 1944 and November 21, 1944.

items.title: Great new airport for San Francisco
items.description: A special supplement for the opening of the new airport, including history and photos of older airports, photos of the new airport and members of the Public Utilities Commission, and numerous related articles and advertisements.

items.title: Hopkins transportation collection, 1711-1959
items.description: Material concerning railroads, shipping, automobiles, and transportation which was once part of the Hopkins Transportation Library at Stanford. One of several of sharing the name, this collection contains multiple accessions from various donors over many years, including a ledger from an English sailing vessel dated 1711-1757, railroad stock and bond certificates signed by Hopkins and Huntington, deeds and legal documents involving a variety of rail companies (including the signatures of founding stockholders for the Oakland Railroad Co. in 1868), and a great deal of Southern Pacific Railroad material, some of which was sent directly to the Hopkins Library while it was under the care of director Jeanette Hitchcock in the 1940s.

items.title: Hopkins transportation collection, 1844-1969 (inclusive), 1936-1954 (bulk)
items.description: Ephemera related to the construction and operation of railroads in the Western United States and the United Kingdom, including dispatcher's records from Beaumont, California; Los Angeles, California; and Mexicali, Baja California. While primarily about railroads, the collection also contains printed material and ephemera about other forms of transport, including automobiles, passenger ships, and airplanes, as well as various mostly related engineering plans and reports.

items.title: Newsclipping collection, 1890-1952
items.description: A miscellaneous collection, including railroad history, ca. 1940-1952, ramifications of the Clayton Act which outlawed as monopolistic the agreements railroads had formed among themselves, aviation in the post World War II era and a bit about its advent, many articles on the effect of World War II on railroads, municipal railroads, particularly in San Francisco, ships for trade and leisure, and a few clippings about the Hopkins family and the sale of the Hopkins house to Hollywood in the 1940s.

items.title: Railroads and trolleys in the United States and Mexico : photographs
items.description: Collection contains over 2,600 photographs documenting various railways and trolley lines in the United States (primarily California) and Mexico.

items.title: Railway and locomotive historical societies : album, 1940-1958
items.description: During the 1950s there were several important local organizations devoted to railroad history: The Pacific Coast Railroad and Locomotive Historical Society, Inc., the California-Nevada Railroad Historical Society, the Bay Area Electric Railroad Association, and the Central Railway Club of San Jose. Society newsletters and magazines, rail excursion flyers, excursion photographs, news clippings, announcements, time tables, ticket stubs, map, etc.

items.title: San Francisco International Airport : album, 1954-1955
items.description: Album prepared as a promotional piece for the British Overseas Airways Corporation and for Lufthansa on the opening of San Francisco International Airport. Ephemera includes photographs; plot and elevation plans; booklet on statistical facts of air traffic; brochures and data describing San Francisco and the airport.

items.title: William Ripley Dorr collection of California railroad club photograph albums
items.description: William Ripley Dorr, a resident of Palos Verdes Estates, California, was a confirmed rail fan. Dorr photographed each trip, and mounted the photographs in two albums, which comprise the collection. They are mainly examples of types of engines and types of cars, from both the era of steam and the more modern diesel era.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Water and public works

items.title: Electrolysis tests on Treasure Island, 1940, 1940 December 19.
items.description: Report on wear and tear of Treasure Island's infrastructure, especially water leakage and salt-water intrusion, "Requested by P.M. Downing and L.J. Brown, Construction Superintendent, Golden Gate International Exposition." Includes six original tipped-in photographs and nine folding plans of various portions of Treasure Island, showing the location of water-system tests in relation to specific proposed exhibition space, etc.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use

items.title: Albert Wilson papers, ca. 1910-1995
items.description: Albert Wilson (1903-1996), was a San Francisco Bay Area botanist, landscape architect, author, teacher and lecturer on gardening and landscaping, as well as a TV and radio talk show personality who wrote several books popularizing gardening, as well as an autobiography. Material related to Wilson's career as horticulturalist, author, and broadcaster.

items.title: California Flower Market records, 1890-2014
items.description: The California Flower Market, Inc. was founded in 1912 by Japanese American flower growers in the San Francisco Bay Area. The records of the California Flower Market, Inc. include photographs, photograph albums, manuscript materials, books, articles, ephemera, and audiovisual materials from the late 1800s to 2014, with the bulk covering the period 1910 to 1990.

items.title: Toichi Domoto papers, ca. 1860-1996
items.description: Japanese American Toichi Domoto (1902-2001) was a noted horticulturist who began in his family's Domoto Brothers Nursery and later founded his own nursery in Hayward, California. The collection contains family and business correspondence, legal advice concerning the Alien Land Law of 1913, early nursery business records, early nursery catalogs (from the Yokohama nursery, the Domoto Bros. nursery, and Toichi Domoto's nursery), photographs of the Domoto family and early nursery business, class notes and subject files.

sectors.name: Education and research — Applied physics

items.title: Albert V. Baez papers, 1949-1995
items.description: The materials consist of research files, correspondence, teaching materials, biographical material, publications, photographs, and some experimental equipment. Albert Vinicio Baez, Ph.D. (1912-2007) was a prominent Mexican-American physicist, and the father of singers Joan Baez and Mimi Fariña. In 1948, along with Stanford University professor Paul Kirkpatrick (1894–1992), Baez developed the X-ray reflection microscope for examination of living cells.

items.title: Anthony Edward Siegman papers, 1916-2013 (inclusive)
items.description: Anthony Siegman was an electrical engineer, primarily focused on masers and lasers. Siegman became an assistant professor at Stanford in Electrical Engineering in 1957. The materials consist of administrative files, research files, correspondence, and publications.

items.title: Bloch symposium; a Stanford centennial symposium celebrating the work of Felix Bloch [videorecording]
items.description: Excelling in both theoretical and experimental physics, Bloch won the Nobel Prize in 1952 for his work in nuclear magnetism. Tapes from a symposium held on October 27 and 28, 1989, at Stanford University; speakers included Robert Hofstadter, James S. Harris, William A. Little, K. Halbach, Erwin Hahn, D. Fisher, H. Gutfreund, Alexander Pines, E. Raymond Andrew, and W.F. Brinkman.
items.era_note: [About half of this symposium, on Felix Bloch's work in nuclear magnetism that won the Nobel Prize in 1952, concerns this period.]

items.title: C. F. Quate papers, circa 1961-1984
items.description: He joined the Stanford faculty in 1961 as professor in the applied physics and electrical engineering departments, serving two terms as chair of the department of applied physics. Correspondence, memoranda, press releases, contracts, grants, course materials and other records pertaining to his research and teaching at Stanford, including work at the Ginzton Laboratory; and offsets, glossies, and slides from the acoustic microscope project.

items.title: David Locke Webster papers, 1914-1976
items.description: He remained Professor of Physics at Stanford until 1954, when he retired. The papers of David Locke Webster document his career as a professor and physicist and include course material from physics classes taught at Stanford (1946-1954); notes and notebooks from his earlier teaching career at Harvard, Michigan and M.I.T.; correspondence and subject files on Army research projects; budget material for the Stanford physics department (1924-1943); reprints of articles; research data; photographs of apparatus used in experiments; manuscripts; correspondence (1939-70) regarding Webster's interests (e.g. Klystron Tube, compton effect); research notebooks (1916-1970); correspondence relating to the Physics Department during the 1940's; glass plates for printing graphs; photographs; maps.

items.title: Felix Bloch papers, 1928-1987
items.description: The Bloch papers document Felix Bloch's role in twentieth century physics as a scientist, teacher and administrator. The collection includes correspondence, grant proposals, lecture notes, minutes and accompanying documentation regarding departmental, university and national committees, research notebooks, grants, patents, and designs; files regarding organizations in which Bloch played an active role; publications (predominantly reprints) by Bloch; and photographs.

items.title: Fu Chun Yu lab notebooks [facsimiles], 1949-1950
items.description: Collection consists of three notebooks (in facsimile) kept by Fu Chun Yu while he was a post-doc in Prof. Felix Bloch's NMR laboratory at Stanford; they cover Yu's work with Warren Proctor that lead to a realization of the chemical shift in molecules.

items.title: High Frequency Direct Writing Oscillograph Project Lantern Slides, circa 1960s
items.description: Richard G. Sweet developed an ink-jet recorder at Stanford University in the early 1960s. Funded by an Army Signal Corps contract, Sweet developed a technique for selective charging and deflection of individual ink droplets, resulting in higher recording speeds for ink-jet printers.

items.title: Nuclear resonance : glass slides, ca. 1945
items.description: Slides show measuring equipment and graphs and measurements.

items.title: Optics and laser spectroscopy, Bell Telephone Laboratories, 1951-1961, and Stanford University since 1961 : oral history transcript / 1998
items.description: co-author, with Charles H. Townes, of Microwave Spectroscopy (1955), dealing with theory and experimental techniques of microwave spectroscopy; marriage in 1951 to Aurelia Townes, and move to Bell Telephone Laboratories: working on superconductivity, in 1957-1958 collaborating with Townes on the optical maser (laser), and publication of "Infrared and Optical Masers"; discussion of the atmosphere at Columbia and at Bell Labs, pressures, publications, patents; joins physics faculty at Stanford University: research group in laser spectroscopy, Ted Hänsch, students, administrative matters, other faculty.

items.title: Paul Harmon Kirkpatrick autobiography, 1971
items.description: Professor of physics at Stanford University since 1931 (emeritus, 1960 - ); best known for his pioneering work in x-ray technology. General reminiscences about his life, including recollections about his work and colleagues at Stanford.
items.era_note: [About half of this autobiography, recollections of his work and colleagues at Stanford before his retirement in 1960, concerns this period.]

items.title: Stanford University, W.W. Hansen Laboratories of Physics, records, 1947-1993
items.description: Contracts, proposals, correspondence, and memoranda from the files of the William W. Hansen Laboratories relating to the construction of the Stanford Linear Accelerator, the development of the Klystron tube, and medical research using linear accelerators.

sectors.name: Education and research — Campus and student life

items.title: Chicanismo
items.description: Official publication for MEChA, Stanford University.

items.title: Mary Hill Skougaard photographs of KZSU activities, 1949
items.description: Mary Hill Skougaard (AB 1950 in communications) was the first female station manager at Stanford?s student radio station, KZSU. Copy negatives of original images in a scrapbook owned by Mary Hill Skougaard, with photocopies of most of the original images. Subjects include KZSU engineers and staff, live broadcasts, and parties; individuals include Bill Kane, Fred Steiner, Rosemarie Armstrong [Ostberg], Peter F. Dawson, Mary Hill [Skougaard], and Steve Phillips.

items.title: Stanford Amateur Radio Club scrapbook, 1941-1957
items.description: The "ham radio" station W6YX at Stanford dates back to 1924 and is still active; electronics professor Oswald G. Villard Jr. served as faculty advisor and trustee for many years. Scrapbook contains clippings, articles, correspondence, membership list, certificates (one issued to Osward G. Villard), photographs, and 1 FCC complaint; some of the correspondence is with the American Radio Relay League regarding records of calls made by the club.

items.title: Stanford Villager's Cook Book
items.description: The Stanford Village complex was developed from converted military housing located in Menlo Park on the current site of SRI International. Cookbook compiled by Stanford Village residents, 1961. Recipes include Meats, Casseroles; Salads, Vegetables; Breads; Cakes, Cookies, Pies, Desserts.

sectors.name: Education and research — Education research and educational technology

items.title: Patrick Suppes papers, 1951-2014
items.description: Patrick Suppes was the Lucie Stern Professor of Philosophy, Emeritus, and a member of the departments of Statistics and Psychology and of the Graduate School of Education at Stanford University. This collection consists of research, notes, papers, and correspondence with a particular emphasis on Suppes' work on computer-assisted education research.

items.title: Pauline Snedden Sears papers, 1931-1990 (inclusive), 1953-1977 (bulk)
items.description: Before joining the Stanford faculty in the School of Education in 1953, she taught at Yale and Harvard and was a research associate at the Child Welfare Research Station at the State University of Iowa. Her research subjects included the classroom effects of computer assisted instruction, development of creativity, and teaching strategies for effective reinforcement of culturally different children. The papers of Pauline Sears primarily pertain to her career at Stanford, with only one folder of materials pertaining to her activities during the 1930s.

items.title: Stanford Consultation Services records, 1949-1956
items.description: The Stanford Consultation Services, under the direction of Education Professor Robert N. Bush, conducted case studies of teachers and administrators in selected school systems in California, Colorado, Washington, and Australia. Records include complete case files from three individual studies at Alameda High School in Alameda, CA, MR Trace Elementary School in San Jose, CA, and Jordan Junior High School in Palo Alto, CA; summary folders from all other cases; and general administrative files.

sectors.name: Education and research — Engineering

items.title: Bernard Roth papers
items.description: Bernard Roth, Professor of Mechanical Engineering, Emeritus, is one of the founders of the Hasso Plattner Institute of Design at Stanford (the d.school) and is active in its development: currently, he serves as Academic Director.

items.title: Frederick Emmons Terman papers, 1901-1978
items.description: The papers of Frederick Emmons Terman, dating from 1920 to 1978, document all phases of his long and influential career as an educator, electronics engineer, administrator, and author. The collection consists of nearly 200 boxes of correspondence, memoranda, minutes, reports, speeches and miscellaneous materials accumulated by Dr. Terman and his staff throughout his professional life.

items.title: Glen E. Myers Stanford class notes, 1956-1962
items.description: Glen E. Myers studied mechanical engineering at Stanford, earning his M.S. in 1957 and his Ph.D. in 1962. This collection contains syllabi, course handouts, problem sets, exams, and Myers' notes from engineering, math, and physics classes he took at Stanford, 1956-59; for the elementary engineering thermodynamics classes for which he was a teaching assistant, 1958-59; and for the class on elementary engineering thermodynamics that he taught at Stanford during the summer of 1962.

items.title: H.O. Fuchs papers, 1950-1988
items.description: Course notes for mechanical engineering undergraduate and graduate classes; correspondence; case histories in engineering problems prepared by Fuchs; records pertaining to the Engineering Case Program; research notes, articles, and papers by Fuchs; and photographs. Fuchs, an expert on fatique in metals, taught mechanical engineering at Stanford University from 1964 to 1973, when he became an Emeritus Professor.

items.title: John Edward Arnold course materials, 1958-1959
items.description: John Edward Arnold was a professor of mechanical engineering and business administration at Stanford University. He was the founding director of the Design Division of the Mechanical Engineering Department. Lectures on creativity from the Creative Engineering Seminar, 1959, by Arnold and guest lecturers J.P. Guilford, Robert S. Hartman, and Robert H. McKim; a lecture by A. H. Maslow, "Emotional Blocks to Creativity," presented to U.S. Army engineers at Fort Belvoir, VA, 1958; a chart on creative process; and a bibliography on creative engineering.

items.title: John Edward Arnold Papers
items.description: Lectures on creativity from the Creative Engineering Seminar, 1959, by Arnold and guest lecturers J.P. Guilford, Robert S. Hartman, and Robert H. McKim; a lecture by A. H. Maslow, "Emotional Blocks to Creativity, " presented to U.S. Army engineers at Fort Belvoir, VA, 1958; a chart on creative process; and a bibliography on creative engineering.

items.title: Neal Van Devender papers, 1964-2003 (inclusive), 1964-1966 (bulk)
items.description: Neal Van Devender earned his master's degree in aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University in 1966. The bulk of the collection consists of syllabi, notes, homework reports, and exams from math, engineering and aeronautics classes at Stanford, 1965-66.

items.title: Stanford University, Engineering Case Program, case files, 1948-1972
items.description: The Engineering Case Program, which began at Stanford University in 1964, provided written accounts of engineering problems to be used in the training of engineers. This collection consists of the master files from 114 cases where the author was a Stanford faculty or staff member or the event described happened in the San Francisco Bay Area.

items.title: Stanford University, Foundry, records, 1945-1952 (inclusive)
items.description: The Stanford Foundry operated by mechanical engineering students in the mid-20th century. The materials consist of news clippings, photographs, and negatives documenting the Stanford University Foundry.

items.title: Stephen Timoshenko papers, 1907-1996 (inclusive), 1921-1970 (bulk)
items.description: Stephen Prokofievitch Timoshenko, a world-renowned authority on theoretical and applied mechanics, was educated at the Munich Polytechnic Institute and at the University of Gottingen. Correspondence, manuscripts, typescripts, galleys, notes, reprints, photographs, passports, awards, and other items; some materials are in Russian or German.

items.title: Wilhelm Flügge papers, 1937-1980
items.description: Wilhelm Flügge, internationally known specialist in engineering mechanics, is best known for his research on shell structures. These papers, dating from 1937-1980, pertain primarily to his professional career at Stanford; included are correspondence, manuscripts, papers, lectures, minutes, memoranda, photographs, and teaching materials.

sectors.name: Education and research — Library, archival and information services

items.title: ARS Audiotape Collection
items.description: Miscellaneous tape recordings, mostly small donations, that span the history of the Archive of Recorded Sound. In a sense, this is a collection that reveals the history of the Archive of Recorded Sound and its role both on the Stanford campus and in the greater community of collectors and researchers of audio recordings.

sectors.name: Education and research — Musical acoustics and computer music

items.title: John R. Pierce papers, 1933-2002 (inclusive), 1960-2002 (bulk)
items.description: He worked at Bell Telephone Laboratories from 1936 to 1971, where his work included electronic tubes, microwave communications, and psychoacoustics. In 1983 he became a visiting professor of music, emeritus, at the Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics at Stanford University. The focus is primarily on his interest in computers and music and his authorship of science fiction stories, with a few published articles and photographs pertaining to the Echo satellite.

items.title: Musical Acoustics Research Library collection, 1956-2007
items.description: Contains research materials, research papers, correspondence, journal run , photographs, glass slides, wood samples, and other artifacts (woodwind and brass mouthpieces). The MARL collection is dedicated to the study of all aspects of musical acoustics.

sectors.name: Education and research — Schools, colleges and training

items.title: College of San Mateo (formerly: San Mateo Junior College)
items.description: Located in San Mateo, California. Founded in 1922 as the San Mateo Junior College. In 1954 became College of San Mateo.

items.title: College of San Mateo (formerly: San Mateo Junior College)
items.description: Located in San Mateo, California. Founded in 1922 as the San Mateo Junior College. In 1954 became College of San Mateo.

items.title: Foothill College
items.description: Located in Los Altos Hills, California. Founded in 1957.

items.title: Gavilan College (formerly: San Benito County Junior College)
items.description: Located in Gilroy, California. Established in 1919 as San Benito County Junior College in Hollister, California. Became Gavilan College in 1963.

items.title: Menlo College and School of Business Administration, 1928-1977
items.description: Located in Menlo Park, California. Menlo School was founded in 1915, Menlo Junior College in 1927, and the School of Business Administration in 1949.

items.title: San Jose Bible College (later: William Jessup University), 1956-1971
items.description: Located in San Jose, California. Founded in 1939 as San Jose Bible College. Became San Jose Christian College in 1989 and moved in 2003 to Rocklin, California becoming William Jessup University in 2004.

items.title: San Jose City College, 1955-1978
items.description: Located in San Jose, California. Founded in 1921 as San Jose Junior College. Became San Jose City College in 1958.

items.title: St. Patrick's Seminary (later: St. Patrick's Seminary and University)
items.description: Located in Menlo Park, California. Founded in 1898.

items.title: To Mr. George Murray in remembrance of the 1969-1970 school year at Nairobi High
items.description: A one-off yearbook of sorts, made from the plain thick card covers of a spiralbound notebook with the pages removed, photos and text mounted on the inside of the boards. Presented to the former Black Panther Minister of Education, George Murray, who had taken the position of principal at the new high school, recruiting fellow students from Stanford as teachers.

items.title: University of Santa Clara (formerly: Santa Clara College; later Santa Clara University)
items.description: Located in Santa Clara, California. Founded in 1851 as Santa Clara College. Became University of Santa Clara in 1912 and Santa Clara University in 1985.

items.title: West Valley College
items.description: Founded in 1963 in Campbell, California. Later moved to Saratoga, California.

sectors.name: Education and research — Science and mathematics

items.title: A partial list of seed plants of the North Coast Ranges of California, 1929-1972
items.description: The lists name some 2,717 species collected between Sonoma and the Oregon border.

items.title: Armin Dale Kaiser papers, circa 1956-1982
items.description: Armin Dale Kaiser (1927-2020) was a professor of Biochemistry at Stanford University, 1959-1982. He was among the first to investigate the quantitative genetics of bacterial viruses. Correspondence, 1966-1972; research notebooks, 1956-ca. 1980; and faculty notebooks, 1979-1982.

items.title: Arthur Kornberg papers, 1938-2007
items.description: With a research career spanning more than sixty years, Arthur Kornberg made many outstanding contributions to molecular biology. Collection documents Kornberg's work concerning the synthesis of DNA in the laboratory, as well as the synthetic pathways of nucleotides, and includes correspondence, 1947 to 1982; research lab notebooks, 1947 to 1969 (which include those studies for which he received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1959); coursework, lectures, and seminars; Stanford University Departmental records; records concerning professional organizations; and reprints, glass research slides, and audiotapes.

items.title: Benjamin M. Page papers, 1929-1996
items.description: Geologist. Page's special fields are structural geology and the relationship between geological structures and plate tectonics. Papers include correspondence, minutes, budgets, class notes, course files, student papers, reports, maps, and research files and pertain to his activities as professor, department administrator, and scientist.

items.title: C.B. Niel papers, 1923-1977
items.description: The van Niel papers primarily document C. B. van Niel's career at the Hopkins Marine Station of Stanford University, his participation in preeminent scientific associations, and his role as a leader in the field of microbiology. The papers include ATCC documents, teaching materials, research notes, publications, correspondences, photographs, audiotapes, and medals.

items.title: Carl Djerassi papers, 1952-2006 (inclusive)
items.description: University research scientist and industrialist, Djerassi is most famous for synthesizing the first oral contraceptive. These papers primarily concern Djerassi's research in organic chemistry and include correspondence, reports, and lab notebooks on optical rotary dispersion and mass spectrometry; other research files containing correspondence, manuscripts, and reprints; reprints of Djerassi's published articles; and grant files.

items.title: Cecil H. Green oral history interview transcript, 1995
items.description: Green was a British-born American geophysicist who trained at the University of British Columbia and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He was a founder of Texas Instruments. Interview conducted by Dr. Ronald E. Doel for the Niels Bohr Library of the American Institute of Physics.
items.era_note: [About half of this 1995 interview, his account of his career in geophysics and as a founder of Texas Instruments, concerns this period.]

items.title: Charles Stacy French papers, 1935-1989
items.description: French, plant physiologist, was director of the Dept. of Plant Biology of the Carnegie Institution, located on the Stanford University campus, from 1947 until his retirement in 1973. Papers include correspondence, articles, speeches, manuscripts, lab notes, charts, and computer printouts pertaining largely to his research interests in the photosynthesis of purple bacteria, spectroscopy of plant pigments, and the construction of spectroscopic equipment.

items.title: Chemist and administrator at UC Berkeley, Rice University, Stanford University, and the Atomic Energy Commission, 1935-1997 : oral history transcript, 1999
items.description: Interviews of Pitzer by Sally Smith Hughes and Germaine LaBerge conducted in 1996, 1997, and 1998.

items.title: Classical electricity and magnetism, 1949
items.description: Lectures, as covered in 33 chapters. Edited by Roger Wallace and Howard Chang.

items.title: Donald Leland Carpenter papers, 1959-1993
items.description: Donald Leland Carpenter was a Professor of Electrical Engineering, Emeritus at Stanford University. His research primarly focused on Very Low Frequency Radio Propogation and Solar Terrestrial Physics. This collection consists of planning notes for Carpenter's studies in Antartica, technical reports, and journal articles.

items.title: Douglas Merritt Whitaker papers, 1926-1963
items.description: Professor of Biology at Stanford (1931-1955); Dean of the School of Biological Sciences (1946-1949); Dean of Graduate Studies (1948-1951); Dean of Humanities and Sciences (1951-1952). Papers include articles, speeches, slides used in lecture on evolution, some correspondence and lecture notes, and material on the Bikini atom bomb tests.

items.title: Ecological study of San Francisquito Creek : typescript, 1968 Sept
items.description: Part of "Resources and Ecology Projects" sponsored by the City of Menlo Park, California.

items.title: Esther M. Lederberg papers, 1906-1998 (inclusive), 1937-1998 (bulk)
items.description: Esther Miriam Zimmer Lederberg, PhD, professor emeritus of microbiology and immunology at the Stanford University School of Medicine, earned her AB at Hunter College in 1942. Collection includes class notes and lab notebooks from her education at Hunter College, 1939-42, Stanford University, 1944-46, and the University of Wisconsin, 1948-50; notes and lab notebooks from subsequent research, primarily with plasmids, 1950 on; records from the Plasmid Reference Center; correspondence; articles and reprints; photographs both professional and personal; family documents; and other materials.

items.title: Gabor Szego papers
items.description: Professor of Mathematics at Stanford University and chairman of the department from 1938 to 1958. Professional and personal correspondence, ephemera, manuscripts, photographs, technical reports and publications, ca. 1910 to 1980.

items.title: Geology of area east of Page Mill Road
items.description: Submitted to the Department of Geology. Student Report--Stanford University, 1942.

items.title: Geology of the Alum Rock Canyon sector, Diablo Range, California
items.description: Student Report--Stanford University, 194-. Submitted to the Department of Geology.

items.title: Geology southeast of Page Mill Road, Palo Alto quadrangle
items.description: Student Report--Stanford University, 194-. Submitted to the Department of Geology.

items.title: George Polya papers, 1884-1985
items.description: Hungarian mathematician George Pólya was educated at the University of Budapest and the University of Paris, and taught at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich from 1914 to 1940. Papers relate to Pólya's research and teaching in mathematics and include professional and personal correspondence with mathematicians worldwide, 1910-1984; course materials including lecture notes; mathematical research notebooks dating from 1917 to 1960; manuscripts including those from his published works Complex Variables , How to Solve It , Mathematical Discovery , and Mathematics and Plausible Reasoning ; ephemera; reprints; and photographs.

items.title: Harry S. Mosher papers, 1944-2000
items.description: During his career at Stanford, Mosher taught organic chemistry and conducted research in a wide range of areas, including natural products chemistry and stereochemistry. Papers include correspondence, manuscripts and reprints, research files, lab notebooks, grant files, and class materials.

items.title: Ingram Olkin papers, 1875-2014, bulk 1950-2014
items.description: Ingram Olkin is best known for developing statistical analyses for evaluating policies, particularly in education. One year later, he moved permanently to Stanford University, where he held a joint appointment with the Department of Statistics and the Graduate School of Education.

items.title: Interview with Arthur Kornberg [videorecording]
items.description: Biochemistry professor at Stanford University (Chairman of the Department of Biochemistry from 1959 to 1969), Kornberg received a Nobel Prize in medicine and physiology in 1959 for pioneering the synthesis of DNA in the laboratory. This interview was conducted by Robert Lehman for the Alpha Omega Alpha Honor Medical Society; collection includes the source tapes (on Beta and VHS) and the edited master tape.
items.era_note: [About half of this interview, with a biochemist whose Nobel Prize of 1959 and department chairmanship of 1959 to 1969 fall in these years, concerns this period.]

items.title: James Murray Luck papers, 1930-1979
items.description: Professor of biochemistry at Stanford (1926-1965; emeritus, 1965- ). Primarily correspondence and subject files relating to Professor Luck's professional activities, the Stanford Chemistry Department and his position as acting Science Attaché at the United States embassies in London, Stockholm and Bern.

items.title: Jens Clausen field notebooks, 1928-1962
items.description: Primarily herbarium specimen collection notes, arranged by number and date.

items.title: John C. Lilly papers, 1933-2012
items.description: John Cunningham Lilly (1915-2001) was a physiologist, biologist, and medical doctor known for his work with dolphins and interspecies communication, as well as research on the brain and consciousness which resulted in his invention of the isolation tank. The John C. Lilly papers contain a variety of material from over fifty years of his research in marine biology, neuroscience, and related fields.

items.title: John E. Cox papers, 1940-1999
items.description: This collection includes photographs, lab notebooks, and a printed copy of an article. The notebooks, one pharmacology laboratory notebook (1942) and two biochemistry laboratory notebooks (1940-1941), date from his time at Stanford School of Medicine.

items.title: John George Herriot papers, 1937-1992
items.description: He served as the first director of the Stanford Computation Center, 1953-61, taught the first programming course at Stanford in 1955, and helped found the computer science department at Stanford in 1965. These papers document his career as a mathematician and include his notes taken while a student at Brown University, 1937-41, and his master's and doctoral theses, 1940-41; research files (notes, computations, articles, computer printouts, some correspondence, and other materials) on Fourier series, Schlicht functions, spline theory, and other topics, 1940-83; memos, minutes, correspondence, and other records pertaining to Stanford's Dept. of Computer Sciences and the Stanford Computation Center, 1946-92; correspondence, notes, and reports pertaining to his Fulbright year, 1962-63; and bibliographic and biographical materials.

items.title: John Warvelle Harbaugh, "Memoirs"
items.description: John Warvelle Harbaugh (1926-2019) was an American geologist and Professor Emeritus in the Geological and Environmental Sciences Department and at the Energy Resources Engineering Department at Stanford University. Contains a memoir of John W. Harbaugh documenting his personal and professional history, including genealogical backgrounds, family member's lives, his service in WWII, academic achievements, and work at Stanford University.
items.era_note: [About two-fifths of this memoir, on his wartime service, education and early work at Stanford, concerns this period.]

items.title: Martin Gardner papers, 1957-1986
items.description: Martin Gardner was the Mathematical Games columnist for SCIENTIFIC AMERICAN from its inception in 1956 until 1986. These papers pertain to his interest in mathematics and consist of files relating to his SCIENTIFIC AMERICAN mathematical games column (1957-1986) and subject files on recreational mathematics. Papers include correspondence, notes, clippings, and articles, with some examples of puzzle toys.

items.title: Paul R. Ehrlich papers, 1954-2001
items.description: Ehrlich was an evolutionary and population biologist who gained worldwide attention for his 1968 book, The Population Bomb , which predicted dire consequences due to the rapidly increasing human population and advocated population control. Correspondence, memos, notes, photographs, posters and other papers relating to Paul Ehrlich's publications and public appearances, his work with the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory, Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve, the Zero Population Growth organization, and the Stanford Biological Sciences Department.

items.title: Peter A. Sturrock papers, 1952-2020
items.description: Peter Andrew Sturrock is an emeritus professor of applied physics at Stanford University. This collection consists of correspondence, research and teaching files, grant proposals, and reports.

items.title: Pierre Van Rysselberghe papers, 1932-1973
items.description: Pierre van Rysselberghe, a chemist and chemical engineer, earned his masters (1928) and doctorate (1929) at Stanford University. He taught at the University of Oregon and at Stanford. Papers include correspondence, class materials, articles and reprints, lab notes, and other materials pertaining to his research and his teaching career.

items.title: Richard H. Jahns papers, circa 1916-1983
items.description: Professor of Geology and Applied Sciences and Dean of the School of Earth Sciences at Stanford University, 1965-1983. Correspondence, memoranda, reports, and articles. The Jahns papers reflect the breadth of his research and teaching interests, from glacial deposits to seismic hazards.

items.title: Robert Arthur Helliwell papers, 1950-1999
items.description: In 1946, he joined the faculty in Stanford's Department of Electrical Engineering. Helliwell's research on whistlers led to many prominent journal articles and technical reports on the subject. This collection primarily consists of Helliwell's lab notebooks, journal articles, and technical reports.

items.title: Robert Hofstadter papers, 1931-1993
items.description: This collection contains the papers of former Stanford professor and Nobel Prize winning physicist Robert Hofstadter. Of particular note are materials on the development of the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center (SLAC), later renamed the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, as well as correspondence on the relationship between SLAC and the Stanford University Department of Phyiscs.

items.title: Ronald Bracewell papers, 1958-2007
items.description: Ronald Newbold Bracewell (July 22, 1921 – August 12, 2007) was the Lewis M. Terman Professor of Electrical Engineering, Emeritus of the Space, Telecommunications and Radioscience Laboratory at Stanford University. In 1998 Dr. Bracewell was named Officer of the Order of Australia (AO) for service to science in the fields of radio astronomy and image reconstruction.

items.title: Stanford booklets
items.description: Booklet contains text on the proposed linear accelerator project at Stanford, text on the academic program at Stanford, and photographs.

items.title: Stanford: I. Its two-mile-long atom smasher II. A university on the march; June 1959
items.description: Booklet contains text on the proposed linear accelerator project at Stanford, text on the academic program at Stanford, and photographs.

items.title: Stephen Jay Gould papers, 1899-2004 (inclusive), 1941-2002 (bulk)
items.description: This collection documents the life of noted American paleontologist, evolutionary biologist, and historian of science, Stephen Jay Gould. The papers include correspondence, juvenilia, manuscripts, subject files, teaching files, photographs, audiovisual materials, and personal and biographical materials created and compiled by Gould.

items.title: Telford H. Work notebook
items.description: Telford H. Work earned his A.B. in biological sciences at Stanford University in 1942 and his M.D. in 1946. Notes on a trip to collect eggs from eagle nests near the Calaveras reservoir, April 1942.

items.title: Willard J. Classen miscellaneous papers, 1955-1991
items.description: This collection contains a reprint of an article by Classen and Joseph J. Graham, "A Lower Eocene Foraminiferal Faunule from the Woodside Area, San Mateo County, California," 1955, with the original illustrations; a letter from Rixford K. Snyder talking about Greystone Quarry, the source of the sandstone used in building the first buildings at Stanford, 1991; and a short article by Classen on the Stanford University seal.

items.title: Willard J. Classen papers
items.description: Willard's long career began as a geologist with Standard Oil Co. of California. This collection contains a reprint of an article by Classen and Joseph J. Graham, "A Lower Eocene Foraminiferal Faunule from the Woodside Area, San Mateo County, California," 1955, with the original illustrations; a letter from Rixford K. Snyder talking about Greystone Quarry, the source of the sandstone used in building the first buildings at Stanford, 1991; and a short article by Classen on the Stanford University seal.

items.title: William M. Fairbank papers, 1961-1989
items.description: William M. Fairbank (1917-1989) was a physics professor at Stanford University. His research interests included superconductivity, gravity waves, individual quarks and monopoles. Materials include correspondence, notes, talks, articles, graphs, charts, articles, reports, research proposals, lab notebooks, and photographs.

items.title: William S. Johnson papers, 1940-1992
items.description: Johnson, professor of chemistry at Stanford University, was generally regarded as one of the major figures in 20th-century organic chemistry. Papers document his teaching and research activities and include notebooks, research reports, subject files, correspondence, grant files, reprints, and slides.

sectors.name: Education and research — Social sciences and humanities

items.title: Albert Léon Guérard papers addenda, 1908-1960
items.description: He taught at Stanford University from 1907 until his retirement in 1946, except for 12 years between 1913-1935 when he was at Rice University and served in the war. He was the author of numerous books and articles on French history and intellectual life. Materials include works on the history and culture of France, correspondence and writings on urban planning in France and in the San Francisco Bay Area, and book reviews.

items.title: Doris H. Linder papers, 1900-2008
items.description: Linder was Professor of History at the College of San Mateo for over forty years, teaching world history and women's studies courses. Doris Linder's papers includes research and teaching files and notes, drafts and correspondence related to her published research, travel and country files, family and personal correspondence and ephemera, slides, and published material.

items.title: Lewis Madison Terman papers, 1910-1992
items.description: He returned to Stanford in 1919 as a professor of psychology and taught until 1943, when he was appointed professor emeritus, a position he held until his death in 1956. In 1919 he began his study of gifted children, which he published in The Genetic Studies of Genius, Vol. I, II, and II. Terman's papers include correspondence and data for his study of the gifted; professional correspondence with colleagues; and correspondence and data on tests and testing: Army Alpha and Beta tests, Stanford revision of the Binet-Simon Intelligence scale, Stanford Achievement Test, Terman McNemar Test of Mental Ability, Terman Group Test, Attitude-Interest Analysis Tests, and Male Female Tests.

items.title: Lois Meek Stolz psychology case interviews, 1957-1958
items.description: In 1947, she came to Stanford as a professor of psychology and started the doctoral program in child development in the School of Education. Transcripts of interviews and summary files from interviews with 41 sets of parents from the Palo Alto area regarding their children and their child rearing practices. The information gathered in this study was used in her book INFLUENCES ON PARENT BEHAVIOR (1967).

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford history and ceremonial life

items.title: "Becoming Stanford: The Making of an American University" [videorecording]
items.description: Part 1, "The Founding," covers the origins and building of the university through World War I; highlights include Stanford family history, the first Big Game between Stanford and UC Berkeley, early student life, the rise of tenure, and the 1906 earthquake. Part 2, "The Transformation," covers the development of Stanford as a world-renowned research university; highlights include the administrations of Provost Frederick E. Terman and President J. E. Wallace Sterling, the role of federal funding in the university's expansion, the turmoil of the 1960s, and the growth of new technologies leading to the personal computer revolution.
items.era_note: [About half of this documentary, its second part on Stanford's growth into a research university under Terman and Sterling, concerns this period.]

items.title: Charles Babbage Institute Oral History collection, 1979-1991
items.description: Founded in 1978, the Charles Babbage Institute is the University of Minnesota's research center for advancing the understanding of computing, information, and culture. This collection contains transcripts of oral history interviews selected for their relevance to the history of computer science at Stanford, including the development of the computer science department and Stanford's Artificial Intelligence Laboratory.
items.era_note: [Most of these interviews, recorded 1979-1991, concern the founding of Stanford's computer science department and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory in the 1960s.]

items.title: Franklin Chiang Photographs, circa 1966-1972
