items.description: In the early 1960s, Chiang became an avid photographer, taking photographs of scenes in Stanford University, Palo Alto, and San Francisco. Photographic negatives and digital scans of photographs taken by Franklin Chiang. Negatives consist of images taken of Stanford University.

items.title: Halsey L. Royden, "The History of the Stanford Mathematics Department"
items.description: Halsey L. Royden earned his B.S. in 1948 and his M.S. in 1949 at Stanford University and his Ph.D. at Harvard in 1951, after which he returned to Stanford to join the faculty in the department of mathematics. Covers the early years (1891-1924), the Blichfeldt era (1925-1938), the Szego period (1938-1949), and the 1950s-60s.
items.era_note: [About half of this history, on the Szego period of 1938 to 1949 and the department in the 1950s and 1960s, concerns this period.]

items.title: Jack Fields photograph collection, 1960
items.description: Professional photographer. Photographs taken on commission in September 1960 regarding Stanford University, used to illustrate a feature article in SATURDAY EVENING POST, 13 December 1960. The collection includes scenes of campus life, views of activities at the Medical School and at the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center, of University president J. E. Wallace Sterling and his family, of faculty and students.

items.title: Patrick Suppes : an interview conducted by David W. Mitchell : transcript, 2007
items.description: Oral history interview conducted in May 2007. Topics include his activities with Dr. Fred Terman; Stanford’s development into a major research university; his interests in logic, computers, learning theory and brain function; and the teaching of math.
items.era_note: [Most of this 2007 interview, on work with Frederick Terman and Stanford's growth into a research university, concerns this period.]

items.title: Rixford Kinney Snyder, "Memories of a Santa Clara Valley Boy Who Never Left, 1908-1991" typescript
items.description: Rixford Kinney Snyder, Professor of History, Dean of Admissions, and first Director of the Alumni Association's Travel/Study Program. In 1950, Snyder was appointed Director of Admissions, by President J.E. Wallace Sterling, beginning a nineteen‐year tenure as director and eventually dean, when the university elevated the post. Original and revised version of Rixford's autobiography.

items.title: SRI: the founding years : videorecording, 1983
items.description: Weldon B. Gibson, who earned his MBA in 1940 and his PhD in 1950 from Stanford University, was one of the first fellows at the Stanford Research Institute and its Senior Director in the 1980's. Interview with Weldon B. Gibson concerning the Graduate School of Business at Stanford University, its dean Ernest C. Arbuckle, other Stanford faculty, collegiate athletics, and the Stanford Research Institute.
items.era_note: [Most of this 1983 interview, on the Graduate School of Business and the early years of the Stanford Research Institute, concerns this period.]

items.title: Stanford Historical Photograph collection, 1887-circa 1996
items.description: The Stanford Photograph Collection contains over 16,000 images of Stanford scenes including photographs of and relating to the Stanford family, views of the campus and individual buildings, photographs of students and student life activities, and photographs of faculty and administrative staff.

items.title: Stanford Historical Society oral history program interviews
items.description: The Stanford Historical Society's Oral History Program explores the institutional history of the University, with an emphasis on the transformative post-WWII period, through interviews with leading faculty, staff, alumni, trustees, and others.
items.era_note: [About a third of these interviews, recollections of Stanford's transformation after the Second World War, concern this period.]

items.title: Stanford News Service records 1931-2023
items.description: The News Service reports and disseminates much of the University's news, via the STANFORD REPORT daily news email. Records include subject files compiled by the News Service in the course of its work, news releases prepared by the News Service, proof sheets of photographs produced by the News Service photographers, taped interviews, office files of the Director of News and Publications Service and of the directors of the individual units, news clippings, and miscellaneous photographic and printed material.

items.title: Stanford Speech Collection
items.description: The Stanford Speech Collection consists of audio recordings on open reel tape of speeches, lectures, interviews and panel discussions at or sponsored by Stanford University from the 1950s through the early 70s. A wide variety of disciplines are represented in the speeches, including English literature, economics, political science, biology, religion, education, history, and foreign policy.

items.title: Stanford Tape Collection
items.description: The Stanford Tape Collection consists of historic music and speech recordings made on the campus of Stanford University. Many were used in the production of broadcasts by university radio station KZSU.

items.title: Stanford University biographical files collection, circa 1891-2011
items.description: The collection contains biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford University.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Records, 1950-2008
items.description: This collection consists of 50th anniversary celebration materials from 2008 and research figures and diagrams from 1950. While the current Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics was structured in 1958, it's previously entitled the Department of Aeronautical Engineering, a department that was formed in 1927 with funding from the Guggenheim Foundation.

items.title: The living legends: a discussion about the establishment of the Computer Science Department at Stanford University : videorecording, 1997
items.description: A discussion amongst John McCarthy, Edward Feigenbaum, Robert W. Floyd, Donald Knuth, Gene Golub, Gio Wiederhold, John G. Herriot, and William F. Miller on the history of computer science at Stanford, recorded on March 22, 1997 by Andy Kacsman.
items.era_note: [Most of this discussion, recollections by its founders of how Stanford's computer science department was established, concerns this period.]

items.title: Williamson M. Evers papers
items.description: Williamson M. Evers is an American libertarian and member of the Libertarian Party National Committee. He was a former research fellow at the Hoover Institution where he specialized in research on education policy. The collection consists primarily of newspaper clippings and correspondence on various topics, such as student housing, land development, ROTC, and the Hoover Institution. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford University

items.title: Herbert Hoover Stanford fund-raising letters
items.description: These two letters, addressed to Mrs. Lynn Smith Abbott (who attended Stanford from 1893-94), pertain to the Stanford Futures campaign to raise money for scholarships.

items.title: Herbert Hoover typed letter signed to Harry Chandler, 1942 Aug. 27
items.description: Hoover, president of Stanford University at this time, sends his thanks for Chandler's service on the Board of Trustees, and expresses the sentiment that Mrs. Roger Gordan (May), his replacement, was elected not only for her "splendid qualities, but out of ... respect to you..."

items.title: Hugh Hildreth Skilling papers, 1954-1964
items.description: Hugh H. Skilling was professor of electrical engineering at Stanford (1928-1929, 1931-1971; emeritus 1971-1990) and served as head of the Department of Electrical Engineering from 1944 to 1967. Collection includes correspondence, memoranda, goal statements, agendas, and notes pertaining to the University's Study of Undergraduate Education (1954-1956) and to the Electrical Engineering Department's Undergraduate and Graduate Administration Committees (1961-1964).

items.title: Kenneth M. Cuthbertson papers, 1941-1990
items.description: Cuthbertson was named one of the university's first three vice presidents in 1960. The papers, which include correspondence, minutes, reports, and memoranda, pertain largely to administration, finance, and planning at Stanford University.

items.title: Kenneth S. Pitzer, President of Stanford University, papers, circa 1968-1970 (inclusive)
items.description: Sixth president of Stanford University, December 1968 to September 1, 1970. The materials consist of inauguration materials, administrative records, records concerning gifts, subject files, speeches, and organizational records, including those of Stanford Research Institute and the American Associations of Universities.

items.title: Richard W. Lyman, Provost of Stanford University, papers, 1959-1972
items.description: Lyman, who served as president from 1970 to 1980, held many posts during the 25 years he spent at Stanford: history professor, associate dean of the School of Humanities and Sciences, provost, president, and founder and director of the center now known as the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies. These are the office files of Richard W. Lyman during his term of Provost from November 22, 1966 to September 24, 1970. Consists primarily of general correspondence files and files pertaining to the Schools and to Committees.

items.title: Robert Averill Walker papers, 1950-1995
items.description: Robert A. Walker was professor of political science at Stanford University from 1949 until his retirement in 1976. Papers pertain largely to his administrative duties at Stanford University and include correspondence, minutes, agenda, memoranda, and reports; subjects include the overseas studies program, the political science department, international studies, curriculum reviews, and faculty/staff housing on campus.

items.title: Sennet W. Gilfillan correspondence with Stanford University
items.description: Gilfillan, Stanford Class of 1912, was an electronics manufacturer and developer of an airport radar landing system. Correspondence with Frederick E. Terman and David S. Jacobson regarding Gilfillan's contributions to scholarships for electrical engineering students and the Gilfillan Wing of the Electronics Laboratory; some of Terman's letters concern faculty and research projects of the department.

items.title: Stanford Computation Center photographs, circa 1968-1972
items.description: 42 photographs of the Stanford Computation Center created by Elizabeth Westlake.

items.title: Stanford Construction Institute correspondence
items.description: The Stanford Construction Institute was a graduate level construction engineering and management program. Includes correspondence with Prof. Clark Oglesby, Engineering Dean Lauress L. Wise, and Pres. J. E. Wallace Sterling pertaining largely to the company's financial support of the School of Engineering and the Stanford Construction Institute, with occasional mention of its programs; copy of an article on the program from THE CONSTRUCTOR, December 1961; and a copy of the "Plan for a Construction Institute at Stanford University" produced by the Dept. of Civil Engineering, April 1960.

items.title: Stanford University, ACME Project, records, 1961-1973
items.description: Collection consists of files relating to the ACME (Advanced Computer Medical Experiments) Project at Stanford, use of computers, and the establishment of a computer center at Stanford. Included are correspondence (including some by Gio Wiederhold), committee records, budget materials, grant files, and publications.

items.title: Stanford University, Assistant to the President for Black Affairs, records
items.description: In 1968, Stanford University created the new office of Assistant Provost for Minority Affairs, naming James E. Simmons to the post; in 1969, Mr. Simmon's title was changed to Assistant to the President for Black Affairs. The records of the office of James E. Simmons under its several titles includes correspondence, memoranda, reports, general material on black affairs at Stanford and some additional files on Native American students.

items.title: Stanford University, Associate Provost for Computing, records, 1968-1971
items.description: William F. Miller (1925-1917), who earned three degrees in physics from Purdue University (B.S. 1949, M.S. 1951, Ph.D. 1956), joined Stanford in 1965 as a professor of computer science. The records in this collection are the office files of Miller as Associate Provost for Computing (1968-70) and Vice President for Research (1970-71). Includes correspondence, memoranda, and proposals; subjects include SPIRES/BALLOTS, research policy, government agencies and research, computer science department, electrical engineering department, and health delivery systems.

items.title: Stanford University, Board of Trustees, records
items.description: The Board administers the invested funds, sets the annual budget, and determines policies for the operation and control of the University. Records of the Trustees pertaining to legal issues, financial affairs, investments, academic departments, student housing, gifts received, real estate, campus development, and other administrative concerns.

items.title: Stanford University, Career Planning and Placement Center, records
items.description: Established in 1952 as the Stanford Placement Service, the office changed its name and concentration to Career Planning and Placement Center in 1965. A sampling of placement files arranged alphabetically by student (including resumes and other placement information) for each year the office has been in operation between 1952 and 1975.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Physics, records, 1905-2025 (inclusive), 1960-1994 (bulk)
items.description: Collection includes minutes of faculty meetings (1905-1948), administrative files, budget and financial records, grant files, technical reports, correspondence, and other materials. Also of note are files pertaining to the recruitment of minority students and women students and files on the Mexican-American Program: Stanford Summer Program of Mexican-American High School Students (mid-1960s).

items.title: Stanford University, Electron Microscope Committee, minutes
items.description: Minutes discuss location of the microscope and its assembly, requests to hire research associate, financial accounts, creation of an academic division, rules of operation, reports on experimental use, and other matters.

items.title: Stanford University, Faculty Senate, records, 1891-2026(inclusive)
items.description: The Academic Council was organized by the Stanford University faculty in 1904 and currently consists of members of the Professoriate and certain officers of the academic administration as specified by the Articles of Organization. In 1968 the Academic Council created the Senate of the Academic Council, composed of representatives elected from the Council. They include minutes, memoranda, correspondence, reports, election records, agendas and supporting documents, rosters, memorial resolutions on deceased members, and audiotapes of meetings.

items.title: Stanford University, Food Research Institute, records, 1916-1990
items.description: The Food Research Institute at Stanford was founded in 1921 for the study of worldwide problems of food supply, distribution, and consumption. Records include correspondence of William O. Jones and others, 1960s-80s; grant files; departmental files, 1920s-70s; funding records; photographs; and other materials, including two passports of Alonzo E. Taylor, 1916-17.

items.title: Stanford University, Office of Vice President for Business and Finance, records, 1949-1985
items.description: Files, 1960-1967, which include correspondence, notes, memos and reports dealing with the Ford Foundation, the Plan of Action for a Challenging Era (PACE), Palo Alto-Stanford Hospital Center and the Stanford Children's Convalescent Hospital; and correspondence and patents, 1949-1959, pertaining to various electronic inventions; and the records of Rodney Adams, Director of Finance and Treasurer, 1976-85, pertaining to endowment funds, research and consulting, and administrative matters.

items.title: Stanford University, President's Office, Sterling - Pitzer transitional records, 1946-1970 (inclusive), 1964-1970 (bulk)
items.description: These records were generated during the tenure of President Kenneth Pitzer as well as his predecessor J. E. Wallace Sterling. Included are files on committees, academic and administrative departments, and the Stanford Research Institute, as well as general administrative files.

items.title: Stanford University, Public Affairs Office, records, 1960-1980
items.description: The University Relations Office acted as liaison between the University and the public. The collection consists of correspondence, memoranda, press releases, photographs, maps, and other documents concerning various events and controversies dealt with by the Public Affairs Office, 1960-1980. Subjects include the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center, Stanford Industrial Park, Ladera Dam and flood control on the San Francisquito Creek, Stanford in Britain overseas campus, dismissal of H. Bruce Franklin, ROTC on campus, the Winds of Freedom Foundation, and the inauguration of university president Kenneth S. Pitzer.

items.title: Stanford University, School of Engineering, Dean's Office records, 1915-1998 (inclusive), 1925-1955 (bulk)
items.description: In 1925, the formerly independent engineering departments were organized into the School of Engineering with Theodore Jesse Hoover as Dean. The collection consists of general office files from the School of Engineering Dean's Office. Included are subject files regarding school and departmental affairs as well as interests of the individual deans; files regarding teaching appointments of non-tenured assistants, lecturers, instructors, assistant professors and visiting faculty; annual budget files (1925-1960) and annual reports to the President (1945-1964) regarding school and departmental activites, goals, faculty achievement and funding.

items.title: Stanford University, Special Services Office, records
items.description: These six boxes contain mainly office correspondence and informative material pertaining to the draft and draft counseling. Also included are 5 volumes of computer printouts of statistical analyses concerning Stanford students and their draft classifications.

items.title: Stanford University, Sponsored Projects Office, records, 1935-1995
items.description: Records from the Sponsored Projects Office pertain to administrative matters and to individual projects; included are correspondence, memoranda, reports, minutes, patent files, and financial records. Specific topics include the Solar Energy Research Institute, 1976-77; the BALLOTS project, 1975; the NIRT project; the Te Vega research ship; the Stanford Electronics Laboratory; the San Joaquin Basin Analysis Project; indirect cost recovery; the Committee on Research; and the Committee on Government Relations.

items.title: Stanford University, University Services, records, 1936-1957
items.description: The University Services office of Stanford University (1942-1954) was established to carry out a program of service on a contractual basis, focusing on the region, the nation, international studies, and business and industry. Correspondence, with some reports, minutes, and pamphlets, relating to the activities of the University Services Office.

items.title: Stanford University, Vice President for Business Affairs, records
items.description: The collection includes minutes, reports, correspondence, leases, proposals, and other records pertaining to financial and business aspects of the administration of Stanford University. Among the subjects covered by the records are property matters, land development, building projects on campus, academic departments and professional schools, faculty and student housing, the hospital and medical center, SLAC, shopping center, industrial park, Jasper Ridge, relations with Palo Alto, roads, and water.

items.title: Stanford-SRI Study Committee records, 1954-1969 (inclusive), 1968-1969 (bulk)
items.description: The Stanford-SRI Study Committee was appointed by the Stanford University president in October 1968 "to explore in detail the relationships between Stanford University and the Stanford Research Institute (SRI)." Collection includes correspondence and memoranda, 1965, 1968-69; completed questionnaires sent to faculty members, 1969; background materials (correspondence, memoranda, reports, articles) 1954-69; and the final report of the Committee, 1969.

items.title: Study and Evaluation of the Status of University Programs...in Computers, Data-processing and Related Fields, report
items.description: Report of a study undertaken at the request of Dr. Albert H. Bowker, head of the Stanford University Statistics Department, with recommendations for building a program at Stanford University.

items.title: William R. Rambo papers, 1939-1992 (inclusive), 1954-1974 (bulk)
items.description: He was made a Professor of Electrical Engineering in 1957, Director of Electronics Labs in 1960, and Associate Dean of the School of Engineering in 1961. These papers, kept in their original arrangement, reflect Prof. Rambo's administrative responsibilities as well as his research interests, largely during his time at Stanford University. Stanford subjects include the School of Engineering, the Electrical Engineering Department, the Stanford Electronic Labs, the Applied Electronics Lab, research policy at Stanford, courses, the Academic Senate, the University Land and Building Development Committee, and student demonstrations.

sectors.name: Education and research

items.title: Gene Golub papers, 1950-2007
items.description: Gene Golub (1932-2007) was a Professor of Computer Science at Stanford University. Gene was a leading pioneer in the field of numerical analysis, creating algorithms and software that allowed researchers to run large engineering and science calculations effectively on computers. This collection is comprised of Professor Golub's professional records and includes notebooks on his research for his publications, lecture notes, articles, manuscripts, grant files, bibliographic materials on contemporaries, and correspondence.

items.title: George B. Dantzig papers, 1934-2005
items.description: George Bernard Dantzig (November 8, 1914 – May 13, 2005) was an American mathematical scientist who made important contributions to operations research, computer science, economics, and statistics. Dantzig was the Professor Emeritus of Transportation Sciences and Professor of Operations Research and of Computer Science at Stanford.

items.title: Lydik S. Jacobsen papers
items.description: Professor Lydik S. Jacobsen (1897-1976) began his teaching career at Stanford in 1924. He headed the Mechanical Engineering Department, 1940-1943, and directed the Earthquake Research Laboratory, 1926-1943 and 1946-1962. Miscellaneous correspondence and other papers relating to Professor Jacobsen's research interests in seismology and structural dynamics.

items.title: Merrill S. Hugo papers, 1901-1960, 1941-1960
items.description: Hugo, a 1924 engineering graduate of Stanford and a Major with the United States Army Ordnance Department, joined the Stanford faculty in 1930 and served as director of the Gage Laboratory, School of Engineering. The materials consist of records the Gage Laboratory and the Stanford School of Engineering. Included are correspondence, research notes, procedural manuals, tolerance tables, technical reports, blueprints , schematics, transparencies, and diagrams.

items.title: On Choosing Combinations of Weapons
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Physics Division, Stanford Research Institute; a finite difference, 1950-1969 : a short history / by Phyllis F. Dorset and Stephen W. Miller
items.description: An illustrated history of the SRI Physics Division of Stanford Research Institute (now SRI International).

items.title: Stanford Research Institute records, 1947-1966
items.description: The Stanford Research Institute was organized in 1946 as an applied research center for industry and government. Collection consists primarily of minutes of the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee, with some reports, financial statements, correspondence, memoranda, articles and brochures.

items.title: Stanford University technical reports, 1956-1970
items.description: Archival copies of technical reports resulting from sponsored research at Stanford.

items.title: Stanford University, Stanford Electronics Laboratories, records, 1948-1990
items.description: Stanford Electronics Laboratories technical reports, electronics research reviews, and research notebooks, including three volumes on early traveling wave tube research.

items.title: Success Story: Stanford University electronics and research lab : videorecording, 1990
items.description: Video copy of a 1954 film produced by Caryl Coleman about electronics research at Stanford University. Persons appearing in the film include Donald B. Harris, Russell H. Varian, Frederick E. Terman, William R. Hewlett, David Packard, and Marvin Chodorow.
items.era_note: [All of this video, a copy of a 1954 film about electronics research at Stanford, concerns this period.]

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Art, music, literature and photography

items.title: Ann Rosener papers, circa 1900-2013
items.description: The collection contains correspondence, photographs, posters, exhibit catalogs, subject files, drafts, and business records documenting Ann Rosener's career as a photographer, designer, and publisher. It includes photographs from her work for the Office of War Information, portraits of artists such as William Brice and Rico Lebrun, and photographs of family, friends, and travels.

items.title: Ansel Adams' Portfolio Four papers 1987
items.description: A keepsake including photocopied letters to sons Leonard and David, ca. 1978, and Virginia Adams, 1984, all concerning the relationship of Ansel Adams and Russell Varian and the resulting portfolio created in 1963 by Adams to benefit Castle Rock State Park and honor Russel Varian.
items.era_note: [This 1987 keepsake of letters recalls the friendship of Ansel Adams and Russell Varian and the portfolio Adams made in 1963 in his honour.]

items.title: Bruce Bliven papers, 1906-1985
items.description: Upon Herbert Croly's demise, Bliven succeeded as editor of New Republic. Continuing his freelance literary career, Bliven completed several works, including Five Million Words Later, his autobiography, and A Mirror for Greatness a biography of six famous Americans. Correspondence, notes, printed materials, photographs, and clippings covering Bliven's journalistic and literary careers.

items.title: David V. Harris papers, circa 1950s-2020s.
items.description: The collection covers the writing career and anti-Vietnam War activism of author and former Stanford student David V. Harris, spanning from the 1950s through the 2020s. The majority of the collection is made up of Harris' research files and notes from his non-fiction books.

items.title: Gerd Stern papers, 1938-2012
items.description: Gerd Stern is a poet, artist, and multimedia innovator whose remarkable life spans 40s bohemia, 50s Beat culture, 60s hippiedom, 70s hip capitalism, and onward. This collection is primarily correspondence, and dated outgoing drafts predominate. The majority of files date from the 1960s and 70s, and represent Stern's USCO and Intermedia work.

items.title: Harold Schmidt Collection
items.description: Sound recordings from Stanford University professor and choral director Harold C. Schmidt (1910-1993), including performances from the Stanford University Chorus, Choir, and Chamber Chorale. As director of the choir, he presided over nearly thirty years of commencements and Sunday services at Memorial Church before his retirement in 1975.

items.title: Matt Kahn papers, 1951-1999
items.description: When he was 21, Kahn joined Stanford's Department of Art (now the Department of Art and Art History). That was in 1949, and over the following 60 years he created pioneering coursework in design and also taught painting, drawing, sculpture and color theory. Materials include professional files, teaching files (including videos of lectures), and photographs.

items.title: Orchard, early spring near Stanford University, California [graphic]
items.description: One (1) gelatin silver photographic print by American photographer Ansel Adams depicting an orchard near Stanford University in 1963.

items.title: Pulsa records, 1966-2019
items.description: The papers of 1960s-70s experimental multimedia collective Pulsa consist of project files, photographs, slides & negatives, and printed material about the group. Pulsa was an experimental multimedia arts collective founded in 1966 and active through 1973.

items.title: Richard Finnie Collection
items.description: Open reel tapes recorded by Richard Finnie, including Bechtel Corporation film soundtrack material featuring traditional music and sound effects from Asia, the Middle East, and elsewhere, and broadcasts and live performances of classical music, jazz, folk, and other types of music. The Richard Finnie Collection consists of a variety of open reel tape recordings made by documentary filmmaker, photographer, ethnographer and historian Richard Sterling Finnie (1906-1987), largely in the 1950s and 60s.

items.title: Roy A. Long Collection
items.description: Open reel tape recordings from approximately 1952 through 1980, including performances from Stanford University, as well as pipe organ music, live jazz and big band music, the Monterey Jazz Festival, the Carmel Bach Festival, and a steel drum band in Antigua, all recorded by donor Roy Long. Long was a graduate of Stanford and an engineer at the Stanford Research Institute.

items.title: The Wells Fargo Steinbeck collection, 1870-1981
items.description: The Wells Fargo Steinbeck Collection, originally the Rodgers Collection of John Steinbeck, contains more that 770 letters, photographs, clippings, unpublished short pieces, and ephemera from John Steinbeck and the Steinbeck and Hamilton families, dating from the 1890s to the early 1980s. Together, these letters provide the researcher a rich portrait of Steinbeck's family, his early years and his adult life, which so influenced his writing.

items.title: Tillie Olsen papers, 1930-1990
items.description: Tell Me A Riddle was originally published in 1962, and its title novella received the O. Henry Award as the best American story of 1961. The collection includes personal and professional correspondence, literary manuscripts by American author Tillie Olsen and others, material on the Longshoremen's Strike and the Socialist Party from during the mid-1930s, teaching material and student work, clippings, pamphlets, book reviews, awards, etc.

items.title: Yvor Winters and Janet Lewis papers, 1906-1982
items.description: Yvor Winters (1900-1968) was an American poet and literary critic; Janet Lewis (1899-1998) was an American poet and writer. Winters' papers, which are subdivided according to genre, consist of personal correspondence (primarily in-coming), professional correspondence with colleagues and publishers, articles and essays, critical texts, poetry, fiction, photographs, and miscellany. The Janet Lewis papers, also subdivided according to genre, include her personal and professional correspondence, articles, essays, lectures, novels, librettos, poems, and miscellany.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Design and architecture

items.title: Birge M. Clark architectural drawings, 1909-1954
items.description: Collection contains architectural drawings by Birge M. Clark, his brother David B. Clark, and other partners Walter Stromquist, David F. Potter and Joseph Ehrlich, with a few drawings by his father A. B. Clark. Projects were mostly located in Palo Alto, Stanford, and other communities on the Peninsula and included residences, schools, businesses, and city offices.

items.title: Bruce Sherman glass geodesic model, no date
items.description: Bruce Sherman was skilled at cabinetry and design, using innovative techniques for framing glass and wood. A culmination of this work was his scale-model of R. Buckminster Fuller's geodesic dome.

items.title: Claude Stoller collection of R. Buckminster Fuller material, 1955-1980
items.description: Claude Stoller (born 1921) was a faculty member in the Department of Architecture at the University of California. Stoller's collection on R. Buckminster Fuller contains correspondence with Fuller as well as Fuller's with others; articles by and about R. Buckminster Fuller; material about specific projects; original sketches by Fuller; and diagrams and charts, among others.

items.title: Hanna house collection, 1900-1995 (inclusive)
items.description: In 1935, Paul and Jean Hanna commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design their home to be built on the Stanford University campus. Correspondence, blueprints, drawings, photographs, and other records relating to the planning, design and construction of the campus home of Professor and Mrs. Paul R. Hanna. The collection focuses on the Hanna's work with architect Frank Lloyd Wright extending from the initial planning of the house through later renovations.

items.title: Hanna House collection, 1935-1982 [microform]
items.description: In 1935, Paul and Jean Hanna commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design their home to be built on the Stanford University campus. Correspondence, blueprints, drawings, photographs, and other records relating to the planning, design and construction of the campus home of Professor and Mrs. Paul R. Hanna. The collection focuses on the Hanna's work with architect Frank Lloyd Wright extending from the initial planning of the house through later renovations.

items.title: Harry Sanders; a Stanford Planner Charts the History of Campus Planning, and Church's Contribution
items.description: Harry L. Sanders was the first full-time director of planning at Stanford University. This interview largely concerns Thomas D. Church's role in Stanford's architecture and planning; other subjects include Frederic Law Olmsted at Stanford, major elements of campus architecture as it was in 1978, use of outside architects, and future development.
items.era_note: [Most of this interview, on Thomas D. Church's part in Stanford's architecture and planning, concerns the campus growth of these years.]

items.title: James Bertrand Wells papers, 1920-1972
items.description: James Bertrand Wells was a professor of civil engineering at Stanford University. Collection consists of drawings, plans, and reports related Stanford University buildings; materials related to San Francisco and Peninsula civil engineering projects; Stanford Academic Council minutes; and correspondence.

items.title: Leland W. King papers, 1930-2000
items.description: Leland W. King was an architect who worked for the State Department, Ampex Corporation, Memorex Corporation and other projects. The Leland W. King papers are composed of personal and professional correspondence, plans, photographs, brochures, booklets, reports, manuscripts and research. The materials document King's work with the post office, the State Department's Office of Foreign Buildings Operations (FBO), restoration of Lafayette Square and other projects.

items.title: Morley Baer photographs
items.description: Morley Baer, former head of the photography department of the San Francisco Art Institute, was a prize-winning photographer, well-known for his photographs of Victorian houses in San Francisco as well as images of California's farmlands and coastline. These photographs of Stanford University buildings were done by Baer for the architects or for the University.

items.title: Peninsula Volunteers photographs and printed promotional items, circa 1965
items.description: Included are four leaves with printed and illustrated matter mounted and seven actual mounted photographs (7.5 x 9 inches) and a promotional piece for a 30-unit "retirement apartment" complex built on El Camino Real, with some text, printed floor plan, brief description and photos. A subtle, quiet building from one of the largest architectural firms in the world, best known for its skyscrapers (and many buildings on Stanford campus).

items.title: Stanford University, Operations and Maintenance, Maps and Records, architectural drawings, 1889-1994 [microform].
items.description: Microfiche copies of architectural drawings of buildings on the Stanford University campus; and photocopy of the department's "vault inventory" of drawings, most of which are included in these copies. There are also some copies of drawings for the Hanna House, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.

items.title: Stanford University, University Architect / Campus Planning and Design, records, 1945-2018
items.description: The Planning Office was officially organized in 1945 under the directorship of Eldridge T. Spencer. In addition to overseeing the architectural aspects of the campus, the office was also responsible for overseeing land use and traffic circulation. The records of the Planning Office date back to its orgins in 1945 and include correspondence, memoranda, minutes, reports, studies, surveys, maps, and plans.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Film, radio and television

items.title: Augmentation of Douglas Engelbart collection, 2019
items.description: This collection consists of digital video files related to the creation of the film Augmentation of Douglas Engelbart.
items.era_note: [These files, made in 2019 for a film about Douglas Engelbart, concern his work of the 1960s.]

items.title: Joint Conference on Educational Television minutes
items.description: The conference was composed of representatives from Bay Area school boards, colleges and universities. Minutes from two meetings of the conference, August 15 and September 11, 1951, discussing the possible use of a television station to education and acquisition of VHF channel 9 which the FCC had reserved for educational use.

items.title: Pacifica Foundation ephemera collection, 1949-1984
items.description: Lew Hill founded the Pacifica Foundation and its flagship radio station KPFA in 1949. KPFA began broadcasting in Berkeley, California on April 15th, 1949, and was was the first listener-subscription FM educational radio station in the country. Primarily programming schedules, articles, and publicity.

items.title: Photographs of KVSM radio broadcasts, 1947 and undated
items.description: Includes photographs of staff reading scripts.

items.title: Programs, 1952 and nd.
items.description: "The five film societies of the Bay Region: Berkeley, Marin, San Francisco, the Peninsula, Carmel, have joined together as the KINESIS Group to secure films not available in this country."

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Press, journalism and broadcasting

items.title: David Bohrman archive of innovation in media & journalism, circa 1960s-2014
items.description: Materials include Bohrman's papers as well as ephemera, and two servers of digital files, and additional digital files received via electronic transfer.

items.title: Frank Taylor papers, 1928-1967
items.description: Includes notes, research material, correspondence, articles, worksheets, drafts, and copies of Taylor's magazine articles for Saturday Evening Post, Reader's Digest, Country Gentlemen, and Collier's. Major subjects include agriculture, gardening, aviation, personalities, foreign countries, Stanford University, and various industrial topics.

items.title: Kate Coleman papers, circa 1960s-1990s
items.description: Collection consists of print, manuscript, photographs and some audiovisual materials relating to the journalism career of Kate Coleman.

items.title: Paul C. Edwards papers, 1895-1986 (inclusive), 1912-1962 (bulk)
items.description: Paul C. Edwards studied journalism at Stanford from 1902-1906 and went on to become, successively, reporter, city editor, and managing editor of the San Francisco News. These papers largely pertain to Edwards' professional career and to his administrative positions with Stanford University. Professional papers include his speeches, essays, and editorials; original poetry and plays; and extensive correspondence with other journalists and newspaper editors.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Sport and recreation

items.title: The grand national livestock exposition, horse show, and rodeo (San Francisco, Calif) : programs, 1941-1956
items.description: Presented by No. 1-A District Agricultural Association (County of San Mateo and City and County of San Francisco). Programs for 1941, 1948, 1949, 1952, 1954, and 1956.

sectors.name: Arts and culture

items.title: Betty Janss papers, circa 1940-1970
items.description: Betty Janss was a theater critic reviewing performances on the San Francisco peninsula in the 1950s and 60s. Collection contains her drama reviews in the form of typescripts and clippings, along with annotated programs, notes, and correspondence.

items.title: Bjarne B. Dahl restoration reports, 1929-2007
items.description: Bjarne B. Dahl was a piano and harpsichord restorer from Sunnyvale, California. Materials include photographic reports (consisting of a written description, photographic prints, and negatives) documenting Dahl's restoration work on antique keyboard instruments.

items.title: Fidelity Sound Recordings Collection
items.description: This collection consists of commercially-released audio recordings created by the independent record company Fidelity Sound Recordings (FSR) based in Redwood City, California. The predominant musical genre featured is marching band music performed by university bands, bands affiliated with the Salvation Army, and miscellaneous ensembles in the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, and elsewhere.

items.title: Fine press keepsakes sponsored by William P. Wreden, 1953-1995
items.description: Bookman and owner of William P. Wreden Books & Manuscripts, established in 1938. In addition to 15 keepsakes sponsored by Mr. Wreden, there is REMINISCENCES, published in 1988 by his son, Bo Wreden, to celebrate the fiftieth anniversary of the opening of the bookshop, as well as Mr. Wreden's memorial service program, 1995.

items.title: Grabhorn Press and fine press ephemera collection, 1920-2000
items.description: Brothers Edwin and Robert Grabhorn established the Grabhorn Press in San Francisco in 1919; it soon became a respected west coast fine press. The majority of items in the collection are related to printing and publishing. There are posters, broadsides, and a smaller number of books and booklets, but most are prospectuses, advertising brochures, handbills, mailorder forms, and related material.

items.title: Jalonen theater & music program collection
items.description: The John W. Jalonen program collection is comprised of various playbill and performance programs mostly from local and regional production companies around the San Francisco Bay Area presented between the 1940s and 2000s.

items.title: Negro music and folk festival; Ravenswood High School : flyer
items.description: A single sheet flyer advertising the Negro Music and Folk Festival at Ravenswood High School on Sunday, February 21, 1965 at 3pm.

items.title: Stalingrad board game and other material, 1963-1968
items.description: The materials consist of the Stanlingrad board game, one of the first board wargames made. Players re-enact the entire Russo-German conflict from 1941-45. The game was formerly owned by Arthur J. Whitaker, who played by mail with several others, including the MIT Strategic Games Society, Con Crane, and Raymond Clark.

items.title: Stanford University Press archival book copies, 1900-2013
items.description: The Stanford University Press was established as an independent printing operation at Stanford University in 1892. It publishes scholarly monographs, textbooks, and professional reference works. The collection consists of archival copies of books published by Stanford University Press.

items.title: Sunset Magazine editorial materials compiled by former employee Martha Rosman May, 1963-1968
items.description: Collection consists of interoffice memorandum, proof sheets, and a small amount of correspondence compiled by former Sunset Magazine employee Martha Rosman May.

items.title: Sunset Magazine records, 1931-1998
items.description: The records of Sunset Magazine primarily consist of over 100,000 photographs as published in the magazine from 1948-1969 and 1977-1998. Given Sunset's focus as the "Magazine of Western Living," however, one may expect to find photographs of gardening and landscaping, architecture and home improvement, cooking and food, entertaining, travel, nature, and recreation.

sectors.name: Society and community — Activism and advocacy

items.title: [Poster for an anti-war demostration to be held in conjunction with the refusal to be inducted in the Armed Forces by Timothy Englilsh, Jeff Browning and Mark Riley] [graphic]
items.description: Poster advertising an anti-war demonstration that reads: "Timothy English, Jeff Browning, & Mark Riley will refuse induction into the armed forces February 14 St. Valentine's Day 1968. Demonstration 10:00 AM Oakland Induction Center."

items.title: American Civil Liberties Union of Northern California records, 1900-2000 bulk 1934-2000
items.description: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) is a non-profit organization committed to the defense, preservation, and extension of civil liberties in the United States. Comprising correspondence, minutes, policy statements, reports, court transcripts, attorney notes, scrapbooks, newspaper clippings, pamphlets, and other printed material created or collected by the ACLU-NC, these records document the establishment and activities of the northern California branch and its wide-ranging efforts to protect and extend individual liberties in California.

items.title: Anti-War and Student Unrest collection, 1968-1972
items.description: Collection pertains to the antiwar movement of college students and the resulting disruptions on college campuses, in particular that of Stanford University. Collection includes press releases from the Stanford News Service, memoranda, statements and handouts from student organizations, statements by the Stanford administration, issues of the Campus Report, magazine articles, and clippings.

items.title: April 3rd Movement records, 1969-2014
items.description: The April 3rd Movement was a student group at Stanford University protesting the university's connection with military and counter-insurgency research, specifically the Stanford Research Institute and the Applied Electronics Laboratory. Collection includes flyers, statements by the April 3rd Movement as well as university officials, information sheets (including one for those planning to be arrested), a booklet on SRI produced by the movement, a booklet titled "The Goods on AEL Declassified by the April 3rd Movement", the newsletter "Declassified" produced during the occupation of the Applied Electronics Laboratory, copies of articles, press releases, and issues of the CAMPUS REPORT and the STANFORD DAILY.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- David Harris & Joan Baez, 1967-2014
items.description: David Harris, opponent of U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War, appeared at the Oakland, California, Federal Induction Center demonstrations during October and December of 1967. In March 1968 David married peace activist and folk singer Joan Baez. Bob Fitch photographed them many times over the years, and images of David Harris and Joan Baez are featured in a number of other galleries, including "Connie Vote," "Farmworker Union Strike" and "Civil Rights - Martin Luther King."

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive, 1965-2013
items.description: The Bob Fitch Photography Archive consists of the photographic work of activist and photojournalist Bob Fitch, documenting the civil rights movement, the farm worker movement, the peace movement, other social justice movements and issues, cultural change, religion, as well as his professional and personal life.

items.title: John W. Gardner papers, 1912-2004
items.description: Gardner served as the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare under President Lyndon Johnson from 1965-1968. He founded the citizen's advocacy group Common Cause and was the chairman of the Commission on White House Fellowships. Collection includes speeches and writings by, as well as articles about Gardner; correspondence, awards and honors, photographs, audiovisual material, and files from many of Gardner's organizations including Common Cause, the White House Fellows, the Haas Center for Public Service, and the John W. Gardner Center.

items.title: Martin Luther King at Stanford [motion picture]
items.description: Film documents a speech given by Martin Luther King at Stanford University on April 14, 1967 about racism and civil rights in American society.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 1, Board of Directors records, 1967-1993
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. MALDEF's Board of Directors is the organization's governing body; the directors assist the lead staff in program planning, fundraising, and administrative decisions.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 5, Legal Programs Department, 1968-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. This record group includes the files generated and collected by Rosen and Baller from 1972 until 1983, as they directed and developed MALDEF's litigation.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 9, Regional and Program Offices, 1967-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. In the early years, the offices concentrated on local legal work, and were funded by the initial Ford grant.

items.title: Michelle Vignes collection, 1966-1974
items.description: Collection of photographs and photographic negatives taken by Michelle Vignes. Part 2. Black Panthers. Part 3. Angela Davis, photographs taken during 1969 press conference at Mills College: 8 work prints, photographs/negatives of her trial at the Civic Center in Marin and San Jose in 1971 and 1974.

items.title: Page Mill Road Co-ordinating Committee records, 1965-1966
items.description: The Page Mill Road Co-ordinating Committee, an early outgrowth of Committee for Green Foothills, worked to get the new road rerouted and a safe underpass constructed below Highway 280 for non-vehicular traffic. Correspondence, committee meeting minutes, news clippings, flyers, photographs, blue prints, and publications.

items.title: Robert P.J. Cooney, Jr. Papers
items.description: Six archival boxes detailing Robert P.J. Cooney's involvement with the Institute for the Study of Nonviolence, as well as related activities.

items.title: Salvador Enrique Alvarez personal archive, 1950s-2015
items.description: Materials consist of Salvador E. Alvarez's papers related to his political activism and community involvement, including the United Farm Workers, the Hispanic Catholics of America, and the founding of the School of Social Work at San Jose State.

items.title: Stanford University student demonstration audio collection
items.description: Audio recordings of Stanford student demonstrations, sit-ins, and Academic Senate and Council meetings.

items.title: Stanford University, News Service, director's records
items.description: Robert W. Beyers directed the Stanford news service from 1961 to 1990. Records cover three topics: Sigma Chi fraternity (issue of discrimination in membership 1965), Proposition 14 (written in 1964 to overturn California's Rumford Fair Housing Act, which prohibited discrimination on the basis of race and national origin), and student demonstrations and the McClellan probe (Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations headed by U.S. Senator John L. McClellan).

items.title: Student Power Conference at Cubberley High School brochure
items.description: The brochure includes the agenda for the Student Power Conference at Cubberley High School, a map, and contact numbers. Speakers included SLP candidate for Lt. Governor Nick Simon, Mark Kleiman, former Northern California Field Secretary for the SDS and others. Plan was to found a radical state-wide high school newspaper.

sectors.name: Society and community — Local and California history

items.title: California biography collection
items.description: Consists of ephemeral items relating to people widely known and relatively unknown in California. Contains mostly newspaper obituaries, but also includes: handwritten biographical documents, invitations, wedding announcements, family reunion newsletters, genealogy forms, family trees, memorials, political speeches, campaign material, correspondence, and newspaper and magazine clippings.

items.title: Minor White photographs
items.description: Minor White (July 9, 1908 – June 24, 1976) was an American photographer and educator. The collection consists of 479 black and white gelatin silver prints and 423 gelatin silver print negatives of urban and rural postwar Bay Area and greater Northern California taken by photographer Minor White while he resided in San Francisco from 1946 to 1953.

items.title: Sherwood Hall photograph album, 1939-1957
items.description: Librarian at Stanford University. Photographs by William Moran, 1942, and clippings, 1942-54, regarding Sherwood Hall, the Menlo Park residence of Timothy Hopkins; estate sale catalog, 1942; letters to Hitchcock from Mary Hopkins, 1939, and William Moran, 1943; two postcards; and miscellaneous clippings.

sectors.name: Society and community — Medicine and public health

items.title: [Interviews and talks presented to the Leon P. Fox Medical History Committee of the Santa Clara County Medical Association].
items.era_note: [About two fifths of these talks, histories of the county's medical specialties, hospitals and sanatoriums, concern this period.]

items.title: Children's Hospital at Stanford records, 1917-1977
items.description: Originally the Stanford Convalescent Home, established on the Stanford campus in 1919 for needy children with long term illness, this privately supported organization changed its name to the Children's Hospital at Stanford in 1970. These records were collected by Ruth Spande Atwood, first superintentdent and administrator of the Stanford Convalescent Home (1923-1961), and include correspondence, memoranda, reports, clippings and photographs.

items.title: Esther Clark papers, 1947-1973
items.description: Collection includes Clark's work with childhood accident prevention, the Palo Alto Medical Clinic, personal subject files, reprints, and photographs.

items.title: Halsted Holman papers, circa 1931-2015
items.description: Most files involve Health care reform, Chronic disease self-care programs, the Robert Wood Johnson Clinical Scholars Program, the Midpeninsula Health Service, and Holman's social and political activism. There is a particular emphasis on the Stanford Peace Movement and Anti-War materials.

items.title: Henry S. Kaplan papers, circa 1960-1983
items.description: Radiologist, cancer research pioneer and educator. Kaplan was best known for his work on leukemia and Hodgkins disease and for his work with Edward Ginzton on the development of the medical linear accelerator for cancer treatment. Professional and administrative correspondence; research and clinical abstract files, and research notebooks; films; biographical material including an oral history interview; and other files.

items.title: Herewith is submitted a record of abstract histories of surgical work
Herewith is submitted a record of detailed histories of surgical work
Jay Haley papers, 1957-2007
items.description: He was a pioneer in family therapy, and his work traces its birth and development during half a century. The Jay Haley collection documents Haley's career through correspondence, manuscripts, typescripts, and media materials.

items.title: Kenneth D. Brock journals, 1949-2018
items.description: Brock was hired in 1984 by the State of California, Department of Health Services, to work as a consultant with the Centers for Disease Control to establish a registry of AIDS cases in California. Journals including some correspondence and photographs.

items.title: Leo Leonidas Stanley papers, 1916-1950
items.description: Chiefly diaries entitled Events of the Day from period of professional work as the Resident Physician of the Medical Department of the California State Prison at San Quentin. These narrative accounts are supplemented by annual reports of the prison hospital, minutes of prison committees, articles and speeches by L.L. Stanley, correspondence, criminal and medical case histories, notes on effects of coffee on sleep and whey experiments, black and white photoprints and collected clippings and articles.

items.title: Mental Research Institute (MRI) records
items.description: The Mental Research Institute (MRI) is a small, independent, multi-disciplinary, non-profit corporation founded in Palo Alto, California, and is one of the pioneering institutions of brief and family therapy methodology. The material described in this finding aid consists of therapy sessions, notes, drafts, research proposals, clinical practice files, grant files, conference proceedings, publications, audiovisual material, born-digital material, and other material related to the operation of MRI.

items.title: Palo Alto-Stanford Hospital collection, 1916-1966 (inclusive), 1952-1966 (bulk)
items.description: In 1921 Stanford University took over the administration of Palo Alto's Peninsula Hospital; ownership was jointly shared by Palo Alto and Stanford. The first pertains to Stanford's acquisition of Palo Alto's share of the hospital and includes correspondence, legal documents, financial reports, and floor plans, 1951-1966. The second part consists of scrapbooks and clippings, 1938-1960, on the Palo Alto-Stanford hospital, health insurance programs, labor unions in hospitals, Stanford Medical School, and other hospitals.

items.title: Roy B. Cohn papers, 1963-1982
items.description: Chiefly articles and correspondence related to work with Samuel Kountz in renal transplantation and the prevention and treatment of transplant rejection.

items.title: Russel V. Lee family papers, circa 1895-2014, bulk 1940s-1970s.
items.description: Dr. Russel Van Arsdale Lee founded the Palo Alto Medical Clinic (PAMC), one of the first group practice clinics in the United States. The materials consist of correspondence, photos, printed material, scrapbooks, ephemera relating to the Lee family, the Palo Alto Medical Clinic and the careers of Russel V. Lee and Philip R. Lee.

items.title: Russel V.A. Lee papers, 1935-1976
items.description: Chiefly correspondence together with supporting subject material, including pamphlets, minutes, and newsletters, related to work as Founder and Director of the Palo Alto Medical Clinic, 1924-61. Major subject groupings in health insurance, health care for the aging, community medical clinics and group medical practice.

items.title: S.O.S. Program Collection
items.description: Lecture recordings and transcripts from the S.O.S. Program, a pioneering divorce therapy group founded in Palo Alto, California in 1963 by Sally Spray (now Sally Moltzen). The S.O.S. Program, which according to Moltzen was "the first organized professionally-led discussion group in the country," provided some of the first access to mental health professionals by persons with marital problems outside of private practice.

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: Emanuel B. McDonald papers, 1912-1958 (inclusive), 1953-1958 (bulk)
items.description: Typescript draft of his autobiography SAM MCDONALD'S FARM (Stanford University press, 1954); miscellaneous business papers, pamphlets, and clippings, 1912-1958; photographs; and his letters to Holly and John Ceideburg, 1956. Emanuel B. "Sam" McDonald joined the Stanford staff in 1903 and became supervisor of athletic grounds.

items.title: Leland Stanford collection, 1869-1975
items.description: Stanford was a leader in organizing the Republican party in California and was elected governor in 1861 at the age of 37. In 1884, Leland and Jane founded Leland Stanford Jr. University in memory of their son. Primary and secondary sources pertaining to the life of Leland Stanford and the history of Stanford University's founding.

items.title: Michael L. Belangie papers, 1945-1980
items.description: In late 1945 he purchased Menlo Textiles, a national purveyor of custom-loomed fabrics in Menlo Park, California, some thirty miles south of San Francisco. His public service efforts led him to run for the Menlo Park City Council in 1950, an election that he won. Personal and professional papers, some also pertaining to his wife, Mary.

items.title: Peter Coutts collection, 1881-1956
items.description: Jean-Baptiste Paulin Caperon (better known in California as Peter Coutts), was a successful French businessman, book collector and editor of the republican, anti-royalist paper, LA LIBERTÉ. Correspondence from Coutts, his granddaughter, Marguerite Berlin, and others regarding Coutts' property and Coutts' background.

items.title: Ray Lyman Wilbur personal papers, 1829-1949 (inclusive) 1875-1949 (bulk)
items.description: He served as lecturer and professor of physiology and of medicine (1897-1903), Dean of the Cooper Medical College (Stanford) (1911-1916), third President of Stanford University (1916-1943), Chancellor of Stanford, and Secretary of the Interior (September 1929-1933) under President Hoover. Includes correspondence; scrapbooks; publications; speeches and trip notes; rough draft of Wilbur's "Memoirs"; R.L. Wilbur's will; honorary degrees; letters from Mrs. R.L. Wilbur to her children; and files on associations with which Wilbur was involved, friends and associates, clubs to which he belonged, conferences, and issues such as environmental protection, civil defense during World Wars I and II, prohibition, and anti-vivisection. Papers also include Wilbur family correspondence (1829-1949).

sectors.name: Society and community — Philanthropy and foundations

items.title: Ben and A. Jess Shenson papers, circa 20th century
items.description: Collection consists of material related to the brothers Ben and A. Jess Shenson, their philanthropic activities, connections to local artists, family history and time at Stanford.

items.title: William Hewlett papers, 1907-2018 (bulk 1960-2001)
items.description: William Hewlett was the co-founder of Hewlett-Packard, one of the most successful technology start-up companies in the history of Silicon Valley. Following the tremendous success of Hewlett-Packard, he became well known for his philanthropy, donating millions of dollars from his fortune to support various causes. The William Hewlett papers consists of correspondence, photographs, financial records, reports, minutes, calendars, hardware, electronic files, videotapes, newspaper clippings, publications, and other materials.

sectors.name: Society and community — Race, ethnicity and immigration

items.title: Dr. George Kambara papers
items.description: George Kambara earned his A.B. at Stanford in 1937 and his M.D. in 1941, but was forced to leave his residency in 1942 and relocate to the Tule Lake internment camp. He was head of the eye, ear, nose and throat service there until he was accepted for a residency in Memphis in 1943. Correspondence with L. R. Chandler, Dean of Stanford University School of Medicine, 1942-47, concerning possible placement at a hospital away from California, war time conditions at Stanford, advice on a surgery at Tule Lake camp, Kambara's move to Memphis, and his post-war career; one letter to Dr. Charles E. Smith, 1942, regarding his medical work at Tule Lake camp and other conditions there; letters to Dr. Michael F. Marmor, November 1996, recalling his internment years; and one letter to Prof. Gordon Chang, November 1996, recalling his student days at Stanford, Prof. Ichihashi, and Tule Lake camp.

items.title: Japanese-American summer retreats at the Gilroy Yamato Hot Springs Resort : photographs, 1954-1960
items.description: Two 10 x 8 inch black-and-white photographs depicting large groups seated in front of a building at the resort; the site is identified in a Japanese caption on the 1954 photo; the other one includes part of a banner in the background which includes the date. Kyuzaburo Sakata, a lettuce grower in Watsonville, had purchased the site in 1938 and turned it into a resort that welcomed Japanese-American visitors.

items.title: Kazuyuki Takahashi papers
items.description: Takahashi was incarcerated with his wife, Soyo Takahashi, at Santa Anita Assembly Center and Manzanar War Relocation Center during World War II. This collection consists of digital scans of letters, photographs, and related materials created and collected by Stanford University graduate Kazuyuki Takahashi and his family, including his wife Soyo Takahashi.

items.title: Kenneth Kann papers and oral histories relating to the Petaluma (CA) Jewish chicken ranchers and egg farmers and the life of Joe Rapoport, circa 1970-1995
items.description: While at Berkeley, Kann began writing a popular history of the Petaluma Jewish chicken ranching community with support from the California Historical Society and the National Endowment for the Humanities. The collection contains interview tapes and transcripts used as research for author Kenneth Kann's two books about the Jewish community in Petaluma, California, during the twentieth century.
items.era_note: [About a third of the interviews, on Petaluma's Jewish chicken ranchers during the Cold War and the Holocaust survivors who settled there after the war, concern this period.]

items.title: Mary Jane Hamachi papers, 1938-1973
items.description: This collection consists of correspondence, photographs, photo albums,school records, financial documents, certificates, and other documents. The correspondence is from Mary Jane Hamachi's family, friends, and acquaintances during World War II. Most of the correspondents were either at internment camps in the United States, such as Topaz, Yellow Springs, and Tanforan, or were enlisted in the United States Army.

items.title: Peter M. Takaichi papers, 1927-1946
items.description: Peter M. Takaichi owned and operated the National Printing Company in San Jose,California. Collection consists of six folders (chronological order) documenting the evacuation of a Japanese American family from San Jose, California, to Heart Mountain Relocation Center, Wyoming. The notes, letters, and post cards describe life in the relocation camp.

items.title: Photograph album : Japanese American families and communities. C1933-1958
items.description: This collection consists of a photo album with 116 black and white photographs. The photographs depict Japanese American families and communities in Berkeley, Oakland, San Jose, and other locations.

items.title: Stan Steiner papers, ca. 1961-1987
items.description: Stan Steiner (1925–1987) was an American social historian, author and teacher who wrote books focusing on American minority communities and their relationship to the broader society as well as the mythology of the American West. Comprising 138 manuscript boxes, the papers are also a trove of clippings and ephemera in the post-War era, documenting everything from right-wing organizations and social movements to Native American tribes and land policy, to the farm worker movements.

items.title: The Baltic video archive : Baltic video testimonies at Stanford Libraries
items.description: The Baltic Video Archive of Stanford Libraries consists of four oral history collections, each of which tells the story of the Baltic countries through video testimonies of the Baltic peoples. The archive also includes stories told by the more recent generation, the so-called “digital nomads,” or the “Estonian mafia,” who have migrated to and established enterprises in California's Silicon Valley.
items.era_note: [Most of the testimonies, on the Second World War, the Nazi and Soviet occupations and the Baltic refugees, concern this period.]

sectors.name: Society and community — Religion, clubs and societies

items.title: Palo Alto Rebekah Cook Book : typed copy, ca. 1944
items.description: The cookbook, compiled by Leona Andrieu and Clara Oeschger, contains favorite recipes of members and friends. It is dedicated to the President of the Rebekah Assembly, Rena A. Trimble.

items.title: The Pacific Rocket Society : historical report
items.era_note: [Nearly all of this 1980 report, a history of the society with copies of its records and 1948-1952 bulletins, concerns this period.]

sectors.name: Society and community — Women, gender and sexuality

items.title: Anne Guthrie papers, ca. 1929-1957
items.description: Secretary and advisor to the Y.W.C.A., particularly in The Philippines. Representative of The International Alliance of Women to the General Assembly of The United Nations, Biographer of Vijaya Lakshimi Pandit, High Commissioner from Irelia to The United Kingdom.

sectors.name: Society and community

items.title: Herman Gallegos papers, 1944-2013
items.description: Herman Gallegos has been an activist and community organizer with a focus on Latino rights and support, as well as a management consultant, director, and trustee on many corporate boards and nonprofits. This collection contains organizational files, grant proposals, meeting dockets, correspondence, reports, newsletters, research and subject files, and notes from Herman Gallegos's corporate, non-profit, philanthropic and advocacy work.

items.title: Kaiser Shipyards women's chorus : photographs, 1942-1945
items.description: A collection of 19 original photographs documenting the activities of an all-girl chorus comprised of a dozen young women who also worked at the Kaiser Permanente Shipyard in Richmond, CA during World War II. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Wendell P. Hammon collection of papers relating to the Economic Opportunity Commission of Santa Clara County, Inc., 1964-1971
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Armed forces and military history

items.title: Fred J. Buenzle papers. circa 1870-1946
items.description: Fred J. Buenzle (1872-1946) was a yeoman in the United States Navy in the late nineteenth century. Included in the collection are manuscripts, typescripts, correspondence, photographs (approx. 900), and publications relating to Buenzle's service in the Navy and afterwards.

items.title: LORAN and GEE archive compiled by John Johnston, 1986-1990
items.description: This collection consists of research John Johnston compiled regaring LORAN and GEE radar operators and technicians during World War II. The materials consist primarily of correspondence. LORAN (Long Range Navigation) and GEE were hyperbolic radio navigation systems used by the United States and the United Kingdom during World War II.
items.era_note: [Nearly all of this collection, research and correspondence with radar technicians about their Second World War service, concerns this period.]

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Arms control, science and technology policy

items.title: National management of high-energy physics facilities papers
items.description: Professor of physics and director of the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center. Memoranda, letters, and a background paper by Panofsky prepared for a meeting of University Presidents concerning national management of high-energy physics facilities; correspondents include Frederick Seitz, president of the National Academy of Sciences, and Edwin M. McMillan of the Lawrence Radiation Laboratory, University of California.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Foreign affairs and diplomacy

items.title: Nixon-Krushchev "Kitchen debate," Moscow, 1959 : [videorecording] / recorded by Joseph Roizen
items.description: Footage of the famous "kitchen debate" between Vice President Richard Nixon and Premier Nikita Khrushchev at the American National Exhibition in Moscow on July 24, 1959. Having assisted with the development of videorecording technology at Ampex, Roizen (1923-1989) supervised the color television installation at the fair, and operated the Ampex recorder used to capture the exchange as filmed by RCA cameras.

items.title: Richard A. Stepp papers, 1937-1995
items.description: The papers of Richard A. Stepp pertain largely to the time he spent in Burma as an advisor on technical services for small industries, 1958-59. Included are correspondence, notebooks, reports, memos, Burmese government documents (in English), other publications, and photographs, 1954-59.

items.title: William M. Roth papers, 1914-1973 (bulk 1950-1973)
items.description: United States Ambassador, American businessman, negotiator.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Government and public administration

items.title: Business and industry's effect on the financing of Palo Alto city services and the Palo Alto Unified School District, 1965 Mar. 1.
items.description: Both tangible and intangible criteria were sought; cross-analyses were made to develop forecasts on probable effects to the city services, the school system, and the city's population growth based on projected changes in business and industry.

items.title: Francis V. Keesling papers, 1908-1972 (bulk 1947-1972)
items.description: He practiced law in San Francisco from 1934 to 1955, and was with West Coast Life Insurance Co. 1936-1977. Correspondence, scrapbooks, legal papers, and miscellaneous material relating to the selective service, the construction of the San Francisco International Airport, and various government committees and projects.

items.title: Olaf Pitt Jenkins papers, 1929-1973 (bulk 1946-1958)
items.description: In 1929 he joined the California State Division of Mines and Mining, serving as State Mineralogist and Chief of the Division from 1947 to his retirement in 1958. This collection, dating from 1929 to 1973, largely relates to Jenkins' career with the California State Division of Mines and Mining and includes correspondence, biographical material, talks, and memorabilia.

items.title: Project MKULTRA collection, 1977
items.description: Project MKULTRA, sponsored by the Central Intelligence Agency, conducted research on various aspects of human behavioral control in the 1950s and 1960s, some of which involved the Stanford University Medical School. Collection consists of photocopies of invoices, receipts and memorandum relating to subprojects 2, 56, 70, 71, 72, 85, and 86 of Project MKULTRA; these documents were sent to Stanford University by the C.I.A. in 1977.
items.era_note: [Most of the collection, copies of invoices and memoranda from CIA-funded research projects of the 1950s and 1960s, concerns this period.]

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Law and legal practice

items.title: Frank B. Yoakum diaries, 1932-1990
items.description: Founding partner in the Los Angeles law firm of Iverson, Yoakum, Papiano and Hatch where he worked until he was 84.

items.title: In the matter of the estate of Jane L. Stanford, deceased: legal briefs, correspondence, and clippings
items.description: Collection pertains to claims against Jane L. Stanford's estate from the adopted children of her niece Amy L. Hansen, who was a legatee in Jane Stanford's will, and includes three legal briefs, clippings, and correspondence between James D. Adams of the law firm representing Stanford and Ruth Scibird, curator of the Stanford Collection, about the appeal decision, 1957.

items.title: Lowell Turrentine papers, 1913-1956
items.description: He practiced law in Cleveland and New York City and was involved in the prosecution of the Elk Hills and Teapot Dome scandal, before joining the faculty of the Stanford Law School in the fall of 1929. Collection pertains largely to his professional life at Stanford University and contains correspondence, both business and personal; his master's thesis; materials for lectures; degrees, awards, and certificates; and a Turrentine genealogy.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Politics and elections

items.title: A native daughter's leadership in public affairs : oral history transcript, 1974. With an introduction by Winifred Heard
items.description: Recollections of growing up in Berkeley; student days at University of California, 1914-1918; work for University Extension and the Engineering, Science and Management War Training program on campus, World War II; her husband, Samuel C. May; Sierra Club trips; her association with League of Women Voters; volunteer work; Berkeley politics; membership on City Council, 1959-1971; efforts to end discrimination in Berkeley in schools, housing and employment; planning for Bay Area Rapid Transit District; membership in Association of Bay Are Governments and Bay Conservation and Development Commission.
items.era_note: [Most of this 1974 interview, on wartime training work, her Berkeley City Council years and Bay Area regional planning, concerns this period.]

items.title: Collection of political match book covers, 1950-1970
items.description: Album containing 695 match book covers, each promoting a politician in California.

items.title: Francis V. Keesling papers, 1906-1957
items.description: Keesling Sr. was a "regular" Republican, one of the few whose papers are extant, and greatly opposed to Hiram Johnson and the Progressives. This collection includes a wide variety of records related to the political activities, civic work, life insurance career, and personal papers accrued by Francis V. Keesling Sr.

items.title: J. Arthur Younger papers, 1951-1968
items.description: The J. Arthur (Jesse Arthur) Younger Papers consist of the office files of J.
