Arthur Younger who was a United States Representative of Congress for California's 11th Congressional District in San Mateo County from 1952-1967. Correspondence, drafts, documents, and printed reference material which forms a written record of ten years in the United States House of Representatives.

items.title: J. Arthur Younger papers, 1964-1968
items.description: He was the Republican representative from the 9th California Congressional District to the United States House of Representatives, 1953-1967. Correspondence, documents, and printed reference materials which form a written record of Younger's career in Washington, D.C. from 1964 until his death in 1967 and the election of his successor.

sectors.name: Ideas and intellectual history — Counterculture

items.title: Fred Turner papers, 1968-2019
items.description: Fred Turner is an Associate Professor in the Department of Communication at Stanford University and Director of Stanford's Program in Science, Technology, and Society. Files consist primarily of research material, manuscripts, and chapter drafts related to Turner's book, From Counterculture to Cyberculture: Stewart Brand, the Whole Earth Network, and the Rise of Digital Utopianism.

items.title: Midpeninsula Free University publications, 1966-1970
items.description: The Midpeninsula Free University (MFU) was a free university, operating primarily between 1966 and 1971 on the San Francisco Midpeninsula. The materials consist of catalogs of course offerings available at the Midpeninsula Free University, as well as its newsletter, The Free You, from 1966-1970. The MFU sponsored, be-ins, street concerts, a restaurant, a store, and was actively involved in every aspect of the flourishing counterculture on the Midpeninsula, including the anti-war movement at Stanford University.

items.title: Midpeninsula Free University, 1967-1970
items.description: Located in Palo Alto, Menlo Park, and Mountain View, California. Founded in 1966 and closed in 1971. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Stewart Brand papers, 1954-2000
items.description: He was loosely associated with the Merry Pranksters, USCO, and other countercultural groups, and spent much of the 1960s traveling and visiting communal experiments. Brand created the original Whole Earth Catalog in 1968 to provide practical information on tools that would be useful for people creating and living in communes. The Steward Brand papers contains correspondence, personal journals, manuscripts, photographs, project records, articles, and publications.

sectors.name: Ideas and intellectual history

items.title: R. Buckminster Fuller materials from Herbert Matter, circa 1960-1969 and undated
items.description: Two short 16 mm film reels of World Game activities as well as numerous negatives related to the World Game and Dymaxion maps. Also included are some manuscript notes (by Herbert Matter or his wife, Mercedes Matter?) on the subject of drawing. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Walter A. Huston collection of R. Buckminster Fuller material, circa 1965-1975
items.description: Collection contains books, articles, manuscripts, ephemera, audio cassettes, tapes, film, photographs and slides collected by Walter A. Huston about R. Buckminster Fuller. Ephemera files contain pamphlets, letters, and other documents about the World Game, geodesic domes, the Samuel Beckett theater, seminars and programs run by Fuller, and some itinerary and travel materials from trips Huston accompanied Fuller on in the early 1970s. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Collections of general regional interest

items.title: Incoming letters from Charles S. Gubser and Andrew Wyeth, 1964 and 1970

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Advertising and marketing

items.title: Archie Boston graphic design files, circa 1970s-2010s
items.description: Archie Boston is an award-winning African-American graphic design artist, educator and author. This collections consists of award certificates, advertising prints and proofs, ephemera, logos, interim reports, brochures, posters, DVDs, books, digital files, academic syllabi, videos, CV, and one thumb drive.

items.title: Regis McKenna papers, 1973-2012
items.description: The Regis McKenna papers document McKenna's innovative leadership in marketing and public relations for technology companies in Silicon Valley and the business operations of his agency, Regis McKenna Inc. (RMI). The collection consists of presentations, reports, proposals, and official correspondence related to McKenna's work on marketing campaigns for Apple Inc. and Intel, among others.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Aerospace and defence

items.title: Howard Seifert papers
items.description: Howard S. Seifert (1911-1977), an authority on rocket propulsion of space vehicles, was professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford from 1960 to 1976. Papers include correspondence, photographs, newsclippings, notes, memoranda, reports, reprints, proposals, and class materials (notes, problems, exams, and reference sources).

items.title: Jay Arthurs papers, 1971 and 1983
items.description: Includes publicity material and photographs of Apollo 15 and transcriptions of the landing dialog from the first Challenger mission.

items.title: Joseph D. Cusick collection of Lockheed Missiles & Space Co. and the U.S. Air Force Satellite Test Center records, 1962-1991
items.description: History, policies, organization, personnel, and technical trainingmaterials collected by Joseph D. Cusick during employment by Lockheed Missiles & Space Co. (LMSC) from August 1962 to May 1968 and the U.S. Air Force, at the Air Force Satellite Test Center [Satellite Operations Center] Onizuka Air Force Base, Sunnyvale, CA), from May 1962 through May 1991.

items.title: NASA/Ames Research Center publications, 1958-2000
items.description: The collection contains issues of internal publications, such as The Astrogram, and reports on NASA-AMES activities.

items.title: Nicholas J. Hoff papers, 1903-1997 (inclusive), 1940-1997 (bulk)
items.description: Nicholas J. Hoff was a professor emeritus of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University at the time of his death in 1997. Collection includes articles and papers by Hoff on aircraft structures and other matters, 1944-1981; diplomas, awards and other biographical materials, 1928-1997; and materials he collected on the history of aviation including articles, reports, and photographs, 1903-1958.

items.title: Rich Potter collection of Ford Aerospace materials, 1969-1989
items.description: Ford Aerospace was a division of the Ford Motor Company that existed from 1956-1990. Materials consist of company memos, documents, reports, organizational charts, and other records of Ford Aerospace, especially those related to personnel and the Aeronutronic Industrial Relations Office.

items.title: Robert T. Jones papers, 1912-1996 (inclusive), 1930-1996 (bulk)
items.description: Research notes and drawings, correspondence, patents, articles, reports, photographs, and other materials. Robert T. Jones, one of the premier theoretical aerodynamicists of the twentieth century, was a research scientist with NASA, and its predecessor NACA, from 1934 until his retirement in 1982, when he joined the Stanford faculty as a consulting professor in aeronautics. He is best known for developing the theory of swept and delta wings.

items.title: Terence O'Laughlin collection of manuals and documentation for several ELINT systems manufactured by the Watkins-Johnson Company, circa 1970s
items.description: The collection consists of notebooks and manuals related to systems manufactured by the Watkins-Johnson Company. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: William Francis Whitmore papers, 1945-1991
items.description: William Francis Whitmore was a mathematician in the field of oceanography and a scientist and consultant with Lockheed Missiles and Space Company. This collection contains papers relating to William Francis Whitmore's work at Lockheed Missile and Space Company and as a consultant to the United States Navy.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Artificial intelligence

items.title: "Shakey the Robot" [videorecording]
items.description: Program of the Bay Area Computer History Perspectives held at SRI International on October 24, 1995, on a 1970 SRI project to create a robot (dubbed Shakey) that used rudimentary artificial intelligence to interact with its surroundings.
items.era_note: [Most of this program, on SRI's 1970 project to build the robot Shakey, concerns this period.]

items.title: AI conference at SRI [videorecording]
items.description: These round table discussions on the history of artificial intelligence research were held at SRI on December 1, 1999. Speakers included Charles Rosen, Peter Hart, Nils Nilsson, Thomas Garvey, Martin Fischler, Robert Bowles, John Lowrance, Richard Waldinger, and Jerry Hobbs.
items.era_note: [Most of these discussions, on the history of artificial intelligence research at SRI, concern this period.]

items.title: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence records, 1969-2011
items.description: Correspondence, manuscripts submitted to AI Magazine, conference presentations, audio visual materials, and a full run of AI Magazine.

items.title: Charles Rosen papers, 1957-1985
items.description: Charles Rosen was an American scientist and pioneering researcher and developer in the field of artificial intelligence and robotics. Five linear feet of material (1957-1985) including, professional papers and presentations given by Rosen; newspaper clippings and articles; correspondence, contract reports, grant proposals and memoranda pertaining to the robotics and Artificial Intelligence Center at Stanford Research Institute; and business planning documents for the Machine Intelligence Corporation.

items.title: Computational linguistics [videorecording]
items.description: Gerald Gazdar (1950-) is a British linguist, computer scientist, and retired professor of computational linguistics at the University of Sussex. Twenty-two lectures of a full-length course on computational linguistics presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University . [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: David Hays papers, 1952-1995
items.description: Hays is an early researcher and writer in the fields of computational linguistics, machine translation (especially English-Russian translation) and various other topics combining computer science, the humanities, and sociology. Contains research notes, correspondence, typescript drafts and articles by Hays and others.

items.title: Edward A. Feigenbaum papers, 1950-2007 (inclusive)
items.description: Feigenbaum is a leading national figure in artificial intelligence and has developed computer resources for interactive research between medical and scientific collaborators on a national and global scale. Collection primarily concerns his work in artificial intelligence at Stanford University and includes administrative files, correspondence, project files, trip files, proposals, reports, reprints, Artificial Intelligence Lab memos, audio tapes, video tapes, and files on computer programs, mainly DENDRAL, MOLGEN, EPAM, and SUMEX.

items.title: John McCarthy papers, 1951-2008
items.description: During his remarkable career, McCarthy co-founded the MIT Artificial Intelligence Project and what became the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Lab, serving as director at Stanford from 1965 until 1980. McCarthy was a giant in the field of computer science and a seminal figure in the field of artificial intelligence. Correspondence, memos, reports, course materials, newsletters, articles, reprints, computer manuals, and other materials pertaining to McCarthy's research and his teaching at Stanford and MIT.

items.title: Knowledge engineering: artificial intelligence research at the Stanford Heuristic Programming Project [videorecording]
items.description: Documentary regarding expert systems and focusing on the Stanford Heuristic Programming Project.

items.title: Knowledge Representation: Pat Hayes and Nils Nilsson [videorecording]
items.description: The materials consist of videorecordings of lectures from a full-length course presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University by Pat Hayes (Xerox PARC and Stanford University) and Nils Nilsson (Stanford University) on the topic of knowledge representation.

items.title: LISP and natural language processing [videorecording]
items.description: Sixteen lectures on 8 cassettes comprise a full-length course presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University .

items.title: Louis G. Robinson papers, 1980-1987
items.description: Correspondence, notes and 26 videotapes relating to the first AAAI conference, Stanford, 1980, together with papers concerning the Seventh International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-81), Vancouver, 1981, and a run of the SPANG ROBINSON REPORT -- THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BUSINESS NEWSLETTER, 1985-1987.

items.title: Prolog and natural language processing [videorecording]
items.description: Fernando Pereira is Distinguished Scientist at Google, where he leads projects in natural-language understanding and machine learning. Sixteen lectures on 16 cassettes comprise a full-length course presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University.

items.title: Richard E. Fikes papers, 1963-2007
items.description: Richard Earl Fikes is Professor (Research) Emeritus in the Computer Science department of Stanford University. Richard has a long and distinguished record as an innovative leader in the development of techniques for effectively representing and using knowledge in computer systems. Papers include project files from his graduate studies; and computer program lists, computer printouts, reports, project files, and some correspondence from his time at SRI International, Xerox Palo Alto Research Center, Price Waterhouse Technology Centre, and Stanford. Richard was elected a Founding Fellow of the American Association for Artificial Intelligence (AAAI) in 1990.

items.title: Robert Engelmore papers, 1976-1998 (inclusive), 1978-1986 (bulk)
items.description: Engelmore was also a Program Manager for research in AI at DARPA, 1979-81, and a co-founder and director of Knowledge Systems Development, Teknowledge Inc., 1982-85. Collection includes documents regarding the computer programs/projects CRYSALIS and SACON; conference papers; copies of overhead slides for talks; and files pertaining to the computer company Teknowledge, Inc.

items.title: Shakey: An Experiment in robot planning and learning [videorecording]
items.description: From 1966 through 1972, the Artificial Intelligence Center at SRI International (then Stanford Research Institute) conducted research on a mobile robot system nicknamed "Shakey." Endowed with a limited ability to perceive and model its environment, Shakey could perform tasks that required planning, route-finding, and the rearranging of simple objects. Film producered by Peter Hart and Nils Nilsson.

items.title: Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Records
items.description: The materials consist of SAIL Dump And Restore Technique (DART) backup files, 1972-1990; digital copies of 16 mm films created from 1963-1980; handbooks; log books; manuals; and photographs and videos from the 35th SAIL reunion held in 2009.

items.title: Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory records, 1963-2009
items.description: The materials consist of SAIL Dump And Restore Technique (DART) backup files, 1972-1990; digital copies of 16 mm films created from 1963-1980; handbooks; log books; manuals; and photographs and videos from the 35th SAIL reunion held in 2009. The Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (also known as Stanford AI Lab or SAIL) is the artificial intelligence (AI) research laboratory of Stanford University.

items.title: Stanford University Medical Experimental Computer Resource (SUMEX) Records, 1975-1991
SUMEX-AIM stained glass panel
items.description: Created by Nicholas Veizades, an engineer who worked on the SUMEX-AIM project, to commemorate the early development of artificial intelligence in medicine project at Stanford. The panel features the name SUMEX-AIM in large letters.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Biotechnology and medical devices

items.title: Eric Vettel collection of Cetus Corporation materials, 1969-1986
items.description: Business records from the Cetus Corporation, one of the first biotechnology companies in the United States. The collection includes their original business plan, documents related to a 1981 public offering as well as material concerning business operations, finances, board, management, and competition.

items.title: Medicine and innovation: oral histories and archive of medical technology, 2019–2023
items.era_note: [About two-fifths of these interviews, recorded from 2019, recall the medical device inventions and companies of these years.]

items.title: Telesensory Systems, Inc. Optacon records, 1957-2022
items.description: Bliss later founded Telesensory Systems, Inc. (also known as TSI and TeleSensory Corporation), an American corporation that invented, designed, manufactured, and distributed technological aids for blind and low vision persons. This collection contains Bliss's dissertation, his related work and publications with the Stanford Research Institute, documents pertaining to the founding of Telesensory Systems, Inc., project files, reports, interviews, audiovisual materials, awards, and photographs.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Business organizations

items.title: Riding the high-tech boom: the American Electronics Association story, 1943-1990, c. 1991
items.description: In addition to the above article, Mr. Elkind has collected various clippings, pamphlets, etc. concerning the history of the electronics industry.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Computer hardware

items.title: [Sonoma County computer clubs newsletters.]
items.description: A collection of newsletters produced by and for Sonoma County computer clubs, including Apple Pickers, Sonoma County Computer Club, and Redwood Empire TRS-80 Users' Group. All focus on reports from the clubs' monthly meetings, other club business, and tips and tricks for various computer programs and systems.

items.title: Apple Computer ephemera collection of J. Steven Schmidt, 1984-1990
items.description: Includes Macintosh User Education, 1984 (2 binders); Macintosh software supplement, 1985; Macintosh buyers guide anniversary issue, 1984-1986; Macworld Expo/San Francisco program guide, 1989; and the Inmac catalog of Macintosh products, winter, 1990.

items.title: Apple Computer original advertising file, 1976
items.description: This small collection documents an episode in the early history of Apple Computer, Inc. Included is a phone message re Jobs, "they are 2 guys -- they build kits -- operate out of a garage," notes re the estimate, one black and white glossy photograph of circuitry and keyboard, and the final Apple-1 Operation Manual that was produced by the typesetter.

items.title: Apple Computer, Inc. and Chartmasters, Inc. marketing slides, 1985-1990
Apple Computer, Inc. records, 1977-1998
items.description: Contains organizational charts, annual reports, company directories, internal communications, engineering reports, design materials, press releases, manuals, public relations materials, human resource information, videotapes, audiotapes, software, hardware, and corporate memorabilia. Also includes information regarding the Board of Directors and their decisions.

items.title: Beth Ann Moore collection of Apple Computer publications, 1986-1990
items.description: Includes seven issues of "Wheels for the Mind," v. 2, no. 1 (Winter, 1986) through v. 3, no.3 (Summer, 1987), "Wheels for the Mind, Europe," Issue no. 1 (March, 1986), and "The Apple Guide to Publishing, Presentations and Interactive Media (1990).

items.title: BMUG newsletter : semiannual, 1985-1992
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Christopher Espinosa papers, 1978-1992
items.description: As a high school student at Homestead High, Chris Espinosa was an early regular at Homebrew Computing Club meetings, and was employee number 8 at Apple. He returned to Apple full-time and was director of documentation for the Macintosh project. Notebooks, 1988-1992; memos, 1979-1986; APPLE II and APPLE III operating, programing, and reference manuals, 1978-1983; Apple Resource dirctories, 1986-1988; three videos (Apple history in the making, 1991; Worldview demo, 1987; and Wild Card demo, 1987); three CD-ROMs (The Beta Release, 1990; The Apple reference & presentations library v4.0, 1990; and The virtual museum, 1992); two audio cassettes (Radio Apple, 1988); 55 floppy 5"-disks; and two t-shirts.

items.title: Computer notes : monthly publication
items.description: Computer-related topics such as applications, troubleshooting, interfacing, software, book reviews, fiction, etc. Contributors include Bill Gates, Paul Allen, Paul Wasmund, Monte Davidoff, Tom Durston, Lloyd J. Austin, David Bunnell, James B. Vice, H. Edward Roberts, and many others.

items.title: Ed Tecot collection of Apple ephemera, circa 1988-1991
items.description: Includes two tote bags from the Apple Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC). [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Edward J. McCluskey papers
items.description: In 1966, he joined Stanford University, where he is Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, as well as Director of the Center for Reliable Computing. His Stanford research focuses on logic testing, synthesis, design for testability, and fault-tolerant computing. The materials consist of subject files, teaching files, chronological files, and compter files.

items.title: Foghorn
items.description: Originally it was the official newsletter of the First Osborne Group. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Fred Wenninger papers, 1971-1995
items.description: By 1977, Wenninger started managing an advanced semiconductor-development project for HP called Focus. The project was designed to leapfrog HP years ahead of commercial semiconductor vendors by producing a 32-bit microprocessor and large memory chips for HP's desktop computers. Fred William Wenninger worked as a researcher and manager at Hewlett-Packard from the 1960s until 1986, when he became president of Allied Signal Corporation's Bendix/King subsidiary. The entire collection contains personal materials and professional materials relating to work done at Hewlett Packard.

items.title: Gene Carter collection of Apple Computer, Inc. material, circa 1977-1995
items.description: He worked in marketing for National Semiconductor and eventually went on to work for Apple Computer in 1976 as Vice President of Sales when the company was still a small startup. This collection primarily consists of various materials related to Apple Computer, Inc.'s sales history, including documents on establishing Apple dealers, selling strategies, reports on sales conference proceedings, correspondence with Apple dealers, and annual reports.

items.title: Homebrew Computer Club Newsletter and Meeting Announcements
items.description: The Homebrew Computer Club played an important role in the early development of microcomputer technology in the Silicon Valley. The Club met from 1975 to 1987 as an informal gathering of enthusiasts, hobbyists, and engineers.

items.title: Housing for movable cursor control (mouse) for a video display : plans and drawings, ca. 1981-1985
items.description: Patent application, business correspondence, design drawings and plans, photographs. Also includes a short history of the mouse project at Apple written by Bill Lapson, 1982.

items.title: ICONCEPTS; the Macintosh User's Monthly Newsletter
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: James Ferris collection of Apple publications and ephemera, circa 1978-1989
items.description: Documents and artifacts related to James Ferris' (aka "The Art God") tenure at Regis McKenna Advertising and as Creative Services Director at Apple Computer, ca. 1979-1985. Apple Inc. pamphlets, magazine articles, manuals, and marketing materials that were distributed to national and international Apple computer dealers.

items.title: Jerrold C. Manock papers relating to his work with Apple Computer, circa 1966-2007
items.description: He worked for Apple Computer from 1977 to 1984, contributing to housing designs for the Apple II, Apple III, and earlier compact Apple Macintosh computers. Design materials from Jerrold Manock's career in product design engineering. Included are blue-line drawings, labeled artifacts such as design models, presentations, and documentation from various projects, particularly at Apple Computer.

items.title: Joseph Meyers collection of Apple computer manuals, 1978-1984
Kilobaud : hobby computer newsletter : clubs-dealers-industry
items.description: Newsletter related to the magazine Kilobaud, which was published monthly from Jan. 1977-Dec. 1978. The newsletter includes solicitations for articles and editorials, meeting notices, and advertising for subscriptions, back issues, and related materials.

items.title: Lee Felsenstein papers, ca. 1975-1995
items.description: Lee Felsenstein is an electronic design engineer known for his contributions to the early history of personal computing. The papers of computer designer Lee Felsenstein contain material about the development of personal computers through the 1970s and 80s.

items.title: Onyx Systems, Inc. records, 1979
items.description: Historical material on original staff positions, stock holdings, etc. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: People's Computer Company
items.description: The People’s Computer Company (PCC) was founded by Bob Albrecht and George Firedrake in Menlo Park, California. Called People’s Computer Company, People’s Computers, or Recreational Computing at various times in its history, the newsletter played an important role in areas such as computer games, computer education, and promotion of the BASIC programming language. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Phil Roybal collection of Apple Computer artifacts, circa 1970s - 1990s.
items.description: The collection consists of the first peripheral manual written circa January 1978, "Parallel Printer Interface Card Installation and Operating Manual," a tote bag, a belt buckle and 15 small pins.

items.title: Raines Cohen papers and t-shirt collection, circa 1985-2001
items.description: Raines Cohen cofounded the Berkeley Macintosh Users Group (BMUG) in 1986 while enrolled at the University of California at Berkeley as a Geography major. Collection includes the Berkeley Macintosh User Group (BMUG) newsletters in print and on CD-ROM discs, and related files kept by Raines Cohen about his involvement with the group and early Macintosh computer communities. Artifacts include buttons, pins, and t-shirts designed for various User Groups including BMUG and associated groups in the computer industry.

items.title: Stanford Macintosh Users' Group newsletter
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Stanford Macintosh Users' Group Newsletter, 1985-1989
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Stanford Macintosh Users' Group records, 1984-1990
items.description: The Stanford Macintosh Users' Group is a volunteer organization composed of Stanford University students and community members whose purpose is to act as a clearinghouse to exchange information about the Apple Macintosh computer. Correspondence, memorabilia, financial records, newsletters, telephone memo books, and other miscellaneous records pertaining to their activities on campus.

items.title: Stanford University, Center for Reliable Computing, records, 1962-1999
items.description: The Center for Reliable Computing (CRC), under the direction of Edward J. McCluskey, is involved in research on fault-tolerant computing, computer architecture, testing, and logic design. Bound volumes of publications produced by the Center for Reliable Computing, published from 1962-1999.

items.title: The Atari Users Group newsletter
items.description: Includes meeting announcements for the Bay Area Atari Users Group, want ads, programming tips and tricks, and software reviews.

items.title: The cider press
items.description: "The monthly newsletter of the Apple Computer Information & Data Exchange of Rochester."

items.title: The Club Mac News
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Time-Life access: Apple (serial publication)
items.description: A report for business users of Apple computers and compatible systems.

items.title: Washington Apple Pi collection of Apple II user group newsletters and publications, circa 1977-1999
items.description: Washington Apple Pi [http://www.wap.org] is a non-profit Apple user group which was founded in 1978 in Washington, D.C., and has published a newsletter since 1979. Washington Apple Pi also traded newsletters with many other Apple user groups in an informal exchange program, and these issues constitute the majority of the collection.

items.title: Welcome to Macintosh [videorecording] : the documentary for the rest of us
items.description: 'Welcome to Macintosh explores the many ways Apple Computer (now Apple, Inc.) has changed the world, from the early days of the Apple-I to the latest the company has to offer"--Container. Includes interviews with Wayne Bibbens, Charles DeVore, Richard Halsey, Andy Hertzfeld, Guy Kawasaki, Leander Kahney, Jim Reekes, Ron Wayne, and Wayne Wenzlaff.
items.era_note: [Most of this 2008 documentary, with interviews of early Apple figures such as Ron Wayne and Andy Hertzfeld, concerns this period.]

items.title: William H. Turner collection of Apple Computer material, late 1970s.
items.description: Collection consists of papers from the late 1970s, mostly related to parts and shipping at Apple Computer. Also included are magazine clippings.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Computing (general)

items.title: Clifford Stowers collection of Apple Computer manuals, circa 1978-1985
Douglas C. Engelbart papers, 1953-2005
items.description: This collection documents that activities of Douglas C. Engelbart, a computer scientist whose pioneering work in the 1950s and 1960s (first at SRI International, later at Tymshare, Inc.) led to the development of the interactive personal computer. Professional papers, including correspondence, research proposals, technical reports, notes, journals, and computer disks, as well as audiovisual material on a variety of media.

items.title: Edward A. Feigenbaum, "Towards a science of scientific thought" [videorecording]
items.description: Videotape of a lecture given September 30, 1976. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Eighth annual institute in Computer Science : program announcement, n.d.
Jef Raskin papers, 1975-2005
items.description: Jef Raskin is an independent consultant on interface design, best known for having created the Macintosh computer project at Apple, the one button mouse and the click-and-drag paradigm for using it, the Apple style of computer documentation, and the Canon Cat and other interface-based products. The collection contains correspondence, print-outs of email, manuscripts of various articles authored by Raskin and his colleagues, appointment books, and various publications collected by Raskin.

items.title: Joel Shurkin interviews for his book, Engines of the Mind, 1977-1982
John L. Hennessy Personal Papers
items.description: Formerly the tenth President of Stanford University, he is also a computer scientist who co-founded MIPS Computer Systems and Atheros Communications. The materials consist of publications, research and teaching files, professional files and correspondence, and audiovisual materials.

items.title: Kathleen Hennessey papers
items.description: Audrey Kathleen Hennessey is a data scientist, researcher, and educator whose work has primarily focused on systems, information processing, and organizational automation. The Kathleen Hennessey papers include a wide range of materials, largely centered around computer science and information processing.

items.title: Mark Weiser papers, ca. 1969-1999
items.description: Dr. Mark Weiser was the Chief Technologist at the Xerox Palo Alto Research Center (PARC). Weiser's work since 1988 focused on Ubiquitous Computing, a program he initiated that envisions PC's being replaced with invisible computers embedded in everyday objects. Collection contains correspondence, project files, patents, business plans, notebooks and computer files.

items.title: Naonori Kohira Photography Archive
items.description: Includes portraits taken by Naonori Kohira of: Steve Jobs, Bill Gates, Douglas Engelbart, Alan Kay, John Sculley, and Timothy Leary.
items.era_note: [Most of this archive, portraits of personal computer pioneers and a photographic history of the personal computer, concerns this period.]

items.title: Robert W. Taylor papers, circa 1932-2017
items.description: Robert William Taylor (February 10th, 1932 – April 13th, 2017) was a project manager, executive director, and laboratory chief known for overseeing a number of advances in personal computing and internet technology throughout the tenure of his career. The Robert W. Taylor papers contain memoranda, correspondence, technical documentation and specifications, photographs, slides, negatives, newspaper and magazine clippings, printed emails, notes, and a variety of media on tape and disc.

items.title: Ron Perrotta collection of Apple Computer material, circa 1980s-1990s.
items.description: Mr. Perrotta worked at Apple Computer from 1982-1993. The collection includes unopened software (Apple II and Lotus 1-2-3), posters, pins, promotional items, material from 1984 including an annual report, Super Bowl advertising photo book, and a Macintosh brochure.

items.title: Stan Augarten computer history collection, ca. 1965-1994
items.description: Augarten is an American author of two books on the history of computing, "State of the art : a photographic history of the integrated circuit" (1983) and "Bit by bit : an illustrated history of computers" (1984). Collection consists of video and photographic material assembled for book and CD-ROM projects, especially "Bit by Bit."

items.title: Stanford University, Computer Science Department, Stanford Computer Forum Distinguished Lecture Series, video recordings, 1978-1998
items.description: Lectures by computer professionals and professors from Stanford and other universities presented to the Computer Systems Laboratory Seminar, the Department of Computer Science Colloquium, and other special events.

items.title: Stanford University, Computer Systems Laboratory, Technical Reports
items.description: Collection contains 384 PDF laboratory technical report files created by various members of the Stanford University Department of Computer Science.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Computer Science, films
items.description: The Department of Computer Science was established in 1965.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Computer Science, technical reports
items.description: Collection contains 972 PDF technical reports by various authors from within the Stanford Computer Science Department.

items.title: The computer chronicles : television series, 1984
items.description: Both Stuart Cheifet and Gary Kildall were involved in the production of the series.

items.title: The Famous Computer Cafe collection, circa 1970s-1980s
items.description: Audio tapes and associated documents of The Famous Computer Cafe, including approximately 15 reel-to-reel recordings, plus production documents, transcripts, and digital files.

items.title: The powersharing series: people, computers and you, : audio cassettes with resource guide, 1986
items.description: An artificial collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of Northern California's Silicon Valley. Includes promotional material, price lists, conference proceedings, newsletters, etc.

items.title: The scope of the computer : portfolio of illustrated articles, 1970-1972
Unicode collection
items.description: Unicode is an international encoding standard that allows consistent encoding, representation, and handling of text expressed in many writing systems globally. This collection primarily consists of meeting notes, reports, minutes, agendas, research material, drafts, correspondence, and other documents highlighting the development and output of the Unicode Standard, a universal character encoding schema, and related internationalization standards by the Unicode Technical Committee.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Construction and civil engineering practice

items.title: Harold W. Burke papers, 1945-1985
items.description: Harold W. Burke was an engineering geologist, with particular interest in structural geology, limestone problems, and small hydroelectrics. He did field work around the world in evaluation of foundation problems, particularly for dams and tunnels. Correspondence, reports, subject files, unpublished research, computer data files, bibliography, photographs, and maps.

items.title: Hermann Zutraun engineering drawings, 1968-1985
items.description: A civil engineer whose office was in San Francisco. He consulted on numerous San Francisco Bay Area projects, most often for Homer J. Olsen, Inc. and Kulchin-Wagner, Inc. Included are plans for the Stanford High Energy Physics Lab, Lawrence Livermore Lab, the Dumbarton Bridge approach structure, the San Francisco Ferry Terminal, San Mateo County waste water treatment plant, BART stations, fountains, tunnels, and other public buildings.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Electronics industry (national and international)

items.title: David C. Jung papers, 1968-1983
items.description: David C. Jung served as Staff Vice President, Information Specialists Group (ISG) Market Development for the McDonnell Douglas Information Systems Group. Market reports, investment evaluations, management studies and similar related materials authored and assembled by Quantum Science Corporation. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Electronic materials technology news : a monthly newsletter from Business Communications Company, Inc., 1987-1990
items.description: Includes columns on business analysis, semiconductor news, technical information, U.S. and foreign patent information, and information sources.

items.title: Global Electronics, 1985
items.description: Global Electronics newsletter, n. 52, April 1985, n. 53, May 1985, n. 54, June 1985. A collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of California's "Silicon Valley."

items.title: International high technology ephemera collection, 1983 - 1994
items.description: Collection contains various issues of foreign language high technology journals and ephemeral items.

items.title: Peter Cunningham INPUT collection, 1975-2000
items.description: Materials include INPUT business records such as reports, backup research materials, contract files, contact reports, project planning documents, media files, and Procurement Analysis Reports. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Steven E. Barryte collection of semiconductor and computer industries : publications and documentation, circa 1970-1999
items.description: He has worked for ITT Aerospace/Optical, Litton Data Systems, Recognition Systems, Hughes Aircraft and Raytheon.

items.title: Ted Nelson collection of technology ephemera, 1950s-1990s.
items.description: Catalogs and other promotional material, mostly concerning electronics, mostly from the 1960s and 70s. Ted Nelson, often referred to as the "father of hypertext," has a long history in the field of computing. This collection primarily contains mailed promotional material in the form of catalogs and advertisements, much of which was requested by Nelson via reader service cards in trade magazines from the 1960s through the early 1990s.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — General manufacturing

items.title: Stauffer Chemical Company records, 1881-1987
items.description: The Stauffer Chemical Company was founded in 1885 in San Francisco by two European immigrants, John Stauffer, Sr. and Christian de Guigne. The company mainly produced herbicides for corn and rice. The materials include minutes books, financial statements, correspondence, and photographs.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Internet and the web

items.title: A History of the Internet, 1962-1992 : poster
items.description: Includes a time-line of key events, together with graphics and portraits.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Labor and professional organizations

items.title: Anne Loftis papers, 1953-1978
items.description: Research materials gathered and compiled for the book Anne Loftis co-authored with Dick Meister, A LONG TIME COMING. The papers document the various efforts to unionize America's farm workers during the 20th century and include materials on major unions.

items.title: Anthony R. Soto papers, 1950-1993
items.description: Antonio R. Soto (1921-1996) was the first Chicano pastor of Santa Clara County. Soto was also very active in civil rights movements, particularly regarding the rights of migrant laborers. Manuscripts, subject files, and newsclippings, primarily relating to Soto's research and teaching on Hispanics in the Catholic Church and migrant workers in California.

items.title: Bay Area Biosystematists records, 1954-1996
items.description: A discussion group formed in the 1930s made up of Bay Area (Stanford, San Francisco, Berkeley, Davis/Sacramento) scientists with an interest in evolutionary biology. John Thomas served as group archivist. The files are predominantly those of John Thomas from 1985 to 1994.

items.title: Beauty shop : portfolio of photographic prints and text, 1974
items.description: The text is primarily quotes from beauty operators and clients, presumably with the photographs of those quoted. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- California Farm Workers, 1970-1974
items.description: This gallery features Bob Fitch's photographs of farm worker labor and housing conditions in Watsonville, Coachella, Fresno, and other parts of California's Central Valley in the early 1970s.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- Cesar Chavez/UFW gallery, 1968-1974
items.description: Between 1968 and 1974, at the invitation of the UFW President and organizer Cesar Chavez, Bob Fitch photographed union organizing activities including; agricultural field work, living conditions, pickets, marches, funerals, anti-picket police brutality, prominent supporters, intimate planning sessions and the first union contracts in 1970 (Coachella Valley, CA).

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- Farmworker Union Field Organizing & Special Actions, 1969-1975
items.description: Using constituency recruitment, coalition building, political lobbying, and media exposure techniques learned from the Black Civil Rights achievements, Cesar Chavez and United Farm Worker union colleagues focused national and global attention on the farmworker plight. UFW member fortitude, tactical cleverness, spiritual tenacity, and bravery in the face of violence are some of the qualities embodied in this gallery of images taken by Bob Fitch.

items.title: David Bacon photography archive, circa 1976-2019
items.description: David Bacon (born 1948) is a photojournalist, author, political activist, and union organizer who has focused on labor issues, particularly those related to immigrant labor. Physical materials are predominantly photographic; primarily prints, with some slides, of David Bacon's work as a photojournalist.

items.title: Electronics workers on the move! : handbill
items.description: Cites the San Francisco Chinatown strike by workers at Lee Mah electronics and the strike at Ruckers Electronics in Concord, summarizing the developments so far, urging the reader to join their picket lines.

items.title: Ernesto Galarza papers, 1936-1993
items.description: Correspondence, reports, minutes, legal documents, notes, newsletters, press releases, newsclippings, statistical information, questionnaires and photographs documenting Galarza's career as a labor organizer, scholar, Research Director in the National Agricultural Workers Union (1947-1960), and nationally prominent Mexican American activist. The Galarza Papers are particularly rich in information about Mexican and Mexican American farm workers in California from 1948 to 1960.

items.title: Frank Bardacke papers, 1960-1990
items.description: Frank Bardacke is a historian, author, educator, trade unionist, and political activist. Contains manuscript drafts of his book "Trampling Out The Vintage," United Farm Worker administrative material, research files, correspondence, and recordings of interviews and UFW meetings.

items.title: Henry Santiestevan papers, circa 1975-2010
items.description: In 1958 he took a position with United Auto Workers (UAW) and worked alongside their President, Walter Reuther. Through Mr. Santiestevan's position as an editor he became a close confidant of labor organizer Cesar Chavez and assist with public relations and media campaigns for the United Farm Workers. Papers relating to Hispanic-American history, Hispanic labor history, activist organizations, etc., including correspondence, reports and other writings of Henry Santiestevan, subject files, photographs, and miscellaneous publications.

items.title: James L. Vizzard papers, 1942-1983
items.description: Correspondence, reports, legislative testimony, speeches, articles, minutes, agendas, newsclippings, oral history tape and transcript, and photographs, documenting Vizzard's career as a lobbyist and worker on behalf of rural poor, migrants and braceros. As the Washington representative for the National Catholic Rural Life Conference (and later for the United Farm Workers), Vizzard was instrumental in influencing legislation aimed at improving the lot of the largely unorganized agricultural labor force.

items.title: Marion Moses, M.D., papers
items.description: The Dr. Marion Moses, M.D., papers consist of her career spanning fifty years as a nurse, physician, and advocate for farmworkers with the United Farm Workers Union (UFW). The collection consists of her many years of work with the UFW, meeting notes, correspondence with Cesar Chavez, Eliseo Medina, Jessica Govea, Marshal Ganz among many more UFW founders and organizers.

items.title: MRP (material requirements planning) data archive and related projects, 1976-1991
items.description: The materials document the activities undertaken as part of a social science research project, "Knowledge acquisition at work." The project investigated the implementation of a material requirements planning system, or MRP, an early computer based system of production control and inventory management. The study focused on the impact that new technologies have on workers and work, and in particular how workers learn to use new information technologies.

items.title: Northern California Botanists : material kept by John H. Thomas, 1970-1991
items.description: Includes correspondence, agendas, minutes, mailing lists, etc. for the Northern California Botanists. One folder each for the Central California Botanists and the San Francisco Bay Area Center for Systematics and Evolutionary Biology (1972).

items.title: Photographs of the United Farm Workers march from San Francisco to Salinas, 1979, and accompanying documentation, 1979-1982
items.description: Consists of 8 photographs, 1 contact sheet and 1 sheet of negatives taken of the United Farm Workers march from San Francisco to Salinas in 1979.

items.title: Protest posters including images of Watsonville and bombing of El Salvador, 1986-1987 : lithographs, nd.
items.description: Nineteen prints from a series, Images of Watsonville, depicting laborers with families based on a strike in 1985 when workers, primarily Mexican women, would not cross the picket line for over a year. Five posters address the repression and bombings in El Salvador and depict images of women and children.

items.title: Solomon Feferman papers, 1938-2016 (inclusive), 1980-1983 (bulk)
items.description: Solomon Feferman was a Professor of Mathematics and Philosophy and the Patrick Suppes Family Professor of Humanities and Sciences at Stanford University, he became Emeritus in 2004. The first series primarily document Feferman's term as president of the Association for Symbolic Logic from 1980 to 1982. The material consists largely of correspondence, meeting agendas and minutes, and material from symposia and lectures.

items.title: Stanford/USE negotiating sessions : minutes, 1973-1975
items.description: USE, United Stanford Employees, Local 680, S.E.I.U., AFL-CIO, won the right to represent technical, maintenance, and service workers at Stanford University in June of 1973. Minutes from contract negotiations between the University and United Stanford Employees, 1973-1975, and a draft of the agreement, 1974.

items.title: Support Rucker Strike! : handbill
items.description: On the strike by women workers at Rucker Electronics in Concord, which had refused to recognize their union. Describes an attack by police on picketers on June 11. Asks the reader to join the picket line or contribute to the strike fund.

items.title: United Farmworker linocut prints / by Susan Due Pearcy, 1972-1973
items.description: Artwork is mainly linocut, also included are two woodcuts.

items.title: Victor Salandini papers, 1952-1989
items.description: Roman Catholic priest who was both a scholar of farm labor problems in California and an active participant with the Mexican American labor movement, particularly the United Farm Workers. Includes correspondence, research files, talks, papers, publications, parish work, community work, articles and information on Cesar Chavez (and correspondence with), book reviews, farm labor contracts, and research on the Reclamation Law of 1902.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Magnetic recording and data storage

items.title: Ampex Corporation records, ca. 1944-2005 (bulk 1944-1999)
items.description: Primarily known for their mass storage systems, instrumentation/data recorders, helical scan tape drives, robotic storage libraries, post-production switchers, digital special effects, tape cartridges, and system components. Artifacts (including audio and video recording devices, recordings, and memorabilia) formerly comprising the Ampex Museum collection; approximately 25,000 photographs (including negatives and prints) and related indexes; documents in hard copy or microfilm form (including manuals, memos, sales materials, public relations materials, articles, drawings, engineering notes, specifications, and manuscripts); and other miscellaneous material relating to the history of the Ampex Corporation and the recording industry.

items.title: Mary Beth and Richard Hess technical manual collection, 1967-2000
items.description: Since focusing on audio preservation Richard has contributed significantly to the field of sound recording preservation, especially magnetic media preservation. Contains technical user manuals for products built and sold by the Ampex Corporation, Grass Valley Group, Hewlett-Packard Corporation and other technology firms. Includes manuals, bulletins, catalogs, brochures, and schematics largely concerning the use, maintenance and repair of audiovisual equipment.

items.title: National Teleconsultants collection
items.description: Collection consists of sales, installation, maintenance, and user documentation for televison broadcasting and professional video and audio equipment. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Ray Dolby papers, circa 1940s - 2000s
items.description: Ray Milton Dolby was an American engineer whose inventions and company, Dolby Laboratories, have had a profound effect on the storage, transmission, and reproduction of audio and video. Materials in the collection include Dolby's schoolwork, circuit drawings and engineering schematics for work both at Ampex and Dolby Laboratories, research notes and calculations, patents, correspondence, ephemera from Ampex and from the early years of Dolby Laboratories, and photographs.

items.title: Read-Rite Corporation records, circa 1969-2004
items.description: Materials consist of the 1983 and 1984 business plans of Read-Write Corporation, as well as a 1969 and 2004 CV of its founder, John Osborne. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Networking and telecommunications

items.title: An annotated bibliography on local computer networks / by John F. Shoch
items.description: This bibliography covers the general area of local computer networking. The references have been divided into two major parts, including the primary sectio on local networks, and a second section on the important related subject of radio-based systems.

items.title: Donald MacQuivey papers, circa 1950-1990
items.description: Donald R. MacQuivey (1913-1993) was an engineer and policy analyst in the field of telecommunications. MacQuivey's work largely centered on radio frequency allocation and management, as well as satellite communication and its implementation. The professional papers of Donald MacQuivey consists primarily of correspondence, memoranda, and reports kept by Macquivey in the course of his work.

items.title: Michael M. Roberts papers, 1967-1986
items.description: Michael M. Roberts was the Deputy Director of Information Technology Services at Stanford University, with executive responsibilities in Stanford's computing, communications, and information systems programs. The contents of this collection primarily consist of documents used in the development and distribution of the telecommunication system on Stanford campus during Robert's tenure as the Deputy Director of Information Technology Services.

items.title: Paul Baran papers, circa 1959-2010
items.description: Included are papers from Baran's time at RAND, Institute for the Future, CableData Associates, Comprint, Equatorial Communications, Telebit, Packet Technologies, Stratacom, Metricom, Interfax, Com21, Rosum, as well as numerous public service committees and non-profit organizations. Paul Baran, 1926-2011, was a Polish-American engineer who helped create the technical underpinnings for the Arpanet, the government-sponsored precursor to today's Internet. He was one of the three earliest researchers of packet switching techniques, and went on to start several companies and develop other technologies that are an essential part of the Internet and other modern digital communication.

items.title: Pup: an internetwork architecture / by David R. Boggs, John F. Shoch, Edward A. Taft, and Robert M. Metcalfe
items.description: Pup is the name of an internet packet format (PARC Universal Packet), a hierarchy of protocols, and a style of internetwork communication. The report explores important design issues, sets forth principles that have guided the Pup design, discusses the present implementation in moderate detail, and summarizes experience with an operational internetwork.

items.title: Stanford NIRT project records, 1974-1978
items.description: Stanford entered into a research project with the National Iranian Radio and Television agency in 1974 to study and recommend a satellite-based communication system for Iran and how to utilize it for Iran's educational radio and television. Records include memoranda, reports, and correspondence, largely of Bruce Lusignan, project director, 1974-77; and the report "A Developmental Plan for Educational Radio and Television of Iran," June 1978, by Stuart Cooney, Lyle M. Nelson, and D. Glenn Starlin of the Dept. of Communications.

items.title: United States of America v. American Telephone & Telegraph, et al: legal documents, 1974-1982
items.description: Key documents and selected testimony in antitrust action. This set consists of photocopied typescripts of documents and testimony presented at this milestone case, which resulted in the breakup of America's largest technology-based corporation. Ths testimony identifies the justifications and consequences of these steps and provides a wealth of information on the nature, size and scope of the American telecommunications industry and the impact of Bells System integration on the progress and strength of American science, technology and industry.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Radio, vacuum tubes and microwave

items.title: CPI/Eimac (Communication & Power Industries, Eimac Division) media collection and files, circa 1944-1990
items.description: The Communication Products Industry (CPI), Eimac Division media collection includes photographic media, motion film, and sound recordings produced from the mid-1940s to late 1980s by Eitel-McCullough Incorporated (Eimac), an early innovator in the development and application of high frequency vacuum tubes and radar technology founded in San Bruno, California in 1934.

items.title: Don Preist papers, circa 1934-2002
items.description: The Don Preist papers include 32 containers of print and photographic materials dating back to the 1930s, and document Preist's life and his involvement with innovative research and development for transmitter tubes and klystron beams while he was a lead engineer with the Eimac and Varian companies. The collection includes technical reports and drawings; inter-office memos; research notes and calculations; correspondence; and photographs.

items.title: Edward Ginzton papers, circa 1937-1992
items.description: Co-founder of Varian Associates and a pioneer in microwave tube technology and linear accelerator development. Papers regarding Ginzton's activities at Stanford University, with Varian Associates, and on national committees and local organizations. Includes correspondence, manuscripts, memoranda, journals, publications, technical reports, manufacturing reports, oral history materials, and photographs.

items.title: Lester L. Libby papers, ca. 1936-1984
items.description: The Lester L. Libby papers consist of files created and maintained by Lester Louis Libby (1916-2002) pertaining to his work in the technical field of sound engineering and the application of microwave frequency technologies in various industries including radio, television, and early electronics from the 1930s to the 1970s. Materials include Libby's resarch notebooks, work papers, diagrams and schematics, articles he authored, and patents received.

items.title: Marvin Chodorow papers, 1929-1993 (inclusive), 1943-1974 (bulk)
items.description: He served as Chair of the Department of Applied Physics from 1962-69 and Director of the Edward L. Ginzton Laboratory, 1959-78. Collection largely pertains to his research in linear accelerators, klystrons, and microwaves; professional activities; classes he taught at Stanford; and administrative duties at Stanford.

items.title: Oswald G. Villard papers, 1932-1998 (inclusive), 1958-1998 (bulk)
items.description: Oswald Garrison Villard Jr. (1916-2004), a leader in electromagnetic theory and experimental methods, earned his engineer's degree in 1943 and his Ph.D. in 1949 at Stanford, studying with Dr. F. E. Terman. The papers include correspondence, articles and research papers, memoranda, reports, research files, contracts, minutes, and other materials, 1958-1998. The collection also includes instruction manuals and a log for radio station W6YX, 1932-1933 (club station at Stanford).

items.title: Tech-notes, 1974-1991
items.description: A technical periodical published bi-monthly dealing with applied engineering and science. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Varian oral history project, 1989-1990, phase one.
items.description: Fifteen people were interviewed for phase one. The transcripts of their interviews are not meant to be a comprehensive written work, but simply the personal recollections of those who had a hand in shaping Varian's first two decades. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: William W. Eitel papers, ca. 1953-1979
items.description: This collection contains the papers of William W. Eitel, co-founder of Eitel-McCollough, Inc. and a distinguished engineer. Included are papers depicting the 1970s battle between private ham radio operators and the federal government over radio wave rights, his involvement with several technical firms and ham radio organizations, and personal correspondence with many friends and associates.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Semiconductors

items.title: "Silicon Run" [videorecording]
items.description: Concerns silicon chip fabrication; filmed at the Center for Integrated Systems at Stanford and at various industrial sites in Santa Clara County, California.

items.title: A case study in realizing the American dream : Sanders and Advanced Micro Devices : the first fifteen years, 1969-1984 : typescript, 2004
items.description: Insider's story of the development of AMD, originally written in 1984 and reworked in 2004. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Andrew S. Grove papers, 1968-2013
items.description: Andrew S. Grove was a businessman and author who is best known for his role in the founding and growth of Intel Corporation, which at one time was the world's largest manufacturer of semiconductors. The papers of Intel founder Andrew Grove include files related to speaking engagements, writing by and about Grove, photographs, and other material.

items.title: Ben M. Warren papers, 1971-2019
items.description: Materials relating to Mr. Warren's work as an engineer on semiconductor chips at Intel from 1971-1978. Items include overlays, articles, advertisements, and a contextualizing memo from Mr. Warren explaining a bit about the items in the collection.

items.title: Don C. Hoefler's Microelectronic News with Manager's Casebook : newsletter, 1982 Sept. 11-1984 Jan. 7.
items.description: Industry and company gossip.

items.title: Fairchild Semiconductor Corporation: files of Steve Allen, photographer, circa 1960-1985
items.description: The Steve Allen photographs of Fairchild Semiconductor contains photographs of professional photographer Steve Allen, a Fairchild Semiconductor and National Semiconductor Corporation employee from 1966 through about 1997. The collection documents executive employees, sales force, fabrication facilities, and products of Fairchild Semiconductor.

items.title: Fairchild Semiconductor technical reports and progress reports, 1965-1987
Gerald Pearson papers, 1934-1987
items.description: Co-inventor of the solar cell, Pearson held a total of 34 U.S. patents relating to thermistors, transistors, silicon power diodes, and solar cells. Correspondence, 1961-1982, research notebooks on optical properties of solids and other subjects, technical reports prepared during his tenure at Bell Telephone Laboratories, reprints, photographs and slides, legal papers relating to patents, transcript of an oral history interview, memorabilia, and other miscellaneous items.

items.title: Gordon Moore papers 1958-2005
items.description: Moore and Robert Noyce left Fairchild in July 1968 to establish the Intel Corporation in Santa Clara with the initial goal of developing and producing large scale integrated products. This collection contains Moore's Intel lab notebooks, personal and business correspondence, Intel presentations, memos and white papers, personal notes from meetings, greeting cards, photographs, cassette tapes and videos. The collection consists of business correspondence related to Intel Corporation, reports, overhead transparencies, presentation slides related to Intel Corporation and the semiconductor industry.

items.title: History of the Integrated Circuit : interviews on 30 cassette tapes, c. 1986
items.description: The most important individuals featured in the article were Jack Kilby and Bob Noyce. The Supreme Court judged them to be co-inventors of the integrated circuit.

items.title: Intel Corporation annual and financial reports, 1972-1996 (inclusive), 1972-1987 (bulk)
items.description: Reports from 1972-1987, and 1996. Also contains notices for meetings. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Intel Corporation collection of Inteleads and other publications, circa 1979-1989
items.description: Intel is a corporation and technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California that was founded by Gordon Moore and Robert Noyce. Collection primarily contains ten years of Inteleads, Intel Corporation's employee newsletter. The collection also includes other magazines, promotional booklets, recruitment brochures, users manuals, technical specifications, etc. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Interviews with Gordon Moore, Robert Noyce, and Roger Borovoy : transcripts and CD, 1982
items.description: Journalist T.R. Reid, author of THE CHIP, recorded these interviews in 1982 while conducting research for his book. Roger Borovoy was counsel for Fairchild and Intel.

items.title: Jack Balletto papers, 1982
items.description: A personal account of the founding of VLSI Technology, an important Silicon Valley semiconductor firm.

items.title: John Backus' "Conductors, Nonconductors and Semiconductors" : two typescripts
items.description: 2 typescripts on "Conductors, Nonconductors and Semiconductors" and original mailing envelope.

items.title: Oral history : interview by Rob Walker, 1991
items.description: Includes comments about VLSI by James A. Rowson and Jack Balletto.
items.era_note: [Most of this 1991 interview, including comments on VLSI by James A. Rowson and Jack Balletto, concerns these years.]

items.title: Oral history; interviews with David A. Hodges conducted by Christophe Lécuyer, 2008-2010
items.description: David Hodges is currently Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences at the University of California at Berkeley. In the 1970s and 1980s Professor Hodges was active in teaching and research on microelectronics technology and design. Since 1984 his research has centered on semiconductor manufacturing systems.
items.era_note: [Most of these 2008-2010 interviews concern his teaching and research on microelectronics in the 1970s and 1980s.]

items.title: Phase locked loops applications book and two data manuals, 1972-1977
Posters, 1985-1986
items.description: THE MAKING OF AN INTEGRATED CIRCUIT, 1985 and SILICON VALLEY GENEALOGY, 1986. An artificial collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of Northern California's Silicon Valley.

items.title: Raytheon Semiconductor files kept to monitor the electronics industry, 1965-1986
items.description: Raytheon's Semiconductor Division was established in Mountain View, California in 1968 by its parent company, Raytheon Company of Lexington, Massachusetts, which, in 1990, was described as "one of the largest and most diversified electronics companies in the United States." The collection consists of files that Raytheon's Semiconductor Division kept to monitor both the progress of their competitors and trends in the electronics industry.

items.title: Research material about Robert Noyce, ca. 1970-2005
items.description: The collection documents the research phase of Berlin's biography of Robert Noyce, entitled THE MAN BEHIND THE MICROCHIP. The collection consists of photographs, transcripts and audiotapes of interviews, speeches given by Noyce and others, and background research on the history of the micro-chip industry and the growth of Silicon Valley.

items.title: Ricardo Alfaro collection of Fairchild material, circa 1963-1998
items.description: Ricardo "Kim" Alfaro worked as the Promotion Manager at Fairchild Semiconductor, writing some of the first marketing brochures for microchips there. The material consists of Fairchild brochures, planning documents, a "Goodbye Fairchild" Party planning binder, ephemera related to the deaths of Lewis H. Young and Robert N. Noyce, conference papers, business cards, computer chips, and other objects.

items.title: Rob Walker papers, 1959-2005
items.description: Rob Walker (1935-2016) was a Silicon Valley native and Silicon Valley educated electrical engineer who was involved with semiconductors since the 1960s at Fairchild, Intel and as a founder of LSI Logic. His collection contains presentation slides, reports, sales material, and other documentation from from LSI Logic Corp.; articles and papers given by him; documents from Fairchild Semiconductor; specifications from Lawrence Livermore Laboratories; and documentation from Philco Corp.

items.title: Robert Lipp oral history : interview by Rob Walker, 1991
items.description: CEO and founder of California Devices Inc. (CDI). [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]
items.era_note: [Most of this 1991 interview, with the founder and chief executive of California Devices Inc., concerns these years.]

items.title: Robert N. Noyce papers, circa 1948-1990
items.description: Robert Noyce (1927-1990) was an American physicist and entrepreneur who co-founded Fairchild Semiconductor in 1957 and Intel Corporation in 1968. Collection includes many personal materials covering family, childhood and his academic career. Also included are documents and materials from Noyce's work at Shockley Semiconductor, Fairchild Semiconductor, Intel, and the Semiconductor Industry Association.

items.title: Robert N. Noyce; an interview conducted by Michael F. Wolff : transcript, 1975 September 19.
Robert Noyce papers, circa 1949-1990
items.description: Robert Noyce and Gordon E. Moore founded Intel in 1968 when they left Fairchild Semiconductor. The Robert N. Noyce papers, circa 1948-1990, contains published materials relating to the work of Robert Noyce and his legacy.

items.title: SILICON DESTINY : oral history cassette tapes, videos, and transcripts, 1995
items.description: In addition to the interviews, the collection contains background and reference material on LSI Logic Corporation and two corrected proofs of the manuscript. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]
items.era_note: [Most of the collection, interviews and background material for a history of LSI Logic Corporation, concerns these years.]

items.title: Stanford University, Center for Integrated Systems, records, 1978-1997
items.description: The proposal for the Center for Integrated Systems was written in 1978 as a joint effort by Electrical Engineering Professors Michael J. Flynn, James F. Gibbons, John G. Linvill, and James D. Meindl. The materials consist of background and planning documents, meeting minutes, correspondence, and proposals relating to the founding of the Center for Integrated Systems at Stanford University. Linvill, Meindl, and other colleagues had realized that the exponential growth of semiconductor technology was creating problems and challenges that were too big and complex for one discipline to tackle.

items.title: Tom Sawyer collection of semiconductor engineering applications and documentation
items.description: Materials related to the semiconductor industry. Collection includes design and systems notes (as well as Sawyer's own notes) for the AT&T No.1 ESS (Electronic Solid-state Switch-Central Office Switching System); materials documenting Sawyer's work as a consultant with Intel (1974-1985), designing and and implementing more than 50 projects using integrated circuits and the very earliest microprocessors; Intel design manuals; and manuals for products from Intel and National Semiconductor, as well as from Texas Instruments, Fairchild, RCA, NEC, Signetics, Digital Equipment Corp, Siemens, Harris, Rockwell, Teledyne Semiconductor, AMD, Mostek, and Motorola.
items.era_note: [Most of the collection, including his consulting work for Intel from 1974 to 1985, concerns this period.]

items.title: William Bradford Shockley papers, 1860-2002 (inclusive), 1940-1988 (bulk)
items.description: Professor of engineering at Stanford (1958-1975; emeritus 1975-1989). Shockley was co-recipient of the Nobel Prize in physics, 1956. Professional and personal papers relating to Professor Shockley's controversial interests in environment and genetic influences on intelligence; research on transistors and electronics; and science education. Also includes extensive family materials including diaries and correspondence.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Silicon Valley technology industry as a whole

items.title: "Portrait of a Pioneer: Fred Terman" [videorecording]
items.description: Interview with Frederick E. Terman conducted at Hewlett-Packard. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: "Silicon Valley" [videorecording]
items.description: Company Town: The first in a series of three documentaries on the Silicon Valley (Santa Clara County, California) introduces the people of the electronics industry, including entrepreneurs, engineers and scientists, blue-collar workers and immigrants. Profiles include Stephen Wozniak, Steven Jobs, Jerry Sanders, James Treybig and Robert Noyce.

items.title: Clyde F. Morgan collection of Silicon Valley pin-back buttons, circa 1970s-1980s
items.description: Collection consists of several dozen campaign-style buttons from Silicon Valley technology companies like Apple and IBM.

items.title: Douglas Menuez photography collection
items.description: Award-winning documentary photographer Douglas Menuez was born in Texas in 1957. Contains photographic materials, including prints, contact sheets, negatives and slides, relating to Menuez's documentation of major Silicon Valley companies, as well as to fine art book projects, photo essays and photo shoots for newspapers, magazines, advertising campaigns, annual reports and other commissioned work.

items.title: Hewlett-Packard ephemera collection, 1957-1994
items.description: Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard were friends and fellow graduates of Stanford University. Following their graduation from Stanford, the two founded the electronics firm Hewlett-Packard Co. in 1938. This collection contains annual reports, sporadic issues of various Hewlett-Packard publications, product information flyers and brochures, and manuals for various Hewlett-Packard products.

items.title: Miscellaneous items, 1975-1989
items.description: Includes WEST COAST COMPUTER FAIRE PREVIEW, February 1989, promotional brochure for Versatec, a Xerox company, a brochure entitled SANTA CLARA COUNTY, PAST, PRESENT, 1985, and the 1979 Lockheed annual report. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Product announcement, ca. 1986-1987
items.description: An artificial collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of Northern California's Silicon Valley. Includes promotional material, price lists, conference proceedings, newsletters, etc.

items.title: Silicon Valley ephemera collection (1st segment, subjects A-C), 1976-
items.description: A collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of California's "Silicon Valley." Includes promotional material, price lists, conference proceedings, newsletters, etc.

items.title: Silicon Valley ephemera collection (2nd segment, subjects D-K), 1976-
items.description: An artificial collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of Northern California's Silicon Valley. Includes promotional material, price lists, conference proceedings, newsletters, etc.

items.title: Silicon Valley ephemera collection (3rd segment, subjects L-N), 1976-
items.description: An artificial collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of Northern California's Silicon Valley. Includes promotional material, price lists, conference proceedings, newsletters, etc.

items.title: Silicon Valley ephemera collection (4th segment, subjects O-St), 1976-
items.description: An artificial collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of Northern California's Silicon Valley. Includes promotional material, price lists, conference proceedings, newsletters, etc.

items.title: Silicon Valley ephemera collection (5th segment, subjects Su - Z), 1976-
items.description: An artificial collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of Northern California's Silicon Valley. Includes promotional material, price lists, conference proceedings, newsletters, etc.

items.title: Silicon Valley ephemera collection, 1969-2001
items.description: An artificial collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of Northern California's Silicon Valley. Includes promotional material, price lists, conference proceedings, newsletters, etc.

items.title: Silicon Valley genealogy : posters, 1984 and 1995
items.description: Two schematic diagrams showing connections among the major electronics industries and their founders in Silicon Valley from 1946 to 1996.

items.title: Silicon Valley Magazine, 1982
items.description: Journal entitled SILICON VALLEY MAGAZINE, July 1982. A collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of California's "Silicon Valley."

items.title: Upside; 100 people who changed our world
