items.description: Special Issue No. 138 focuses on the history of Silicon Valley (Santa Clara County, California) and the electronics industry; topics include its agricultural and mining history, the role of the military (Lockheed), instrument makers (Varian and Hewlett Packard), medical technology, mainframe computers, venture capital and banking, computer games (Nolan Bushnell and Atari), computer graphics and imaging, marketing, storage industry (IBM), legal firms, and the role of UC Berkeley and Stanford University.
items.era_note: [This 2001 special issue is a history of Silicon Valley, and most of it concerns the electronics industry of these years.]

items.title: Varian Associates: an early history
items.description: Includes "Invention of the Klystron" by E. L. Ginzton; "The Founding of Varian Associates" by Russell Varian; and sections on "NMR, the Physics Experiment that Revolutionized Chemistry," "The Linear Accelerator," and "Vacuum Development."

items.title: Varian, Inc. records, 1950-2003
items.description: Varian, Inc. (known as Varian Associates from its founding until 1999) was one of California's first Silicon Valley companies. It was founded by Russell Varian, Sigurd Varian, and Edward Ginzton in 1948. Records include files on company history and anniversaries; press releases; photographs; annual reports and newsletters; manuals and other publications on products; and audio and video tapes.

items.title: Vernon Russell Anderson papers, 1953-2000
items.description: Papers include class notes, files, and records relating to the Vidar Corporation and Silicon Graphics. In addition to the bound memoir covering Anderson's life, there is a 14-page review written by Anderson about his engineering career.

items.title: Xerox Corporation records, 1986
items.description: Product announcements and advertising. Includes John H. Dessauer's book, MY YEARS WITH XEROX, Palo Alto (Calif.): PARC; 1986. An artificial collection of ephemeral publications issued by or referring to the microelectronics industry of Northern California's Silicon Valley.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Software

items.title: Alan Feinberg personal archive, 1977-2006
items.description: Materials consist of items related to Alan Feinberg's career in the Electronic Design Automation (EDA) and CAD/CAM industries. Major companies represented include Computervision and Synopsys.

items.title: Andy Hertzfeld notebooks, 1981-1983
items.description: Photocopies of original notebooks kept by Andy Hertzfeld while at Apple. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Ashton-Tate computer user manuals : evaluation copies, 1984-1990
items.description: Ashton-Tate (Ashton-Tate Corporation) was a US based software company best known for developing the popular dBASE database application.

items.title: Charles H. Irby papers, 1962-1975
items.description: Primarily correspondence, memos, working notes and technical reports from work on ARPANET, Control Meta Language, Modular Programming System and software and interface applications while Irby was at SRI International and Xerox Park.

items.title: Donald E. Knuth papers, 1962-2010
items.description: Donald Ervin Knuth's work established the analysis of algorithms as an academic field. In addition to fundamental contributions in several branches of theoretical computer science, Knuth is the creator of the TeX computer typesetting system, the related METAFONT font definition language and rendering system, and the Computer Modern family of typefaces. Papers reflect his work in the study and teaching of computer programming, computer systems for publishing, and mathematics.

items.title: DOS / Windows : software and manuals, ca. 1985-1995
Introduction to LISP for linguists [videorecording]
items.description: The Linguistics Society of America is a scholarly society whose mission is to advance the scientific study of language. A series of 16 lectures on 16 tapes comprises a full-length course presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Introduction to PROLOG for linguists [videorecording]
items.description: Eight lectures on eight U-matic videocassettes comprise a full-length course presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Keith Henson papers relating to Project Xanadu, XOC, Memex, Ted Nelson, and Eric Drexler, 1977-1997
items.description: Henson was also a member of the Board of Directors of the Xanadu Operating Company, founded in 1983 to support development of Ted Nelson's Xanadu system. The collection includes files from XOC, Memex, VHS tapes, cassette tapes, and Drexler drafts and galley proofs. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Ned Chapin papers, 1960-2008
items.description: Dr. Ned Chapin was a leader in the field of Computer Science, particularly the discipline of Software Maintenance, from its infancy. This collection primarily consists of conference materials, manuscripts, minicartridges, floppy disks, publications, and computer printouts relating to the courses and system development primarily created by Chapin during his tenure at Stanford University.

items.title: Parker James Gillespie, Jr. papers, 1974-1998 (inclusive)
items.description: Parker Gillespie was a Principle System Software Developer in Stanford IT Services from 1975-2004. The materials consist of user manuals, computer files and documentation regarding computer programs, databases, and other tools maintained by Stanford IT Services.

items.title: Problem reporting and tracking system developed at SLAC, 1981-1996
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Richard William Weiland papers, 1969-2006
items.description: His first job was with his former high school classmates Bill Gates and Paul Allen at Microsoft, where he managed the completion of the COBOL compiler and helped develop the BASIC interpreter. The collection includes personal correspondence, 1969-2002; materials pertaining to Microsoft, both his career there and the company, 1976-99; his research materials and notebooks on computers, the software industry, investments, and other interests, 1988-2006; papers, yearbooks, notebooks, and other items from his student career, 1971-80 (high school, Oregon State University, Stanford University, and Harvard Business School); materials pertaining to his philanthropic interests; and photographs and other AV materials.

items.title: Robert W. Floyd papers, 1960-1995
items.description: Robert W. Floyd joined the Stanford faculty in 1968 as an associate professor of computer science. His most important scientific achievement was pioneering systematic methods of program verification. These papers include his Stanford course files, 1976-94; correspondence, 1968-95, including that with Donald Knuth, 1963-1987; research and subject files; reprints and manuscripts; computer printouts; and note cards.

items.title: Santa Cruz Operation, Inc. documentation, 1980-1990
items.description: Santa Cruz Operation, Inc. (SCO) was a software company founded in 1979 and based in Santa Cruz, California. It is best known for developing Unix operating system variants—Xenix, SCO UNIX, and UnixWare—for Intel x86 processors. Manuals and software from the software company, Santa Cruz Operation, Inc. (SCO) concerning the XENIX and HCR/C++ systems.

items.title: SPIRES retrospectives by the original developers
items.description: SPIRES [Stanford Physics Information Retrieval System] was first developed to provide access to preprints of physics research; it then grew to be a broader based data management and retrieval tool, with the acronym meaning Stanford Public Information Retrieval System. This collection includes a DVD transfer of the original videorecording done by Harley Goes and Bo Parker and a transcript of the interviews recorded.
items.era_note: [Most of these interviews, recollections by the original developers of the SPIRES retrieval system, concern its growth in these years.]

items.title: Ted Nelson papers, 1950s-2019
items.description: Theodor Holm "Ted" Nelson is an information technology pioneer and systems humanist. Nelson founded Project Xanadu in 1960, a global hypertext system designed to permanently connect different types of documents, display visible connections between documents, and include a simplified copyright system.
items.era_note: [The papers run to 2019, and roughly a third of them concern these years of his hypertext work.]

items.title: The Unix System; the beginning : oral history, 1989
items.description: "The Unix system reflects the ethos of a community of researchers who combined different backgrounds and interests into an unusually coherent programming environment, and it is of interest to know just how that came about." Interviewees include Ken Thompson, Dennis Ritchie, Rudd Canaday, Doug McIlroy, Brian W. Kernighan, Joe Condon, Robert Morris, and A.G. "Sandy" Fraser.

items.title: The Whole Universe Catalog
items.description: Demonstration of the Whole Universe Catalog accessing system by Kirk Kelley, June 3, 1974.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Transportation and utilities

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records, 1862-1997
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 5, Office of the Secretary records, 1904-1983
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Southern Pacific Railroad Company records. Record Group 6, Legal Department records, 1905-1979
items.description: The Southern Pacific Railroad was founded in 1865 and was purchased in 1869 by Collis Huntington, Leland Stanford, Charles Crocker and Mark Hopkins, better known as the Big Four. Contains board minutes, ledgers, engineering report books, mechanical car books, maps, mechanical specifications, valuation maps, leases, and cash receipts for the Southern Pacific Company and more than 500 other companies acquired by the Southern Pacific Company between 1895 and 1991.

items.title: Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station information packet for legislators' tour, Oct. 2, 1973
items.description: Packet contains: a cover letter, addressed to Dear Legislator and signed by the presidents of Metropolitan Edison Co. and Pennsylvania Electric Co. (4 p.) and 4 loose pages (Owners of Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station; Future capacity commitments; The heat goes up and away! (illustrated with picture of cooling tower); and a map of Pennsylvania electric service areas and transmission lines). The plant was owned by Metropolitan Edison Company (50%), Pennsylvania Electric Company (25%), and Jersey Central Power & Light Company (25%).

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Venture capital and finance

items.title: Something Ventured collection, circa 2011
items.description: Footage and documentation relating to the production of the 2011 film Something Ventured. Includes approximately 100 tapes with interview and B-roll footage; a few documents such as brochures; and digital files, including transcripts of interviews, interviewee releases, and memoranda of understanding with Zeitgeist Films and Western Association of Venture Capitalists.
items.era_note: [The film interviews, recorded around 2011, chiefly concern the venture capital firms and the companies they funded in these years.]

items.title: West Coast Venture Capital -- 25 years, 1958-1983 : graphic timeline, 1984
items.description: Lists individuals and companies with dates of activities and name changes.

items.title: West Coast Venture Capital -- 25 years, 1958-1983 : poster, 1984
items.description: Lists individuals and companies with dates of activities and name changes.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Video games

items.title: Al Alcorn papers relating to the history of video games, 1973-1974
items.description: He was the designer of the video arcade game Pong, creating it under the direction of Bushnell and Dabney. Business and design records from the early days of the Atari Corporation. Includes contracts, schematics, video game designs, and production orders for Pong.

items.title: Atari Design interviews, 2015-2017
items.description: A note on the collection by Raiford Guins: The interviews in this collection were conducted for the research and writing of Atari Design: Impressions on Coin-Operated Video Game Machines (Bloomsbury Press, 2022). If anything, it's a rich collection of candid conversations meant to inform an interviewer of the interviewee's training and professional work as a designer at Atari (or, in some cases working at design agencies and as an educator).
items.era_note: [Most of these interviews, recorded in 2015-2017 with former Atari designers, concern their work at the company in this period.]

items.title: Atari, Inc. business plans, 1974-1975
items.description: The two business plans, [1974 and 1975], include details on products and technology, marketing, management, finances, media coverage, and actual games brochures.

items.title: Bay Area video arcades : photographs by Ira Nowinski, 1981-1982
items.description: The Bay Area video arcade photographs were taken in 1980 and 1981 at several locations in the San Francisco Bay Area. Materials include black & white prints and approximately 650 35mm images on contact sheets with their negatives.

items.title: Castle Wolfenstein [electronic resource]
items.description: Action adventure game in which player must find Nazi war plans and escape from Castle Wolfenstein.

items.title: David Cook personal archive on Atari cabinet design, 1974-1999
items.description: David Cook is a game cabinet designer. He designed the Atari Tank 8 cab. Materials consist of Atari cabinet design documentation, including concept renderings, hand and CAD drawings, procedures manuals, photographs, patents, sell sheets, awards, and more.

items.title: Gregory Yob papers, 1964-1979
items.description: Materials include copies of Yob's unpublished work "The Anatomy of the Electric Creation" in various states, as well as his published PET manuals in Japanese, one letter from teacher John Maryanopolis, a 1964 copy of Scientific American, and born-digital files. The born digital materials document the work of Gregory Yob including "The Anatomy of the Electric Creation," "The Fool," and "Hunt the Wumpus." [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Matt Householder papers, 1980-1983
items.description: Material relating to the video game and film version of Krull, including graphics, designs, code, and promotional material. Also included is material relating to the creation of Moon Patrol.

items.title: Michael Jang collection of Atari materials, 1978-1991
items.description: Mike Jang designed Atari video game cabinets. Prints and original concept sketches of Atari game cabinets, often in the form of photocopies or photographs.

items.title: Muñoz Family's Atari Collection
items.description: This collection is representative of early home computing in the 1980s when software and hardware manufacturers created products for nontechnical users who wished to use computing for entertainment (i.e. gaming) and practical uses in the home (i.e. personal finances and education). Collection consists of an Atari 800XL home computer, color monitor and complete set of peripherals, as well as an "Andy" Robot. The collection also includes 127 consumer software titles published between 1980 and 1987.

items.title: Nintendo vs. Magnavox : documents relating to the intellectual property suit, 1986-1991. [Photocopies]
items.description: Legal documents relating to the intellectual property suit filed by Nintendo against Magnavox. Stanford University features prominently due to exposure to the technology via the Spacewar presentation at the University. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Preserving Virtual Worlds
items.description: The Preserving Virtual Worlds project was a collaborative project undertaken by teams at four U.S. universities: Stanford University, University of Illinois, University of Maryland, and Rochester Institute of Technology. Eight test cases were developed for this purpose: Spacewar! (1962), Adventure (1977), Star Raiders (1979), Mystery House (1980), Mindwheel (1984), DOOM (1993), Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos (2002) and Second Life (2003-) Data gathered by the project team for these titles was deposited in the Preserving Virtual Worlds collection after the conclusion of the project.

items.title: Richard Bartle papers, 1979-1997
items.description: Richard added his own enhancements and completed the rest of the game. In order to market MUD, Richard and Roy formed a game company with Simon Dally called MUSE. There are two main parts to this collection: 1) MUD1 archival materials and 2) MUD1 source code. The MUD1 archival materials include files for "Dungen," MUDDLE reference manual, maps, design notes, etc.

items.title: Stephen M. Cabrinety Collection in the History of Microcomputing, circa 1975-1995
items.description: He founded the non-profit organization, the Computer History Institute for the Preservation of Software (C.H.I.P.S.) in 1989. Collection contains approximately 8,500 software titles, as well as computer hardware, peripheral devices, hand-held games, and computer industry literature documenting the microcomputing gaming industry during its formative years.

items.title: Steve Bristow papers, 1968-1980
items.description: Consists of business papers such as reports, legal & patent documents, and sales & trade show material; notebooks; service manuals & user guides; schematics; advertisements; articles and photographs. Most of the papers concern Bristow's career at Atari.

items.title: Steve Meretzky papers relating to computer game design and interactive fiction history, 1978-2009
items.description: He has been involved in almost every aspect of game development, from writing to design to quality assurance and product design. The papers include design and game development documents, correspondence, paper files, electronic games, magazines, data disks, original game package artwork, PR and marketing materials, and miscellaneous electronic game industry memorabilia.

items.title: Video players : photographs by Ira Nowinski, 1982
items.description: Photographs were taken in various video game arcades in the San Francisco Bay Area.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work

items.title: Alan J. Adler papers, 1966-2006
items.description: Alan Adler, a consulting electronics engineer and lecturer at Stanford University, invented the Aerobie, a flying disc toy, in 1984. These materials were gathered and generated for an exhibition at the Engineering Library at Stanford and include drawings, exhibit text and captions, articles, clippings, Awesome Games of Catch (VHS videocassette), examples of commercial Aerobie rings and orbiter, and several pre-production models of the ring.

items.title: Global Business Network records, 1984-2012
items.description: Global Business Network (GBN) was a consulting and research organization founded in Berkeley, California in 1987 and later based in San Francisco. Materials in this collection primarily consist of records created and collected by Global Business Network (GBN) over the course of the organization's history, including WorldView meeting reports and interviews, publications, public reports, white papers, training resources, reference materials, marketing materials, and business plans.

items.title: John Newell collection on the history of the electric vehicle, 1962-1993
items.description: He became co-founder and Chair of the Board of Directors of the Electric Automobiles Assocation (EAA) in 1967, an interest-based organization that was the outcome of a symposium on the Electric Auto held that same year and organized by the Engineering Department at San Jose State College. The collection includes photographs, correspondence, newsletters, subject files, and a sampling of project papers and schematics for electric vehicle conversion projects.

items.title: John Sunier Collection
items.description: Open reel tape recordings of interviews with prominent figures in the audio and sound recording industry conducted by John Sunier for his radio program Audiophile Audition. Sunier broadcast the weekly national radio program from 1985 to 1998, drawing from the material contained on these reels to create hour-long profiles from virtually every corner of the audio world: engineers, musicians, conductors, producers, manufacturers, designers, label owners, journalists, and scientists.

items.title: Karl P. Cohen papers, circa 1931-2010
items.description: Dr. Karl Paley Cohen was a physicist and advisor involving nuclear energy and reactor development who began his career making scientific advances in uranium production with the Manhattan Project at Columbia University in the 1940s. While the collection includes many declassified lab notebooks and journals from this time, it largely covers Cohen's long period of service with General Electric as well as various consultancies, and includes reports, correspondence, notes, and other material related to nuclear electric power generation and its safety, economic viability, public policy and other concerns.

items.title: Laurence W. "Bill" Lane, Jr. papers, circa 1953-2010
items.description: The papers include speeches, personal correspondence, and correspondence and documents relating to Lane Publishing Co., producers of Sunset Magazine, books, and films. Laurence William Lane Jr. often known as Bill Lane (November 7, 1919 - July 31, 2010) was an American magazine publisher and philanthropist. The Lane family owned and published Sunset Magazine.

items.title: Mark C. Suchman collection of technology businesses records, circa 1980-1992
Martin E. Hellman Papers
items.description: The materials consist of published papers, correspondence, and files from Martin E. Hellman, an American cryptologist.

items.title: Martin Packard papers, c. 1946-1990
items.description: In the late 1940s and early 50s, physicist Martin Packard made significant contributions to the emerging field of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) technology at Stanford University. Packard was later employed by Varian Associates, where he became head of the analytical instrumentation department, Corporate Vice President, and finally Assistant to Board Chairman Edward Ginzton. The collection is largely from his time at Varian, consisting of correspondence and memoranda, subject files maintained as Varian's reference library, and files related to Varian's corporate history.

items.title: Metal shop : online journal, 1985-1986
items.description: Includes "articles on telcom (phreaking/hacking), anarchy (guns and death & destruction) or kracking."

items.title: Phil Fialer papers
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Richard Southall papers, 1981-1986
items.description: These papers pertain to Southall's work on METAFONT and fall into four broad categories. Richard Southall, lecturer in the Department of Typography and Graphic Communication at the University of Reading, England, worked with Donald Knuth at Stanford between 1983 and 1986 on the Metafont Project.

items.title: Robert (Bob) Stein papers, 1970-2005
items.description: Robert (Bob) Stein papers document Stein's career as co-founder of Criterion Collection and Voyager Company, his work with the Atari Research Group, and as an early pioneer of electronic publishing. The collection consists of contracts, correspondence, proposals, and planning documents relating to film distribution, laserdisc video projects, and electronically published works on CD-ROMs.

items.title: Roger K. Summit papers, circa 1961-2005
items.description: Roger Kent Summit is an information scientist and businessmen best known for being the creator of the Dialog information retrieval system (sometimes stylized as DIALOG) as well as the president and CEO of Dialog Information Services, Inc. The papers of Roger Summit consist primarily of his work with industry-leading information retrieval company DIALOG.

items.title: Selket Corporation records, circa 1967-1997
items.description: Materials include company documents, drawings, printed material, product development plans, and artifacts, as well as reference materials used by Rojo to set up and run his company.

items.title: Stanford Energy Lectures recordings
items.description: The Institute for Energy Studies, organized in 1973, was designed to stimulate, facilitate, and promote the development of research and academic programs in energy within existing schools and departments. Lectures, primarily by non-Stanford professors and energy professionals, on all aspects of energy studies, including fossil fuels, nuclear power, conservation, solar energy, energy industries, energy policy, and political considerations.

items.title: Stanford Energy Lectures, 1974-1984
items.description: Lectures, primarily by non-Stanford professors and energy professionals. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Stanford University, Euler Project, records
items.description: The Euler Project at Stanford produced a digital typeface, consisting of over 500 mathematical characters, for the American Mathematical Society (AMS). Collection consists of Hermann Zapf's original drawings used to develop the Euler typeface, as well as computer printouts and proofs; correspondence between Zapf and Donald E. Knuth concerning the typeface design; and the working papers of the Digital Typography Group, which produced the final digital typeface, including correspondence, character proofs, galleys, computer programs, notebooks, logs, and research notes.

items.title: Sterling Beckwith papers, 1929-1992
items.description: He was an engineer and inventor who worked on many developments in generator technology. Papers pertain to his interest and work in engineering and include drawings, notes, publications, correspondence, reports, plans, financial records, manuals, photographs, and patent files.

items.title: Thomas J. Carr papers, circa 1940s-1990s
items.description: This archive documents military, computing and space history.

items.title: Transforming information into knowledge : videorecording, nd.
VPL Research collection
items.description: VPL Research was one of the first companies that developed and sold virtual reality products. It was founded by computer scientist Jaron Lanier in 1984.

items.title: William Kaufmann papers, circa 1950-2004
items.description: In 1971, he established William Kaufmann Inc. in Los Altos, California, which Kaufmann operated with his wife, Virginia and their daughter, Gail. The William Kaufmann papers include business records, publishing files, and correspondence documenting Kaufmann's career as an independent publisher of science and technology publications and book titles on topics including humor, human ecology, environmentalism, and psychology.

items.title: William P. Wreden, Books & Manuscripts archive, 1936-1993
items.description: Correspondence, financial records, catalogue checking copies, orders, appraisals, account books, jeweler's inventory books, flyers, publications, scrapbook, and photographs.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Environment and conservation

items.title: 20-20 Vision; in celebration of the peninsula hills : ephemeral publication of the Committee for Green Foothills, 1982
items.description: Article written by Stegner in a special publication for the Committee for Green Foothills. Also included is the summer, 1993, issue of GREEN FOOTNOTES, the Committee for Green Foothills quarterly, which was the Wallace Stegner Memorial issue.

items.title: Baylands resource book : mimeograph copy, 1975
items.description: "The purpose of this book is to encourage teachers and group leaders to use the Baylands area for field trips. It is designed to prepare teachers for the field trip through suggested activities and preparation... " Included is "background information for special areas, general recommendations for field trip organization and preparation, and a bibliography of suggested books and special resources."

items.title: Castle Rock Gazette : newsletter, 1974 & 1976
items.description: Newsletter lists activities (hikes, clean-ups, tree-plantings) and conservation projects (open space acquisitions, planned growth in cities, mass transit planning, etc.).

items.title: Recreational carrying capacity of Searsville Lake Park : project ECC 4526 / prepared by Gloria M. Esdale, Terrence Cullinan, Sidney J. Everett, Robert E. Freeman, Buford R. Holt, and Sue Inglis.
San Mateo County Resource Conservation District records, 1935-2008
items.description: The San Mateo County Resource Conservation District (formerly known as the San Mateo County Soil Conservation District) is a non-regulatory public benefit district to help protect, conserve, and restore natural resources through information, education, and technical assistance programs. The records of the San Mateo County Resource Conservation District span the history of the organization and include administrative and financial files, meeting minutes, reports, maps, and other material.

items.title: Santa Clara County Planning Department records, 1929-1983
items.description: The Santa Clara County Planning Office is responsible for managing planning studies related to the county, reviewing development project proposals, zoning enforcement, and providing information on land use and demographic trends. It is primarily composed of environmental impact reports (EIRs) dating from the 1970s-1980s, with a smaller amount of published materials on other aspects of demography, land use, zoning, and development.

items.title: Sempervirens Fund Photographs, 1902-2001
items.description: California's oldest land trust, the Sempervirens Fund's mission is to protect and permanently preserve redwood (Sequoia sempervirens) forests, wildlife habitat, watersheds, and other important natural and scenic features of California's Santa Cruz Mountains, and to encourage public appreciation and enjoyment of this environment. Sempervirens Fund photographic prints and negatives dating from 1902-2001.

items.title: Sempervirens Fund records, 1974-2006
items.description: The Sempervirens Fund seeks to preserve and protect the natural character of California's Santa Cruz Mountains and to encourage appropriate public enjoyment of this environment. Material from redwood conservation group Sempervirens Fund including their newsletter The Mountain Echo and annual reports.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Farming, canning and food processing

items.title: California wine label and ephemera collection, 1920s-1940s, 1960s-1987
items.description: The bulk of the collection comprises wine labels and ephemera created by California winemakers and wine companies in the 1930s, 1940s, 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s. The core of the collection consists of wine labels printed by Lehmann Printing and Lithographing Co. in San Francisco in the 1930s and '40s.

items.title: Steele Ranch records, 1855-1973
items.description: Compilation of ranch records from the Steele Ranches of San Mateo County, California. Includes financial papers, legal papers, photographs, maps, and miscellaneous background notes written by Mrs. Catherine Steele. The collection covers over 100 years of ranching in California.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Mining and quarrying

items.title: William Hillman Shockley papers, circa 1860-circa 1920
items.description: William Hillman Shockley (1855-1925) was an American mining engineer and amateur photographer. The materials consist of photographs, lecture notes, letters, books, and manuscripts documenting Shockley's career as a mining engineer and professor at Stanford, including documentation of geology expeditions to Alaska, China and Russia.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Petroleum and natural gas

items.title: Earl E. Brabb collection of Chevron oil well logs
items.description: Logs contain information for an estimated 6,000 oil test wells in California from an area extending from Eureka to the Salton Sea.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Real estate and land development

items.title: Land use and planning documents, San Mateo and Santa Clara Counties, 1958-1995
items.description: Crowder served as Palo Alto City Planner from 1972-1982 and was on the Portola Valley Planning Commission from 1974-1982. The collection consists primarily of reports and other publications regarding land use in California, particularly in San Mateo and Santa Clara Counties, 1958-1980.

items.title: Stanford University, Housing Advisory Committee, records, 1968-1974
items.description: The ad hoc Housing Advisory Committee, established in 1969 by the President of Stanford University, studied the possibilities of development of low and middle income housing on Stanford land; final recommendations were submitted in 1974. Records include correspondence, notes, data, draft and final report, committee meeting minutes, newsclippings, and other documents assembled by committee chairman, Professor Gordon Wright.

items.title: Stanford University, Office of the General Counsel, records
items.description: The Office of the General Counsel (OGC) is responsible for addressing all of the legal issues arising out of the activities of Stanford University, Stanford Hospital and Clinics and Lucile Salter Packard Children's Hospital at Stanford. Records from the legal office pertain to real estate matters, including the Stanford Shopping Center, other leases, and gift deeds.

items.title: Stanford University, Pearce-Mitchell Project, records, 1966-1977
items.description: Correspondence, clippings and other materials relating to the planning, building and inhabiting of this faculty-staff condominium project.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Surveying and mapping

items.title: Don Cooke papers, 1980s-1990s.
items.description: Materials include historical mapping software and an Etak Navigator. The Etak was designed by Stanford alum Stan Honey, and the company was funded by Nolan Bushnell of Atari (in the early 1980s).

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Transportation

items.title: San Francisco Cable Car Reconstruction Program : slide collection, 1983-1984
items.description: In the late 1970s it became apparent that the San Francisco Cable Car System was falling into disrepair. At this point Chester Gerhardt decided to document the project, including the demolition, engineering, and reconstruction of the system.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Water and public works

items.title: Flood (inundation) studies for Searsville, Lagunita and Felt Dams
items.description: These studies were commissioned in compliance with the California Dam Safety Act of 1972 (SB 896), which required that maps be prepared on all jurisdictional dams within California. Copies of three flood study reports and related record sheets attached.

items.title: Perry L. McCarty papers, 1953-2023
items.description: Perry L. McCarty, Silas H. Palmer Professor Emeritus, came to Stanford University in 1962 to found a new multidisciplinary education and research program in environmental engineering and science that became a model for others throughout the country. The focus of McCarty's research, teaching, and writing has been on water, with a primary interest in biological processes for the control of environmental contamination. This collection consists of various funding proposals and related correspondence, technical reports, conference presentations, book chapters, journal articles, news articles, professional correspondence, and awards.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use

items.title: Albert Wilson papers, ca. 1910-1995
items.description: Albert Wilson (1903-1996), was a San Francisco Bay Area botanist, landscape architect, author, teacher and lecturer on gardening and landscaping, as well as a TV and radio talk show personality who wrote several books popularizing gardening, as well as an autobiography. Material related to Wilson's career as horticulturalist, author, and broadcaster.

sectors.name: Education and research — Applied physics

items.title: Anthony Edward Siegman papers, 1916-2013 (inclusive)
items.description: Anthony Siegman was an electrical engineer, primarily focused on masers and lasers. Siegman became an assistant professor at Stanford in Electrical Engineering in 1957. The materials consist of administrative files, research files, correspondence, and publications.

items.title: Arthur Schawlow papers, 1949-1997
items.description: Arthur L. Schawlow, professor of physics at Stanford University from 1961 to 1991, received the Nobel Prize in physics in 1981 for his contributions to the development of laser spectroscopy. These papers primarily document Schawlow's career at Stanford and include correspondence, 1951-1995; lecture notes and class files, 1980-1988, containing problem sets and solutions, exams, and other information; grant files; records from participation in professional organizations including American Physical Society, American Institute of Physics, and the Optical Society of America; and reprints of his and his students' articles, 1949-1994.

items.title: C. F. Quate papers, circa 1961-1984
items.description: He joined the Stanford faculty in 1961 as professor in the applied physics and electrical engineering departments, serving two terms as chair of the department of applied physics. Correspondence, memoranda, press releases, contracts, grants, course materials and other records pertaining to his research and teaching at Stanford, including work at the Ginzton Laboratory; and offsets, glossies, and slides from the acoustic microscope project.

items.title: Felix Bloch papers, 1928-1987
items.description: The Bloch papers document Felix Bloch's role in twentieth century physics as a scientist, teacher and administrator. The collection includes correspondence, grant proposals, lecture notes, minutes and accompanying documentation regarding departmental, university and national committees, research notebooks, grants, patents, and designs; files regarding organizations in which Bloch played an active role; publications (predominantly reprints) by Bloch; and photographs.

items.title: Oleg Jardetzky papers, 1957-2003
items.description: He was director of the Stanford Magnetic Resonance Laboratory from 1975 to 1997. His research interests include structural basis of pharmacological action, biological signal processing, and fundamentals of drug design. Collection includes papers from his years at Harvard, 1957-67; records from the Dept. of Molecular Pharmacology at Stanford and the Stanford Magnetic Resonance Laboratory, 1970-2001; and papers pertaining to his other professional activities, including the International Conference on Magnetic Resonance in Biological Systems (1964-2002), the International Society for Magnetic Resonance, and the World Federation of Scientists and the Ettore Majorana Centre for Scientific Culture (1988-2003).

items.title: Oscar Buneman papers, 1913-1989 (inclusive), 1941-1989 (bulk)
items.description: Oscar Buneman, prominent scientist in the fields of plasma electrodynamics, fundamental electromagetic theory, and numerical anaylsis, was Professor of Electrical Engineering at Stanford University from 1960 until he reached emeritus status in 1984. Research notes, papers, reprints, correspondence, lectures, and class materials from his teaching career and research while at Stanford University, with some materials from the 1940s and 1950s relevant to his work on magnetrons.

items.title: Steven Chu papers, 1949-2013 (inclusive), 1975-2004 (bulk)
items.description: Steven Chu is the William R. Kenan, Jr. Professor of Physics and Professor of Molecular and Cellular Physiology at Stanford University. While at Bell labs, Chu led the group that showed how to first cool and then trap atoms with light. Papers pertain primarily to topics in physics and include notes, overhead transparencies from his lectures, reprints, articles, memos, proposals, correspondence, charts, and drawings. Subjects include electric dipole moment, diode lasers, and dye lasers; and there are some materials pertaining to departmental matters.

items.title: Theodore H. Geballe papers, 1942-1997
items.description: Professor of Applied Physics and Materials Science Engineering at Stanford University. Professional correspondence; materials from meetings, conferences, workshops, and symposia; and abstracts, notes, and transparencies from talks relating to his teaching and research in materials science, superconductivity, and electronics.

items.title: William A. Little papers, 1967-1996 (inclusive)
items.description: William A. Little was a Professor of Physics, Emeritus, who joined Stanford as an Assistant Professor in 1957. Little specialized in high temperature superconductivity, superconductivity in organic materials and polymers, and condensed matter physics. The materials consist of correspondence and conference files.

sectors.name: Education and research — Education research and educational technology

items.title: Alfredo Castañeda papers, 1935-1978
items.description: Alfredo Castaneda, a nationally prominent expert in multicultural education, was the first Mexican American to be appointed to a full professorship at Stanford University. This collection reflects Dr. Castaneda's work in multicultural and bilingual education, especially as it relates to Mexican American students. It includes elementary and secondary curriculum materials, grant applications for bilingual/bicultural education projects under Title VII legislation, materials from bilingual/multicultural programs in public schools, and secondary sources that he used in his university courses.

items.title: Diane Middlebrook, English 258, Tutored Video Instruction, Videorecordings. 1977
items.description: The collection consists of 19 videotapes used as instruction tools in Dianne Middlebrook's course English 258: Twentieth-Century Neo-Romantic British and American Poetry.

items.title: Liza Loop papers, 1972-1988
items.description: California educator whose interests include computers and education, public-access computing, and software. Papers concerning Atari, People's Computer Company, ComputerTown, Homebrew Computer Club, Northwest Computer Club, etc., together with correspondence and the draft of the first VISICALC manual.

items.title: Patrick Suppes papers, 1951-2014
items.description: Patrick Suppes was the Lucie Stern Professor of Philosophy, Emeritus, and a member of the departments of Statistics and Psychology and of the Graduate School of Education at Stanford University. This collection consists of research, notes, papers, and correspondence with a particular emphasis on Suppes' work on computer-assisted education research.

items.title: Stanford University, Academic Computing and Information Services, academic software development collection, 1984-1995
items.description: This collection pertains primarily to the Faculty Author Development Project (1984-1986), which sought to encourage Stanford professors to develop courseware on microcomputers. The collection consists largely of binders containing programming instructions, handbooks, manuals, computer disks, and other materials on the final projects.

items.title: Stanford University, Information Technology Services, audiovisual materials, 1980-1995
items.description: She was a longtime employee in the Information Technology Services group at Stanford. Audio and video recordings of committee proceedings, panel discussions, and research.

sectors.name: Education and research — Engineering

items.title: Aldo Vieira da Rosa papers, 1977-1992
items.description: Aldo became a Professor (Research) in Electrical Engineering in 1980. His research interests were in ionospheric processes, energy processes and renewable energy. Collection materials include drafts of reports, book chapters, course materials, and research proposals.

items.title: Frederick Emmons Terman papers, 1901-1978
items.description: The papers of Frederick Emmons Terman, dating from 1920 to 1978, document all phases of his long and influential career as an educator, electronics engineer, administrator, and author. The collection consists of nearly 200 boxes of correspondence, memoranda, minutes, reports, speeches and miscellaneous materials accumulated by Dr. Terman and his staff throughout his professional life.

items.title: H.O. Fuchs papers, 1950-1988
items.description: Course notes for mechanical engineering undergraduate and graduate classes; correspondence; case histories in engineering problems prepared by Fuchs; records pertaining to the Engineering Case Program; research notes, articles, and papers by Fuchs; and photographs. Fuchs, an expert on fatique in metals, taught mechanical engineering at Stanford University from 1964 to 1973, when he became an Emeritus Professor.

items.title: James L. Adams papers, 1925-2017 (inclusive)
items.description: He joined the Stanford faculty in the School of Engineering in 1966. Adams' administrative positions included Associate Dean for Academic Affairs; Chair of the Program in Values, Technology, Science and Society; Director of the Design Division of Mechanical Engineering; and Chair of the Department of Industrial Engineering and Engineering Management. Papers largely reflect James L. Adam’s teaching career at Stanford University and include class materials, correspondence, memoranda, reports, publications, and some photographs (largely of student projects).

items.title: Project Nairobi report
items.description: Cost study and design proposal for the addition of a library and science facility for Nairobi College in East Palo Alto, California; prepared by students in Civil Engineering 197, Engineering Synthesis.

items.title: Thomas Cover papers, circa 1964-2011
items.description: Cover joined the faculty at the Stanford School of Engineering in 1964, becoming a professor in 1972. In 1990, the Information Theory Society of the IEEE awarded him the Claude E. Shannon Award, the highest honor for lifetime achievement in information theory. This collection primarily consists of correspondence, notes, teaching materials, publications, and administrative files.

sectors.name: Education and research — Library, archival and information services

items.title: Meyer Library flood of 1978 collection
items.description: The basement of Meyer Library at Stanford University was flooded in November 1978 from a ruptured water main. Affected books were frozen and then dried in a vacuum chamber at the Lockheed Missiles & Space Company in Sunnyvale, California. Collection includes four photographs of library staff at the Lockheed facilities and two articles on the freezing process.

items.title: Meyer Library Lecture Tapes
items.description: Originally a set of circulating open reel tapes available at Stanford University's J. Henry Meyer Memorial Library. The tapes contain a variety of non-musical material supporting the educational mission of the university and include lectures by Stanford faculty and class audio reserves (including commercially distributed tapes) of poetry and prose readings, radio broadcasts, speeches, and other spoken word recordings.

items.title: Research Libraries Group (RLG) records, 1974-2006
items.description: The Research Libraries Group, Inc. (RLG) was a non-profit consortium founded in 1974 by major U.S. libraries (NYPL, Columbia, Harvard, Yale) to foster collaborative, technology-driven resource sharing. The RLG collection includes historical corporate documents, program and project files, grant proposals, system and software development files, digital material, photographs, and other documents and memorabilia.

items.title: Research Libraries Group records, 1970-1987
items.description: Reports, manuals, proposals, surveys, statistics; BALLOTS System books and reference manuals; PLAN Systems books.

items.title: Silicon Valley Archives
items.description: The Silicon Valley Archives are the world’s greatest repository of materials related to the history and development of Silicon Valley.

sectors.name: Education and research — Musical acoustics and computer music

items.title: CCRMA Tape Archive
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics (CCRMA)
items.description: Works by students and faculty of CCRMA.

items.title: John M. Chowning papers, 1974-1997
items.description: John M. Chowning, professor emeritus of music at Stanford, developed the technique for creating digital sounds in the late 1960s which was patented and then licensed to Yamaha in 1973. Collection consists largely of correspondence between Chowning, the Yamaha Corporation, and the Technology Licensing Office at Stanford, 1974-97; other items include patents and related documents, 1978-87, technical writings (not all by Chowning), 1974-87, publications and leaflets on Yamaha products, and miscellaneous notes. He was the founding director in 1975 of Stanford's Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics.

items.title: John R. Pierce papers, 1933-2002 (inclusive), 1960-2002 (bulk)
items.description: He worked at Bell Telephone Laboratories from 1936 to 1971, where his work included electronic tubes, microwave communications, and psychoacoustics. In 1983 he became a visiting professor of music, emeritus, at the Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics at Stanford University. The focus is primarily on his interest in computers and music and his authorship of science fiction stories, with a few published articles and photographs pertaining to the Echo satellite.

items.title: Max V. Mathews papers, 1953-2011
items.description: The collection includes correspondence, articles, lab notebooks, musical scores, audio recordings, computer files, and other materials related to the professional work of computer music pioneer Max V. Mathews. While at Stanford, he was affiliated with the Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics.

items.title: Musical Acoustics Research Library collection, 1956-2007
items.description: Contains research materials, research papers, correspondence, journal run , photographs, glass slides, wood samples, and other artifacts (woodwind and brass mouthpieces). The MARL collection is dedicated to the study of all aspects of musical acoustics.

items.title: Stanford University, Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics, records, 1967-2001
items.description: The Stanford University Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics (CCRMA) is a multi-disciplinary facility where composers and researchers work together using computer-based technology both as an artistic medium and as a research tool. Correspondence, grant files, research files, patents, concert programs, articles, clippings, photographs, and other records.

sectors.name: Education and research — Schools, colleges and training

items.title: Cañada College
items.description: Located in Redwood City, California. Established in 1968.

items.title: Conceptualization of KAIST and Prof. Frederick E. Terman, 2004
items.description: Text of Etchemendy's talk at the dedication of Terman Hall at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, May 17, 2004, along with a copy of the "Survey Report on the Establishment of the Korea Advanced Institute of Science," prepared for US Agency for International Development, 1970.

items.title: De Anza College, 1967-1979
items.description: Located in Cupertino, California. Opened in 1967.

items.title: John Etchemendy, "Conceptualization of Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology and Prof. Frederick E. Terman"
items.description: John Etchemendy (1952-) is former Provost of Stanford University, the Patrick Suppes Family Professor in the School of Humanities and Sciences, and the Denning Family Co-Director of Stanford Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI). Text of Etchemendy's talk at the dedication of Terman Hall at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, May 17, 2004, along with a copy of the "Survey Report on the Establishment of the Korea Advanced Institute of Science," prepared for US Agency for International Development, 1970.
items.era_note: [Most of the collection, a 1970 survey report on establishing the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and a talk about it, concerns this period.]

items.title: Ravenswood High School collection, 1971-1976
items.description: A collection of audio and video material-analog originals and preservation-quality digital copies (transferred and preserved by the Bay Area Video Coalition) relating to (and produced at) Ravenswood High School in East Palo Alto, ca. early 1970s, along with additional printed and photographic material.

sectors.name: Education and research — Science and mathematics

items.title: A.B.C. Walker papers, 1983-1990
items.description: Arthur B. C. Walker, an innovative astrophysicist and a mentor of women and minority students, was a professor of applied physics at Stanford University from January 1974 until his death in 2001. Collection pertains to his research and teaching and includes grant files (proposals, budgets, correspondence, etc.); photographs of stellar phenomena (prints and negatives); drawings, graphs, charts and computer printouts; and files from the classes he taught at Stanford.

items.title: Allan Cox papers, 1954-1987
items.description: In 1967 he joined the faculty at Stanford University, where he became Cecil and Ida Green Professor of Geophysics. Papers document his professional life as teacher, administrator, and researcher and include correspondence; memoranda; research notes, charts, proposals, and reports; grant applications; outlines, tests, lecture notes, and other teaching materials; manuscripts; minutes; date books; papers and theses by his students; reprints; maps; and his notes while a student at UC Berkeley. Cox studied paleomagnetism and plate tectonics theory; some materials pertain to research done on the Galapagos Islands and in China.

items.title: Arthur Kornberg papers, 1938-2007
items.description: With a research career spanning more than sixty years, Arthur Kornberg made many outstanding contributions to molecular biology. Collection documents Kornberg's work concerning the synthesis of DNA in the laboratory, as well as the synthetic pathways of nucleotides, and includes correspondence, 1947 to 1982; research lab notebooks, 1947 to 1969 (which include those studies for which he received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1959); coursework, lectures, and seminars; Stanford University Departmental records; records concerning professional organizations; and reprints, glass research slides, and audiotapes.

items.title: B. Noah Tilghman papers, 1972-2003
items.description: The materials consist of approximately 1000 color transparencies (35mm) taken by B. Noah Tilghman documenting various United States and New Zealand research bases in Antarctica, including the construction of Siple Station, as well as general living conditions, individuals, and landscapes. The Siple experiment was a Stanford, NSF funded, VLF- triggered emission experiment that took place from 1973 to 1988.

items.title: Barry M. Trost papers, 1961-2019
items.description: Barry M. Trost (b.1941) is the Job and Gertrud Tamaki Professor in the School of Humanities and Sciences, Emeritus for the Department of Chemistry. The collection consists primarily of postdoctoral researcher, graduate students, and undergrad student lab reports and data generated during their time with the Trost Group research program.

items.title: Bruce A.D. Stocker papers, 1972-2004
items.description: Bruce Arnold Dunbar Stocker was Professor of Microbiology and Immunology at Stanford University from 1966 to 1987 Collection includes lab notebooks, note pads, correspondence, and reprints.

items.title: Carl Djerassi papers, 1952-2006 (inclusive)
items.description: University research scientist and industrialist, Djerassi is most famous for synthesizing the first oral contraceptive. These papers primarily concern Djerassi's research in organic chemistry and include correspondence, reports, and lab notebooks on optical rotary dispersion and mass spectrometry; other research files containing correspondence, manuscripts, and reprints; reprints of Djerassi's published articles; and grant files.

items.title: Charles Stacy French papers, 1935-1989
items.description: French, plant physiologist, was director of the Dept. of Plant Biology of the Carnegie Institution, located on the Stanford University campus, from 1947 until his retirement in 1973. Papers include correspondence, articles, speeches, manuscripts, lab notes, charts, and computer printouts pertaining largely to his research interests in the photosynthesis of purple bacteria, spectroscopy of plant pigments, and the construction of spectroscopic equipment.

items.title: Charles Stein papers, 1945-2010
items.description: Charles M. Stein, professor emeritus of statistics, was one of the world's premier mathematical statisticians. Materials include professional and personal papers, technical reports, notebooks, and computer media.

items.title: Daniel Mazia papers, 1969-1996
items.description: Daniel Mazia, cell biologist, was professor emeritus at Stanford University's Hopkins Marine Station at the time of his death in 1996. Papers include correspondence, research notes, organizational files (including the International Cell Research Organization), course files, publications and reprints, photographs, and videotapes.

items.title: David S. Hogness, 1925-2019
items.description: David Hogness, PhD, was a Stanford biochemist who helped found the field of genomics. This collection comprises biographical materials, awarded grants, manuscript drafts, Hogness Group Laboratory records, and records related to the development and administration of Developmental Biology at Stanford University.

items.title: Douglas L. Brutlag papers, 1968-1999
items.description: Brutlag's work bridges the fields of biology and computer sciences, in the rapidly expanding field of bioinformatics. The papers document Brutlag's research and teaching in biochemistry and his work in bioinformatics.

items.title: George Polya papers, 1884-1985
items.description: Hungarian mathematician George Pólya was educated at the University of Budapest and the University of Paris, and taught at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich from 1914 to 1940. Papers relate to Pólya's research and teaching in mathematics and include professional and personal correspondence with mathematicians worldwide, 1910-1984; course materials including lecture notes; mathematical research notebooks dating from 1917 to 1960; manuscripts including those from his published works Complex Variables , How to Solve It , Mathematical Discovery , and Mathematics and Plausible Reasoning ; ephemera; reprints; and photographs.

items.title: Harry S. Mosher papers, 1944-2000
items.description: During his career at Stanford, Mosher taught organic chemistry and conducted research in a wide range of areas, including natural products chemistry and stereochemistry. Papers include correspondence, manuscripts and reprints, research files, lab notebooks, grant files, and class materials.

items.title: Ingram Olkin papers, 1875-2014, bulk 1950-2014
items.description: Ingram Olkin is best known for developing statistical analyses for evaluating policies, particularly in education. One year later, he moved permanently to Stanford University, where he held a joint appointment with the Department of Statistics and the Graduate School of Education.

items.title: Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve: The Herb Dengler Collection
items.description: Collection of photographs and field notebooks by Herbert Dengler of the Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve.

items.title: John George Herriot papers, 1937-1992
items.description: He served as the first director of the Stanford Computation Center, 1953-61, taught the first programming course at Stanford in 1955, and helped found the computer science department at Stanford in 1965. These papers document his career as a mathematician and include his notes taken while a student at Brown University, 1937-41, and his master's and doctoral theses, 1940-41; research files (notes, computations, articles, computer printouts, some correspondence, and other materials) on Fourier series, Schlicht functions, spline theory, and other topics, 1940-83; memos, minutes, correspondence, and other records pertaining to Stanford's Dept. of Computer Sciences and the Stanford Computation Center, 1946-92; correspondence, notes, and reports pertaining to his Fulbright year, 1962-63; and bibliographic and biographical materials.

items.title: John Hunter Thomas notebooks, 1949-1992 (inclusive)
items.description: Thomas became Associate Curator (1962), Curator (1963) and then Director (1972) of the 850,000 specimen Dudley Herbarium, with which he had a long and varied association. John was a leading plant biogeographer, and remained a specialist in the plants of central California in general and the Santa Cruz mountains in particular. The materials consist of 39 volumes of collecting notebooks.

items.title: Lucy Shapiro papers, 1940-2024
items.description: Lucy Shapiro is professor emerita of developmental biology and director of Stanford Medicine's Beckman Center. This collection consists of administrative records, seminars and lectures, Shapiro dissertation, lab notebooks and data, manuscripts and related correspondence, research files related to bioterrorism, patents and licensing related to biotech companies AnaCor and BorAgen.

items.title: Martin Gardner papers, 1957-1986
items.description: Martin Gardner was the Mathematical Games columnist for SCIENTIFIC AMERICAN from its inception in 1956 until 1986. These papers pertain to his interest in mathematics and consist of files relating to his SCIENTIFIC AMERICAN mathematical games column (1957-1986) and subject files on recreational mathematics. Papers include correspondence, notes, clippings, and articles, with some examples of puzzle toys.

items.title: Paul Berg papers, 1953-2014
items.description: Biochemistry Professor at Stanford University since 1960, Berg received the Nobel Prize for chemistry in 1980 for "fundamental studies of the biochemistry of nucleic acids with particular regard to recombinant DNA." Collection focuses on Berg's work with recombinant DNA and includes professional correspondence, 1959-1985; research lab notebooks for the years 1953-1986 which document his work with protein synthesis in bacterial cells and tumor viruses; records concerning the National Academy of Sciences conference on recombinant DNA research guidelines; records from his Stanford positions including administrative files, grant files, departmental records, student files, lectures, and symposia; reprints and illustrations; and videotapes and audiotapes.

items.title: Paul R. Ehrlich Papers
items.description: Correspondence, memos, notes, photographs, posters and other papers relating to Paul Ehrlich's publications and public appearances, his work with the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory, Jasper Ridge Biological Presrve (California), the Zero Population Growth organization, and the Stanford Biological Sciences Department.

items.title: Paul R. Ehrlich papers, 1954-2001
items.description: Ehrlich was an evolutionary and population biologist who gained worldwide attention for his 1968 book, The Population Bomb , which predicted dire consequences due to the rapidly increasing human population and advocated population control. Correspondence, memos, notes, photographs, posters and other papers relating to Paul Ehrlich's publications and public appearances, his work with the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory, Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve, the Zero Population Growth organization, and the Stanford Biological Sciences Department.

items.title: Peter A. Sturrock papers, 1952-2020
items.description: Peter Andrew Sturrock is an emeritus professor of applied physics at Stanford University. This collection consists of correspondence, research and teaching files, grant proposals, and reports.

items.title: Photographs from unmanned NASA space exploration, circa 1967-1976
items.description: The five images come from these NASA explorations: 1. Viking lander, 1-3 August 1976, the surface of Mars (the meteorological boom supporting the lander's miniature weather station divides the photograph. -- 2. Lunar orbiter 2, 1967, Copernicus crater, 45 miles above the lunar surface. -- 3. Lunar orbiter 1, late 1960s, first view of earth from 730 miles above the dark side of the moon. -- 4. Mariner 10, 3 November 1973, photo-mosaic of Earth, from a probe enroute to Mercury and Venus using the earth for calibration purposes. -- 5. Unknown.

items.title: Pierre Van Rysselberghe papers, 1932-1973
items.description: Pierre van Rysselberghe, a chemist and chemical engineer, earned his masters (1928) and doctorate (1929) at Stanford University. He taught at the University of Oregon and at Stanford. Papers include correspondence, class materials, articles and reprints, lab notes, and other materials pertaining to his research and his teaching career.

items.title: Protein synthesis [motion picture]
items.description: Following a short explanation of protein synthesis by Professor Paul Berg, Chairman, Dept. of Biochemistry at Stanford, a choreographic interpretation of the current biochemical model is presented by 200 students, demonstrating the rhythm and beauty of intercellular processes.

items.title: Research Activities in Physics at Stanford (Physics 260): Student notes
items.description: Notes contributed by members of the Physics 260 class covering the lectures and discussions presented by faculty members of the department and SLAC on their research.

items.title: Richard E. Taylor papers
items.description: Richard Edward Taylor, a professor emeritus of physics at Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, was an early user of the 2-mile-long linear accelerator at SLAC and carried out experiments that revealed subatomic particles called quarks for the first time – a discovery that earned him the Nobel Prize in physics along with colleagues from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. This collection features physics notebooks, slides, Nobel Prize Correspondence, papers from the Institute of Theoretical Physics, Department of Physics.

items.title: Robert Hofstadter papers, 1931-1993
items.description: This collection contains the papers of former Stanford professor and Nobel Prize winning physicist Robert Hofstadter. Of particular note are materials on the development of the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center (SLAC), later renamed the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, as well as correspondence on the relationship between SLAC and the Stanford University Department of Phyiscs.

items.title: Robert L. Kovach papers, 1959-1972
items.description: Robert L. Kovach serves as Emeritus Professor of Geophysics in the School of Earth, Energy, and Environmental Sciences, Stanford University. Includes personal research notebooks, correspondence, mission reports and transcripts, films, photographs, and ephemera collected by Kovach reflecting his role as a principal investigator for the Apollo 14, 16, and 17 missions. Film reels and photographs depict seismic experiments designed by Kovach and conducted by NASA astronauts.

items.title: Ronald Bracewell papers, 1958-2007
items.description: Ronald Newbold Bracewell (July 22, 1921 – August 12, 2007) was the Lewis M. Terman Professor of Electrical Engineering, Emeritus of the Space, Telecommunications and Radioscience Laboratory at Stanford University. In 1998 Dr. Bracewell was named Officer of the Order of Australia (AO) for service to science in the fields of radio astronomy and image reconstruction.

items.title: Science, biotechnology, and recombinant DNA: a personal history
items.era_note: [Most of this 1995 interview, a personal history of recombinant DNA research, concerns this period.]

items.title: Stanford University, Herzenberg Laboratory, Records, circa 1966-2016
items.description: Pioneers in the study of genetics, Lee and Len Herzenberg came to Stanford in 1959 to join the newly created genetics department run by Nobel laureate Joshua Lederberg. They would go on to develop the Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorter (FACS) and monoclonal antibodies that are widely used as reagents in life science research and are models for the therapeutic antibodies used in several diseases. Laboratory notebooks, slides, patent files, and FACS files.

items.title: Stanford University, Radio Astronomy Institute, records, 1961-1978
items.description: Collection of GLINTS (internal reports) of the Stanford Radio Astronomy Institute. Many GLINTS are first drafts of published papers.

items.title: Stanford University, the California Bay Area earthquake symposium, earthquake damage, and SITN classroom footage [video recordings]
items.description: Tape of a symposium following the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake, featuring speakers from the Stanford-United States Geological Survey Center for Research in Earthquake Engineering - Haresh Shah, Helmut Krawinkler, and Anne Kiremidjian. Topics discussed include geophysics of earthquakes, ground motion, and building failures. Also included is video footage taken on October 19, 1989, of damage to Green Library, Geology Corner, the Museum, the anatomy building, and Encina Hall at Stanford University.

items.title: Stanford-Cambridge Radar Film Digitization Project
items.description: The Stanford-Cambridge Radar Film Digitization Project is an Antarctic survey conducted by an international consortium of American, British and Danish geoscientists.

items.title: Stephen Jay Gould papers, 1899-2004 (inclusive), 1941-2002 (bulk)
items.description: This collection documents the life of noted American paleontologist, evolutionary biologist, and historian of science, Stephen Jay Gould. The papers include correspondence, juvenilia, manuscripts, subject files, teaching files, photographs, audiovisual materials, and personal and biographical materials created and compiled by Gould.

items.title: William M. Fairbank papers, 1961-1989
items.description: William M. Fairbank (1917-1989) was a physics professor at Stanford University. His research interests included superconductivity, gravity waves, individual quarks and monopoles. Materials include correspondence, notes, talks, articles, graphs, charts, articles, reports, research proposals, lab notebooks, and photographs.

items.title: William R. Normark memorial archive collection, 1970-2006
items.description: Collection includes materials related to the work of William R. Normark, a Geologist at the Geological Survey in Menlo Park, California.

items.title: William S. Johnson papers, 1940-1992
items.description: Johnson, professor of chemistry at Stanford University, was generally regarded as one of the major figures in 20th-century organic chemistry. Papers document his teaching and research activities and include notebooks, research reports, subject files, correspondence, grant files, reprints, and slides.

items.title: Wray Huestis papers, 1979-2004
items.description: Professor Wray Huestis’ research concerns the molecular mechanisms whereby cells control their shape, motility, deformability and the structural integrity of their membranes. This collection comprises student lab notebooks from the Wray Huestis Lab.

sectors.name: Education and research — Social sciences and humanities

items.title: Archeological evaluation of the Greystone Quarry in the Santa Teresa hills report
items.description: The Greystone Quarry, formerly known as the Goodrich Quarry, was the source of the stone used to build Stanford University. It includes an archival study of archeological resources in the area of the quarry, a surface survey of the land, and recommendations.

items.title: Basic concepts of GPSG [videorecording]
items.description: Eight lectures of a full-length course on generalized phase structure grammar presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University.

items.title: Child Phonology Collection
items.description: The Child Phonology Collection consists of open reel tape recordings produced in a study on speech sound production in children. The Child Phonology Project was conducted by Stanford's Department of Linguistics and The Hearing and Speech Sciences division of Stanford University Medical Center.

items.title: Doris H. Linder papers, 1900-2008
items.description: Linder was Professor of History at the College of San Mateo for over forty years, teaching world history and women's studies courses. Doris Linder's papers includes research and teaching files and notes, drafts and correspondence related to her published research, travel and country files, family and personal correspondence and ephemera, slides, and published material.

items.title: Eugene J. Webb papers, 1961-1994
items.description: Eugene J. Webb, a pioneer in the development of research and teaching of organizational behavior in business schools, joined the faculty of the Graduate School of Business at Stanford in 1968. Professional papers relating to courses Webb taught at the Graduate School of Business at Stanford University and his research interests such as philanthropy, altruism, effect of deadlines on human behavior, and organizational behavior.

items.title: Frank Hawkinshire papers, 1969-2017
items.description: Frank B.W. Hawkinshire, V. was Stanford University's first tenured Black professor in Educational Psychology from 1967-1971. The focus of his academic interests have been on the applications of sociology, psychology, and physiology to solving social problems.

items.title: George Leland Bach Papers, 1937-1994
items.description: The author of several books and articles on inflation, monetary policy and basic economic theory, Bach also worked for a variety of organizations and corporations, and frequently gave testimony before Congress on economic policy. The collection covers Bach's professional career from his graduate student days at the University of Chicago in the late 1930s to the dedication of the George L. Bach Auditorium at Carnegie-Mellon University in 1993.

items.title: Head-driven phrase structure grammar [videorecording]
items.description: Sixteen lectures on 8 DVDs comprise a full-length course presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University.

items.title: Lexical-functional grammar [videorecording]
items.description: Sixteen lectures of a full-length course presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University .

items.title: Moses Abramovitz and Paul A. David papers, 1947-2000
items.description: Moses Abramovitz and Paul A. David were prominent economists who made significant contributions to the study of economic growth and its impact on economies. This collection consists of papers on economic growth impact and theory. Specific materials include research data, professional correspondence, notes, manuscripts, and publications created by Moses Abramovitz and Paul A. David.

items.title: Paul A. David papers, 1920-2010
items.description: Paul A. David (1935-2023) was an economic historian at Stanford best known for his research on technological change and how it affects social and economic behavior. This collection consists of publication drafts, grant grant proposals, research files, correspondence, and ECON course materials.

items.title: Renato Rosaldo papers, circa 1948-2012
items.description: The Renato Rosaldo papers document the professional activities of the cultural anthropologist, field researcher and poet Renato Rosaldo. The materials consist of field notes, correspondence, administrative files, photographs, audio cassettes, and other materials. The collection covers Renato Rosaldo's field work with the Ilongot people in northern Luzon, Philippines, as well as field work in Ecuador and the San Jose Cultural Citizenship Project.

items.title: Semantics [videorecording]
items.description: Twenty-two lectures on 22 cassettes comprise a full-length course presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University .

items.title: Stanford University, School of Humanities and Sciences, Tiro project collection, 1982-2006
items.description: The Tiro Project (named for Marcus Tullius Tiro, Cicero's slave-amanuensis) was designed to encourage humanities scholars to use computers. Collection includes slides of project participants, office and classroom space, equipment, source materials, and graphs, 1983-84; two papers by Peter Lyman on the project, 1983-84; Tiro Project Research Reports, 1984-85; transcripts of interviews with faculty who participated in the project, 1983-84; paper by William M. Chace on the project presented at a conference, 1984; and audio cassettes and a transcript of a conversation held in 2006 recalling the project and related academic issues of computer use.

items.title: Stanley Peters papers, 1970-2017
items.description: Stanley Peters (b.1941) is Director Emeritus of the Center for the Study of Language and Information (2008-2013) and a Professor Emeritus of Linguistics at Stanford University. This collection contains correspondence, research files, grant applications, and audiovisual materials related to the Department of Linguistics and the Stanford Center for the Study of Language and Information (CSLI).

items.title: Unification and grammatical theory [videorecording]
