items.description: Eight lectures comprise a full-length course presented at the 1987 Linguistic Institute held at Stanford University.

items.title: Walter G. Vincenti papers, 1971-2007
items.description: Collection contains Vincenti's lectures from a class on the history of the industrial revolution taught at Stanford's overseas campus in Cliveden, undated; class materials and lectures from VTS 121 Technology in Society: Historical Perspective, 1981; lectures by Claude B. Fohlen on the Industrial Revolution 1972; lectures by Paul A. David on technology, society, and economy 1971; letters from Harriet Jones with photocopied papers of aeronautical scientist R. T. Jones, 1999-2000; and a seminar on fluid mechanics. He was a research scientist with the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA), working at the Ames Aeronautical Laboratory at Moffett Field until he joined the Stanford faculty in 1957. He cofounded Stanford's Program in Values, Technology, and Science in 1971 and served several terms as its chair.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford history and ceremonial life

items.title: "Computer Science at Stanford: The Impact of the First Ten Years" [videorecording]
items.description: Video recordings of sessions discussing the impact of the first 10 years of the Computer Science Dept.

items.title: "Cornerstone: Making History Again" [videorecording]
items.description: Video recordings of the events and ceremonies during the celebration marking the centennial of the start of construction of Stanford University. Speakers included George P. Shultz, Joe Clark, Bernardo Sepúlveda Amor, Donald Kennedy, Warren Christopher, David M. Kennedy, and H. Donald Winbigler.

items.title: Conference with President Francois Mitterand at the Center for Integrated Systems : video recording
items.description: Mitterand visited Stanford's Center for Integrated Systems on March 26, 1984 and spoke with academic researchers, capitalists, and industry representatives concerning high technology research and industry.

items.title: Dorothy Regnery papers, 1980-1991
items.description: Historian, particularly interested in central California and Stanford University. Research materials for several projects, including the Stanford's Sacramento house and the Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve history.

items.title: John F. Manley papers, 1946-2000 (inclusive), 1983-2000 (bulk)
items.description: John F. Manley (1939-2020) was a professor of political science, emeritus at Stanford University with a thirty-year tenure, which began in 1971. Clippings, press releases, statements, memoranda, correspondence, petitions, and other papers pertaining to the relationship between Stanford University and the Hoover Institution, the proposed Ronald Reagan Presidential Library at Stanford, working conditions for farmworkers on Webb Ranch (located on Stanford lands), Stanford presidents Donald Kennedy and Gerhard Casper, University Provost Condoleezza Rice, and other political issues.

items.title: Materials on the history of the Stanford University endowment, 1903-2004
items.description: Robert Augsburger was Stanford's vice president for business and finance from 1971 to 1977 and a lecturer in management at the Graduate School of Business from 1971 until he retired in 1995. Collection consists of original documents (in part, generated by Rodney Adams, Director of Finance 1976-85), copies of documents (in part, from Stanford University Archives collections), and Augsburger's notes and completed research, including spreadsheets on endowment figures for 1903-2002.

items.title: Notes on a visit to Stanford [motion picture] : a Film
items.description: Presents Congressman John Anderson's visit to Stanford University in 1981.

items.title: Peninsula-Times Tribune  photographs of Stanford University
items.description: The Peninsula-Times Tribune was organized in April 1979 from a merger of the Palo Alto Times and the Redwood City Tribune, both owned by the parent company Peninsula Newspapers Incorported. These photographs pertaining to Stanford University were selected from the morgue of the Peninsula Times-Tribune after its closing.

items.title: Stanford Alumni Association, the Audible Stanford
items.description: Founded in 1892 by the University's inaugural graduates, Stanford Alumni Association (SAA) orchestrates a wide spectrum of offerings and programming to provide support throughout individuals' Stanford journeys, encompassing their student years and subsequent lives as alumni. Audiocassettes from university and alumni events, 1984-1990, including lectures, classes, seminars, panels, and conferences.

items.title: Stanford Historical Society oral history program interviews
items.description: The Stanford Historical Society's Oral History Program explores the institutional history of the University, with an emphasis on the transformative post-WWII period, through interviews with leading faculty, staff, alumni, trustees, and others.
items.era_note: [About a quarter of these interviews, recollections of faculty, staff and students, concern these years.]

items.title: Stanford News Service records 1931-2023
items.description: The News Service reports and disseminates much of the University's news, via the STANFORD REPORT daily news email. Records include subject files compiled by the News Service in the course of its work, news releases prepared by the News Service, proof sheets of photographs produced by the News Service photographers, taped interviews, office files of the Director of News and Publications Service and of the directors of the individual units, news clippings, and miscellaneous photographic and printed material.

items.title: Stanford Oral History Project interviews, 1971-1995
items.description: The Stanford Oral History Project (SOHP), a joint effort of the Stanford University Archives and the Stanford Historical Society, began in 1978 as an extension of their efforts to collect, preserve and make available to researchers the historical record of the Stanford University community. These taped interviews and their transcriptions supplement the already strong collection of written and photographic materials in the University Archives, and provide a unique resource containing experiences and viewpoints not often found in traditional documents.

items.title: Stanford Tape Collection
items.description: The Stanford Tape Collection consists of historic music and speech recordings made on the campus of Stanford University. Many were used in the production of broadcasts by university radio station KZSU.

items.title: Stanford University Audio collection, circa 1949-2006 (inclusive)
items.description: The materials consist of audio recordings of Stanford events and activities.

items.title: Stanford University biographical files collection, circa 1891-2011
items.description: The collection contains biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford University.

items.title: Stanford University video collection, 1934-2016
items.description: Collection contains videorecordings and DVDs pertaining to Stanford University including lectures, cultural events, academic programs, faculty interviews, buildings, the university's history, and athletics other than football.

items.title: Stanford University, Center for Professional Development, Audiovisual Recordings
Stanford University, School of Humanities and Sciences, Department of Applied Physics, records 1955-2017
items.description: Applied Physics began as the Division of Applied Physics in 1962 in response to a recognition of the expanding boundaries of physics as applied to particle accelerators, condensed matter, and devices. Administrative and historical records of the program including creating the Division of Applied Physics and its later Departmentalization; Hubert (Hu) C. Heffner files; photographs, flyers, and event materials; audiovisual media including interviews.

items.title: Stanford: a sentimental journey : video recordings, 1987
items.description: This film in celebration of Stanford University's centennial includes interviews with faculty and alumni; scenes of academic and student activities; views of the campus; and still photographs transferred to video, primarily concerning the history of Stanford.

items.title: Uncommon man dinner [videorecording]
items.description: Awards presented to William R. Hewlett, Lucille Packard, and David Packard; speakers included Peggy Menzinger, president of Stanford Associates, William R. Hewlett, and David W. Packard. Event also included "Uncommon Musical Salute," created and narrated by Peter Arnot.

items.title: Visit of Li Peng to Stanford University : video recording, 1985
items.description: Li Peng, vice premier of China, visited Stanford University and the Center for Integrated Systems as part of a tour of Silicon Valley industries in July of 1985. While at Stanford he participated in a panel discussion with Stanford professors and Silicon Valley experts and gave a talk.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford University

items.title: Academic Computing Interview Project, 1983-1986
items.description: Academic Computing provides technology expertise, resources, and services directly to students and faculty, and to other organizations that in turn support aspects of the mission This collection consists of Jefferey Olson's doctoral research materials and recorded inteviews held in 1986 with administrators in charge of Academic Computing at Stanford.

items.title: Donald Kennedy, President of Stanford University, papers
items.description: Kennedy was Stanford's eighth president, serving from 1980 to 1992. Contains materials related to his time as Stanford's eighth president and vice president and provost under his predecessor President Richard W. Lyman.

items.title: Edward E. Shaw papers
items.description: Edward E. Shaw, born November 8, 1942, Stanford B.A. in economics 1965, joined the administrative staff of Stanford in the fall of 1965 as a contract administrator in the controller's office. These records reflect the wide variety of assignments carried out by Shaw as Executive Assistant to William F. Miller. Included are correspondence, reports, minutes, memoranda, proposals, grant files, calendars, patent files, and other materials regarding computation, research funding, budgetary matters, and university administration.

items.title: H. Bruce Franklin Collection
items.description: This collection includes newspapers clippings, Stanford news releases, leaflets and pamphlets relating to Franklin's tenure and dismissal hearings, the full text of the Advisory Board's recommendations, and transcripts of hearing proceedings.

items.title: Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve records, 1931-1992
items.description: Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve, which lies on 1,189 acres of Stanford land, routinely supports 45 to 50 research projects annually, with the majority directed by Stanford faculty and students. Correspondence, memoranda, reports, proposals, financial records, articles, class schedules and syllabi, student papers, questionnaires, and other records largely pertaining to administrative matters such as fencing, security, mosquito control, docents, tours, permits, Searsville Lake, and fundraising.

items.title: Joshua Lederberg papers, 1959-1979
items.description: He taught genetics at the University of Wisconsin before coming to the Stanford University School of Medicine in 1959 as Professor of genetics and biology. Papers consist of Lederberg's administrative files while head of the department of genetics at Stanford University Medical School from 1959 to 1978; they are divided into five series.

items.title: Kenneth M. Cuthbertson papers, 1941-1990
items.description: Cuthbertson was named one of the university's first three vice presidents in 1960. The papers, which include correspondence, minutes, reports, and memoranda, pertain largely to administration, finance, and planning at Stanford University.

items.title: Richard W. Lyman personal papers, 1778-2011
items.description: Lyman, who served as president from 1970 to 1980, held many posts during the 25 years he spent at Stanford: history professor, associate dean of the School of Humanities and Sciences, provost, president, and founder and director of the center now known as the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies.

items.title: Stanford University, ACME Project, records, 1961-1973
items.description: Collection consists of files relating to the ACME (Advanced Computer Medical Experiments) Project at Stanford, use of computers, and the establishment of a computer center at Stanford. Included are correspondence (including some by Gio Wiederhold), committee records, budget materials, grant files, and publications.

items.title: Stanford University, Assistant to the President for Black Affairs, records
items.description: In 1968, Stanford University created the new office of Assistant Provost for Minority Affairs, naming James E. Simmons to the post; in 1969, Mr. Simmon's title was changed to Assistant to the President for Black Affairs. The records of the office of James E. Simmons under its several titles includes correspondence, memoranda, reports, general material on black affairs at Stanford and some additional files on Native American students.

items.title: Stanford University, Board of Trustees, records
items.description: The Board administers the invested funds, sets the annual budget, and determines policies for the operation and control of the University. Records of the Trustees pertaining to legal issues, financial affairs, investments, academic departments, student housing, gifts received, real estate, campus development, and other administrative concerns.

items.title: Stanford University, Committee on Land and Building Development, records, 1950-1999
items.description: The Committee on Land and Building Development is responsible for providing input and/or recommendations to the President and other administrative officers on the planning and development of academic campus lands; on basic design guidelines for architecture and landscaping; and planning for transportation services. The collection primarily contains minutes, with some correspondence and reports. Specific projects covered in these records include the VA hospital, the Palo Alto Hospital, the Pine Hill Subdivision, the fraternity clusters project, additions to the Stanford Linear Accelerator (SLAC), plans for the Cowell Student Health Center, and the Peter Coutts faculty housing project.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Computer Science, Magnetic Computer Tapes
Stanford University, Department of Physics, research grants
items.description: Research grant files containing abstracts, proposals, correspondence, and budget memoranda; faculty members represented include William Fairbank, Melvin Schwartz, John Dirk Walecka, Robert Hofstadter, and Felix Bloch.

items.title: Stanford University, Faculty Senate, records, 1891-2026(inclusive)
items.description: The Academic Council was organized by the Stanford University faculty in 1904 and currently consists of members of the Professoriate and certain officers of the academic administration as specified by the Articles of Organization. In 1968 the Academic Council created the Senate of the Academic Council, composed of representatives elected from the Council. They include minutes, memoranda, correspondence, reports, election records, agendas and supporting documents, rosters, memorial resolutions on deceased members, and audiotapes of meetings.

items.title: Stanford University, Government and Community Relations, records
Stanford University, Information Technology Services, records, 1960-1985
items.description: This collection contains the office files from Information Technology Services and its various predecessors, dating from 1960 to 1985. The records include correspondence, minutes, reports, proposals, contracts, budgets, manuals, bulletins, newsletters, conference proceedings, consultants' files, licensing records, computer printouts, and a small number of computer tapes. The records pertain to computer systems used in the University, the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center, and the Medical Center as well as other operations of ITS.

items.title: Stanford University, School of Engineering, photograph collection, 1963-2014
items.description: Accession 2010-026 contains portraits of faculty that were once on display in the department. Accession 2010-027 contains assorted photographs from the Design Division, circa 1970-1998, which includes casual portraits of faculty, meetings, and social events, one photograph album (1984-85), and one folder of clippings and brochures.

items.title: Stanford University, Special Services Office, records
items.description: These six boxes contain mainly office correspondence and informative material pertaining to the draft and draft counseling. Also included are 5 volumes of computer printouts of statistical analyses concerning Stanford students and their draft classifications.

items.title: Stanford University, Sponsored Projects Office, grant award files 1983-1984
items.description: The Office of Sponsored Research (OSR), under the Office of Research of Administration (ORA), provided pre-award and post-award administrative services for sponsored projects. Collection also includes Report on the Research Program on Situated Language at the Center for the Study of Language and Information, 1984.

items.title: Stanford University, Sponsored Projects Office, records, 1935-1995
items.description: Records from the Sponsored Projects Office pertain to administrative matters and to individual projects; included are correspondence, memoranda, reports, minutes, patent files, and financial records. Specific topics include the Solar Energy Research Institute, 1976-77; the BALLOTS project, 1975; the NIRT project; the Te Vega research ship; the Stanford Electronics Laboratory; the San Joaquin Basin Analysis Project; indirect cost recovery; the Committee on Research; and the Committee on Government Relations.

items.title: Stanford University, University Committee on Minority Issues, records
items.description: The University Committe on Minority Issues was established by the President and Provost in October 1987 in response to a demand by the Rainbow Agenda (a coalition of minority groups) to explore the critical concerns of minority students, faculty, and staff at Stanford University. Records include correspondence, reports, surveys, questionnaires, interviews, tables, articles, brochures, clippings, audio tapes, and other items pertaining to minority students, faculty, and staff at Stanford University, compiled from University documents, reports, and data files and from interviews and surveys with students, faculty, and staff conducted by SRI International and Pacific Management Systems.

items.title: Stanford University, Vice President for Business Affairs, records
items.description: The collection includes minutes, reports, correspondence, leases, proposals, and other records pertaining to financial and business aspects of the administration of Stanford University. Among the subjects covered by the records are property matters, land development, building projects on campus, academic departments and professional schools, faculty and student housing, the hospital and medical center, SLAC, shopping center, industrial park, Jasper Ridge, relations with Palo Alto, roads, and water.

items.title: William F. Miller papers, 1957-2013
items.description: He was the last faculty member recruited to Stanford University by the legendary Frederick Terman, who was then Vice President and Provost of Stanford. Miller himself later became Vice President and Provost of Stanford. He conducted research and directed many graduate students in Computer Science. The collection consists of the professional and personal papers of Dr. William F. Miller including Provost's correspondence and memos, private correspondence, policy and memos, appointment books and date notebooks, talks given by Miller, articles written by Miller, photographs, news clippings and news releases.

items.title: William R. Rambo papers, 1939-1992 (inclusive), 1954-1974 (bulk)
items.description: He was made a Professor of Electrical Engineering in 1957, Director of Electronics Labs in 1960, and Associate Dean of the School of Engineering in 1961. These papers, kept in their original arrangement, reflect Prof. Rambo's administrative responsibilities as well as his research interests, largely during his time at Stanford University. Stanford subjects include the School of Engineering, the Electrical Engineering Department, the Stanford Electronic Labs, the Applied Electronics Lab, research policy at Stanford, courses, the Academic Senate, the University Land and Building Development Committee, and student demonstrations.

sectors.name: Education and research

items.title: Cecilia P. Burciaga papers, circa 1952-2006
items.description: One of the first high-ranking Chicana administrators at a private university, Cecilia Preciado Burciaga (1945-2013) was a leader in civil rights and education who inspired generations of students during a twenty year career at Stanford University and later California State University-Monterey Bay. Contains correspondence, published and unpublished writing and speech transcripts, articles and publicity featuring Burciaga, and a variety of publications, reports, and organizational materials.

items.title: Gene Golub papers, 1950-2007
items.description: Gene Golub (1932-2007) was a Professor of Computer Science at Stanford University. Gene was a leading pioneer in the field of numerical analysis, creating algorithms and software that allowed researchers to run large engineering and science calculations effectively on computers. This collection is comprised of Professor Golub's professional records and includes notebooks on his research for his publications, lecture notes, articles, manuscripts, grant files, bibliographic materials on contemporaries, and correspondence.

items.title: George B. Dantzig papers, 1934-2005
items.description: George Bernard Dantzig (November 8, 1914 – May 13, 2005) was an American mathematical scientist who made important contributions to operations research, computer science, economics, and statistics. Dantzig was the Professor Emeritus of Transportation Sciences and Professor of Operations Research and of Computer Science at Stanford.

items.title: Lincoln E. Moses papers, 1947-1991 (inclusive dates) 1962-1984 (bulk dates)
items.description: Lincoln E. Moses (1921-2007), PhD, was a professor emeritus of health research and policy and of statistics, who spearheaded the development of biostatistics at Stanford. This collection consists of Moses’ research notes, drafts, publications, committee records, speaker consultations, course materials, and correspondence.

items.title: Martin Edward Hellman papers, 1971-2013 (inclusive)
items.description: Returning to Stanford in 1971, he served on the regular faculty until becoming Professor Emeritus in 1996. Hellman is best known for his invention, with Diffie and Merkle, of public key cryptography. The materials consist of research files, subject files, publications and correspondence documenting public key cryptography and the Beyond War project.

items.title: Mathematical writing (CS 209) : lectures, 1987
items.description: Video taped lectures from Knuth's computer science course Mathematical Writing, given in the fall of 1987; guest lecturers were Herb Wilf, Jeff Ullman, Leslie Lamport, Nils Nilsson, Mary-Claire van Leunen, Rosalie Stemer, and Paul Halmos.

items.title: Mathematical writing (CS 209) videorecordings
items.description: Professor of computer science at Stanford University. Videotaped lectures from Knuth's computer science course Mathematical Writing, given in the fall of 1987. The course focused on issues of technical writing and the effective presentation of mathematics and computer science.

items.title: Stanford University technical reports, 1956-1970
items.description: Archival copies of technical reports resulting from sponsored research at Stanford.

items.title: Stanford University, Stanford Electronics Laboratories, records, 1948-1990
items.description: Stanford Electronics Laboratories technical reports, electronics research reviews, and research notebooks, including three volumes on early traveling wave tube research.

items.title: W. Conyers Herring papers, 1970-2003
items.description: Professor emeritus of applied physics at Stanford University. Herring was a leader in the field of solid-state physics, the study of the arrangement and interaction of atoms in solid materials. The materials consist of two reports where Herring was the chairman: "Report of the Panel on Economics of the Science Information Council," January 1973, and "Report of the Task Group on the Economics of Primary Publication" (published by the National Academy of Sciences, 1970); and notes prepared for a series of lectures on the evolution of solid-state physics.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Art, music, literature and photography

items.title: 3:16 BIBLE TEXTS ILLUMINATED production records, 1978-1996 (inclusive), 1985-1996 (bulk)
items.description: Professor of computer science at Stanford University. Collection includes Knuth's research notes, drafts of the manuscript and readers' comments, correspondence with Hermann Zapf, artistic co-worker, correspondence with illustrators and publishers, artwork, proofs, and "exabyte" computer tapes of the artwork, text, and fonts used in the book.

items.title: Abraham Aronow photograph archive, circa 1980-2013
items.description: Abe Aronow lives in the San Francisco Bay Area, and has focused his work on portraiture of photographers, artists, authors, musicians, scholars, scientists, physicians, and other people he admires. Approximately two-thirds of these 185 prints are of unnamed people in the "street," interesting to see in their own surroundings.

items.title: Art Com records, circa 1970-2005
items.description: La Mamelle / Art Com was a non-profit arts organization and artist-run space in San Francisco, California active from 1975 through 1995. Contains books, catalogues, periodicals, artwork, photography, publications, publicity, correspondence, financial documents and other material.

items.title: Barbara Carrasco papers, circa 1971-1997
items.description: Barbara Carrasco is a painter and muralist in Los Angeles whose work has been important in the development of Chicano art, U.S. contemporary political and public art, and women's cultural production. Collection consists of correspondence, particularly with Harry Gamboa, Gloria Molina, Edward James Olmos, Cesar Chavez, Dolores Huerta, and Robert Rodriguez, original artwork, material about Cesar Chavez and the UFW, publications about Mexican American art and her own work including issues of Chismearte, Corazón de Aztlán, Americas 2001, Caminos, and La Raza Magazine, photographs and videos.

items.title: Bruce Bliven papers, 1906-1985
items.description: Upon Herbert Croly's demise, Bliven succeeded as editor of New Republic. Continuing his freelance literary career, Bliven completed several works, including Five Million Words Later, his autobiography, and A Mirror for Greatness a biography of six famous Americans. Correspondence, notes, printed materials, photographs, and clippings covering Bliven's journalistic and literary careers.

items.title: Califas [videorecording] : Chicano art and culture in California, 1989
items.description: Contains the taped Califas Conference (held at the University of California, Santa Cruz, in 1982) as well as presentations of musical and theatrical works, interviews with performers, artists, and authors, and exhibitions of art. A comprehensive presentation of Chicano culture and society in California.

items.title: Carolyn Caddes papers and photographs, circa 1980-2015
items.description: Carolyn Caddes (1935- ) is an American photographer who spent years photographing portraits of famous Californian innovators. Her book, Portraits of Success: Impressions of Silicon Valley Pioneers, focused on Silicon Valley technology visionaries such as Steve Jobs, Robert Noyce and David Packard. Included in this collection are Caddes' interviews, portraits, research, correspondence and work files depicting Silicon Valley's technology industry, California wine makers and Caddes' personal work.

items.title: Crane, Bo. "Ticket to rock Palo Alto: descriptions of '60s-'90s musicians and their neighborhoods."
items.description: This collection consists of a booklet produced by Bo Crane and Palo Alto Stanford Heritage Small bound publication containing descriptions of Palo Alto musicians circa 1960-1990s.

items.title: David V. Harris papers, circa 1950s-2020s.
items.description: The collection covers the writing career and anti-Vietnam War activism of author and former Stanford student David V. Harris, spanning from the 1950s through the 2020s. The majority of the collection is made up of Harris' research files and notes from his non-fiction books.

items.title: Dexter Morrill Collection
items.description: Dexter George Morrill (1938-2019) was a composer, trumpet player, and professor of music best known for his collaboration with jazz saxophonist, Stan Getz during the premiere of 'Getz Variations for tenor saxophone and tape' (1984); a Morrill composition which merged jazz improvisation with computer-generated sounds. The collection focuses on the compositions and other documents created by Dexter Morrill during his career as a musician and composer.

items.title: Emmanuel Montoya collection of Chicano publications, 1969-1993
items.description: Emmanuel Montoya assembled this collection of Chicano publications, primarily concerning San Francisco Bay Area artists (including muralists), writers, musicians, political activists, etc. Included are artists' exhibition catalogs, and the anniversary issue of LOW RIDER ("projecting the positive image of Low Riding Culture").

items.title: Gerd Stern papers, 1938-2012
items.description: Gerd Stern is a poet, artist, and multimedia innovator whose remarkable life spans 40s bohemia, 50s Beat culture, 60s hippiedom, 70s hip capitalism, and onward. This collection is primarily correspondence, and dated outgoing drafts predominate. The majority of files date from the 1960s and 70s, and represent Stern's USCO and Intermedia work.

items.title: Harold Schmidt Collection
items.description: Sound recordings from Stanford University professor and choral director Harold C. Schmidt (1910-1993), including performances from the Stanford University Chorus, Choir, and Chamber Chorale. As director of the choir, he presided over nearly thirty years of commencements and Sunday services at Memorial Church before his retirement in 1975.

items.title: Ilka Hartmann photographs: "California Thinkers", 1966-2022
items.description: A collection of approximately 160 photographs, chiefly comprised of portraits, taken by Ilka Hartmann, ca. 1960s-2000s, and focusing on notable activists, environmentalists, writers, poets, artists, musicians in Northern California.

items.title: Ira Nowinski photograph collection, ca. 1965-2017
items.description: Ira Nowinski is an American photographer of Polish and Hungarian Jewish descent. In addition, he had been the staff photographer of the San Francisco Opera since 1978. The archive of photographer Ira Nowinski (b. 1942) contains prints, negatives, and proofsheets documenting multiple projects.

items.title: José Antonio Burciaga papers, circa 1940-1997
items.description: José Antonio "Tony" Burciaga was a Chicano writer, artist and poet. With his artwork, poetry, and writing, Jose Antonio Burciaga was a major contributor to Chicano culture and the Chicano Movement in the Bay Area California during the 1980s-1990s. His collection consists of correspondence, writings, artwork, articles and clippings, Chicanismo ephemera, and other materials.

items.title: Kitrick "Kit" Galloway and Sherrie Rabinowitz papers, 1971-1993
items.description: Collection consists of computer media, audiovisual media, thermal prints and other materials related to Kitrick "Kit" Galloway. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Leland C. Smith papers, 1958-1992
items.description: Leland Clayton Smith (1925-2014) was a Stanford Professor Emeritus of Music. Smith was a co-founder of the Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics (CCRMA) alongside John Chowning. This collection consists of research files, correspondence, sheet music, and audiovisual material.

items.title: Linda Connor photography collection
items.description: Accession 2018-559: this accession consists of a total of 33 photographs from Connor's Lick Observatory series (ten (10) 8” x 10” gelatin silver prints, twenty‐two (22) 11” x 14” gelatin silver prints, and one (1) 20” x 24” gelatin silver print).

items.title: Lola de la Riva papers
items.description: Lola de la Riva (born 1938 in Stockton, California) is a Chicana activist and artist. Includes documents, correspondence, research material, artworks, books and other publications, audio cassettes, and other materials.

items.title: Lorna D. Smith papers, 1930-1981 (inclusive), 1965-1975 (bulk)
items.description: She worked as a student nurse and as a researcher for novelist Theodore Dreiser (1938-1945), but is noted as a civil rights and social reform worker. Chiefly letters written to Lorna Smith from authors and politicians with whom she regularly corresponded. Much of the correspondence concerns Upton Sinclair, and authors Erna Holyer and Theodore Dreiser are also represented.

items.title: Lynn Hershman-Leeson papers, 1976-2004
items.description: Lynn Hershman Leeson (1941-) is an American new media artist and filmmaker. Her collection of archival papers, audiovisual media, publications, artifacts, photographs, and letters document Hershman Leeson's artworks and projects created since the 1970s.

items.title: Mary Jane Moffat papers, 1970-2004
items.description: Mary Jane Moffat (1933-2004) was an poet and memoirist who taught creative writing at San Francisco State, Foothill College, and other venues. She focused on the art of autobiography and the writing of memoirs.

items.title: Matt Kahn papers, 1951-1999
items.description: When he was 21, Kahn joined Stanford's Department of Art (now the Department of Art and Art History). That was in 1949, and over the following 60 years he created pioneering coursework in design and also taught painting, drawing, sculpture and color theory. Materials include professional files, teaching files (including videos of lectures), and photographs.

items.title: Original drawings for Ernesto Galarza's CHOGORROM, c. 1972
items.description: Attached to each drawing is a carbon of the text being illustrated, together with a pencil description of what should be portrayed.

items.title: Princeton Josquin Project collection, 1970-1980
items.description: The collection consists of computer printouts and musical notation produced by the computer programs corresponding to compositions by the renaissance composer Josquin des Prez.

items.title: Pulsa records, 1966-2019
items.description: The papers of 1960s-70s experimental multimedia collective Pulsa consist of project files, photographs, slides & negatives, and printed material about the group. Pulsa was an experimental multimedia arts collective founded in 1966 and active through 1973.

items.title: Rich Gold papers, 1978-2005
items.description: Rich Gold (1950-2003) was a digital artist, inventor, cartoonist, composer, lecturer and inter-disciplinary researcher. Rich Gold papers include notebooks (114), artwork, correspondence, and manuscript for The Plenitude, which was posthumously published in 2008.

items.title: Robert McDowell papers, circa 1970s-1990s
items.description: Collection includes manuscripts, drafts, journals and diaries, correspondence, and ephemera. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Sandor Salgo papers 1939-2005
items.description: Professor emeritus of Music, Sandor Salgo conducted the Marin Symphony for 33 years (1956-1989), the Carmel Bach Festival for 35 years (1956-1991), the San Jose Symphony for 19 years (1951-1970), and the Modesto Symphony for nine years (1951-1970). This collection contains audio recordings of concerts, posters, sheet music, and correspondence.

items.title: Stanford Program for Recordings in Sound Collection
items.description: The Stanford Program for Recordings in Sound was a project begun by English Department graduate student Mike Stillman that sponsored readings by poets and novelists either in residence or visiting Stanford. The collection consists of original open reel tapes of these readings.

items.title: Tillie Olsen papers, 1930-1990
items.description: Tell Me A Riddle was originally published in 1962, and its title novella received the O. Henry Award as the best American story of 1961. The collection includes personal and professional correspondence, literary manuscripts by American author Tillie Olsen and others, material on the Longshoremen's Strike and the Socialist Party from during the mid-1930s, teaching material and student work, clippings, pamphlets, book reviews, awards, etc.

items.title: Ylem records, 1971-2019 (bulk 1981-2012)
items.description: YLEM, Artists using science and technology, was an international networking organization of artists, scientists, authors, curators, educators, and art enthusiasts who explored the intersection of the arts and sciences. Includes directories, calendars, press releases, newsletters, YLEM journal, exhibit material, slides and photographs, administrative papers, clippings, flyers, videos, and CDs.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Design and architecture

items.title: Birge M. Clark papers, 1914-1985
items.description: Palo Alto architect. Served as advising architect on the Lou Henry Hoover house and created numerous distinctive public buildings and private homes in Palo Alto. Class records and memorabilia, 1914, design notebook from Columbia, 1915, correspondence, 1983-1985, Historical Society material and class and subject files.

items.title: Hanna house collection, 1900-1995 (inclusive)
items.description: In 1935, Paul and Jean Hanna commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design their home to be built on the Stanford University campus. Correspondence, blueprints, drawings, photographs, and other records relating to the planning, design and construction of the campus home of Professor and Mrs. Paul R. Hanna. The collection focuses on the Hanna's work with architect Frank Lloyd Wright extending from the initial planning of the house through later renovations.

items.title: Hanna House collection, 1935-1982 [microform]
items.description: In 1935, Paul and Jean Hanna commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design their home to be built on the Stanford University campus. Correspondence, blueprints, drawings, photographs, and other records relating to the planning, design and construction of the campus home of Professor and Mrs. Paul R. Hanna. The collection focuses on the Hanna's work with architect Frank Lloyd Wright extending from the initial planning of the house through later renovations.

items.title: Memorial Church acoustics papers
items.description: Typescript paper "Acoustical Renovation of Memorial Church at Stanford University," 1996, a copy of ACOUSTICS OF WORSHIP SPACES (edited by Wetherill and David Lubman, 1983), which has an entry on Memorial Church, and 99 slides of the interior and exterior of the church, 1979-87.

items.title: Sabin and O'Neal, Architects : photograph catalog of firm's designs, circa 1983
items.description: Residential, civic, industrial, and commercial architectural designs and photographs, primarily from the San Francisco Bay Area and within it primarily in Palo Alto and Stanford.

items.title: Stanford University, Operations and Maintenance, Maps and Records, architectural drawings, 1889-1994 [microform].
items.description: Microfiche copies of architectural drawings of buildings on the Stanford University campus; and photocopy of the department's "vault inventory" of drawings, most of which are included in these copies. There are also some copies of drawings for the Hanna House, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.

items.title: Stanford University, University Architect / Campus Planning and Design, records, 1945-2018
items.description: The Planning Office was officially organized in 1945 under the directorship of Eldridge T. Spencer. In addition to overseeing the architectural aspects of the campus, the office was also responsible for overseeing land use and traffic circulation. The records of the Planning Office date back to its orgins in 1945 and include correspondence, memoranda, minutes, reports, studies, surveys, maps, and plans.

items.title: Synergetics folio : set of ten screen printed posters, 1976-1977
items.description: This folio was published as a result of an exhibition on the work of Buckminster Fuller presented at the Penang Museum in 1978. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Victor K. Thompson Architectural Drawings, 1948-2000
items.description: Victor King Thompson (1913-2007) was a Stanford University professor emeritus of architecture. This collection contains the architectural drawings of Victor K. Thompson's private practice, with some additional drawings from Robert Peterson. The drawings primarily consist of building additions for the Ladera Community Church, Filoli Gardens, Filoli Center, Los Altos Hunt riding club, and numerous private homes throughout the San Francisco Peninsula.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Film, radio and television

items.title: Dorothy Fadiman/Concentric Media papers, 1955-2018
items.description: Dorothy Fadiman is the founder of Concentric Media, and has been producing films for 40 years. The collection consists of materials related to the career of filmmaker, producer, author and teacher Dorothy Fadiman from 1976-2018. Papers document publicity, interviews, production, fundraising, reception of films, festival showings, and work with television, such as PBS.

items.title: HEARTS & QUARKS : production materials, 1987-1988
items.description: Collection consists of original 16mm film negatives (with 3/4 inch video copies), audio tapes, and transcripts of interviews with Dr. Norman Shumway and Prof. Sidney Drell and of a conversation between Shumway and Drell. HEARTS & QUARKS, a film about the ethics and application of modern science and technology, was Jane Wagner's masters thesis project for the Dept. of Communications Documentary Film Program at Stanford.

items.title: KSFO Collection
items.description: The KSFO collection consists of audiovisual material and ephemera from this San Francisco radio station's years owned by Golden West Broadcasting, 1956-1983. The majority of this collection involves station marketing, promotions, and fundraisers, although there are airchecks and other broadcast recordings.

items.title: Peter Conn papers, circa early 1970s-1996
items.description: Peter Conn is a director and producer known for his advances in 3D computer-generated animation, graphics, and motion capture technology, primarily through his production company Homer & Associates. The bulk of the Peter Conn papers pertains to music videos and other Homer & Associates projects, such as commercials, short films, and contributions to feature films.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Press, journalism and broadcasting

items.title: David Bohrman archive of innovation in media & journalism, circa 1960s-2014
items.description: Materials include Bohrman's papers as well as ephemera, and two servers of digital files, and additional digital files received via electronic transfer.
items.era_note: [About a quarter of this archive, papers from Bohrman's television news work of the 1970s and 1980s, concerns this period.]

items.title: Kate Coleman papers, circa 1960s-1990s
items.description: Collection consists of print, manuscript, photographs and some audiovisual materials relating to the journalism career of Kate Coleman.

items.title: Reese Erlich papers, circa 1931-2015
items.description: Reese Erlich (1947-2021) was an author and freelance journalist living and working in the Bay Area for much of his career. Files, photographs, and recordings pertaining to Bay Area journalist Reese Erlich's career reporting on a variety of topics including local stories and US foreign policy from the late 1960s through 2010s.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Sport and recreation

items.title: Basic mountaineering course : typescript, 1971
items.description: Includes chapters on equipment (Ed Goddard), food, map and compass, weather, first aid, and a reprint of a John Fowles article, "Weeds, Bugs, Americans." Also includes the training schedule with a list of the people responsible for each subject.

items.title: Camp Unalayee Association records, 1949-2025
items.description: Camp Unalayee was founded in 1949 with Lucile Manley's donation of her home and land in the Santa Cruz Mountains to the American Friends Service Committee (AFSC) with the intent to operate an "interracial camp managed by Friends." The collection contains various historical administrative records from the Camp Unalayee Association pertaining to the operations of the summer camp program's backpacking trips, fundraising activities to support low-income campers, and the use of land in California's Trinity Alps Wilderness.

items.title: Leigh N. Ortenburger papers and photographs, 1929-1996
items.description: The papers of Leigh N. Ortenburger contain correspondence, personal papers, maps, manuscripts, and photographic negatives and prints, with emphasis on the Cordillera Blanca in Peru and the Teton Range in Wyoming. He was the early author and eventual co-author of the definitive climber?s guide to the Teton Range, had nearly finished a manuscript on the early exploration of the range, including the controversy on the first ascent of the Grand Teton, and in ten trips to the Cordillera Blanca had obtained extensive material for a photo essay on the range which was never finished.

sectors.name: Arts and culture

items.title: Fidelity Sound Recordings Collection
items.description: This collection consists of commercially-released audio recordings created by the independent record company Fidelity Sound Recordings (FSR) based in Redwood City, California. The predominant musical genre featured is marching band music performed by university bands, bands affiliated with the Salvation Army, and miscellaneous ensembles in the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, and elsewhere.

items.title: Jalonen theater & music program collection
items.description: The John W. Jalonen program collection is comprised of various playbill and performance programs mostly from local and regional production companies around the San Francisco Bay Area presented between the 1940s and 2000s.

items.title: Stanford University Press archival book copies, 1900-2013
items.description: The Stanford University Press was established as an independent printing operation at Stanford University in 1892. It publishes scholarly monographs, textbooks, and professional reference works. The collection consists of archival copies of books published by Stanford University Press.

items.title: Sunset Magazine records, 1931-1998
items.description: The records of Sunset Magazine primarily consist of over 100,000 photographs as published in the magazine from 1948-1969 and 1977-1998. Given Sunset's focus as the "Magazine of Western Living," however, one may expect to find photographs of gardening and landscaping, architecture and home improvement, cooking and food, entertaining, travel, nature, and recreation.

sectors.name: Society and community — Activism and advocacy

items.title: "Freiheit für Angela Davis" ephemera collection, 1971-1972
items.description: Angela Davis (born 1944) is an American political activist, who was arrested in 1970 in relation to a murder case. Materials include correspondence from the East German "Freiheit für Angela Davis" Campaign, 1971-1972. Archive of approximately 90 items, chiefly signed postcard petitions, including 13 letters and broadsides, single pages and folded many with original illustrations and envelopes, addressed to Judge Richard Arnason at the Santa Clara District Court or the United Committee to Free Angela Davis on the cover.

items.title: Adele Panofsky collection of Mid-Peninsula Citizens for Fair Housing materials, 1963-2009
items.description: She was a member of the Mid-Peninsula Citizens for Fair Housing (MCFH) and served as the Treasurer from 1969-1978. MCFH continued to fight discrimination in housing in Palo Alto, Menlo Park, Mountain View and other municapalities of the Mid-Peninsula region of the San Francisco Bay Area. The collection contains documents collected by Adele Panofsky in her association with the Mid-Peninsula Citizens for Fair Housing organization.

items.title: American Civil Liberties Union of Northern California records, 1900-2000 bulk 1934-2000
items.description: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) is a non-profit organization committed to the defense, preservation, and extension of civil liberties in the United States. Comprising correspondence, minutes, policy statements, reports, court transcripts, attorney notes, scrapbooks, newspaper clippings, pamphlets, and other printed material created or collected by the ACLU-NC, these records document the establishment and activities of the northern California branch and its wide-ranging efforts to protect and extend individual liberties in California.

items.title: Armando Valdez papers, 1965-2005
items.description: In 1966, Valdez cofounded the LA CAUSA Center (Latin American Community Action to Uplift Student Activities), an educational clearinghouse for Chicano youth in Oakland, California, where he also served as Director. Accession 1985-002 contains records of the organizations and activities Dr. Valdez directed between 1965 and 1977. The organizations are all related to his activities in promoting Mexican American and Chicano achievement in education and political leadership in the Spanish-speaking community.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- Dorothy Day and the Catholic Worker Movement, 1968-1973
items.description: Dorothy Day (November 8, 1897 - November 29, 1980) was an American journalist, social activist, and devout Catholic convert. These images were primarily taken in 1973 (with a few from 1968) at the Catholic Worker Movement house located in the Bowery neighborhood in New York City, at the Catholic Worker Movement farm in Tivoli, New York, and at United Farm Workers (UFW) demonstrations in California.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive, 1965-2013
items.description: The Bob Fitch Photography Archive consists of the photographic work of activist and photojournalist Bob Fitch, documenting the civil rights movement, the farm worker movement, the peace movement, other social justice movements and issues, cultural change, religion, as well as his professional and personal life.

items.title: California social, protest, and counterculture movements ephemera collection, 1965-1980
items.description: Consists of a variety of ephemera created by activist groups and organizations relating to social, protest, and counterculture movements in California, particularly in San Francisco and the greater Bay Area. The collection includes flyers, brochures, announcements, newsletters, broadsides, newsletters, newspapers, and other printed materials related to social justice, civil rights, gay and lesbian rights, womens' rights, the Anti-Vietnam War Movement and the Free Speech Movement.

items.title: Christopher Jones papers, 1965-2016
items.description: Jones was a Vietnam War draft resister and was sentenced to Safford Federal Prison from 1970-1971. This collection consists of correspondence, notes, newsletters, underground newspapers, school documents, legal documents, audiovisual materials, and photographs.

items.title: Collection of materials opposing the Simpson-Mazzoli Bill, 1982
items.description: The Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1982 (the Simpson-Mazzoli Bill) called on employers to attest to employee immigration status and made it illegal to knowingly hire unauthorized immigrants. The 17 pieces in this collection were mainly generated by the Bay Area Committee Against the Simpson/Mazzoli Bill. They include flyers, information packets, model telegram to lawmakers, blank petition, tabloid newspaper-format brochures, notes from a Nov. 8, 1982, BACASM meeting, and other materials published by opponents of the bill.

items.title: Community Service Organization History Project records, 1997-2009
items.description: The Community Service Organization was an important California Latino civil rights organization, most famous for training Cesar Chavez. The Community Service Organization History Project papers includes oral history interviews and other media as well as files from the CSO itself, especially pertaining to its Bakersfield Chapter, 1955-2002.

items.title: Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility (CPSR) records, 1980-2004
items.description: Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility (CPSR) was an organization promoting the responsible use of computer technology. It educated policymakers and the public on a wide range of issues including privacy, design, and the role of computers in defense. Records of the policy group Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility (CPSR), consisting of correspondence, memoranda, newsletters, board minutes, publications, media, and other material.

items.title: East Palo Alto Council of Tenants records, undated
items.description: The East Palo Alto Council of Tenants, founded in 1982, is an organization dedicated to protecting tenants' rights in East Palo Alto, California.

items.title: John W. Gardner papers, 1912-2004
items.description: Gardner served as the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare under President Lyndon Johnson from 1965-1968. He founded the citizen's advocacy group Common Cause and was the chairman of the Commission on White House Fellowships. Collection includes speeches and writings by, as well as articles about Gardner; correspondence, awards and honors, photographs, audiovisual material, and files from many of Gardner's organizations including Common Cause, the White House Fellows, the Haas Center for Public Service, and the John W. Gardner Center.

items.title: Lois Crozier Hogle papers, 1950-2002
items.description: Lois Crozier Hogle was a pioneer in the San Francisco Bay Area environmental movement, co-founding the Committee for Green Foothills with Ruth Spangenberg in 1962. Between 1986 and 1992 she had a column in the Palo Alto Weekly about environmental and social issues.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records, 1967-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. Included in the collection are more than 2000 linear feet of litigation case files focusing on such issues as employment discrimination, education rights, reproductive rights, voting rights, and other related civil rights issues.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 1, Board of Directors records, 1967-1993
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. MALDEF's Board of Directors is the organization's governing body; the directors assist the lead staff in program planning, fundraising, and administrative decisions.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 5, Legal Programs Department, 1968-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. This record group includes the files generated and collected by Rosen and Baller from 1972 until 1983, as they directed and developed MALDEF's litigation.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 6, Community Education and Activation program, 1976-1982
items.description: Files of James Perez, subject files, and correspondence files of Vilma Lacayo. The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. In 1976 MALDEF createdthe Community Education and Activation Project, with a Public Policy Research component, which later spun off into a separate department.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 6.5, Leadership Programs, 1979-1994
items.description: Ralph Hurtado's files, chronological files, and program files. The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. The Leadership Development and Advocacy Program was also a spin-off of CEAP, and was created in 1980 to prepare a pool of Chicanos for appointments to commissions and boards by increasing their sophistication about the political process in their communities.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 9, Regional and Program Offices, 1967-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. In the early years, the offices concentrated on local legal work, and were funded by the initial Ford grant.

items.title: National Committee to Defend the Rights of South Vietnamese Students records, 1972
items.description: This collection consists of correspondence, petitions, and newspaper clippings regarding the National Committee to Defend the Rights of South Vietnamese Students. The materials in the collection primarily document the efforts of the National Committee to Defend the Rights of South Vietnamese Students to prevent Nguyen Tang Huyen from being returned to South Vietnam.

items.title: National United Committee to Free Angela Davis records, circa 1970-1972
items.description: This collection was created in the course of a massive defense campaign following the capture and trial of Angela Davis. The records of the National United Committee to Free Angela Davis consists overwhelmingly of support letters, most sent from East Germany and the Soviet Union, which the group used to demonstrate global opinion about her conspiracy trial in California. The collection also contains some of the organization's administrative records, publications and correspondence with a variety of other political organizations.

items.title: Pacific Life Community records, 1972-1982, 2017
items.description: Pacific Life Community began as a small group committed to resisting the coming of Trident [nuclear submarines] to the Pacific Northwest. Materials consist of publications, notes, correspondence, newspaper clippings, minute meetings, photographs, slides and related ephemera.

items.title: Pacific Studies Center records, circa 1969-2017
items.description: Materials from the Pacific Studies Center on subject matter such as Silicon Valley companies, the electronics and communications industries, environmental issues and records from company president Lenny Siegel's participation in committees on these issues, labor issues, U.S. military and weaponry, government reports, and regional country files. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Physicians for Social Responsibility, Mid-Peninsula & Stanford Chapter, Prescription for Prevention proceedings
items.description: Proceedings from a symposium on nuclear war held at Stanford University in October 1983. Speakers included Gordon A. Craig, Admiral Noel A.M. Gaylor, Sidney D. Drell, Erik H. Erikson, Alexander Sakharov, Helen Caldicott, Victor W. Sidel, Melvin Konner, and Robert Karl Manoff.

items.title: Robert C. Aldridge papers, circa 1970s-1990s
items.description: Collection consists of collected writings, research materials, correspondence, printed material, photographs and printed ephemera relating to the life and career of Robert C. [Creston] Aldridge (1926-2022) with a particular focus on his activities as an anti-nuclear and peace activist and an advisor/consultant/sponsor in many groups and organizations including Ground Zero Center for Nonviolent Action, Nuclear Age Peace Foundation, British-American Security Information Council, Institute for Law and Peace, Fellowship of Reconciliation, the Pacific Life Community, Veterans for Peace and others.

items.title: Robert P. J. Cooney, Jr. papers on the Institute for the Study of Nonviolence, 1965-1987
items.description: Materials consist of correspondence, photos, letters, papers, notes, mailing lists, printed material, books, CDs, a thumb drive, and other material from Robert Cooney's time working as a staff member at the Institute for the Study of Nonviolence. Topics include the Institute's "Power to the People" campaign, the Agape Foundation, draft resistance, and more.

items.title: Salvador Enrique Alvarez personal archive, 1950s-2015
items.description: Materials consist of Salvador E. Alvarez's papers related to his political activism and community involvement, including the United Farm Workers, the Hispanic Catholics of America, and the founding of the School of Social Work at San Jose State.
items.era_note: [The archive runs to 2015, and about two-fifths of it, his activism and community work, concerns this period.]

items.title: Stanford Physicians for Social Responsibility records, circa 1981-2005
items.description: The Stanford chapter of Physicians for Social Responsibility (PSR) was established in 1981 as a regional extension of the national organization, which was founded in 1961. The bulk of the records focuses on the organization's efforts during the 1980s and early 1990s to advocate for nuclear test bans, the reduction and elimination of nuclear weapons, and fostering positive relations between the United States and the Soviet Union.

items.title: Unity/La Unidad Archive Project collection, circa 1970-1990
items.description: Unity/La Unidad was a newspaper published from 1978 to 1990 by the League of Revolutionary Struggle (M-L). Unity/La Unidad offered a radical perspective on national and international news along with first-hand reports from the frontlines of battles for self-determination, worker’s rights, women’s liberation, and social justice. The collection consists of 170.19 gigabytes of born-digital materials captured from a hard drive provided by the donor.

sectors.name: Society and community — Local and California history

items.title: California biography collection
items.description: Consists of ephemeral items relating to people widely known and relatively unknown in California. Contains mostly newspaper obituaries, but also includes: handwritten biographical documents, invitations, wedding announcements, family reunion newsletters, genealogy forms, family trees, memorials, political speeches, campaign material, correspondence, and newspaper and magazine clippings.

items.title: Dreams of a city [videorecording] : creating East Palo Alto
items.era_note: [Most of this 1997 documentary concerns the campaign that made East Palo Alto a city, incorporated in 1983.]

items.title: The valley of Santa Clara; historic buildings : research papers, 1965-1975
items.description: Notes, maps, photographs, and clippings used in the preparation of Butler's THE VALLEY OF SANTA CLARA: HISTORIC BUILDINGS.

sectors.name: Society and community — Medicine and public health

items.title: [Collection of records from Lucile Packard Chldren's Hospital and predecessors], 1959-2002
items.description: Consists of files from organizations listed in this record, including Board meeting minutes, committee meeting minutes (legal, finance, audit, credentials and policies/procedures), chronological files and construction files.

items.title: Halsted Holman papers, circa 1931-2015
items.description: Most files involve Health care reform, Chronic disease self-care programs, the Robert Wood Johnson Clinical Scholars Program, the Midpeninsula Health Service, and Holman's social and political activism. There is a particular emphasis on the Stanford Peace Movement and Anti-War materials.

items.title: Henry S. Kaplan papers, circa 1960-1983
items.description: Radiologist, cancer research pioneer and educator. Kaplan was best known for his work on leukemia and Hodgkins disease and for his work with Edward Ginzton on the development of the medical linear accelerator for cancer treatment. Professional and administrative correspondence; research and clinical abstract files, and research notebooks; films; biographical material including an oral history interview; and other files.

items.title: Jay Haley papers, 1957-2007
items.description: He was a pioneer in family therapy, and his work traces its birth and development during half a century. The Jay Haley collection documents Haley's career through correspondence, manuscripts, typescripts, and media materials.

items.title: Joseph Hopkins papers, circa 1970-1990
items.description: Dr. Joseph R. Hopkins, MD, MMM, is Clinical Professor Emeritus at Stanford University's Department of Medicine, Division of Primary Care and Population Health. The bulk of the material reflects the organizational operations of the Midpeninsula Health Service and The Birth Place through memos, correspondence, letters, financial reports, and public relations documents.

items.title: Kenneth D. Brock journals, 1949-2018
items.description: Brock was hired in 1984 by the State of California, Department of Health Services, to work as a consultant with the Centers for Disease Control to establish a registry of AIDS cases in California. Journals including some correspondence and photographs.

items.title: Mental Research Institute (MRI) records
items.description: The Mental Research Institute (MRI) is a small, independent, multi-disciplinary, non-profit corporation founded in Palo Alto, California, and is one of the pioneering institutions of brief and family therapy methodology. The material described in this finding aid consists of therapy sessions, notes, drafts, research proposals, clinical practice files, grant files, conference proceedings, publications, audiovisual material, born-digital material, and other material related to the operation of MRI.

items.title: Russel V.A. Lee papers, 1935-1976
items.description: Chiefly correspondence together with supporting subject material, including pamphlets, minutes, and newsletters, related to work as Founder and Director of the Palo Alto Medical Clinic, 1924-61. Major subject groupings in health insurance, health care for the aging, community medical clinics and group medical practice.

items.title: Stanford Prevention Research Center, Five-City Project, videorecordings, 1980-1984
items.description: The Five City Project education campaign began in 1978 and ran for six years. The media campaign was designed to test if measurable risk reduction could be produced in a free-living population. Collection includes videorecordings from the Five City Project education campaign.

items.title: Thomas C. Merigan papers 1967-2016
items.description: Thomas C. Merigan is the George E. and Lucy Becker Professor of Medicine, Emeritus at the Stanford University. He helped introduce the use of human interferon into the United States as a treatment for viral diseases and helped develop anti-viral drugs to treat HIV/AIDS. This collection consists of correspondence, news releases, clippings, lectures, photographs, and audio cassette tapes.

items.title: William C. Dement papers, circa 1960s-1990s
items.description: William C. Dement is Professor Emeritus in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Stanford. He founded the Sleep Research Center at Stanford and co-founded the Sleep Research Society. Collection mainly consists of correspondence, administrative records from various sleep research organizations he was involved in, and sleep studies and research.

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: Michael L. Belangie papers, 1945-1980
items.description: In late 1945 he purchased Menlo Textiles, a national purveyor of custom-loomed fabrics in Menlo Park, California, some thirty miles south of San Francisco. His public service efforts led him to run for the Menlo Park City Council in 1950, an election that he won. Personal and professional papers, some also pertaining to his wife, Mary.

items.title: Richard W. and Elizabeth Lyman personal papers, 1940-2013
items.description: Elizabeth (Jing) Lyman (wife of Richard Lyman, seventh president of Stanford University) was active in community affairs, the Women's Resource Center, and other foundations. Primarily contains materials relating to Elizabeth (Jing) Lyman's activities in community affairs, personal correspondence, and activities of both Elizabeth and Richard Lyman.

sectors.name: Society and community — Philanthropy and foundations

items.title: Anne Firth Murray papers, 1970-2018
items.description: For the past twenty-five years, she has worked in the field of philanthropy, serving as a consultant to many foundations. She is the Founding President of The Global Fund for Women, which provides funds internationally to seed, strengthen, and link groups committed to women's well being. Papers include Murray's Global Fund for Women and Hewlett Foundation files; teaching files; professional files; and subject files.

items.title: System Development Foundation records, 1957-1993
items.description: The System Development Foundation was a scientific funding organization which distributed all its funds within a finite period of time. The documents from SDF's active period include minutes and agenda materials, administrative correspondence files for proposals received, financial and administrative records of the Foundation itself, and general reference files.

items.title: William Hewlett papers, 1907-2018 (bulk 1960-2001)
items.description: William Hewlett was the co-founder of Hewlett-Packard, one of the most successful technology start-up companies in the history of Silicon Valley. Following the tremendous success of Hewlett-Packard, he became well known for his philanthropy, donating millions of dollars from his fortune to support various causes. The William Hewlett papers consists of correspondence, photographs, financial records, reports, minutes, calendars, hardware, electronic files, videotapes, newspaper clippings, publications, and other materials.

sectors.name: Society and community — Race, ethnicity and immigration

items.title: Emory M. Lee collection of Asian American papers, circa 1960-2008
items.description: Newspapers, newsletters, journals and periodicals pertaining to the Asian American experience. Emphasis is on the local San Francisco Bay Area, but also includes nationwide material. Also includes administrative material on the Stanford Asian Pacific American Alumni Club (SAPAAC).

items.title: Issei Oral History Project in Watsonville Collection
items.description: The Issei Oral History Project in Watsonville was created by historian Kazuko Nakane in preparation for the book Nothing Left in my Hands : The Issei of a Rural California Town, 1900-1942. Interviews were conducted by Nakane from 1978 to 1983 with fifteen Japanese-American residents in Watsonville, California. The collection contains the original audiocassettes of these interviews and their transcripts in English.

items.title: Jewish life in the San Francisco Bay Area, 1981-2010
items.description: The collection documents non-traditional Jewish life in the Bay Area, especially newsletters and announcements from various organizations. There are also liturgical creations around life-cycle events. Material collected by Roger S. Kohn and Zachary M. Baker, both Stanford University Library curators, from local synagogues, individuals, organizations, and businesses.

items.title: Kenneth Kann papers and oral histories relating to the Petaluma (CA) Jewish chicken ranchers and egg farmers and the life of Joe Rapoport, circa 1970-1995
items.description: While at Berkeley, Kann began writing a popular history of the Petaluma Jewish chicken ranching community with support from the California Historical Society and the National Endowment for the Humanities. The collection contains interview tapes and transcripts used as research for author Kenneth Kann's two books about the Jewish community in Petaluma, California, during the twentieth century.

items.title: Kistler family papers, circa 1940-2013
items.description: This small archive consists mainly of information relating to Olga Ritso's family history, and her husband Walter Kistler's scientific work. It illustrates the interconnectivity between Estonia and the US in the twentieth century. Includes files, correspondence, photographs, awards, and audiovisual material including audio interviews with Olga Ritso Kistler and Aadu Ritso.

items.title: Paul Louie papers, circa 1820-2004
items.description: He was active in several parishes in both northern and southern California as a Minister of Christian Education, and was also a consultant on the staff of the Los Angeles County Human Relations Commission, as well as a founder of the Chinese Historical Society of Southern California. This collection includes newspapers, newspaper clippings, reports, slides, and books related primarily to the Asian-American experience.

items.title: Stan Steiner papers, ca. 1961-1987
items.description: Stan Steiner (1925–1987) was an American social historian, author and teacher who wrote books focusing on American minority communities and their relationship to the broader society as well as the mythology of the American West. Comprising 138 manuscript boxes, the papers are also a trove of clippings and ephemera in the post-War era, documenting everything from right-wing organizations and social movements to Native American tribes and land policy, to the farm worker movements.

sectors.name: Society and community — Religion, clubs and societies

items.title: Fortnightly Music Club records, circa 1910-2008
items.description: Music club with members primarily from the Stanford University and Palo Alto, California, communities. Printed ephemera, clippings, photographs and other materials, many assembled during the club's 75th anniversary in 1983; and their Centennial Memory Album issued in 2008.

items.title: Stanford Area Chinese Club records, 1964-1996
items.description: The Stanford Area Chinese Club was founded in 1965 with a goal of bringing education about Chinese culture to Palo Alto. Collection consists of administrative records, photographs, and materials and ephemera related to club events.

items.title: Woodside-Atherton Garden Club records, circa 1929-2013
items.description: The club organizes civic and educational projects, and hosts and participates in local and national flower shows. Records consist primarily of meeting minutes, annual reports, news clippings, event programs, photograph albums and scrapbooks, and miscellaneous records of activities of the club from its inception forward.

sectors.name: Society and community — Women, gender and sexuality

items.title: Career Action Center and the Resource Center for Women records. 1973-2002
items.description: The nonprofit center began with a staff of volunteers and the goal of providing guidance to a variety of women in transition, including well-educated women, women re-entering the work force, women with children, widowed and divorced women, and women active in their communities as volunteers. This collection includes administrative records, financial records, photographs, scrapbooks, publications, program materials, video and audio tapes related to the founding and history of the Career Action Center-Resource Center for Women, a job resource center active on the San Francisco Peninsula between 1973 – 2002.

items.title: Elizabeth Lyman papers, 1958-2009 (inclusive)
items.description: Elizabeth "Jing" Lyman (1925-2013) was communitiy activist who organized and sustained many foundations and coalitions, including Women and Foundations/Corporate Philanthropy, HUB, and the Women's Resource Center, among many others. Primarily files relating to Jing Lyman's activities in community affairs, the Women's Resource Center, the Women and Foundations/Corporate Philanthropy, HUB, and with various foundations and executive boards. Jing Lyman played an instrumental role in creating what is now the Michelle R. Clayman Institute for Gender Research at Stanford.

items.title: Feminist, Lesbian, and Gay publications collection, 20th century
items.description: The collection consists of an assortment of publications from various sources covering women's liberation, the feminist movement, and the gay rights movement. Series 1 includes publications of various sorts including newsletters, pamphlets, zines, journals, magazines, and directories.

items.title: Jane Evans collection of clippings related to women in chemistry, business, and technology, 1979-1987
items.description: Materials consist of newspaper articles and magazine clippings from the 1970's and 1980's related to the history of women in chemistry, business, and technology.

sectors.name: Society and community

items.title: Dorothea K. Almond papers, 1936-1998 (inclusive), 1960-1998 (bulk)
items.description: Dorothea Kaufmann Almond, longtime child and family advocate, grew up in Cologne, Germany, and moved to the United States in 1934 to study at Teachers College, Columbia University, where she earned a master's degree in 1941. She served as chair of the Committee on Childcare at Stanford from 1969 to 1977, was co-director of the Stanford Childcare Resource and Referral Center from 1978 to 1986, and was a consultant on childcare to the dean of student affairs from 1979 to 1986.
