Papers include correspondence, newsletters, memos, reports, articles, minutes, and other materials pertaining to childcare at Stanford, child welfare in general, and other social and civic issues, 1960-1998.

items.title: Herman Gallegos papers, 1944-2013
items.description: Herman Gallegos has been an activist and community organizer with a focus on Latino rights and support, as well as a management consultant, director, and trustee on many corporate boards and nonprofits. This collection contains organizational files, grant proposals, meeting dockets, correspondence, reports, newsletters, research and subject files, and notes from Herman Gallegos's corporate, non-profit, philanthropic and advocacy work.

items.title: Indicators for a sustainable San Mateo County; a report card of our county's quality of life, 1977
items.description: The report measures 30 indicators, including such vital elements as air and water quality, unemployment, crime, homelessness, housing affordability, transportation, voter participation, and high school dropouts."

items.title: Stanford Mid-Peninsula Urban Coalition, records
items.description: Stanford alum Ira Hall joined Hewlett-Packard (HP) in Palo Alto in 1967 in corporate marketing. He launched the Stanford Mid-Peninsula Urban Coalition in Palo Alto with HP's founders William Hewlett and David Packard in 1968 and served as executive director for six years.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Arms control, science and technology policy

items.title: Computer reliability + nuclear war [videorecording]
items.description: Alan Borning is Professor Emeritus in the Paul G Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering at the University of Washington, where he was a faculty member from 1980 to 2016. Alan Borning, professor of Computer Science at the University of Washington, addresses two main questions: could false alerts due to computer failure trigger nuclear war, and, if nuclear war should begin, could it be fought in a "limited" manner?

items.title: Michael M. May papers
items.description: Michael May is Professor Emeritus (Research) in the Stanford University School of Engineering and a senior fellow with the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies at Stanford University. The primary topics include May's work for CISAC (Committee on International Security and Arms Control) - which includes research on nuclear proliferation, management of plutonium, and international relations - as well as logistical planning to do with May's travels, conferences, and papers.

items.title: Stanford SDI Video Group videorecordings
items.description: The Stanford SDI Video Group, composed of seven students, obtained a grant from the Associated Students to produce a film exploring issues raised by the participation of Stanford scholars in research related to the Strategic Defense Initiative. Collection consists of unedited tapes of "SDI at Stanford: A Forum" with Lt. Col. Robert Allen, Dr. Bernard Roth, Dr. Joseph W. Goodman, Dr. David Bernstein, and Marc Strassman (moderator); a panel discussion by graduate students; and interviews with John M. Madey, Sidney Drell, Donald Kennedy, John Harris, John McCarthy, and Terry Winograd; and the edited master of the final video.

items.title: Stuart W. Leslie oral histories on the cold war and American science, 1982-1991
items.description: Collection contains 51 audiocassettes from interviews with Stanford faculty in physics, electrical engineering, aeronautics and material science, along with scientists and engineers at Bay Area companies, for his book: THE COLD WAR AND AMERICAN SCIENCE: THE MILITARY-INDUSTRIAL-ACADEMIC COMPLEX AT MIT AND STANFORD.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Foreign affairs and diplomacy

items.title: Richard A. Stepp papers, 1937-1995
items.description: The papers of Richard A. Stepp pertain largely to the time he spent in Burma as an advisor on technical services for small industries, 1958-59. Included are correspondence, notebooks, reports, memos, Burmese government documents (in English), other publications, and photographs, 1954-59.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Law and legal practice

items.title: California Rural Legal Assistance records, 1966-2014
items.description: The records of the California Rural Legal Assistance, Inc. (CRLA) document CRLA's ongoing work to provide legal aid to farmworkers and the rural poor in California. Included in the collection are administrative records, litigation files, and special program and subject files.

items.title: Frank B. Yoakum diaries, 1932-1990
items.description: Founding partner in the Los Angeles law firm of Iverson, Yoakum, Papiano and Hatch where he worked until he was 84.

items.title: Harry J. Rathbun papers, 1934-1996
items.description: He joined the faculty in the Law School that same year, reaching the rank of professor in 1937; his specialty was business law. Addenda 2010-022 includes publications, correspondence, speeches, manuscripts, and other documents related to Rathbun's business law courses and his work for the Creative Initiative Foundation.

items.title: Legal Aid Society of San Mateo County, Records, 1974-1994
items.description: A private non-profit law firm, Legal Aid has provided legal services to low-income families, seniors, adults and children with disabilities, and domestic violence survivors since 1959. Collection consists primarily of administrative records, correspondence, and case files.

items.title: Mary Timothy papers concerning the trial of Angela Davis, 1972-1974
items.description: Mary Timothy was foreperson of the 1972 Angela Davis trial jury. Trial transcripts, tape recordings of impressions of the daily trial proceedings, articles and newsclippings about the trial and Ms. Davis, photographs of the jury, and letters received by Mary Timothy.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Politics and elections

items.title: Byron Sher papers, circa 1950-2004
items.description: Byron Sher was a member of the California state senate, 1996-2004; a member of the California state assembly, 1980-1996; a Palo Alto city council member, 1965-1967 and 1973-1980. The Byron Sher papers consists of office and bill files, public policy calendars and artifacts, faculty papers, district and campaign files, personal papers and effects, incoming and outgoing correspondence, photographs, audio cassettes and video tapes.

items.title: Dianne McKenna archive, circa 1970s-1990s
items.description: Dianne McKenna served on the Sunnyvale City Council from 1977 to 1984, including two terms as mayor, before being elected to the Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors, where she served from 1985 to 1996.

items.title: No on 6 : cut discrimination not schoolworkers
items.description: Colorful poster of children holding hands in a circle.

items.title: U.S. Senate Primary election campaign rally photographs, 1976
items.description: Collection of 15 black-and-white photos of the U.S. Senate Primary election campaign rally in 1976. Those photographed include Cesar Chavez, Jane Fonda and Tom Hayden.

items.title: Walter Mondale Rally at Stanford [videorecording]
items.description: Video tapes of a political rally with Mondale at Stanford University, October 16, 1984.

sectors.name: Ideas and intellectual history — Counterculture

items.title: Christopher Hills papers, circa 1936-1997
items.description: Christopher Hills, known as 'The Father of Spirulina', was an author, business person, alternative educator, and founder of alternative communities. Topics dealt with include Hills' organization and leadership of the World Conference on Scientific Yoga (1970); Centre House, London; The University of the Trees (Boulder Creek, CA); aquaculture and microalgae research (including spirulina), microalgae marketing and distributing and a variety of additional spiritual, educational and philanthropic initiatives.

items.title: Danica Remy collection of Point Foundation records, 1968-1998
items.description: The Point foundation was a nonprofit organization based in San Francisco and founded by Stewart Brand and Richard "Dick" Raymond, growing out of their work with the Portola Institute and the Whole Earth Catalog. The majority of this collection consists of subject files pertaining to various grant projects funded by the Point Foundation, as well as general orginzational files. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Fred Turner papers, 1968-2019
items.description: Fred Turner is an Associate Professor in the Department of Communication at Stanford University and Director of Stanford's Program in Science, Technology, and Society. Files consist primarily of research material, manuscripts, and chapter drafts related to Turner's book, From Counterculture to Cyberculture: Stewart Brand, the Whole Earth Network, and the Rise of Digital Utopianism.

items.title: From counterculture to cyberculture: the legacy of the Whole Earth Catalog : videorecordings, 2006
items.description: Videorecordings (Betacam and DVD disc) of the symposium held at Stanford University, November 9, 2006, which featured Stewart Brand, Kevin Kelly, Howard Rheingold, and Fred Turner.
items.era_note: [Most of this 2006 symposium looks back at the Whole Earth Catalog and its legacy in these years.]

items.title: From Satori to Silicon Valley : San Francisco and the American counterculture / Theodore Roszak
Georgiana Sims collection of Whole Earth and Portola Institute materials, circa 1971
items.description: Materials include documentation, primarily photographs, relating to the history of the Whole Earth Catalog, Portola Institute, and related materials. Includes contact sheets and negatives. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: New Dimensions Media records, 1968-2024
items.description: The New Dimensions Foundation is an independent, listener supported, educational broadcasting group based in Ukiah, California. New Dimensions might be superficially described as about new age philosophy and self-help; as their website says, "Our purpose is to share knowledge that has the potential to deepen our connections to self, family, community, planet and the natural world. We encourage public awareness of various approaches towards creating a world that works for everyone." Recordings and files from long-running radio program New Dimensions Radio, along with recordings of related programming.

items.title: Point foundation records, 1964-1975
items.description: The Point foundation was a nonprofit organization based in San Francisco and founded by Stewart Brand and Richard "Dick" Raymond, growing out of their work with the Portola Institute and the Whole Earth Catalog. Point was conceived from the profits of The Last Whole Earth Catalog and was dedicated to perpetuating the energies and ideals of the catalog, including environmentalism, sustainability, and innovation. Files including reports, correspondence, board materials, project reports, etc.

items.title: Simple Living Newsletter, 1976-[1977].
items.description: Includes articles and poetry by Gary Snyder, E.F. Schumacher, Ted Taylor, Ken Darrow, Dorothy Lee, Lee Swenson, Todd Gitlin, Beth Collison, Alan Strain, Gurney Norman, Richard Merrill, Liz Walker, David B Werner, Bob Nickols, Milton Mayer, Cesar Chavez, Elsie Renne, Eric Hjertberg, Ivan Illich, Clay Wertheimer, Daine Luther, Bill Pool, Nancy Malich, Dave Freitag, David Steinberg, Barbara Garson, Jan Hartsough, Marcia Atwood, and Robert Aldridge. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Stewart Brand papers, 1954-2000
items.description: He was loosely associated with the Merry Pranksters, USCO, and other countercultural groups, and spent much of the 1960s traveling and visiting communal experiments. Brand created the original Whole Earth Catalog in 1968 to provide practical information on tools that would be useful for people creating and living in communes. The Steward Brand papers contains correspondence, personal journals, manuscripts, photographs, project records, articles, and publications.

items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: The updated last whole earth catalog : access to tools
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Theodore Roszak papers, circa 1940-2017
items.description: Theodore Roszak (1933-2011) was an American author, academic and social critic who first achieved fame for his 1969 book The Making of a Counter Culture and subsequently wrote prolifically about history, science, technology, literature, belief, society, and the life of the mind. Roszak's papers consist of drafts and notes for his writing, published articles and essays, and related research files including newspaper and magazine clippings, ephemera related to readings, workshops and promotional material.

items.title: Whole Earth Catalog records, 1968-1986
items.description: The collection contains the editorial files of founder Stewart Brand as well as Jay Kinney, reader correspondence, photographic materials, and memorabilia. The Whole Earth Catalogs, 26 issues, 1968-1986, complete. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Whole earth epilog; access to tools : subscription teaser, 1974
items.description: A reprint including 9 pages from The Coevolution Quarterly which, as an enitity, were published in WRAPAROUND in Harper's Magazine, April 1974. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.description: Pamphlet entitled SILICON VALLEY: PARADISE OR PARADOX? THE IMPACT OF HIGH TECHNOLOGY INDUSTRY ON SANTA CLARA COUNTY, prepared by Alan Bernstein, Bob DeGrasse, Rachael Grossman, Chris Paine and Lenny Siegel.

items.title: Buckminster Fuller's World Game : film, video and audio media, circa 1968-1980
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Institute for the Future : reports, 1969-2015
items.description: The Institute for the Future (IFTF) is a non-profit strategic futures organization located in Palo Alto, California. The IFTF was founded in 1968 by a group of former RAND Corporation researchers with a grant from the Ford Foundation. Materials consist of reports, special reports, papers, and working papers primarily related to forecasting.

items.title: John Perry Barlow papers
items.description: Often called "the father of cyberlibertarianism," Barlow was a founding member of the Electronic Frontier Foundation and a lyricist for the Grateful Dead. The collection also contains Barlow's email account dating from 1996-2009. The email contains correspondence related to Barlow's life, work with the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and personal and family relationships. There are also series for Barlow's writing, as well as writing about him.

items.title: Peter Schwartz papers
items.description: Collection consists of books, articles, speech drafts, and papers written by Schwartz. Also included are materials related to his research and time at SRI, Royal Dutch Shell, Global Business Network, Monitor, and Salesforce. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Walter A. Huston collection of R. Buckminster Fuller material, circa 1965-1975
items.description: Collection contains books, articles, manuscripts, ephemera, audio cassettes, tapes, film, photographs and slides collected by Walter A. Huston about R. Buckminster Fuller. Ephemera files contain pamphlets, letters, and other documents about the World Game, geodesic domes, the Samuel Beckett theater, seminars and programs run by Fuller, and some itinerary and travel materials from trips Huston accompanied Fuller on in the early 1970s. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: William Shockley and eugenics collection, 1966-1978
items.description: William Shockley was a Professor of engineering at Stanford (1958-1975; emeritus 1975-1989). He was a co-recipient of the Nobel Prize in physics, 1956. The materials consist of correspondence, news clippings, publications and ephemera related to Shockley's embrace of and advocacy for eugenics, including his work on heredity, I.Q., and race.

items.description: Materials consist of Van Rensselaer's papers, including slides and some photographs.

items.description: Correspondence, pilot logs, passports, one film reel and one dvd.

items.title: Regis McKenna papers, 1973-2012
items.description: The Regis McKenna papers document McKenna's innovative leadership in marketing and public relations for technology companies in Silicon Valley and the business operations of his agency, Regis McKenna Inc. (RMI). The collection consists of presentations, reports, proposals, and official correspondence related to McKenna's work on marketing campaigns for Apple Inc. and Intel, among others.

items.title: NewSpace Global Reports
items.description: NSG's Deep Dive Reports, such as the NewSpace Global SmallSat Reports, provide in-depth analyses of a particular market or topic.

items.title: Scott Hubbard papers, 1972-2016
items.description: He spent time as NASA's Mars program director and was the director of NASA's Ames Research Center from 2002-2006. This collection primarily consists of correspondence and administrative files relating to Hubbard's work at NASA. It also includes materials from his work on the Columbia Accident Investigation Board (CAIB).

items.description: Alan Alda follows Flakey the robot around and learns a bit about artificial intelligence.

items.title: Applied artificial intelligence research: the heuristic programming project
Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence records, 1969-2011
items.description: Correspondence, manuscripts submitted to AI Magazine, conference presentations, audio visual materials, and a full run of AI Magazine.

items.title: Edward A. Feigenbaum papers, 1950-2007 (inclusive)
items.description: Feigenbaum is a leading national figure in artificial intelligence and has developed computer resources for interactive research between medical and scientific collaborators on a national and global scale. Collection primarily concerns his work in artificial intelligence at Stanford University and includes administrative files, correspondence, project files, trip files, proposals, reports, reprints, Artificial Intelligence Lab memos, audio tapes, video tapes, and files on computer programs, mainly DENDRAL, MOLGEN, EPAM, and SUMEX.

items.title: Nils J. Nilsson papers, 1958-2009
items.description: Nils J. Nilsson, Kumagai Professor of Engineering (Emeritus) in the Department of Computer Science at Stanford University, received his PhD degree in Electrical Engineering from Stanford in 1958. Collection pertains to Nilsson's research and teaching and includes correspondence, notes and text for talks, papers, published articles, conference and meeting materials, and AV materials on artificial intelligence.

items.title: OpenAI 5 Team interviews collection, circa 2019-2024
items.description: Digital files of interviews with members of the OpenAI 5 Team members from producer Jennifer 8. Lee.

items.title: Research Datasets for MPEG
items.description: MPEG is considering standardizing technologies that will enable efficient and interoperable design of visual search applications. In particular we are seeking technologies for visual content matching in images or video. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory records, 1963-2009
items.description: The materials consist of SAIL Dump And Restore Technique (DART) backup files, 1972-1990; digital copies of 16 mm films created from 1963-1980; handbooks; log books; manuals; and photographs and videos from the 35th SAIL reunion held in 2009. The Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (also known as Stanford AI Lab or SAIL) is the artificial intelligence (AI) research laboratory of Stanford University.

items.title: The History of Artificial Intelligence
items.description: The rich archival documentation available in the Stanford Libraries on the history of artificial intelligence includes important film, video and audio resources. These materials provide access to a variety of events and activities from Stanford, Silicon Valley, or the artificial intelligence community as a whole, including tours of labs and project, robots in action, and public lectures, to name only a few examples.

items.title: The One Hundred Year Study of Artificial Intelligence (AI100)
items.description: The One Hundred Year Study on Artificial Intelligence, or AI100, is a 100-year effort to study and anticipate how the effects of artificial intelligence will ripple through every aspect of how people work, live and play.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Biotechnology and medical devices

items.title: Eric Sabelman papers, 1961-2019
items.description: Eric E. Sabelman received his Ph.D. from Stanford University, and served for 20 years at the Palo Alto VA Rehabilitation Research and Development Center followed by 15 years at Kaiser Redwood City hospital as a Functional Neurosurgery Bioengineer. This collection consists of grant proposals, engineering course materials, manuscript drafts, correspondence, and research files.

items.title: Exoskeleton Training Data
items.description: Data Repository for "How adaptation, training, and customization contribute to benefits from exoskeleton assistance" [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

Oral Cavity Fluorescence 2021
items.description: The data contained in this repository were used to support end-to-end simulations of a camera (version 4 of the OralEye camera) that was designed to measure fluorescence in the oral cavity. We provide real camera image data and the data that was used to calculate simulated camera image data.

items.title: Stanford Bioengineering
items.description: Main collection for depositing any and all documents developed by members of the Stanford Bioengineering community.

items.title: Stanford University, Byers Center for Biodesign, audiovisual recordings
Vascular Model Repository
items.description: Collection of medical images, 3D models, and flow simulations of patient-specific vasculatures.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Computer hardware

items.title: Apple Computer ephemera collection, 1978-2004
items.description: Apple Computer, Inc., ignited the personal computer revolution in the 1970s with the Apple II, and reinvented the personal computer in the 1980s with the Macintosh, of which it had sold more 30 million systems as of the end of 1998. Contains annual reports, internal communications, corporate communications, engineering reports, manuals, product information files, catalogs, price lists, Apple publications, human resource information, conference and workshop information, software, hardware, and corporate memorabilia.

items.title: Apple Computer, Inc. records, 1977-1998
items.description: Contains organizational charts, annual reports, company directories, internal communications, engineering reports, design materials, press releases, manuals, public relations materials, human resource information, videotapes, audiotapes, software, hardware, and corporate memorabilia. Also includes information regarding the Board of Directors and their decisions.

items.title: Articles and newsclippings, 1998
items.description: Includes a special computer issue of DIE ZEIT MAGAZIN (Nr. 35, 20 Aug. 1998) with accompanying newsclipping, and an article by Howard Alexander, "Behold the lowly mouse : clever technology close at hand," published in the NEW YORK TIMES, 1 Oct. 1998, page D9.

items.title: David S. H. Rosenthal collection of NVidia artifacts and documentation, circa 1989-1996
items.description: David Stuart Holmes Rosenthal is a computer scientist. He worked as chief scientist at Nvidia in the 1990s. Artifacts and documents relating to the history of NVidia, Inc., and the history of computer graphics technology, including but not limited to: technical manuals, graphics cards, controlers, CD-ROMs for NV1, NVIDIA T-shirt, presentations, and reference cards.

items.title: Edward J. McCluskey papers
items.description: In 1966, he joined Stanford University, where he is Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, as well as Director of the Center for Reliable Computing. His Stanford research focuses on logic testing, synthesis, design for testability, and fault-tolerant computing. The materials consist of subject files, teaching files, chronological files, and compter files.

items.title: Fred Wenninger papers, 1971-1995
items.description: By 1977, Wenninger started managing an advanced semiconductor-development project for HP called Focus. The project was designed to leapfrog HP years ahead of commercial semiconductor vendors by producing a 32-bit microprocessor and large memory chips for HP's desktop computers. Fred William Wenninger worked as a researcher and manager at Hewlett-Packard from the 1960s until 1986, when he became president of Allied Signal Corporation's Bendix/King subsidiary. The entire collection contains personal materials and professional materials relating to work done at Hewlett Packard.

items.title: Juiced. GS : a quarterly Apple II journal
Juiced.GS : a quarterly Apple II journal, 1996-2016
items.description: Physical holdings include issues from vol. 1, no. 1 (1996) through vol. 19 (2014). Digital holdings include issues from vol. 1, no. 1 (1996) through vol. 20, no. 4 (2015). [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Lee Felsenstein papers, ca. 1975-1995
items.description: Lee Felsenstein is an electronic design engineer known for his contributions to the early history of personal computing. The papers of computer designer Lee Felsenstein contain material about the development of personal computers through the 1970s and 80s.

items.title: Making the Macintosh; Technology and Culture in Silicon Valley : research materials including recordings and transcripts of original interviews, DVD copies of photographs, and two video tapes, 1999-2001
items.description: The two video tapes are reels 1-10 of the SRI AI Group Conference, 1 Dec. 1999. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

Mouse droppings : monthly newsletter of the Macintosh Users Group of Corvallis, Oregon, 1984-2002
items.description: Philip C. Russell was the editor through 1991; the set of volumes originally belonged to him. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Raines Cohen papers and t-shirt collection, circa 1985-2001
items.description: Raines Cohen cofounded the Berkeley Macintosh Users Group (BMUG) in 1986 while enrolled at the University of California at Berkeley as a Geography major. Collection includes the Berkeley Macintosh User Group (BMUG) newsletters in print and on CD-ROM discs, and related files kept by Raines Cohen about his involvement with the group and early Macintosh computer communities. Artifacts include buttons, pins, and t-shirts designed for various User Groups including BMUG and associated groups in the computer industry.

items.title: Steve Jobs : obituaries and biographical material, 2011
items.description: Biographical material collected by Henry Lowood after Jobs' death on October 5, 2011. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: The ... BMUG newsletter
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]
items.era_note: [Most of this newsletter run, issued from 1986 into the later 1990s with diskettes and then CD-ROMs, concerns this period.]

items.title: Washington Apple Pi collection of Apple II user group newsletters and publications, circa 1977-1999
items.description: Washington Apple Pi [http://www.wap.org] is a non-profit Apple user group which was founded in 1978 in Washington, D.C., and has published a newsletter since 1979. Washington Apple Pi also traded newsletters with many other Apple user groups in an informal exchange program, and these issues constitute the majority of the collection.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Computing (general)

items.title: Barbara L. Kevles collection of computer technology
items.description: Published and unpublished documents, software, and miscellaneous equipment reflecting the rapid evolution of home computer technology from 1993 through 2006. Collection of operating manuals, software, and related material, assembled by journalist Barbara Kevles.

items.title: Clifford I. Nass papers, 1977-2010
items.description: Nass was the co-creator of The Media Equation theory, and a renowned authority on human-computer interaction. The papers include Nass' teaching files, research files, and publications related to the social-psychological aspects of human-interactive media interaction, chronic media multitasking, and automotive interfaces.

items.title: Computer and software marketing material, 1997-1999 and undated
items.description: Includes advertising for Active Software, Inc., Apple's Lisa launch, NeXTLevel launch, and Adobe typeface posters.

items.title: CS191 Computer Science Independent Research Project
items.description: The CS191 collection is a set of project reports from the CS191 course at Stanford University. Students conduct research under the supervision of faculty and produce a conference-style paper artifact as a deliverable.

items.title: Douglas C. Engelbart papers, 1953-2005
items.description: This collection documents that activities of Douglas C. Engelbart, a computer scientist whose pioneering work in the 1950s and 1960s (first at SRI International, later at Tymshare, Inc.) led to the development of the interactive personal computer. Professional papers, including correspondence, research proposals, technical reports, notes, journals, and computer disks, as well as audiovisual material on a variety of media.

items.title: Douglas Engelbart symposia records, 1998, 2000, 2008
items.description: The Stanford University Libraries in conjunction with the Institute for the Future presented on December 9, 1998 a celebration of the 30th anniversary of Douglas Engelbart's invention of the computer mouse. The materials consist of videorecordings, brochures and handouts from the symposia, clippings, press releases, press kit, photographs from the event, and a videotape of TV coverage from various news shows.

items.title: Jef Raskin papers, 1975-2005
items.description: Jef Raskin is an independent consultant on interface design, best known for having created the Macintosh computer project at Apple, the one button mouse and the click-and-drag paradigm for using it, the Apple style of computer documentation, and the Canon Cat and other interface-based products. The collection contains correspondence, print-outs of email, manuscripts of various articles authored by Raskin and his colleagues, appointment books, and various publications collected by Raskin.

items.title: John L. Hennessy Personal Papers
items.description: Formerly the tenth President of Stanford University, he is also a computer scientist who co-founded MIPS Computer Systems and Atheros Communications. The materials consist of publications, research and teaching files, professional files and correspondence, and audiovisual materials.

items.title: Kathleen Hennessey papers
items.description: Audrey Kathleen Hennessey is a data scientist, researcher, and educator whose work has primarily focused on systems, information processing, and organizational automation. The Kathleen Hennessey papers include a wide range of materials, largely centered around computer science and information processing.

items.title: Kurt Akeley papers, 1982-2000
items.description: Kurt Akeley, one of the founders of Silicon Graphics, Incorporated, earned his M.S.E.E. from Stanford University in 1982. He has published papers on computer graphics architectures and taught courses on graphics programming at the annual SIGGRAPH conferences. This collection includes memoranda, reports, manuals, publications, notebooks, outlines and text for presentations, email printouts, patents, slides, and videos pertaining to research and product development for Silicon Graphics and its customers; collection also includes Akeley's notes from a class with Jim Clark, 1987.

items.title: Marc Levoy papers
items.description: Marc Levoy is the VMware Founders Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering, Emeritus. In the 2000's he worked on computational photography and microscopy, including light field imaging as commercialized by Lytro and other companies. Outside of academia, Levoy co-designed the Google book scanner, launched Google's Street View project, and currently leads a team in Google Research that has worked on Project Glass and the Nexus 6 HDR+ mode.

items.title: Mark Weiser papers, ca. 1969-1999
items.description: Dr. Mark Weiser was the Chief Technologist at the Xerox Palo Alto Research Center (PARC). Weiser's work since 1988 focused on Ubiquitous Computing, a program he initiated that envisions PC's being replaced with invisible computers embedded in everyday objects. Collection contains correspondence, project files, patents, business plans, notebooks and computer files.

items.title: Stanford University, Computer Science Department, HCI Group, CS547 seminar videorecordings, 1990-2012
items.description: The Stanford Human-Computer Interaction Group (HCI Group) was a section of the Computer Science Department. CS 547 was a repeatable seminar course hosting weekly guest lecturers to speak on topics related to designing and evaluating human-computer interactions. This collection contains recordings of CS 547 Human-Computer Interaction Seminars.

items.title: Stanford University, Computer Systems Laboratory, Technical Reports
items.description: Collection contains 384 PDF laboratory technical report files created by various members of the Stanford University Department of Computer Science.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Computer Science, technical notes
items.description: Collection includes 93 PDF technical notes files created by various members of the Stanford University Department of Computer Science.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Computer Science, technical reports
items.description: Collection contains 972 PDF technical reports by various authors from within the Stanford Computer Science Department.

items.title: Sun Microsystems Reports, 1992-2001
items.description: Technical reports and general interest essays published by Sun Microsystems Laboratories. Also essays from the Perspectives series written by individuals expressing ideas on subjects of general rather than technical interest.

items.title: Terry Allen Winograd papers, 1963-2006
items.description: Terry Allen Winograd (1946-), an impressive scholar and professor of computer science at Stanford University, is known for his research on artificial intelligence and natural language. The collection includes professional files, publications, research files, teaching files, audiovisual materials, computer files, and subject files on individual students.

items.title: Unicode collection
items.description: Unicode is an international encoding standard that allows consistent encoding, representation, and handling of text expressed in many writing systems globally. This collection primarily consists of meeting notes, reports, minutes, agendas, research material, drafts, correspondence, and other documents highlighting the development and output of the Unicode Standard, a universal character encoding schema, and related internationalization standards by the Unicode Technical Committee.

items.description: Center for Integrated Facility Engineering (CIFE) Technical Reports, Working Papers and related materials.

items.description: New Mew Media Archive, including the Cyberslacker material is two bankers’ boxes and includes content related to the development, production, etc. of very early dotcom media.

items.title: John Goerzen collection of Internet Gopher (protocol) sites, 2007
items.description: Materials include Gopher server data available on the internet in 2007, including digitized legal case archives from the Cleveland Public Library; a copy of The WELL Gopher (one of the famous early Internet sites); a large collection from the Biology Department at Indiana University, with a particular emphasis on genome data, molecular biology, and biology software; a large collection of DNA-related data from the Japan National Institute of Agrobiological Sciences; a server from an Internet provider in Peru, and more.

items.title: Nancy White collection of research materials related to online communities, 1996-2016
items.description: Includes documentation related to online communities such as Electric Minds, the Well, and the Knowledge Ecology Network, principally during the period from 1999-2008. Materials also include journal articles, newsletters, conference proceedings, message board printouts, blog posts, and other similar materials.

items.title: Parham Sina's business records for Ultraworld Communications, 1998-2001
items.description: Ultraworld Communications was an internet service on the Active Worlds virtual world platform; it was discontinued in 2001.

items.title: SLAC Earliest Websites
items.description: This collection includes the SLAC archive of the earliest websites, dating 1992-1998.

items.title: Stanford Internet Observatory, Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies
items.description: Publications produced through the activities of the Stanford Internet Observatory, a cross-disciplinary program of research, teaching and policy engagement for the study of abuse in current information technologies, with a focus on social media.

items.title: Web caching using access statistics [electronic resource]
items.description: We present the problem of caching web pages under the assumption that each user has a fixed, known demand vector for the pages. We wish to place web pages in the caches in order to optimize the latency from user to page, under the constraints that each cache has limited memory and can support a limited total number of requests.

items.title: Yotsuba Society Archives - 4Chan Imageboard Files
items.description: The Yotsuba Society, or Society for the Study and Preservation of Yotsuba Channel is a "website devoted to documenting and preserving the history of the imageboard/*chan culture/scene." This collection includes more than 25,000 discussion threads from the 4Chan Imageboard gathered between 2007 and August 2013 by Ndubuisi Okeh for the Yotsuba Society and given to the Stanford University Libraries by Mr. Okeh.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Labor and professional organizations

items.title: "Watsonville: Some Place Not Here" flyers, 2013-2015
items.description: From the flyer: "Watsonville: Some Place Not Here" returns to the lives of Dolores Valle and her fellow campesinas, who have struggled to rebuild their families after their children died of cancer and the pesticide-suffocated vineyard of their old home went up in flames. They now juggle work in the fields with work in the canneries and food processing plants that have given the town of Watsonville the nickname "frozen food capital of the world." Contains copies of flyers for "Watsonville: Some Place Not Here."

items.title: Chinese Railroad Workers in North America Project at Stanford Research Files
items.description: This collection contains the research files for The Chinese Railroad Workers in North America Project at Stanford University. The Chinese Railroad Workers in North America Project at Stanford began in 2012 as the first comprehensive effort to recover and interpret the work of the Chinese railroad workers who built the first transcontinental railroad across the United States and other rail lines throughout North America in the 1860s, with the objective of recapturing the lived experience of the Chinese workers themselves.

items.title: Dolores : silkscreen print of labor leader Dolores Huerta, 1999
items.description: The print bears the hand-signed signature of Dolores Huerta and the artist Barbara Carrasco.

items.title: Instituto Laboral de la Raza records, 1982-1998
items.description: Founded in 1982 by Jose Medina, the institute is a nonprofit workers' rights organization and a drop-in center that addresses the immediate needs of both the Latino worker and the unemployed alike in San Francisco and the surrounding Bay Area counties. The historical (inactive) records of the institute.

items.title: Marion Moses, M.D., papers
items.description: The Dr. Marion Moses, M.D., papers consist of her career spanning fifty years as a nurse, physician, and advocate for farmworkers with the United Farm Workers Union (UFW). The collection consists of her many years of work with the UFW, meeting notes, correspondence with Cesar Chavez, Eliseo Medina, Jessica Govea, Marshal Ganz among many more UFW founders and organizers.

items.title: Solomon Feferman papers, 1938-2016 (inclusive), 1980-1983 (bulk)
items.description: Solomon Feferman was a Professor of Mathematics and Philosophy and the Patrick Suppes Family Professor of Humanities and Sciences at Stanford University, he became Emeritus in 2004. The first series primarily document Feferman's term as president of the Association for Symbolic Logic from 1980 to 1982. The material consists largely of correspondence, meeting agendas and minutes, and material from symposia and lectures.

items.title: Special Libraries Association, San Andreas Chapter: oral histories, circa 1990s.
items.description: The collection consists of audio tapes, transcripts, and 1 CD-ROM (transcripts, captured from electronic media) from an oral history series conducted with librarians in Silicon Valley. These oral histories were conducted under the auspices of the Special Libraries Association, San Andreas Chapter.

items.title: Stanford Student And Labor Alliance, records
items.description: SALA is dedicated to educating members and the Stanford community about worker issues; fostering relationships with and supporting all workers on campus; and shaping a strong, sustainable social justice movement through coalition building in the Stanford community and beyond. Photographs of student demonstrations, student initiated course materials, and SLAC meeting minutes.

items.title: Women at Work
items.description: Highlights the work lives of women employed at ROLM systems, exploring their career paths and work-life balance.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Magnetic recording and data storage

items.title: Ampex museum : photographs, 1995
items.description: Mr. Durfey started working for Ampex in 1954. Now retired, he is a research historian and curator at the Perham Foundation. He and his wife Edith took these photographs before the museum was dismantled. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Grass Valley Group, Inc. : publications, 1999-2002
items.description: Papers pertaining to custom video hardware and video server products. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Mary Beth and Richard Hess technical manual collection, 1967-2000
items.description: Since focusing on audio preservation Richard has contributed significantly to the field of sound recording preservation, especially magnetic media preservation. Contains technical user manuals for products built and sold by the Ampex Corporation, Grass Valley Group, Hewlett-Packard Corporation and other technology firms. Includes manuals, bulletins, catalogs, brochures, and schematics largely concerning the use, maintenance and repair of audiovisual equipment.

items.title: Ray Dolby papers, circa 1940s - 2000s
items.description: Ray Milton Dolby was an American engineer whose inventions and company, Dolby Laboratories, have had a profound effect on the storage, transmission, and reproduction of audio and video. Materials in the collection include Dolby's schoolwork, circuit drawings and engineering schematics for work both at Ampex and Dolby Laboratories, research notes and calculations, patents, correspondence, ephemera from Ampex and from the early years of Dolby Laboratories, and photographs.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Networking and telecommunications

items.title: Cisco Systems Annual reports, product information, press releases, 1990-2005
items.description: Manufacturer of internetworking systems and software.

items.title: David V. James papers, circa mid-1970s-2006
items.description: A holder of 72 patents as either originator or collaborator, Mr. James worked on wireless router devices, digital television research, and other electronics-related innovations. Included are Mr. James's masters and doctoral theses, as well as papers given at conference and documents from IEEE and standards committees.
items.era_note: [About three-quarters of these papers, which run to 2006, date from after 1990.]

items.title: Paul Baran papers, circa 1959-2010
items.description: Included are papers from Baran's time at RAND, Institute for the Future, CableData Associates, Comprint, Equatorial Communications, Telebit, Packet Technologies, Stratacom, Metricom, Interfax, Com21, Rosum, as well as numerous public service committees and non-profit organizations. Paul Baran, 1926-2011, was a Polish-American engineer who helped create the technical underpinnings for the Arpanet, the government-sponsored precursor to today's Internet. He was one of the three earliest researchers of packet switching techniques, and went on to start several companies and develop other technologies that are an essential part of the Internet and other modern digital communication.

items.title: Samuel L. Ginn papers, circa 1960-2010
items.description: Samuel L. Ginn is a retired business executive who worked in the telecommunications industry for over 40 years, with an emphasis on wireless technology and mobile communications. Materials consist of documents related to the history of the telecommunications and wireless industries, especially the history of the companies AirTouch and Pacific Telesis.

items.title: Simulation of iterative matching for combined input and output queueing [electronic resource]
items.description: Recently this algorithm has found application in the area of switch scheduling algorithms for high performance switches. In this report we investigate the convergence time of the parallel stable matching algorithm.

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Radio, vacuum tubes and microwave

items.title: Oswald G. Villard papers, 1932-1998 (inclusive), 1958-1998 (bulk)
items.description: Oswald Garrison Villard Jr. (1916-2004), a leader in electromagnetic theory and experimental methods, earned his engineer's degree in 1943 and his Ph.D. in 1949 at Stanford, studying with Dr. F. E. Terman. The papers include correspondence, articles and research papers, memoranda, reports, research files, contracts, minutes, and other materials, 1958-1998. The collection also includes instruction manuals and a log for radio station W6YX, 1932-1933 (club station at Stanford).

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work — Semiconductors

items.title: Andrew S. Grove papers, 1968-2013
items.description: Andrew S. Grove was a businessman and author who is best known for his role in the founding and growth of Intel Corporation, which at one time was the world's largest manufacturer of semiconductors. The papers of Intel founder Andrew Grove include files related to speaking engagements, writing by and about Grove, photographs, and other material.

items.title: Bob Noyce -- teen idol : T-shirt, 1990
items.description: SEMATECH declared June 1, 1990, "Bob Noyce Day." SEMATECH made up T-shirts printed with the quote, Noyce's photo, and the phrase "Bob Noyce - teen idol." [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Christophe Lécuyer research material on the history of Silicon Valley, 1999-2003
items.description: Academic research files and recorded interviews created by Christophe Lécuyer, a published historian of Silicon Valley high tech industries. He has written books on Fairchild Semiconductor and the history of Silicon Valley. The bulk of materials within the collection is comprised of research notes, photocopied resource materials, presentations, and academic works by Lécuyer.

items.title: Gordon Moore papers 1958-2005
items.description: Moore and Robert Noyce left Fairchild in July 1968 to establish the Intel Corporation in Santa Clara with the initial goal of developing and producing large scale integrated products. This collection contains Moore's Intel lab notebooks, personal and business correspondence, Intel presentations, memos and white papers, personal notes from meetings, greeting cards, photographs, cassette tapes and videos. The collection consists of business correspondence related to Intel Corporation, reports, overhead transparencies, presentation slides related to Intel Corporation and the semiconductor industry.

items.title: Gordon S. Kino Papers, 1955-2017
items.description: Gordon S. Kino was the W. M. Keck Foundation Professor of Electrical Engineering, Emeritus, and a professor of applied physics at Stanford University until his death on Oct. 9, 2017. He was best known for inventing new microscopes that improved semiconductor manufacturing and transformed medical diagnostics. Condolence letters, memorial programs, and articles re Kino's life; photograph album from Kino's retirement party; patent files related to Therma-Wave, Inc. & Boxer Cross, Inc.; miscellaneous publications.

items.title: Interviews with pioneers of the semiconductor industry for the book SPINOFF : cassette tapes, ca. 1995-2000
items.description: Charlie Sporck became vice president and general manager of Fairchild Semiconductor during a period when sales grew from a few hundred thousand dollars a year to hundreds of millions. He conducted these interviews while preparing his book SPINOFF; A PERSONAL HISTORY OF THE INDUSTRY THAT CHANGED THE WORLD, 2001.

items.title: Richard Previte papers, 1998-2020
items.description: A collection of videos and related material documenting the history of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) Corporation. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Robert Hills papers, circa 1983-2011
items.description: Robert Hills worked in various sales and marketing positions in the semiconductor equipment business in Silicon Valley beginning in 1967. The bulk of the collection is comprised of business cards of Hills' associates, and with additional materials including staff meeting notes, documentation on marketing strategies, and technical reports on semiconductors.

items.title: Silicon genesis : oral histories of semiconductor technology, 1995-2025
items.description: "Silcon Genesis" is a series of interviews with individuals active in California's Silicon Valley technology sector beginning in 1995 and through at least 2018. Rob Walker (1935-2016) and later Rob Blair interview key figures of the microelectronics industry.

items.title: Stephen Zelencik collection of Advanced Micro Devices video, circa 1963-1998
items.description: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) is an American multinational semiconductor company based in Sunnyvale, California, that develops computer processors and related technologies. This small collection contains 12 VHS videotapes and 1 DVD-R related to AMD, as well as a set of slides from Amphenol.

items.title: Denise Caruso papers
items.description: Denise Caruso is an American journalist and analyst specializing in the industries of digital technology and biotechnology. Materials include Caruso's work about technology in Silicon Valley; conference papers; promotional material.

items.title: Douglas Menuez photography collection
items.description: Award-winning documentary photographer Douglas Menuez was born in Texas in 1957. Contains photographic materials, including prints, contact sheets, negatives and slides, relating to Menuez's documentation of major Silicon Valley companies, as well as to fine art book projects, photo essays and photo shoots for newspapers, magazines, advertising campaigns, annual reports and other commissioned work.

Collection includes video tape of the event, text of the speech by Gerhard Casper, color photographs from the event, computer printouts of the exhibit panels on display, copies of historical photographs, and an 1989 booklet on the history of HP. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Kathy Cotton media collection, 2019
items.description: Documentary filmmaker Kathy Cotton held an event at ICE Safety Solution in Fremont, California, on September 28, 2019. Henry Lowood and Leslie Berlin, representing the Silicon Valley Archives, and Kathy Cotton lead a roundtable discussion with subjects from Kathy Cotton's documentary film, "A Place at the Table," documenting the histories of African American technology pioneers in Silicon Valley. Kathy Cotton filmed the event and, in addition, had a photographer take photos.

The collection contains interviews with Karin Hibma (September 6, 2023) and Dagmar Dolby (October 9, 2023).

items.description: The Stanford Technology Ventures Program (STVP) is the entrepreneurship center at Stanford University's School of Engineering. The Draper Fisher Jurvetson (DFJ) Entrepreneurial Thought Leaders (ETL) Seminar is a weekly lecture series on entrepreneurship featuring entrepreneurs, innovators and industry leaders.

items.description: Consists of an alphabetical listing of companies with their founders, date of establishment, and company profile.

items.title: Ann Jones collection of IBM Manuals, 1984-1993
items.description: This collection consists of IBM manuals created between 1984 and 1993. Subjects covered include Virtual Machine Library, Virtual Machine Enterprise Systems Architecture, Content Management Systems, Resource Access Control Facility, The System Product Interpreter (REXX), Advanced Program-to-Program Communication for the IBM Personal Computer, Virtual Machine System Product and labels from binder spines of Virtual Machine Enterprise Systems Architecture (VM/ESA) manuals.

items.title: Code Rush records, 1998-2000
items.description: Collection of video footage, interview transcripts and editorial material from the 2000 PBS documentary Code Rush, directed by David Winton and produced by Winton/duPont Films. Code Rush follows the lives of Netscape engineers (Michael Toy, Jamie Zawinski, Scott Collins, Jim Roskind, Tara Hernandez, Brendan Eich, Stuart Parmenter, and others) during Silicon Valley's first dotcom boom.

Donald E. Knuth papers, 1962-2010
items.description: Donald Ervin Knuth's work established the analysis of algorithms as an academic field. In addition to fundamental contributions in several branches of theoretical computer science, Knuth is the creator of the TeX computer typesetting system, the related METAFONT font definition language and rendering system, and the Computer Modern family of typefaces. Papers reflect his work in the study and teaching of computer programming, computer systems for publishing, and mathematics.

items.title: DOS / Windows : software and manuals, ca. 1985-1995
HP3000 reel-to-reel tapes of ASK Computer Systems, 1991-1995
items.description: 7 reels of HP3000 reel-to-reel tapes of ASK Computer Systems. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.description: Henson was also a member of the Board of Directors of the Xanadu Operating Company, founded in 1983 to support development of Ted Nelson's Xanadu system. The collection includes files from XOC, Memex, VHS tapes, cassette tapes, and Drexler drafts and galley proofs. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Lani Spund collection of Apple VITAL files, 1982-2000
items.description: Publications, presentations, video tapes, and digital files dating back to the 1990s from Dr. Lani Spund, former Chief Information Systems Architect for Apple Computer Inc. while he was project leader for the Apple VITAL (Virtually Integrated Technical Architecture Lifecycle), a blueprint for designing and managing business enterprise systems.

items.title: Ned Chapin papers, 1960-2008
items.description: Dr. Ned Chapin was a leader in the field of Computer Science, particularly the discipline of Software Maintenance, from its infancy. This collection primarily consists of conference materials, manuscripts, minicartridges, floppy disks, publications, and computer printouts relating to the courses and system development primarily created by Chapin during his tenure at Stanford University.

items.title: NeXT computer ephemera collection of Oliver Johns, circa 1985-circa 1997
items.description: NeXT was a technology company that specialized in computer workstations. This collection includes copies of NeXT software, printed user guides, advertising brochures, programming and software manuals for NeXT products like NeXTSTEP and OpenStep, and other related publications.

items.title: Problem reporting and tracking system developed at SLAC, 1981-1996

items.title: Robert W. Floyd papers, 1960-1995
items.description: Robert W. Floyd joined the Stanford faculty in 1968 as an associate professor of computer science. His most important scientific achievement was pioneering systematic methods of program verification. These papers include his Stanford course files, 1976-94; correspondence, 1968-95, including that with Donald Knuth, 1963-1987; research and subject files; reprints and manuscripts; computer printouts; and note cards.

items.title: Showstopper!; the breakneck race to create Windows NT and the next generation at Microsoft : research material for book, 1989-1993
items.description: G. Pascal Zachary is a senior writer for The Wall Street Journal. He has published two technology-related books -- Showstopper (1994), on innovation at Microsoft, and Endless Frontier, a biography of Vannevar Bush, the organizer of the Mahattan Project. Contains research files, notes, audiovisual materials, notebooks, and manuscripts of Gregg Zachary's book Showstopper, documenting the history of the Microsoft.

items.title: Ted Nelson papers, 1950s-2019
items.description: Theodor Holm "Ted" Nelson is an information technology pioneer and systems humanist. Nelson founded Project Xanadu in 1960, a global hypertext system designed to permanently connect different types of documents, display visible connections between documents, and include a simplified copyright system.
items.era_note: [Roughly two-fifths of these papers, including his email and his later teaching posts, concern this period.]

items.title: TEX publications collection, 1979-2010
items.description: TeX Live is a free software distribution for the TeX typesetting system that includes major TeX-related programs, macro packages, and fonts. Collection consists of TeX discs and publications manuals.

items.title: The Roma personal metadata service [electronic resource]
items.description: We introduce the Roma personal metadata service to make it easier to locate current file versions and ensure their availability across different repositories. In this paper we describe the design requirements, architecture and current prototype implementation of Roma.

items.title: Walnut Creek shareware collection, 1993-2006
items.description: Collection of shareware on optical disc, all distributed by the company Walnut Creek and its successors. About half of the collection is composed of shareware anthologies. Discs often contain an amalgamation of games, fonts, pictures, utilities (i.e. diagnostic programs), and productivity suites (i.e. word processors).

items.description: Franklin Pitcher Johnson, Jr., known colloquially as "Pitch" Johnson, is an American venture capitalist known for his investments in Silicon Valley biotechnology and computer companies. "Pitch" Johnson papers include materials ranging from the 1980s to the 2010s, with the bulk of the collection comprising documents related to Johnson's Eastern European venture capital endeavors from the 1990s to early 2000s.

items.description: 126 concepts (objects) form a controlled vocabulary for computerplatforms, focused primarily on games.

items.title: Hal Barwood papers, 1985-1993
items.description: Hal Barwood worked as a screenwriter and video game designer. Included are papers relating to video game design, video games, and fifty-six 3.5" diskettes. There is a later addendum that contains published video game materials from Lucasfilms Games as well as a Space Snatchers from Aratoon booklet.

items.title: Harpoon game series collection, 1984-2010
items.description: Harpoon is a naval and air warfare simulator computer game produced by Three Sixty Pacific, Inc. The Harpoon game series collection consists of software and design materials documenting the history of the Harpoon, Sub Battle Simulator, War Patrol, PT-109, and Orbiter game series, including related business and marketing records from Advanced Gaming Systems, Inc. and Kesmai Inc.

items.title: Historical game collection, circa 1982-2009
items.description: A collection of historical games and software. Includes video games and software for the Sega Genesis 32X, Sega Master System, Nintendo Super Famicom, Sega Saturn (NTSC-J), Nintendo Dsi (NTSC-U/C), Nintendo Family Computer, Atari 5200 Super System, various computer systems, and more.

items.title: History of Computer Game Design records, 2001-2004
items.description: Papers from a Stanford University class on computer game design taught by Henry Lowood (STS 145).

items.title: Jeff Braun / Maxis Corporation papers, circa 1987-circa 1995
items.description: This small collection consists of a bound collection of Maxis IPO documents, an IPO artifact and an issue of Microtimes profiling Braun and Maxis. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]
items.era_note: [The bound documents from Maxis's initial public offering, the core of this small collection, date from the mid-1990s.]

items.title: Michael R. Dornbrook papers
items.description: Collection consists of an email archive from Dornbrook's time as COO of Harmonix Music Systems. Also includes video games in original packaging, marketing materials, swag for dealers and trade shows, financial documents, and printed copies of emails.

items.title: MUD1/British Legends source code
items.description: This implementation of MUD (Multi-User Dungeon) was developed and is operated by Viktor T. Toth. MUD1 was originally developed circa 1978 at Essex University, England. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Myst III : computer game artwork, 2002
items.description: Two CD originals and two CD use copies, together with high-resolution print images, screenshots, and concepts.

items.title: Official exhibit guide of the Electronic Entertainment Expo (E3), 2001
PC Gamer demo disc collection, 1996-2006
items.description: PC Gamer, founded in 1993 in the United Kingdom, is a monthly magazine about PC gaming. Collection of PC Gamer demo discs, 1996-2006.

items.title: Press packet, 2002
items.description: Includes clippings, images, "Steam broadband business platform" powerpoint slides, and "Valve unveils Steam at 2002 game developer's conference (press release).

items.title: Stephen M. Cabrinety Collection in the History of Microcomputing, circa 1975-1995
items.description: He founded the non-profit organization, the Computer History Institute for the Preservation of Software (C.H.I.P.S.) in 1989. Collection contains approximately 8,500 software titles, as well as computer hardware, peripheral devices, hand-held games, and computer industry literature documenting the microcomputing gaming industry during its formative years.

items.title: Steve L. Kent collection relating to the video game industry, 1999-2003
items.description: The collection is particularly strong in the history of the Japanese video game industry, and includes 23 audiocassettes of interviews, 1 VHS tape, industry publications, two video game consoles (1 X-box gaming center, 2 Nintendo game test boxes), and X-box ephemera.

items.title: Steve Meretzky papers relating to computer game design and interactive fiction history, 1978-2009
items.description: He has been involved in almost every aspect of game development, from writing to design to quality assurance and product design. The papers include design and game development documents, correspondence, paper files, electronic games, magazines, data disks, original game package artwork, PR and marketing materials, and miscellaneous electronic game industry memorabilia.

items.title: The Syndicate : twice yearly guild newsletter by guildmaster Sean Stalzer, 2004-2006
items.description: Sean Stalzer is guild master and President & CEO of the MMO gaming organization The Syndicate which was founded in 1996. Four issues: volumes 3, 4, 5, & 6.

items.title: Virtual U [video game]: A Simulation of University System Management
items.description: Virtual U is a computer simulation game that engages participants in exercises designed to improve understanding of universities as systems. Begun in 1994, Enlight Software of Hong Kong designed and developed the game, which was first released in 1997. Participants take the point of view of a university president.

items.title: Virtual Worlds and MMOs Websites
items.description: The Virtual Worlds and MMO archive is dedicated to the academic investigation and historical preservation of documentation of virtual worlds. This collection is a collaborative effort of the How They Got Game Project of the Stanford Humanities Lab and Stanford Libraries.

items.title: War games : HPS Simulations production materials, circa 1990-1999

sectors.name: Business, Technology, and Work

items.title: A tribute to Ed Ginzton 1998: ephemera, 1998-1999
items.description: Agenda, correspondence, and images (photographs, printed scans) pertaining to a gathering in August, 1998, of "Varian Frequency Standard Veterans" honoring Ed Ginzton.

items.title: Alan J. Adler papers, 1966-2006
items.description: Alan Adler, a consulting electronics engineer and lecturer at Stanford University, invented the Aerobie, a flying disc toy, in 1984. These materials were gathered and generated for an exhibition at the Engineering Library at Stanford and include drawings, exhibit text and captions, articles, clippings, Awesome Games of Catch (VHS videocassette), examples of commercial Aerobie rings and orbiter, and several pre-production models of the ring.

items.title: Documents and videos about the Bootstrap Institute, 1960-1996
items.description: Patricia B. Seybold interviews Doug Engelbart about his Bootstrap Strategy for achieving high-performance organizations. Engelbart presents the history of NLS at the 1986 ACM Conference on the History of the Personal Workstation.

items.title: Emoji Project Unicode Consortium interviews, 2020-2023
items.description: Digital files of oral history interviews with members of the Emoji Project Unicode Consortium from producer Jennifer 8. Lee. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Ephemera printed by Emigre, 1991-1998
items.description: Printed ephemera include catalogs of Emigre's products and booklets of font formats and typeface.

items.title: Global Business Network records, 1984-2012
items.description: Global Business Network (GBN) was a consulting and research organization founded in Berkeley, California in 1987 and later based in San Francisco. Materials in this collection primarily consist of records created and collected by Global Business Network (GBN) over the course of the organization's history, including WorldView meeting reports and interviews, publications, public reports, white papers, training resources, reference materials, marketing materials, and business plans.

items.title: Henry Santiestevan oral history conducted by Steve Pitti, 1995
items.description: Santiestevan Associates, a Hispanic-oriented consulting firm providing services in media relations, publications management, and program development, was founded in 1974 by Henry and Stina Santiestevan.

items.title: Information Access Corporation records, 1977-2009
items.description: The collection consists of manuals, user guides, product literature, handbooks, memos, staff directories, codes lists, suggested headings, and internal newsletters.

items.title: John Newell collection on the history of the electric vehicle, 1962-1993
items.description: He became co-founder and Chair of the Board of Directors of the Electric Automobiles Assocation (EAA) in 1967, an interest-based organization that was the outcome of a symposium on the Electric Auto held that same year and organized by the Engineering Department at San Jose State College. The collection includes photographs, correspondence, newsletters, subject files, and a sampling of project papers and schematics for electric vehicle conversion projects.

items.title: Laurence W. "Bill" Lane, Jr. papers, circa 1953-2010
items.description: The papers include speeches, personal correspondence, and correspondence and documents relating to Lane Publishing Co., producers of Sunset Magazine, books, and films. Laurence William Lane Jr. often known as Bill Lane (November 7, 1919 - July 31, 2010) was an American magazine publisher and philanthropist. The Lane family owned and published Sunset Magazine.

items.title: Revs Vehicle Dynamics Database
items.description: Multimedia collection of vehicle data collected as part of the Revs Vehicle Dynamics Database. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Robert (Bob) Stein papers, 1970-2005
items.description: Robert (Bob) Stein papers document Stein's career as co-founder of Criterion Collection and Voyager Company, his work with the Atari Research Group, and as an early pioneer of electronic publishing. The collection consists of contracts, correspondence, proposals, and planning documents relating to film distribution, laserdisc video projects, and electronically published works on CD-ROMs.

items.title: Robert Wing electric vehicles (EV) collection, 1970-2001
items.description: An EV enthusiast and hobbyist, Robert Wing became an early member of the first chapter of the Electric Vehicle Association (EVA) in Santa Clara, California and went on to help found subsequent chapters in Oregon and Santa Rosa, California. The Robert Y. Wing Electric Vehicles (EV) collection consists of material regarding electric vehicle history, technology and organizations.

items.title: Roger K. Summit papers, circa 1961-2005
items.description: Roger Kent Summit is an information scientist and businessmen best known for being the creator of the Dialog information retrieval system (sometimes stylized as DIALOG) as well as the president and CEO of Dialog Information Services, Inc. The papers of Roger Summit consist primarily of his work with industry-leading information retrieval company DIALOG.

items.title: Selket Corporation records, circa 1967-1997
items.description: Materials include company documents, drawings, printed material, product development plans, and artifacts, as well as reference materials used by Rojo to set up and run his company.

items.title: Shani Sandy works and papers, 1996-2024
items.description: Shani Sandy is an artist, a graphic designer, a creative director, and an executive. She has worked at IBM from 2018 to present as a design executive. The materials consist of design works, art, notes, writings, research, photographs, and other materials.

items.title: Stanford Executive Briefings Series, 2010-2015
items.description: The Stanford Executive Briefings Series was a sponsored business presentation on the Stanford campus. They invited speakers who are leaders in their fields - speakers noted for their ability to provide both innovative solutions and practicval advice for the challenges you face every day in the workplace.

items.title: William P. Wreden, Books & Manuscripts archive, 1936-1993
items.description: Correspondence, financial records, catalogue checking copies, orders, appraisals, account books, jeweler's inventory books, flyers, publications, scrapbook, and photographs.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Environment and conservation

items.title: James A. Roberts papers, 1971-2000
items.description: Papers pertain to his work as an environmental engineer in the United States and abroad and include reports, impact statements, proposals, correspondence, memoranda, contracts, financial records, publications, maps, and plans.

items.title: Rodney C. Ewing papers, 1946-2024
items.description: Rodney Charles Ewing (1946-2024) was acclaimed for his multidisciplinary work in the fields of science, specifically the mineral sciences, nuclear materials and security, materials science and engineering, as well as geochemistry. Materials consist of research files regarding nuclear waste management and environmental impacts, the Yucca Mountain Repository, course materials, audiovisual recordings of lectures, and publications authored by Ewing.

items.title: San Mateo County Sea Level Rise Vulnerability Assessment Project
items.description: Shapefiles from the San Mateo County Sea Level Rise Vulnerability Assessment Project.

items.title: The Conservation Lands Network regional biodiversity GIS database [electronic resource]
items.description: Between 2006 and 2011, the Bay Area Open Space Council partnered with 125 regional experts to develop the Conservation Lands Network as a tool for conservation practitioners, landowners, land managers, policy makers and the public. This collection contains vector and raster data related to biodiversity and environmental conservation within the San Francisco Bay Area.

items.title: Thomas Reid Associates conservation agreement for the California tiger salamander at Stanford University
items.description: Thomas Reid Associates was an environmental consultancy founded in 1972 by Thomas Reid. This volume is a draft of the agreement to be entered into by the County of Santa Clara, Department of Fish and Game of the State of California, the United States Fish and Wildlife Service, and Stanford University.

items.title: U.S. Geological Survey Library, Menlo Park, superfund reports
items.description: The companies represented in this bibliography are on the San Francisco peninsula, many on land leased from Stanford University. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Farming, canning and food processing

items.title: Cliff Pierce, "The Webb Ranch: Pioneers to Pumpkins"
items.description: Leased from Stanford University and subleased by James Rolph in 1922, George Webb started Webb Ranch as a strawberry farm. The book "The Webb Ranch: Pioneers to Pumpkins" by Cliff Piece provides a history of the ranch from 1922-2000 and includes photographs from the Stanford Historical Photograph collection.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Petroleum and natural gas

items.title: The Stanford Rock Fracture Project
items.description: The Rock Fracture Project was an industrial affiliates project within the Structural Geology and Geomechanics Program in the School of Earth Sciences at Stanford University from 1990 to 2015. The Rock Fracture Project was one of the largest and most active research groups in the world devoted to conducting state-of-the-art research on problems of rock fracture and related crustal deformation and fluid flow, with special attention to the needs of the petroleum industry. The 405 scientific reports from 25 annual workshops are archived here.

items.title: The Stanford Shale Smear Project
items.description: The Stanford Shale Smear Project was an industrial affiliates project within the Stanford Structural Geology and Geomechanics Program in the Geological and Environmental Sciences Department in the School of Earth Sciences at Stanford University. The project was directed by Professor Atilla Aydin. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Real estate and land development

items.title: Sand Hill Road development : videorecordings, 1996-1997
items.description: These video tapes pertain to Stanford University's development plan for the Sand Hill Road corridor between El Camino Real and Santa Cruz Avenue, which falls under the jurisdiction of the City of Palo Alto.

items.title: Stanford University sustainable development study
items.description: Includes the final report (December 2008), the Executive Summary, a Stanford News Service press release (Nov. 19, 2008) concerning its presentation to the Santa Clara County Planning Commission, and a PDF file of the final report.

items.title: Stanford University, Munger dormitory collection, 2003-2006
items.description: Peter Stansky, who earned his Ph.D. in History from Harvard University, is the Frances and Charles Field Professor of Modern British History, Emeritus, at Stanford. Collection concerns a proposed new graduate dormitory for the Stanford Law School, funded by Nancy and Charles Munger, and local opposition to the plans; it includes reports, correspondence, committee materials (Committee on Land and Building Development), clippings and news coverage, and documents gathered by the law firm hired by Stansky to represent his and others' concerns with the project.

items.title: Stanford University, Office of the General Counsel, records
items.description: The Office of the General Counsel (OGC) is responsible for addressing all of the legal issues arising out of the activities of Stanford University, Stanford Hospital and Clinics and Lucile Salter Packard Children's Hospital at Stanford. Records from the legal office pertain to real estate matters, including the Stanford Shopping Center, other leases, and gift deeds.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Surveying and mapping

items.title: San Mateo County, California GIS Maps & Data [electronic resource]
items.description: This collection of data is produced by the County of San Mateo Information Services Department. Data layers in this collection cover a variety of themes, including: parcels, boundaries, zoning, points of interest, water supply management, public safety, and utilities.

items.title: Santa Clara County, California GIS Maps & Data [electronic resource]
items.description: This collection of data is produced by the County of Santa Clara County GIS program. Data layers in this collection cover a variety of themes, including: parcels. boundaries, zoning, points of interest, water supply management, public safety, and utilities.
