items.title: Stanford Lands 2010 [electronic resource]
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Transportation

items.title: Metropolitan Transportation Commission GIS Maps & Data [electronic resource]
items.description: These are geospatial data layers acquired from the Bay Area Metropolitan Transportation Commission (MTC) spatial data library. Layers contain feature data related to transportation, administrative boundaries, demographics, environmental factors, census activities, and regional projects.

items.title: The Alfred A. Hart Photo Project collection
items.description: From 1864 to 1869, Alfred A. Hart took 364 pictures along the line of the Central Pacific Railroad in order to help solicit investment in the railroad. Between 2008-2011, Jesse White repeated Hart's journey taking photographs from exactly (or approximately) the same sites. The materials consist of digtial images and the project web site.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use — Water and public works

items.title: Jacob Rubin papers, undated
items.description: Returning to the U.S. in 1961, he became a chief scientist in the Water Resources Division of the U.S. Geological Survey in Menlo Park, and joined the Stanford University faculty as a consulting professor. He was known as a pioneer of water infiltration theory, and was most proud of his work in founding the USGS National Water-Quality Assessment Program.

items.title: Perry L. McCarty papers, 1953-2023
items.description: Perry L. McCarty, Silas H. Palmer Professor Emeritus, came to Stanford University in 1962 to found a new multidisciplinary education and research program in environmental engineering and science that became a model for others throughout the country. The focus of McCarty's research, teaching, and writing has been on water, with a primary interest in biological processes for the control of environmental contamination. This collection consists of various funding proposals and related correspondence, technical reports, conference presentations, book chapters, journal articles, news articles, professional correspondence, and awards.

items.title: Re-inventing the Nation's Urban Water Infrastructure (ReNUWIt)
items.description: ReNUWIt is an interdisciplinary, multi-institution engineering research center. Our goal is to change the ways we manage urban water.

sectors.name: Agriculture, environment, and land use

items.title: George Waters photographs of Toichi Domoto and others, 1993 July 18.
items.description: Included in the photographs are San Francisco Bay Area horticultural leaders.

items.title: Yerba Buena Memories : typescript (photocopied), 1997
items.description: Included with the personal memories are two memoirs by Gerda Isenberg of Gertrud Aronstein and Helmut Schneider, both of whom helped her get started but who are now no longer living. Also included is information about the Yerba Buena Foundation, 1989-1995, written by Bob Young and Betsy Clebsch. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Education and research — Applied physics

items.title: Anthony Edward Siegman papers, 1916-2013 (inclusive)
items.description: Anthony Siegman was an electrical engineer, primarily focused on masers and lasers. Siegman became an assistant professor at Stanford in Electrical Engineering in 1957. The materials consist of administrative files, research files, correspondence, and publications.

items.title: High Dynamic Range Imaging of Natural Scenes
items.description: ISET Scene data generated from calibrated RGB values. The scene luminance ranges span two to six orders of magnitude. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: ISET Multispectral Image Database
items.description: This is a collection of multispectral image data that were generated in two different ways. Two datasets were collected in the years between 2004-2008, by capturing a series of images with a calibrated digital camera and a collection of color fiters. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Robert H. Hammond papers
items.description: He was among the early pioneers in the field of superconductivity, and worked at both UC Berkeley and Stanford University. Collection materials include notebooks, lab notebooks, and research files related to superconductivity projects, grants, and instruction.

items.title: ShockGas-IR Spectral Database
items.description: ShockGas-IR is a database of gas-phase infrared absorption spectra measured at elevated temperatures and pressures. The measurements are performed in the Hanson Research Group shock tube facilities using rapid-tuning, broad-scan lasers to collect quantitative, spectrally-resolved absorption cross section data over a wide wavelength range.

items.title: Steven Chu papers, 1949-2013 (inclusive), 1975-2004 (bulk)
items.description: Steven Chu is the William R. Kenan, Jr. Professor of Physics and Professor of Molecular and Cellular Physiology at Stanford University. While at Bell labs, Chu led the group that showed how to first cool and then trap atoms with light. Papers pertain primarily to topics in physics and include notes, overhead transparencies from his lectures, reprints, articles, memos, proposals, correspondence, charts, and drawings. Subjects include electric dipole moment, diode lasers, and dye lasers; and there are some materials pertaining to departmental matters.

items.title: Theodore H. Geballe papers, 1942-1997
items.description: Professor of Applied Physics and Materials Science Engineering at Stanford University. Professional correspondence; materials from meetings, conferences, workshops, and symposia; and abstracts, notes, and transparencies from talks relating to his teaching and research in materials science, superconductivity, and electronics.

sectors.name: Education and research — Campus and student life

items.title: Sheldon Breiner photograph collection
items.description: Sheldon Breiner is a scientist trained in geophysics and specializing in exploration and research of the earth. The materials consist of scans and digital photographs taken by Sheldon Breiner documenting his undergraduate days and the Stanford campus.

items.title: Stanford Cat Network, records
items.description: The Stanford Cat Network (SCN) was founded in 1989, at which time there were approximately 1,000 feral cats on campus. The collection includes Stanford Cat Network policy documentation, newsletters, and photographs of working cats on Stanford campus.

items.title: Stanford Women in Computer Science, records
items.description: Stanford Women in Computer Science was founded in 2012 to achieve three broad goals: raise awareness about issues faced by women in computer science; provide aspiring computer science professionals with tools to compete; and encourage more women to pursue computer science. Includes meeting minutes, flyers, mentorship materials, door signage, and related materials.

sectors.name: Education and research — Education research and educational technology

items.title: Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching. Knowledge Media Laboratory (KML) : research material, 1999-2008
items.description: The Knowledge Media Lab records contain notes from all phases of the project, including the initial proposal, planning documents, agendas and memoranda relating to meetings and convenings, and reports.

items.title: Carnegie Foundation records, circa 1990-2015
items.description: The Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching (CFAT) is an education policy and research center. Materials consist of records kept by the Carnegie Foundation.

items.title: Patrick Suppes papers, 1951-2014
items.description: Patrick Suppes was the Lucie Stern Professor of Philosophy, Emeritus, and a member of the departments of Statistics and Psychology and of the Graduate School of Education at Stanford University. This collection consists of research, notes, papers, and correspondence with a particular emphasis on Suppes' work on computer-assisted education research.

items.title: The knowledge navigator [videorecording] : technologies to get us there and beyond
items.description: Members of Apple Computer's Advanced Technology Group describe future possibilities in educational technology using the Macintosh computer. Emphasis is on applications in higher education.

sectors.name: Education and research — Engineering

items.title: Barry M. Katz papers, 1956-2011
items.description: Barry M. Katz is a design historian based in the Design Group, Department of Mechanical Engineering. This collection consists of the contents of John Arnold's "Creative Engineering Seminars" held at MIT in 1956, which included presentations by Buckminster Fuller, Abraham Maslow, Al Capp, and other notable individuals who introduced radical concepts at the time such as "brainstorming," "operational creativity," and "applied imagination.".

items.title: CUREE (Consortium of Universities for Research in Earthquake Engineering) (1988-2016)
items.description: Publications from CUREE (Consortium of Universities for Research in Earthquake Engineering) (1988-2016), a non-profit organization devoted to earthquake engineering research, education and implementation and promotion of public learning about civil engineering.

items.title: James L. Adams papers, 1925-2017 (inclusive)
items.description: He joined the Stanford faculty in the School of Engineering in 1966. Adams' administrative positions included Associate Dean for Academic Affairs; Chair of the Program in Values, Technology, Science and Society; Director of the Design Division of Mechanical Engineering; and Chair of the Department of Industrial Engineering and Engineering Management. Papers largely reflect James L. Adam’s teaching career at Stanford University and include class materials, correspondence, memoranda, reports, publications, and some photographs (largely of student projects).

items.title: John A. Blume Earthquake Engineering Center Technical Report Series
items.description: This series includes technical reports prepared by faculty, students and staff who are associated with the John A. Blume Earthquake Engineering Center at Stanford University. While the primary focus of Blume Center is earthquake engineering, many of the reports in this series encompass broader topics in structural engineering and materials, computational mechanics, geomechanics, structural health monitoring, and engineering life-cycle risk assessment.

items.title: John A. Blume papers, 1903-1994 (inclusive), 1928-1994 (bulk)
items.description: Blume, known as the father of earthquake engineering, earned his B.S. in civil engineering in 1933 and his engineer's degree in 1935 at Stanford University. Collection includes subject and reference files on earthquakes and earthquake-resistant design; slides, photographs, and videos pertaining to earthquakes and earthquake engineering; course files as both student and teacher; reports and other materials on Diablo Canyon Nuclear Plant; and talks, lectures, and reprints by Blume.

items.title: Max C. Yost report on Stanford engineering curricula
items.description: Max C. Yost earned his BS in mechanical engineering at Stanford in 1952. Collection consists of tables compiled by Yost comparing engineering requirements for his years at Stanford (1944-1952), the Pioneer Class (entered 1891, graduated 1895), and the academic year 1996/97; also included is his cover letter to Dean John Hennessy explaining his research and his summary.

items.title: ME310 Project Based Engineering Design
items.description: Students enrolled in ME310 participate in a product design project over the course of an entire school year in collaboration with another team from a foreign university. The ME310 collection is a set of project reports from the ME310 course at Stanford University.

items.title: Mechanical Engineering-310
items.description: Students in ME310 take on real world design challenges brought forth by corporate partners. Unlike many other academic engineering projects, which require students to optimize one variable, students must design a complete system while being mindful of not only the primary function but also the usability, desirability, and societal implications.

items.title: Reliability of Marine Structures Program
items.description: The Reliability of Marine Structures (RMS) Program operated out of the Blume Center from 1988 to 2002, leading advanced research in marine structures behavior and reliability. The Program combined post-M.S. graduate study with basic research in structural reliability applications. The pioneering work performed by the RMS Program remains relevant today, and so the theses and research reports produced by the Program are now archived at the Blume Center.

items.title: Rudolf E. Kálmán papers, 1954-2016
items.description: Rudolf Emil Kálmán (May 19, 1930 – July 2, 2016) was a Hungarian-American electrical engineer, mathematician, and inventor. He is most noted for his co-invention and development of the Kalman filter, a mathematical algorithm that is widely used in signal processing, control systems, and guidance, navigation and control. This collection consists of biographical materials, information regarding awarded prizes, technical grants and publications, lectures, course materials, and correspondence.

items.title: Sheri D. Sheppard papers, 1956-2024
items.description: In addition to teaching undergraduate and graduate design-related classes, Sheppard conducts research on fracture mechanics and applied finite element analysis, and on how people become engineers. This collection includes publications; surveys, data, and notes relating to Shepperd's research; correspondence, notes, and presentation materials related to conferences and workshops; course lectures and notes; and audiovisual recordings of talks and workshops.

items.title: Thomas Cover papers, circa 1964-2011
items.description: Cover joined the faculty at the Stanford School of Engineering in 1964, becoming a professor in 1972. In 1990, the Information Theory Society of the IEEE awarded him the Claude E. Shannon Award, the highest honor for lifetime achievement in information theory. This collection primarily consists of correspondence, notes, teaching materials, publications, and administrative files.

sectors.name: Education and research — Library, archival and information services

items.title: Digital Library announcement : videorecording, 1995 March 27.
items.description: The Digital Library Program coordinates initiatives of various Library departments to produce and offer online access to documents, texts, journals, databases, and other digital resources to the Stanford community.

items.title: Inside the Apple archives : newspaper article about the Stanford Libraries' holdings of Apple Computer material
items.description: The article discusses the large collection (600 linear feet) of Apple historical materials at Stanford University, interviewing both Henry Lowood and Leslie Berlin who have overseen the collection.

items.title: Into the Future; On the Preservation of Knowledge in the Electronic Age [videorecording], 1997
items.description: Discusses the issue of whether digitally stored information and knowledge will survive into the future. Features Peter Norton and Tim Berners-Lee.

items.title: R. Joseph Anderson and Orville R. Butler history of physicists in industry report
items.description: At the time of the report, R. Joseph Anderson was the director of the American Institute of Physics' (AIP) Niels Bohr Library and Archives and associate director of the AIP Center for History of Physics in College Park, Maryland. Orville R. Butler (1952-) is a retired historian who worked at the AIP history center. "This project is the first systematic study of the organizational structure, communications patterns, and archival records of industrial physicists in the U.S., and it provides general guidelines for understanding and documenting their work." – from the Executive Summary.

items.title: Research Libraries Group (RLG) records, 1974-2006
items.description: The Research Libraries Group, Inc. (RLG) was a non-profit consortium founded in 1974 by major U.S. libraries (NYPL, Columbia, Harvard, Yale) to foster collaborative, technology-driven resource sharing. The RLG collection includes historical corporate documents, program and project files, grant proposals, system and software development files, digital material, photographs, and other documents and memorabilia.

items.title: Silicon Valley Archives events collection, 2023-2024
items.description: The collection consists of three recorded Silicon Valley Archives events: 1. Silicon Valley Talks: Henry Lowood, Replayed (November 14, 2023, Green Library). 2. Silicon Valley Talks: Barbara Boissevain, Salt of the Earth (March 7, 2024, Green Library). 3. Silicon Valley Talks: Anna Schechtman (April 4, 2024, Green Library).

items.title: Stanford University, Libraries, HighWire Press records, 1999-2000
items.description: The records primarily contain overhead slides for presentations on HighWire Press by Vicky Reich, 2000 and undated; titles include Electronic Publishing between Two Poles, The HighWire Perspective Electronic Journal License Agreements, What *Do* Librarians Want? and E-Materials: Barriers to Revolutionizing Scientific Information. HighWire Press is a division of the Stanford University Libraries producing online versions of peer-reviewed journals and scholarly content.

items.title: The Stanford and Silicon Valley Project : video, 1996 Mar. 1.
items.description: Describes the collecting efforts of community members and the Stanford University Libraries in documenting the rise of the electronics industry in the south Bay Area. Co-produced by Rob Walker and Jane Chai, with commentary by Henry Lowood.

sectors.name: Education and research — Musical acoustics and computer music

items.title: John R. Pierce papers, 1933-2002 (inclusive), 1960-2002 (bulk)
items.description: He worked at Bell Telephone Laboratories from 1936 to 1971, where his work included electronic tubes, microwave communications, and psychoacoustics. In 1983 he became a visiting professor of music, emeritus, at the Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics at Stanford University. The focus is primarily on his interest in computers and music and his authorship of science fiction stories, with a few published articles and photographs pertaining to the Echo satellite.

items.title: Max V. Mathews papers, 1953-2011
items.description: The collection includes correspondence, articles, lab notebooks, musical scores, audio recordings, computer files, and other materials related to the professional work of computer music pioneer Max V. Mathews. While at Stanford, he was affiliated with the Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics.

items.title: Musical Acoustics Research Library collection, 1956-2007
items.description: Contains research materials, research papers, correspondence, journal run , photographs, glass slides, wood samples, and other artifacts (woodwind and brass mouthpieces). The MARL collection is dedicated to the study of all aspects of musical acoustics.

items.title: Thomas D. Rossing papers, 1990-2016
items.description: He continued research in magnetism, some of it in collaboration with scientists at Argonne National Laboratory, but he became more and more interested in musical acoustics. In 2004 he became a Visiting Professor at in the Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics (CCRMA) at Stanford University, where he taught until the age of 90. This collection contains research notes, correspondence, and administrative files.

sectors.name: Education and research — Schools, colleges and training

items.title: Stanford University, Alliance for Lifelong Learning, records
items.description: The Alliance for Lifelong Learning was a not-for-profit distance learning venture between Oxford, Stanford, and Yale Universities. The collection contains program documentation and administrative resources as well as recordings of lectures and lessons.

sectors.name: Education and research — Science and mathematics

items.title: Anita Burdman Feferman papers, 1932-2001, bulk 1993-1996
items.description: Anita Burdman Feferman and her husband Solomon Feferman are the co-authors of a biography of the logician Alfred Tarski. Audio interviews conducted for Feferman's book, Alfred Tarski: Life and Logic , which she co-authored with her husband Solomon Feferman.

items.title: Barry M. Trost papers, 1961-2019
items.description: Barry M. Trost (b.1941) is the Job and Gertrud Tamaki Professor in the School of Humanities and Sciences, Emeritus for the Department of Chemistry. The collection consists primarily of postdoctoral researcher, graduate students, and undergrad student lab reports and data generated during their time with the Trost Group research program.

items.title: Benoit B. Mandelbrot papers, circa 1932-2012
items.description: The papers document the life and work of Benoit B. Mandelbrot, mathematician and pioneer of fractal geometry. The collection contains biographical material, personal and professional correspondence, drafts and typescripts for books and articles, subject files, and reprints.

items.title: Bruce A.D. Stocker papers, 1972-2004
items.description: Bruce Arnold Dunbar Stocker was Professor of Microbiology and Immunology at Stanford University from 1966 to 1987 Collection includes lab notebooks, note pads, correspondence, and reprints.

items.title: Carolyn R. Bertozzi papers, circa 1990-2016
items.description: Carolyn Bertozzi is the Anne T. and Robert M. Bass Professor of Chemistry and Professor of Chemical and Systems Biology and Radiology (by courtesy) at Stanford University, and an Investigator of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute. Collection consists of Bertozzi Group Research Lab notebooks.

items.title: David S. Hogness, 1925-2019
items.description: David Hogness, PhD, was a Stanford biochemist who helped found the field of genomics. This collection comprises biographical materials, awarded grants, manuscript drafts, Hogness Group Laboratory records, and records related to the development and administration of Developmental Biology at Stanford University.

items.title: Donald Leland Carpenter memoirs
items.description: Emeritus professor of Engineering, Carpenter earned his PhD at Stanford in 1962. Carpenter's research focused on very low frequency radio propagation and solar terrestrial physics. Memoirs of Don Carpenter.

items.title: Folding@home Collection
items.description: Metadata associated with publications derived from data generated on the Folding@home distributed computing network. Includes trajectory and Markov state model (MSM) data. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Gravity Probe B records, 1983-2008
items.description: Gravity Probe B was a relativity gyroscope experiment funded by NASA and led by the Stanford University Department of Physics, with Lockheed Martin as the primary subcontractor. Records include audiovisual materials, administrative records pertaining to the project, photographs, and public relations materials.

items.title: Harden M. McConnell papers
items.description: Harden Marsden McConnell (1927-2014) was the Robert Eckles Swain Professor Emeritus of Chemistry at Stanford University. He was a leading 20th-century physical and biophysical chemist known for incisive contributions in both theory and experiment. Over his career, he significantly advanced understanding of magnetic resonance, cell membrane biophysics and immunology.

items.title: Harrison Minge Brown papers
items.description: He had several articles published in leading mathematics journals. Working and research files, correspondence, and journal entries.

items.title: Harry S. Mosher papers, 1944-2000
items.description: During his career at Stanford, Mosher taught organic chemistry and conducted research in a wide range of areas, including natural products chemistry and stereochemistry. Papers include correspondence, manuscripts and reprints, research files, lab notebooks, grant files, and class materials.

items.title: Henry Taube papers, 1941-2003
items.description: Henry's research interests were in both inorganic and organic chemistry; his work has been central to many different fields such as electron transfer at semiconductor electrodes, solar energy conversion, and photosynthesis. Collection pertains to his teaching and research, primarily while at Stanford University, and includes grant files, articles and papers, reprints, class files, correspondence, travel records, and biographical materials.

items.title: Ingram Olkin papers, 1875-2014, bulk 1950-2014
items.description: Ingram Olkin is best known for developing statistical analyses for evaluating policies, particularly in education. One year later, he moved permanently to Stanford University, where he held a joint appointment with the Department of Statistics and the Graduate School of Education.

items.title: Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve: Photographs
items.description: Photographs taken by faculty and staff of Jasper Ridge.

items.title: Joseph B. Keller papers, 1949-2007
items.description: Joseph B. Keller is Professor Emeritus of Mathematics and of Mechanical Engineering at Stanford University, and former Honorary Professor of Mathematical Sciences at the University of Cambridge. These papers consist primarily of correspondence files maintained by Keller from 1949-2007. Also included are article reviews and refereeing reports, honorary degrees and other awards, and course evaluations, as well as figures and problems.

items.title: Lucy Shapiro papers, 1940-2024
items.description: Lucy Shapiro is professor emerita of developmental biology and director of Stanford Medicine's Beckman Center. This collection consists of administrative records, seminars and lectures, Shapiro dissertation, lab notebooks and data, manuscripts and related correspondence, research files related to bioterrorism, patents and licensing related to biotech companies AnaCor and BorAgen.

items.title: Martin Gardner papers, 1957-1986
items.description: Martin Gardner was the Mathematical Games columnist for SCIENTIFIC AMERICAN from its inception in 1956 until 1986. These papers pertain to his interest in mathematics and consist of files relating to his SCIENTIFIC AMERICAN mathematical games column (1957-1986) and subject files on recreational mathematics. Papers include correspondence, notes, clippings, and articles, with some examples of puzzle toys.

items.title: Paul Joseph Cohen papers, 1981-2015
items.description: Paul Joseph Cohen won two of the most prestigious awards in mathematics—in completely different fields. He won the American Mathematical Society's Bôcher Prize in 1964 for analysis and the Fields Medal, considered the "Nobel Prize" of mathematics, in 1966 for logic. Collection consists of Cohen's photographs, audiovisual materials, and computer files.

items.title: Peter A. Sturrock papers, 1952-2020
items.description: Peter Andrew Sturrock is an emeritus professor of applied physics at Stanford University. This collection consists of correspondence, research and teaching files, grant proposals, and reports.

items.title: Ronald Bracewell papers, 1958-2007
items.description: Ronald Newbold Bracewell (July 22, 1921 – August 12, 2007) was the Lewis M. Terman Professor of Electrical Engineering, Emeritus of the Space, Telecommunications and Radioscience Laboratory at Stanford University. In 1998 Dr. Bracewell was named Officer of the Order of Australia (AO) for service to science in the fields of radio astronomy and image reconstruction.

items.title: SLACspeak
items.description: Glossary of SLAC-related Photon Science, Particle and Astroparticle Science, and HEP-related acronyms and terms.

items.title: Solar Physics Group Software and Data for Publications
items.description: Thie collection contains software and data used for figures in articles published in scientific journals by the Observational Solar Physics Group.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Chemistry, Waymouth Group, Records, 1989-2015
items.description: Led by Robert Eckles Swain Professor in Chemistry Robert Waymouth, the Waymouth group applies mechanistic principles to develop homogeneous catalysts for the selective synthesis of both macromolecules and fine chemicals. Series consists of lab notebooks.

items.title: Stanford University, Department of Statistics, technical reports
items.description: The Department of Statistics was established in 1948, and by 1950, it boasted a faculty of five esteemed members: Albert Bowker, Abraham Girshick, Quinn McNemar (who had a joint appointment with Psychology), Kenneth Arrow (who shared a joint appointment with Economics), and Herman Rubin. This collection contains technical reports and a version of the department's website.

items.title: Stanford University, Herzenberg Laboratory, Records, circa 1966-2016
items.description: Pioneers in the study of genetics, Lee and Len Herzenberg came to Stanford in 1959 to join the newly created genetics department run by Nobel laureate Joshua Lederberg. They would go on to develop the Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorter (FACS) and monoclonal antibodies that are widely used as reagents in life science research and are models for the therapeutic antibodies used in several diseases. Laboratory notebooks, slides, patent files, and FACS files.

items.title: Stephen Jay Gould papers, 1899-2004 (inclusive), 1941-2002 (bulk)
items.description: This collection documents the life of noted American paleontologist, evolutionary biologist, and historian of science, Stephen Jay Gould. The papers include correspondence, juvenilia, manuscripts, subject files, teaching files, photographs, audiovisual materials, and personal and biographical materials created and compiled by Gould.

items.title: William James Nelson Laboratory, records, 2000-2018
items.description: The Nelson lab's research seeks to understand how cell interactions specify the correct cellular organization of complex tissues, and how structurally and functionally different plasma membrane domains are assembled and tailored to specific tissue and organ functions. Collection consists of lab research notes.

items.title: William R. Normark memorial archive collection, 1970-2006
items.description: Collection includes materials related to the work of William R. Normark, a Geologist at the Geological Survey in Menlo Park, California.

items.title: William S. Johnson Symposium in Organic Chemistry [videorecording]
items.description: Since its inception in 1985, the Johnson Symposium in Organic Chemistry has been held annually at Stanford University to honor the contributions of William S. Johnson and to also recognize current and future top scientists in Organic Chemistry. The materials consist of videorecordings of symposium events.

items.title: Wray Huestis papers, 1979-2004
items.description: Professor Wray Huestis’ research concerns the molecular mechanisms whereby cells control their shape, motility, deformability and the structural integrity of their membranes. This collection comprises student lab notebooks from the Wray Huestis Lab.

items.title: Zoe Chandik Birding Field Notes and Slides, 1951-2011
items.description: Zoe Chandik was a Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve volunteer who worked to make historical records available to a wider audience. The materials consist of international lists and slides of bird species.

sectors.name: Education and research — Social sciences and humanities

items.title: Doris H. Linder papers, 1900-2008
items.description: Linder was Professor of History at the College of San Mateo for over forty years, teaching world history and women's studies courses. Doris Linder's papers includes research and teaching files and notes, drafts and correspondence related to her published research, travel and country files, family and personal correspondence and ephemera, slides, and published material.

items.title: Eugene J. Webb papers, 1961-1994
items.description: Eugene J. Webb, a pioneer in the development of research and teaching of organizational behavior in business schools, joined the faculty of the Graduate School of Business at Stanford in 1968. Professional papers relating to courses Webb taught at the Graduate School of Business at Stanford University and his research interests such as philanthropy, altruism, effect of deadlines on human behavior, and organizational behavior.

items.title: Frank Hawkinshire papers, 1969-2017
items.description: Frank B.W. Hawkinshire, V. was Stanford University's first tenured Black professor in Educational Psychology from 1967-1971. The focus of his academic interests have been on the applications of sociology, psychology, and physiology to solving social problems.

items.title: Geographic clustering and spillovers : an empirical approach using geographic information systems and firm-level data
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Henry Etzkowitz papers, circa 1990s
items.description: Collection consists of documentation, publications, floppy disks and other hardware related to the Triple Helix research projects, primarily interviews and interview transcripts. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Paul A. David papers, 1920-2010
items.description: Paul A. David (1935-2023) was an economic historian at Stanford best known for his research on technological change and how it affects social and economic behavior. This collection consists of publication drafts, grant grant proposals, research files, correspondence, and ECON course materials.

items.title: Robert E. Horn papers, 1982-2001
items.description: Robert E. Horn (b.1933) is a political scientist, futurist, and strategist specializing in visualizing information through large information murals or visual posters. This collection consists of research materials assembed by Robert E. Horn such as articles, newspaper clippings, and journals.

items.title: Stanford Center for Chicano Research records, 1984-1998
items.description: Records pertain primarily to the Ernesto Galarza Commemorative lecture series and the Galarza Prize for Excellence in Undergraduate or Graduate Research. Collection includes correspondence, committee records, publicity materials, invitations, text of lectures, papers submitted by students, clippings, photographs and other records.

items.title: Stanford Humanities Lab records, circa 1999-2009
items.description: The materials consist of administrative records, subject files, conference materials, and email documenting the functions and projects of the Stanford Humanities Lab. Founded by Jeffrey Schnapp (Comparative Literature) in 1999, the Stanford Humanities Lab (SHL) enabled scholars in the humanities to undertake mid- to large-scale team-based research projects.

items.title: Stanford University, Center for Computer Assisted Research in the Humanities at Stanford, records, 1976-2003
items.description: Founded in 1984, the Center for Computer Assisted Research in the Humanities (CCARH) is engaged in the developement of large databases of musical and textual materials for applications in research, teaching, and performance. Records consist of music software manuals in both print and electronic formats.

items.title: Stanley Peters papers, 1970-2017
items.description: Stanley Peters (b.1941) is Director Emeritus of the Center for the Study of Language and Information (2008-2013) and a Professor Emeritus of Linguistics at Stanford University. This collection contains correspondence, research files, grant applications, and audiovisual materials related to the Department of Linguistics and the Stanford Center for the Study of Language and Information (CSLI).

items.title: Thomas S. Mullaney papers
items.description: Thomas S. Mullaney is Professor of History and Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures, by courtesy. This collection contains reserach notes, journals, audio recordings, and materials used for exhibits in the East Asia Library.

items.title: Willis W. Harman papers
items.description: Willis W. Harman (1918-1997) was a professor emeritus of engineering at Stanford University, senior social scientist at SRI International of Menlo Park, president of the Institute of Noetic Sciences, cofounder of the World Business Academy, and served on the University of California Board of Regents. The collection consists of correspondence, memos and other documents regarding the Institute of Noetic Sciences' Pathfinding Project, photographs of Willis Harman, and Harman's writings.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford history and ceremonial life

items.title: "To Touch History: Gorbachev at Stanford" [videorecording]
items.description: Tape of Mikhail Gorbachev's visit to Stanford University on June 4, 1990, including full text of his speech. Narrated by Stanford University president Donald Kennedy with some comments by George P. Shultz.

items.title: John Hennessy, president of Stanford University, inauguration [videorecording]
items.description: In addition to Hennessy's speech, the program also included remarks by Isaac Stein, president of the Board of Trustees, the Rev. Scotty McLennan, dean for religious life, and former university presidents Gerhard Casper, Donald Kennedy and Richard W. Lyman; the reading by English Professor Eavan Boland of a poem by Denise Levertov; and a varied selection of music and performers that included a song, "The Call of the West," composed by Giancarlo Aquilanti, DMA '96, especially for the occasion.

items.title: John L. Hennessy, president of Stanford University, essays and public statements
items.description: Reflective essay on term as Stanford president during his fifth year and a public statement re: 9/11 10th Anniversary.

items.title: Lecture by the President of the Portuguese Republic at Stanford University
items.description: Aníbal António Cavaco Silva (b.1939) was the 19th President of the Portuguese Republic (2006-2016), prime minister (1985-1995), and finance minister (1980-1981). Title of lecture: "Portugal: The Other Story -- Connecting with the Future" In 2011, then President Cavaco Silva met with University President John Hennessy during his visit to Stanford.

items.title: Stanford Historical Society oral history program interviews
items.description: The Stanford Historical Society's Oral History Program explores the institutional history of the University, with an emphasis on the transformative post-WWII period, through interviews with leading faculty, staff, alumni, trustees, and others.

items.title: Stanford News Service records 1931-2023
items.description: The News Service reports and disseminates much of the University's news, via the STANFORD REPORT daily news email. Records include subject files compiled by the News Service in the course of its work, news releases prepared by the News Service, proof sheets of photographs produced by the News Service photographers, taped interviews, office files of the Director of News and Publications Service and of the directors of the individual units, news clippings, and miscellaneous photographic and printed material.

items.title: Stanford Pioneers in Science [videorecordings], 2008-2010
items.description: Inaugurated in 2008-09, this series honors the lives and accomplishments of Stanford University's most celebrated scientists—faculty members who have been awarded Nobel Prizes, National Medals of Science or Technology, and MacArthur Fellowships. The Stanford Pioneers in Science video lecture series includes videorecordings on DVCAM, MiniDV, and DVD.

items.title: Stanford University biographical files collection, circa 1891-2011
items.description: The collection contains biographical files on faculty, staff, and other individuals affiliated with Stanford University.

items.title: Stanford University Founders' Day, March 10, 1991 : videorecording, 1991
items.description: Ceremony marking the centennial of the founding of Stanford; includes multi-media presentation "Stanford: Portrait of a Family," narrated by Anna M. Chavez, remarks by Richard W. Lyman, President Emeritus, and keynote address by Wallace Stegner.

items.title: Stanford University video collection, 1934-2016
items.description: Collection contains videorecordings and DVDs pertaining to Stanford University including lectures, cultural events, academic programs, faculty interviews, buildings, the university's history, and athletics other than football.

items.title: Stanford University, Center for Professional Development, Audiovisual Recordings
Stanford University, Class of 1954, email
items.description: Original text and email printout of message sent establishing the first electronic network of Stanford alumni, October 6, 1994; and letter to Margaret Kimball, University Archivist, from Richard Tryce, concerning this event, October 6, 1994.

items.title: The 114th annual commencement at Stanford : videorecording, 2005
items.description: Disc 1 contains the Baccalaureate service with an address by Dr. Sylvia Boorstein, co-founder of the Spirit Rock Meditation Center, with talks by Rev. Scotty McLennan and Stanford student Jazib Zahir. Disc 2 contains the commencement services with an address by Steve Jobs and welcoming remarks by President John Hennessy.

sectors.name: Education and research — Stanford University

items.title: Donald Kennedy, President of Stanford University, papers
items.description: Kennedy was Stanford's eighth president, serving from 1980 to 1992. Contains materials related to his time as Stanford's eighth president and vice president and provost under his predecessor President Richard W. Lyman.

items.title: Gerhard Casper, President of Stanford University, papers
items.description: Gerhard Casper is President Emeritus of Stanford University and a Senior Fellow at both the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies (FSI Stanford) and the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research (SIEPR). He served as President of Stanford University from 1992-2000.

items.title: John L. Hennessy, President of Stanford University, records
items.description: Records from his term as President of Stanford University, along with the records of the Provost. Some of the records were generated by the previous administration of Gerhard Casper.

items.title: Kenneth M. Cuthbertson papers, 1941-1990
items.description: Cuthbertson was named one of the university's first three vice presidents in 1960. The papers, which include correspondence, minutes, reports, and memoranda, pertain largely to administration, finance, and planning at Stanford University.

items.title: Richard W. Lyman personal papers, 1778-2011
items.description: Lyman, who served as president from 1970 to 1980, held many posts during the 25 years he spent at Stanford: history professor, associate dean of the School of Humanities and Sciences, provost, president, and founder and director of the center now known as the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies.

items.title: Stanford University Press records, 1915-2013
items.description: Records of the Stanford University Press include correspondence files, financial records, contracts, inventories, reports, and other general records; minutes of the editorial board, 1976-88, the Faculty Committee on University Publications, 1945-76, and the Press Special Committee, 1927-45; press catalogs and newsletters; some production materials (including photographs and illustrations) and correspondence pertaining to specific publications; and various test forms, answer sheets, etc., for the Strong vocational interest blank and the Stanford hypnotic susceptibility scale, both of which were published by the Stanford University Press; and includes The Zohar - Pritzker Edition records.

items.title: Stanford University website collection
items.description: The materials consist of Stanford University websites captured by University Archives staff. Included are the websites of Stanford's seven schools, their departments, and many school-affiliated labs and research centers; independent research centers and institutes reporting to the Dean of Research; interdisciplinary programs; and administrative units overseeing academic affairs, faculty development, student life, research, public affairs, human resources, and other areas of the university.

items.title: Stanford University, Board of Trustees, records
items.description: The Board administers the invested funds, sets the annual budget, and determines policies for the operation and control of the University. Records of the Trustees pertaining to legal issues, financial affairs, investments, academic departments, student housing, gifts received, real estate, campus development, and other administrative concerns.

items.title: Stanford University, Faculty Senate, records, 1891-2026(inclusive)
items.description: The Academic Council was organized by the Stanford University faculty in 1904 and currently consists of members of the Professoriate and certain officers of the academic administration as specified by the Articles of Organization. In 1968 the Academic Council created the Senate of the Academic Council, composed of representatives elected from the Council. They include minutes, memoranda, correspondence, reports, election records, agendas and supporting documents, rosters, memorial resolutions on deceased members, and audiotapes of meetings.

items.title: Stanford University, Government and Community Relations, records
Stanford University, Office of Technology Licensing, records, 1971-2010
items.description: The Office of Technology Licensing (OTL) stands as a cornerstone of Stanford University's operational framework, its inception dating back to 1970, aimed at overseeing and maximizing the university's intellectual property assets. First series includes the report "Technology Based Companies Founded by Members of the Stanford University Community" and Wiesendanger's "History and Operation of the Office of Technology Licensing Stanford University," 1996.

items.title: UCSF/Stanford Hospital Merger records
items.description: The Board of Regents approved the merger uniting UCSF Medical Center; UCSF Mount Zion Hospital, with Stanford Health Services, which comprises Stanford University Hospital and related clinics; and the Lucile Salter Packard Children's Hospital. UCSF Stanford Health Care (USHC) began operation in 1997.

sectors.name: Education and research

items.title: "Connections" [videorecording]
items.description: Film on the collaboration between researchers at Stanford and the Stanford Office of Technology Licensing to patent their new technologies. Includes interviews with Dr. Stanley N. Cohen on DNA recombinant technology; Prof. Walter Murray on MINOS optimization software and its various applications; Prof. John M. Chowning on frequency modulation synthesis and Yamaha's use of it in making keyboard synthesizers; Prof. Julius Smith on wave guide synthesis for music synthesizers; Prof. Calvin Quate on the atomic force microscope; Drs. Alan Krensky and Carol Clayberger on their work to develop drugs to increase transplant tolerance; and Katherine Ku, director of the Office of Technology Licensing, on the process of patenting and developing products.

items.title: Cecilia P. Burciaga papers, circa 1952-2006
items.description: One of the first high-ranking Chicana administrators at a private university, Cecilia Preciado Burciaga (1945-2013) was a leader in civil rights and education who inspired generations of students during a twenty year career at Stanford University and later California State University-Monterey Bay. Contains correspondence, published and unpublished writing and speech transcripts, articles and publicity featuring Burciaga, and a variety of publications, reports, and organizational materials.

items.title: Dynamic Design Lab
items.description: Downloadable content for research activities in the Dynamic Design Lab at Stanford University.

items.title: Gene Golub papers, 1950-2007
items.description: Gene Golub (1932-2007) was a Professor of Computer Science at Stanford University. Gene was a leading pioneer in the field of numerical analysis, creating algorithms and software that allowed researchers to run large engineering and science calculations effectively on computers. This collection is comprised of Professor Golub's professional records and includes notebooks on his research for his publications, lecture notes, articles, manuscripts, grant files, bibliographic materials on contemporaries, and correspondence.

items.title: Global Climate and Energy Project, records
items.description: The Global Climate and Energy Project (GCEP) at Stanford University was established in partnership with corporations such as Exxon and Toyota to direct and innovate energy research. This collection consists of various meeting agendas, handouts, and notes along with correspondence about the creation of the Global Climate and Energy Project.

items.title: Paul Kruger papers, 1958-1996
items.description: Paul Kruger was Professor of Civil Engineering at Stanford. Collection contains files, photographs, and reports relating to Kruger's civil engineering research.

items.title: Research Datasets for Image, Video, and Multimedia Systems Group at Stanford
items.description: We make available the datasets commonly used in the research activities of the Image, Video, and Multimedia Systems group at Stanford.

items.title: Stanford University, Symbolic Systems Program, honors theses, 1993-2011
items.description: The collection consists of honors theses written by undergraduates in the Stanford University Symbolic Systems Program.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Art, music, literature and photography

items.title: [Salvatore Michael Taormina collection of Samwise Didier art] [graphic]
items.description: 4 original works of art by Samwise Didier, collected by Salvatore Michael Taormina. Didier would create the art and give copies to a limited number of family and friends.

items.title: Art Com records, circa 1970-2005
items.description: La Mamelle / Art Com was a non-profit arts organization and artist-run space in San Francisco, California active from 1975 through 1995. Contains books, catalogues, periodicals, artwork, photography, publications, publicity, correspondence, financial documents and other material.

items.title: Carolyn Caddes papers and photographs, circa 1980-2015
items.description: Carolyn Caddes (1935- ) is an American photographer who spent years photographing portraits of famous Californian innovators. Her book, Portraits of Success: Impressions of Silicon Valley Pioneers, focused on Silicon Valley technology visionaries such as Steve Jobs, Robert Noyce and David Packard. Included in this collection are Caddes' interviews, portraits, research, correspondence and work files depicting Silicon Valley's technology industry, California wine makers and Caddes' personal work.

items.title: Chris Chafe Collection
items.description: Media created by Chris Chafe - composer, cellist, music researcher, and director of Stanford University's Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics.

items.title: Christopher Felver videos, 1982-2000
items.description: West coast; beat and beyond, a documentary tribute to Jack Kerouac and the San Francisco literary renaissance, featuring Allen Ginsberg, Philip Lamantia, Lawrence Ferlinghetti, Ken Kesey and others, 1982-1983.

items.title: Conservation treatment report, John MacQuarrie mural, 1941, Caltrain Station, Palo Alto : reports and photographs, 2003-2005
items.description: John A. MacQuarrie, San Francisco artist, painted a mural for the Palo Alto train station depicting transportation in the West and the coming of the railroad with a portrait of Leland Stanford. Includes examination report, 2003, and treatment report, 2005; black and white photographs and color slides before, during and after treatment, 2005; and digital files of images and reports.

items.title: David V. Harris papers, circa 1950s-2020s.
items.description: The collection covers the writing career and anti-Vietnam War activism of author and former Stanford student David V. Harris, spanning from the 1950s through the 2020s. The majority of the collection is made up of Harris' research files and notes from his non-fiction books.

items.title: Douglas Menuez professional photography portfolios, 1990-2005
items.description: Doug Menuez began freelancing as a photographer in the 1980s. Professional portfolios and collections by photographer Douglas Menuez from the 1990s and early 2000s. The portfolios include everyday photographs, curated collections, commission and advertising work, and photos from Silicon Valley in the 1980s and 1990s.

items.title: Fearless genius : the digital revolution in Silicon Valley, 1985-2000 / photographs by Doug Menuez
items.description: Doug Menuez spent over fifteen years documenting the leading innovators of the digital revolution in Silicon Valley. Limited edition box set of twenty silver gelatin prints signed by the photographer from the project "Fearless Genius: The Digital Revolution in Silicon Valley 1985-2000."

items.title: Floricanto at Stanford University, Chicano/Latino poetry and music [videorecording]
Jeannie Barroga papers, circa 1966-2010
items.description: Jeannie Barroga (b. 1949) is a playwright, teacher, director and video producer. Barroga's papers consist primarily of multiple drafts of her plays, production binders, notes and journals, administrative files (involving funding, venues, auditions, and other matters), audiovisual material, publicity such as posters and programs, photographs, personal writing and ephemera, and research files.

items.title: Jonathan Berger Collection
items.description: Berger is the Denning Family Provostial Professor in Music at Stanford University, where he teaches composition, music theory, and cognition at the Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics (CCRMA). Audio, video, score, libretto and performance materials for Jonathan Berger's compositions.

items.title: Kitrick "Kit" Galloway and Sherrie Rabinowitz papers, 1971-1993
items.description: Collection consists of computer media, audiovisual media, thermal prints and other materials related to Kitrick "Kit" Galloway. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Lola de la Riva papers
items.description: Lola de la Riva (born 1938 in Stockton, California) is a Chicana activist and artist. Includes documents, correspondence, research material, artworks, books and other publications, audio cassettes, and other materials.

items.title: Lynn Hershman-Leeson papers, 1976-2004
items.description: Lynn Hershman Leeson (1941-) is an American new media artist and filmmaker. Her collection of archival papers, audiovisual media, publications, artifacts, photographs, and letters document Hershman Leeson's artworks and projects created since the 1970s.

items.title: Poems : typescript collections, 1998 and nd.
items.description: Photocopied collections, one titled "Drive," 1998 (copy #8 of 10 created) with an inscription from the author, 166 p; and the other titled "From the cables of genocide: poems on love and hunger," with author's signature, nd, 72 leaves, a prepublication photocopy typescript including three poems not present in the final published book.
items.era_note: [About half of this material, the typescript collection titled Drive, dates from 1998.]

items.title: Rich Gold papers, 1978-2005
items.description: Rich Gold (1950-2003) was a digital artist, inventor, cartoonist, composer, lecturer and inter-disciplinary researcher. Rich Gold papers include notebooks (114), artwork, correspondence, and manuscript for The Plenitude, which was posthumously published in 2008.

items.title: Robert McDowell papers, circa 1970s-1990s
items.description: Collection includes manuscripts, drafts, journals and diaries, correspondence, and ephemera. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Senses Places hybrid reality collection, 2002-2014
items.description: The collection consists of digital objects related to Senses Places including websites, images, videos, chats, and scholarly articles. Senses Places is a somatics-technological dance collaboration project that creates mixed-reality performance and participatory environments for audiences in physical-world locations and the Second Life virtual reality environment created by Linden Labs.

items.title: William [Bill] Riley Marken papers, 1937-2010s
items.description: Collection consists of manuscript, printed, and photographic materials created and collected by Marken, ca. 1960s-2000s. Materials focus on a variety of writing projects, including Marken's 2012 Stanford MLA thesis—California Tomorrow, 1961-1983: An Enduring Environmental Legacy; misc. writing projects involving food in California, the history and legacy of Sunset Magazine; mid-century modern architecture; gardening.
items.era_note: [About three quarters of this collection, writing projects and research files from the 1990s to the 2010s including a 2012 thesis, dates from this period.]

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Design and architecture

items.title: Building 1; history and changes of Varian's Building 1, Palo Alto, 1993
items.description: Text, site plans, architectural drawings, additions, master plan, and drawings.

items.title: Building plans for the Apple R&D Campus, Cupertino, California, September 27, 1991
items.description: Consists of 1 volume of blueline prints, bound with a 3 screw blueprint binding strip. The strip is labelled: Apple R&D Campus, 10700 N. DeAnza Blvd., Cupertino, Ca : a joint venture of Apple Computer, Inc., and Sobrato Development Companies 900.

items.title: Carnegie building collection, 1998-2001
items.description: Includes architectural designs and blueprints, photographs, programmatic requirements, press release, and correspondence about whether the foothills site was appropriate for building.

items.title: Cecil H. Green Library West earthquake repair : reports, 1990-1991
items.description: The west wing of the Cecil H. Green Library comprises the original Stanford University Library designed by architects Bakewell and Brown and completed in 1919. It sustained considerable damage during the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake. Collection consists of two feasibility study reports, 1990 and 1991, by The Architects collaborative Inc., which include architectural drawings and photographic illustrations; and a 1991 report on the site exploration and testing work prepared by Forell/Elsesser Engineers, Inc.

items.title: Hanna House board of governors meeting minutes, 1989-1998
items.description: In 1937, the distinguished architect Frank Lloyd Wright finalized the design of a residence for the Hanna family atop a hill overlooking Stanford University. The materials consist of meeting minutes of the Hanna House board of governors documenting renovations.

items.title: Hanna House reconstruction collection, 1998
items.description: Hanna House, formerly the home of Paul and Jean Hanna on the Stanford University campus, was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, using a hexagonal grid system. This collection contains documents pertaining to the reconstruction of Hanna House following the 1989 earthquake.

items.title: Michael J. Willis & Associates Building 2-500 Annex Seismic Strengthening project profile
items.description: One page of text, three photographs, and two floor plans on the seismic repair and renovations on building 02-500, used by the Mechanical Engineering Department.

items.title: Stanford University, University Architect / Campus Planning and Design, photographs
items.description: Photographs produced by the Planning Office or by related offices prior to the inception of the Planning Office (such as Buildings and Grounds), as well as photographs from other sources that were acquired by the Planning Office. Of note are campus aerials, 1951-1970; a series of negatives with matching prints of academic buildings, largely from the late 1930s; a series of negatives with matching prints of the construction of Frost Amphitheater, 1936-37, Cubberley School of Education, and of the San Juan Hill reservoir, 1941; negatives from the construction of Hoover Tower; color images of the construction of the Science and Engineering Quad, 1997-98; and negatives of drawings, plans, and other documents for presentations at Board of Trustees Meetings, 1960s-70s.

items.title: Stanford University, University Architect / Campus Planning and Design, records, 1945-2018
items.description: The Planning Office was officially organized in 1945 under the directorship of Eldridge T. Spencer. In addition to overseeing the architectural aspects of the campus, the office was also responsible for overseeing land use and traffic circulation. The records of the Planning Office date back to its orgins in 1945 and include correspondence, memoranda, minutes, reports, studies, surveys, maps, and plans.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Film, radio and television

items.title: Dorothy Fadiman/Concentric Media papers, 1955-2018
items.description: Dorothy Fadiman is the founder of Concentric Media, and has been producing films for 40 years. The collection consists of materials related to the career of filmmaker, producer, author and teacher Dorothy Fadiman from 1976-2018. Papers document publicity, interviews, production, fundraising, reception of films, festival showings, and work with television, such as PBS.

items.title: Peter Conn papers, circa early 1970s-1996
items.description: Peter Conn is a director and producer known for his advances in 3D computer-generated animation, graphics, and motion capture technology, primarily through his production company Homer & Associates. The bulk of the Peter Conn papers pertains to music videos and other Homer & Associates projects, such as commercials, short films, and contributions to feature films.
items.era_note: [About a quarter of these papers, the company's music videos, commercials and film effects from 1990 until it closed in 1996, concern this period.]

items.title: UNAFF (United Nations Association Film Festival) ephemera, 1998-2014
items.description: The materials consist of posters, programs, bookmarks and promotional calendars advertising the annual United Nations Association Film Festival, as well as California newspapers containing information or articles about the film festival, including Palo Alto Weekly, Metro, Daily Post, and the Stanford Daily.

items.title: United Nations Association Film Festival materials, 2012-2019
items.description: Posters, programs, ephemera.

sectors.name: Arts and culture — Press, journalism and broadcasting

items.title: David Bohrman archive of innovation in media & journalism, circa 1960s-2014
items.description: Materials include Bohrman's papers as well as ephemera, and two servers of digital files, and additional digital files received via electronic transfer.
items.era_note: [Most of this archive, including two servers of digital files, dates from 1990 to 2014 and concerns this period.]

items.title: Kate Coleman papers, circa 1960s-1990s
items.description: Collection consists of print, manuscript, photographs and some audiovisual materials relating to the journalism career of Kate Coleman.

items.title: Reese Erlich papers, circa 1931-2015
items.description: Reese Erlich (1947-2021) was an author and freelance journalist living and working in the Bay Area for much of his career. Files, photographs, and recordings pertaining to Bay Area journalist Reese Erlich's career reporting on a variety of topics including local stories and US foreign policy from the late 1960s through 2010s.

sectors.name: Arts and culture

items.title: A Century of Western Living, 1898-1998 : centennial keepsakes, 1998
items.description: Exhibit catalog, copy of the original May, 1898 issue, pin, and ephemera. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: A Century of Western Living, 1898-1998 : poster for centennial exhibit, 1998
Avenue; Second Life community convention special, 2009 August
items.description: AVENUE was the appointed Official Media Partner for Second Life Community Convention 2009 where the first fashion and lifestyle magazine out of SL was printed in real life. It is a leading fashion and lifestyle publication that is dedicated to fashion, lifestyle, business, entertainment and the arts in Second Life.

items.title: Bay Area Regional Planner board game, 2015
items.description: A board game: "Solve the housing crisis in an interactive city planning simulation for 2-12 people."

items.title: Fidelity Sound Recordings Collection
items.description: This collection consists of commercially-released audio recordings created by the independent record company Fidelity Sound Recordings (FSR) based in Redwood City, California. The predominant musical genre featured is marching band music performed by university bands, bands affiliated with the Salvation Army, and miscellaneous ensembles in the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, and elsewhere.

items.title: Jalonen theater & music program collection
items.description: The John W. Jalonen program collection is comprised of various playbill and performance programs mostly from local and regional production companies around the San Francisco Bay Area presented between the 1940s and 2000s.

items.title: Moxon Chappel : printing ephemera, 1993-2015
items.description: Ephemera from various presses belonging to the Companions of the Moxon Chappel. The Companions of the Moxon Chappel is a group of private printers, active in the San Francisco Bay Area.

items.title: Roman palimpsest, ca. 170
items.description: A palimpsest of fine parchment depicting a plan of a Roman fort in North Africa. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Stanford University Press archival book copies, 1900-2013
items.description: The Stanford University Press was established as an independent printing operation at Stanford University in 1892. It publishes scholarly monographs, textbooks, and professional reference works. The collection consists of archival copies of books published by Stanford University Press.

items.title: Sunset Magazine : video, 18 Oct. 1998
items.description: Includes interviews of Mel and Bill Lane. Discusses the role of Sunset Magazine over the last one hundred years.

items.title: Sunset Magazine records, 1931-1998
items.description: The records of Sunset Magazine primarily consist of over 100,000 photographs as published in the magazine from 1948-1969 and 1977-1998. Given Sunset's focus as the "Magazine of Western Living," however, one may expect to find photographs of gardening and landscaping, architecture and home improvement, cooking and food, entertaining, travel, nature, and recreation.

items.title: Teatro Visión collection of scripts, circa 1986-2015
items.description: The collection consists of more than 500 scripts received, commissioned, developed, and/or produced by Teatro Visión, a Chicanx theater company located in San Jose, California. The scripts consist of play adaptations of classic novels and original plays written by Latinx playwrights, including Rudolfo Anaya, Silvia Gonzalez, Oliver Mayer, and Luis Valdez.

items.title: William R. Hewlett library
items.description: These CD-ROMs contain a database for William R. Hewlett's personal library (1997); the PC version also contains childhood photographs of Hewlett, scanned on the ocassion of his 85th birthday (1998). [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Society and community — Activism and advocacy

items.title: American Civil Liberties Union of Northern California records, 1900-2000 bulk 1934-2000
items.description: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) is a non-profit organization committed to the defense, preservation, and extension of civil liberties in the United States. Comprising correspondence, minutes, policy statements, reports, court transcripts, attorney notes, scrapbooks, newspaper clippings, pamphlets, and other printed material created or collected by the ACLU-NC, these records document the establishment and activities of the northern California branch and its wide-ranging efforts to protect and extend individual liberties in California.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive -- Guerrero Azteca Peregrinación Por la Paz, Tijuana to San Francisco, 2006
items.description: The Guerrero Azteca Peace Project promotes peace, provides help to military families who have lost a loved one, and provides disadvantaged youths with scholarships and alternatives to military service. In March 2006, Guerrero Azteca embarked on a Peregrinación Por la Paz (March for Peace) beginning in Tijuana, Mexico and ending in San Francisco, California. Because of his prior work with the Latino community and draft resistance movement, Bob Fitch was invited to document the march.

items.title: Bob Fitch photography archive, 1965-2013
items.description: The Bob Fitch Photography Archive consists of the photographic work of activist and photojournalist Bob Fitch, documenting the civil rights movement, the farm worker movement, the peace movement, other social justice movements and issues, cultural change, religion, as well as his professional and personal life.

items.title: Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility (CPSR) records, 1980-2004
items.description: Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility (CPSR) was an organization promoting the responsible use of computer technology. It educated policymakers and the public on a wide range of issues including privacy, design, and the role of computers in defense. Records of the policy group Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility (CPSR), consisting of correspondence, memoranda, newsletters, board minutes, publications, media, and other material.

items.title: Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility, records, 1980-2007
items.description: In 1982, the group created the Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility (CPSR) to raise awareness of the potential dangers of information and communications technology on integral governmental computer systems, especially in the computerization of war and nuclear proliferation. This collections contains the administrative materials of the Computer Professionals for Social Responsibility, including meeting minutes, project proposals, conference materials, and correspondence.

items.title: David Veniot materials relating to Earth Day International, 1992
items.description: Veniot served as a Director and Officer of Earth Day International. Collection containing printed materials, correspondence, videotapes (2) and photographs relating to Earth Day International, 1992, ca. 1991-1993.

items.title: Earth Day 1990 collection, 1990-1991
items.description: Materials dealing with the planning, promotion and reception of Earth Day 1990, an international event, coordinated from Stanford, California. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Felicia Smith recordings relating to the Black Lives Matter movement, 2020
items.description: Includes two video recordings created by Felicia Smith: a video recorded for Juneteenth 2020 originally made available via YouTube titled: "Juneteenth Feel Me Updated," and a video of a Black Lives Matter protest held in June 2020 at Galvez St. and El Camino Real, in Palo Alto, California, just outside of Stanford University.

items.title: Interviews with five striking Chicana/o students after three days into hunger strike [videorecording] : May 6, 1994
items.description: Four Stanford Chicana and one Chicano students discuss the reasons behind their hunger strike and the emotions involved.

items.title: Jack Owicki photographs of the Black Lives Matter movement at Stanford University
items.description: Jack Owicki is the founder of Pro Bono Photo, which connects social and environmental justice organizations with photographers and videographers who wish to donate their expertise. Includes photographs of the Black Lives Matter memorial installation on the Oval by the entrance to Stanford University, created July 10, 2020 by the student-led group Abolish Stanford.

items.title: John W. Gardner papers, 1912-2004
items.description: Gardner served as the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare under President Lyndon Johnson from 1965-1968. He founded the citizen's advocacy group Common Cause and was the chairman of the Commission on White House Fellowships. Collection includes speeches and writings by, as well as articles about Gardner; correspondence, awards and honors, photographs, audiovisual material, and files from many of Gardner's organizations including Common Cause, the White House Fellows, the Haas Center for Public Service, and the John W. Gardner Center.

items.title: Maurice "Mo" Jourdane, Esq., papers, 1966-2018
items.description: Maurice Jourane is a civil rights lawyer, judge, and author. He worked with the California Rural Legal Assistance, United Farm Workers, and other organizations to improve civil rights for agricultural laborers in California. This collection consists of manuscripts, notes, research materials, newspaper clippings, legal correspondence and cases, photographs and other materials documenting the life of Maurice "Mo" Jourdane.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records, 1967-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. Included in the collection are more than 2000 linear feet of litigation case files focusing on such issues as employment discrimination, education rights, reproductive rights, voting rights, and other related civil rights issues.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 1, Board of Directors records, 1967-1993
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. MALDEF's Board of Directors is the organization's governing body; the directors assist the lead staff in program planning, fundraising, and administrative decisions.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 5, Legal Programs Department, 1968-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. This record group includes the files generated and collected by Rosen and Baller from 1972 until 1983, as they directed and developed MALDEF's litigation.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 6.5, Leadership Programs, 1979-1994
items.description: Ralph Hurtado's files, chronological files, and program files. The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. The Leadership Development and Advocacy Program was also a spin-off of CEAP, and was created in 1980 to prepare a pool of Chicanos for appointments to commissions and boards by increasing their sophistication about the political process in their communities.

items.title: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF) records. Record Group 9, Regional and Program Offices, 1967-2000
items.description: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund records contain the administrative records, litigation files, and special program files of one of the most influential and effective civil rights organizations focusing on defining and protecting the civil rights of Mexican Americans throughout the United States. In the early years, the offices concentrated on local legal work, and were funded by the initial Ford grant.

items.title: Pacific Studies Center records, circa 1969-2017
items.description: Materials from the Pacific Studies Center on subject matter such as Silicon Valley companies, the electronics and communications industries, environmental issues and records from company president Lenny Siegel's participation in committees on these issues, labor issues, U.S. military and weaponry, government reports, and regional country files. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Racism Lives Here Too Movement records, 2018
items.description: Includes 3 photographs depicting Stanford Law School students with a banner stating "Racism Lives Here Too," as well as 23 posters bearing quotes attributed to Stanford students and professors. The banner and posters were hung at Stanford Law School in February 2018 by students associated with the Racism Lives Here Too Movement.

items.title: Robert C. Aldridge papers, circa 1970s-1990s
items.description: Collection consists of collected writings, research materials, correspondence, printed material, photographs and printed ephemera relating to the life and career of Robert C. [Creston] Aldridge (1926-2022) with a particular focus on his activities as an anti-nuclear and peace activist and an advisor/consultant/sponsor in many groups and organizations including Ground Zero Center for Nonviolent Action, Nuclear Age Peace Foundation, British-American Security Information Council, Institute for Law and Peace, Fellowship of Reconciliation, the Pacific Life Community, Veterans for Peace and others.

items.title: Salvador Enrique Alvarez personal archive, 1950s-2015
items.description: Materials consist of Salvador E. Alvarez's papers related to his political activism and community involvement, including the United Farm Workers, the Hispanic Catholics of America, and the founding of the School of Social Work at San Jose State.
items.era_note: [The archive runs to 2015, and about a quarter of it, his later papers and recordings, concerns this period.]

items.title: Stanford Open Space Alliance records
