items.description: Stanford Open Space Alliance is a network of students, faculty, staff, alumni, and neighbors concerned about development in the Stanford University foothills Letters sent to members, 1999-2004, copy of the SUMMARY AND EXPLANATION of Stanford University's general use permit application, 1999, two articles, 2000, and several documents printed from their website.

items.title: Stanford Physicians for Social Responsibility records, circa 1981-2005
items.description: The Stanford chapter of Physicians for Social Responsibility (PSR) was established in 1981 as a regional extension of the national organization, which was founded in 1961. The bulk of the records focuses on the organization's efforts during the 1980s and early 1990s to advocate for nuclear test bans, the reduction and elimination of nuclear weapons, and fostering positive relations between the United States and the Soviet Union.

items.title: Stanford University, Black Lives Matter website collection
The CPSR newsletter
items.era_note: [Somewhat more than half of this newsletter run, published from 1983 until it ceased in 1999, dates from this period.]

items.title: The Movement Oral History Project interviews
items.description: The collection contains around thirty interviews with former Stanford students on the topic of activism during the 1960s and 1970s on the Stanford campus, with a specific focus on the April 3rd Movememnt and the occupation of the Applied Electronics Laboratory.

items.title: Women's March 2018, San Jose, California, ephemera, January 20, 2018
items.description: Materials include pamphlets, flyers, brochures, and other documents gathered from the Call to Action Alley providing information for marginalized communities, as well as a CD.

sectors.name: Society and community — Local and California history

items.title: Albert M. Camarillo collection of Juana Briones material, 2004-2014
items.description: Collection consists of Juana Briones Heritage Foundation materials, California Historical Society exhibit materials, 2 VHS, 1 dvd, 1 digital video cassette, write-ups, flyers, pamphlets, presentation notes, correspondence, lists of media coverage, exhibition planning materials, grant applications, planning meeting notes, list of trustees, spreadsheet of borrowed objects for the exhibition, budgets, etc.

items.title: California biography collection
items.description: Consists of ephemeral items relating to people widely known and relatively unknown in California. Contains mostly newspaper obituaries, but also includes: handwritten biographical documents, invitations, wedding announcements, family reunion newsletters, genealogy forms, family trees, memorials, political speeches, campaign material, correspondence, and newspaper and magazine clippings.

sectors.name: Society and community — Medicine and public health

items.title: Halsted Holman papers, circa 1931-2015
items.description: Most files involve Health care reform, Chronic disease self-care programs, the Robert Wood Johnson Clinical Scholars Program, the Midpeninsula Health Service, and Holman's social and political activism. There is a particular emphasis on the Stanford Peace Movement and Anti-War materials.

items.title: Jay Haley papers, 1957-2007
items.description: He was a pioneer in family therapy, and his work traces its birth and development during half a century. The Jay Haley collection documents Haley's career through correspondence, manuscripts, typescripts, and media materials.

items.title: Kenneth D. Brock journals, 1949-2018
items.description: Brock was hired in 1984 by the State of California, Department of Health Services, to work as a consultant with the Centers for Disease Control to establish a registry of AIDS cases in California. Journals including some correspondence and photographs.

items.title: Loren R. Mosher papers, 1933-2004
items.description: Biographical material, correspondence, articles and papers, reports, interviews, photographs, and audiovisual material relating to Loren R. Mosher, a clinician specializing in the treatment of schizophrenia without drugs.

items.title: Mental Research Institute (MRI) records
items.description: The Mental Research Institute (MRI) is a small, independent, multi-disciplinary, non-profit corporation founded in Palo Alto, California, and is one of the pioneering institutions of brief and family therapy methodology. The material described in this finding aid consists of therapy sessions, notes, drafts, research proposals, clinical practice files, grant files, conference proceedings, publications, audiovisual material, born-digital material, and other material related to the operation of MRI.

items.title: Norman Shumway Project videorecordings and papers, circa 1960-1996 (inclusive), 1985-1996 (bulk)
items.description: Noted heart transplant pioneer, Shumway has been surgeon and professor at the Stanford University School of Medicine since 1958. Videorecordings (beta source tapes with some VHS window dubs) that were created and/or compiled to be used for a film on Norman E. Shumway; included are interviews, medical procedures, television appearances, films, and other sources.

items.title: SARS-CoV2 seroprevalence in selected Californian counties
items.description: CA-FACTS (The Californians Fighting Against Coronavirus Together Study) is a collaboration between Stanford University and local health departments to assess the SARS-CoV2 seroprevalence in Placer, Santa Clara and Solano counties.

items.title: STOP AIDS Project records, 1985-2011
items.description: Founded in 1984 (non-profit status attained, 1985), the STOP AIDS Project is a community-based organization dedicated to the prevention of HIV transmission among gay, bisexual and transgender men in San Francisco. The STOP AIDS Project records are comprised of behavioral risk assessment surveys; social marketing campaign materials, including HIV/AIDS prevention posters and flyers; community outreach and workshop materials; volunteer training materials; correspondence; grant proposals; fund development materials; administrative records; photographs; audio and video recordings; and computer files.

items.title: William C. Dement papers, circa 1960s-1990s
items.description: William C. Dement is Professor Emeritus in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Stanford. He founded the Sleep Research Center at Stanford and co-founded the Sleep Research Society. Collection mainly consists of correspondence, administrative records from various sleep research organizations he was involved in, and sleep studies and research.

sectors.name: Society and community — Memoirs and family papers

items.title: Gschwind / Swent, Langan, Waterman, Mendenhall, and Herz Family papers
items.description: Personal papers of Langan and Eleanor Swent and related families, as well as material on mining and travel. Collection contains correspondence, photographs, oral histories, memoirs & journals, mining company reports & documents, World War II memorabilia, travel souvenirs and other material.

items.title: Reflection and Possibilities, 2018
items.description: Snapshot of Stanford, Palo Alto, and Silicon Valley from 2012-2016. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Society and community — Philanthropy and foundations

items.title: Anne Firth Murray papers, 1970-2018
items.description: For the past twenty-five years, she has worked in the field of philanthropy, serving as a consultant to many foundations. She is the Founding President of The Global Fund for Women, which provides funds internationally to seed, strengthen, and link groups committed to women's well being. Papers include Murray's Global Fund for Women and Hewlett Foundation files; teaching files; professional files; and subject files.

items.title: David and Lucile Packard: A lifetime of Stanford philanthropy
items.description: Dave and Lucile Packard's philanthropic activities have had a major impact on Stanford University through grants provided through the the David and Lucile Packard Foundation.

items.title: Global Fund for Women records, 1964-2014
items.description: The Global Fund for Women was founded in Palo Alto, Calif. in 1987 by Anne Firth Murray, Frances Kissling and Laura Lederer. Its mission is to support women's rights by providing grant funds to women's organizations throughout the world. The records consist of files from Anne Firth Murray's tenure as Founding President of the Global Fund for Women (1987-1996). Included are chronological files from Firth and other administrators, correspondence, clippings and articles, press releases and other promotional materials, and meeting and event files.

items.title: William Hewlett Memorial Service [videorecording]
items.description: Service was held in Stanford University's Memorial Church on January 20, 2001; includes tributes by Herant Katchadourian, Maggie Lacey Schneider, Arjay Miller, David W. Packard, and Walter B. Hewlett. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: William Hewlett papers, 1907-2018 (bulk 1960-2001)
items.description: William Hewlett was the co-founder of Hewlett-Packard, one of the most successful technology start-up companies in the history of Silicon Valley. Following the tremendous success of Hewlett-Packard, he became well known for his philanthropy, donating millions of dollars from his fortune to support various causes. The William Hewlett papers consists of correspondence, photographs, financial records, reports, minutes, calendars, hardware, electronic files, videotapes, newspaper clippings, publications, and other materials.

sectors.name: Society and community — Race, ethnicity and immigration

items.title: A3C Oral Histories
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Black Alumni Stories and Oral Histories
items.description: Records pertaining to the Stanford National Black Alumni Association, including video from events and oral history interviews with alumni.

items.title: Him Mark Lai papers, circa 1907-2010
items.description: Him Mark Lai was a writer, historian, and archivist of Chinese America. This collection primarily consists of his own family history, particularly that of the Mark/Mai clan, and his parents' immigration to California.

items.title: Jewish life in the San Francisco Bay Area : ephemera from Eve Sutton, 1980-2004
items.description: Primarily material from Palo Alto and Stanford University, including Congregation Kol Emeth, Stanford Hillel, Resource magazine, and the Bureau of Jewish Education.

items.title: Jewish life in the San Francisco Bay Area, 1981-2010
items.description: The collection documents non-traditional Jewish life in the Bay Area, especially newsletters and announcements from various organizations. There are also liturgical creations around life-cycle events. Material collected by Roger S. Kohn and Zachary M. Baker, both Stanford University Library curators, from local synagogues, individuals, organizations, and businesses.

items.title: Ken and Caretha Coleman archive of Black histories in Silicon Valley, circa 2020s
items.description: Collection includes oral histories of Harry Bremond, Caretha Coleman, Al Cotton, Kathy Cotton, Peggy Forbes, Maynard Holliday, Pamela Isom, Max Pearl, Marc Ramsey. Additional material related to African Americans in Silicon Valley forthcoming.

items.title: No Boundaries - The Digital Nomads of Estonia, 1947-1953
items.description: Oral history interviews with Estonians whose lives have been changed by the intersection of the country's digital revolution and its rejoining of the free world; ranging from key people involved with initiating and shaping the policies that made the digital revolution possible, to those who grew up with, and were able to make full use of, the new possibilities to learn, create and live in the new, interconnected world, focusing on Estonians who have migrated to California's Silicon Valley.

items.title: Shau Wing Chan papers, 1911-1994
items.description: He joined the Stanford faculty in 1938 and retired in 1972. He was instrumental in founding what is now the Department of Asian Languages, serving as its executive head from 1958-1962. Notebooks, exams, reading notes, and a draft of his thesis from his graduate studies, 1930-1933; professional and personal correspondence, 1938-1949, including letters pertaining to his immigration status; correspondence, memoranda, and reports pertaining to Stanford administrative and departmental matters, 1935-1982; and family papers, 1911-1994.

items.title: The Baltic video archive : Baltic video testimonies at Stanford Libraries
items.description: The Baltic Video Archive of Stanford Libraries consists of four oral history collections, each of which tells the story of the Baltic countries through video testimonies of the Baltic peoples. The archive also includes stories told by the more recent generation, the so-called “digital nomads,” or the “Estonian mafia,” who have migrated to and established enterprises in California's Silicon Valley.

sectors.name: Society and community — Religion, clubs and societies

items.title: 20th anniversary Simcha dinner : commemorative publication, 1996
items.description: Includes notes about the history of the group and current activities. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Chadesh yamenu; renew our days, a machzor for Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, ca. 1996
Current Events Club records, 1908-2023
items.description: Founded in 1905, the Current Events Club was a social group that informally discussed current events. At its inception, the club members were young women and wives of Stanford faculty. These materials contain club meeting minutes, organizational records, reports related to contemporary current events, and member biographical files.

items.title: Stanford Club of Palo Alto records, 1946-2000 (inclusive)
items.description: The Stanford Club of Palo Alto was founded in 1907 to organize and sponsor dances and musical performances. The materials consist of organizational records, event flyers, and photographs.

items.title: Stanford University Medical Center Auxiliary, 1920-2015
items.description: This collection includes materials from the Stanford University Medical Center Auxiliary from its beginning in 1959 as the Palo Alto Hospital Auxiliary to its dissolution in 2015.

items.title: Woodside-Atherton Garden Club records, circa 1929-2013
items.description: The club organizes civic and educational projects, and hosts and participates in local and national flower shows. Records consist primarily of meeting minutes, annual reports, news clippings, event programs, photograph albums and scrapbooks, and miscellaneous records of activities of the club from its inception forward.

sectors.name: Society and community — Women, gender and sexuality

items.title: Elizabeth Lyman papers, 1958-2009 (inclusive)
items.description: Elizabeth "Jing" Lyman (1925-2013) was communitiy activist who organized and sustained many foundations and coalitions, including Women and Foundations/Corporate Philanthropy, HUB, and the Women's Resource Center, among many others. Primarily files relating to Jing Lyman's activities in community affairs, the Women's Resource Center, the Women and Foundations/Corporate Philanthropy, HUB, and with various foundations and executive boards. Jing Lyman played an instrumental role in creating what is now the Michelle R. Clayman Institute for Gender Research at Stanford.

items.title: Lesbian, Gay and Bisexual Awareness Program records, 1988-2000 (inclusive), 1997-2000 (bulk)
items.description: The Lesbian, Gay and Bisexual Awareness Program, formed in 1985, worked to end intolerance and stereotypes of lesbian, gay and bisexual persons. Collection consists largely of the evaluation forms completed by students at Bay Area high schools and colleges following a presentation; other records include training manuals, speakers' resources, and clippings.

items.title: Oral histories of young lesbian, bisexual, transgender and intersexed Jewish women of the San Francisco Bay Area, 1996
YWCA of the Mid-Peninsula records, circa 1948-2013
items.description: The YWCA of the Mid-Peninsula opened in 1948 as a recreation center for business women. It expanded to provide recreational and social services for women that met the organization's mission of "empowering women and eliminating racism." This collection documents the organization's history, its administrative structure and daily operations, major programming and public policy efforts, and ties to the Stanford and national YWCA.

sectors.name: Society and community

items.title: Herman Gallegos papers, 1944-2013
items.description: Herman Gallegos has been an activist and community organizer with a focus on Latino rights and support, as well as a management consultant, director, and trustee on many corporate boards and nonprofits. This collection contains organizational files, grant proposals, meeting dockets, correspondence, reports, newsletters, research and subject files, and notes from Herman Gallegos's corporate, non-profit, philanthropic and advocacy work.

items.title: Hidden Silicon Valley: Oral histories from the margins of high-tech, 2025
items.description: [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Armed forces and military history

items.title: The Battle of 73 Easting, Gulf War : simulation project papers, 1991-1993
items.description: Papers concerning the simulation of a tank battle in the 1991 Gulf War. The simulation of this tank-on-tank engagement from the 1991 war against Iraq was run by the Institute for Defense Analyses and DARPA (the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency). The product was a learning tool for current and future soldier training, as well as historical analysis.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Arms control, science and technology policy

items.title: "Cyberspace" [videorecording]
items.description: Tapes of the program held in Kresge Auditorium on Sept. 18, 2002, on the national cybersecurity draft plan [The National Strategy to Secure Cyberspace]; speakers included Robert Mueller, Richard Clarke, Jennifer Granick, and Cedric Bennett.

items.title: Computers, Freedom, and Privacy conference papers, Judi Clark collection, 1991-1997
items.description: Judi Clark was one of the organizers of the annual conference of Computers, Freedom, and Privacy (CFP), which started in 1991. Conference presentation topics included freedom of speech protections, security of personal data stored by private companies, government regulation and technology, and cultivating civility on Internet bulletin boards. The collection includes published conference proceedings in print, audio, and video formats for the first three conferences held during the 1990s; and supplemental conference materials including position papers submitted by speakers and presentations given by companies on developing strategies for an Internet presence.

items.title: John Young papers and Cryptome archive, circa 1980-2025
Michael M. May papers
items.description: Michael May is Professor Emeritus (Research) in the Stanford University School of Engineering and a senior fellow with the Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies at Stanford University. The primary topics include May's work for CISAC (Committee on International Security and Arms Control) - which includes research on nuclear proliferation, management of plutonium, and international relations - as well as logistical planning to do with May's travels, conferences, and papers.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Foreign affairs and diplomacy

items.title: Richard A. Stepp papers, 1937-1995
items.description: The papers of Richard A. Stepp pertain largely to the time he spent in Burma as an advisor on technical services for small industries, 1958-59. Included are correspondence, notebooks, reports, memos, Burmese government documents (in English), other publications, and photographs, 1954-59.

items.title: Robert Slobodan Djurdjevic papers, 1978-1997
items.description: Serbian-American computer industry analyst; president, Annex Research; founder, Truth in Media, 1992. Travel reports, correspondence, bulletins, writings, press releases, clippings, other printed matter, video tapes, and memorabilia, relating to political conditions in Yugoslavia, the breakup of Yugoslavia, the civil war in Bosnia, reportage of Yugoslav news in the American media, American foreign policy in Yugoslavia, and the computer industry.

items.title: Why Estonia : the 30-year journey from the USSR to e-Estonia

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Government and public administration

items.title: Bay Area governments [electronic resource].
items.description: This collection focuses on collecting the Web sites and government documents of the local and regional governments geographically centered around the San Francisco bay area.

items.title: City of Mountain View, California comprehensive annual financial report for the fiscal year ended June 30 ...
Oral history interviews on e-Estonia, 2024
items.description: The interviews cover the development, challenges, and opportunities of digital governance in Estonia. This collection includes five oral histories with Toomas Hendrik Ilves, Luukas Ilves, Sten Tamkivi, Kersti Kaljulaid, and Anna-Maria Osula.

items.title: Santa Clara County Blue Ribbon Commission on Improving Custody Operations collection, 2006-2020
items.description: This collection documents the Blue Ribbon Commission on Improving Custody Operations, Santa Clara County, 2015. The Blue Ribbon Commission was appointed in 2015 by the Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors to investigate and evaluate the county jails in the aftermath of the murder of Michael Tyree, a mentally ill inmate. The documents consist of reports, meeting minutes, agendas, correspondence and other materials.

items.title: The History of E-Estonia: Oral History Interviews with Estonian Experts on the Development of Estonia's Digital Society, 1991-2021
items.description: This collection of interviews with 60 Estonian experts, researchers, and officials documents the Estonian experience in developing digital society and e-governance across various platforms.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Law and legal practice

items.title: California Rural Legal Assistance records, 1966-2014
items.description: The records of the California Rural Legal Assistance, Inc. (CRLA) document CRLA's ongoing work to provide legal aid to farmworkers and the rural poor in California. Included in the collection are administrative records, litigation files, and special program and subject files.

items.title: Joaquin Avila oral history interview materials, 2012
items.description: The materials consist of the recorded oral history itself on a thumb drive, DVDs, Joaquin Avila's CV, articles, information on Avila's legal cases, and over eighty pages of transcribed interviews, as well as interviewer Ignacio Ornelas Rodriguez's notes and planning documents. This oral history is the only avaiable full length interview with Joaquin Avila.

items.title: John H. Barton papers, 1980-2000
items.description: John H. Barton (1936-2009) was on the faculty of Stanford Law School for 40 years. This collection mainly consists of articles, notes, and correspondence relating to Barton's work in International Law and intellectual property rights.

items.title: Legal issues in cyberspace : videorecordings, 1997
items.description: Ten programs from the telecourse Legal Issues in Cyberspace taught by Prof. Margaret Jane Radin in the fall of 1997. Subjects include encryption, copyright, business models, payment systems, trademark issues, and governance.

sectors.name: Government, law and politics — Politics and elections

items.title: Byron Sher papers, circa 1950-2004
items.description: Byron Sher was a member of the California state senate, 1996-2004; a member of the California state assembly, 1980-1996; a Palo Alto city council member, 1965-1967 and 1973-1980. The Byron Sher papers consists of office and bill files, public policy calendars and artifacts, faculty papers, district and campaign files, personal papers and effects, incoming and outgoing correspondence, photographs, audio cassettes and video tapes.

items.title: California Stem Cell Initiative collection, 2003-2020
items.description: Collection consists of files from two external hard drives and one file transfer, as well as posters, banners, and publicity materials related to the California Stem Cell Initiative. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Dianne Feinstein Senatorial papers, 1992-2023
items.description: The collection consists of the Senatorial papers of Dianne Feinstein.

items.title: San Mateo and Santa Clara 2018 Midterm Election
Stanford Internet Observatory Oral History collection
items.description: The interviews produced as part of the Stanford Internet Observatory's 2020 Elections Oral History Project: https://cyber.fsi.stanford.edu/2020-elections-oral-history-project. This collection includes sixteen interviews with state and federal officials who served during the 2020 U.S. elections.

sectors.name: Ideas and intellectual history — Counterculture

items.title: Fred Turner papers, 1968-2019
items.description: Fred Turner is an Associate Professor in the Department of Communication at Stanford University and Director of Stanford's Program in Science, Technology, and Society. Files consist primarily of research material, manuscripts, and chapter drafts related to Turner's book, From Counterculture to Cyberculture: Stewart Brand, the Whole Earth Network, and the Rise of Digital Utopianism.

items.title: Howard Rheingold papers, 1976-2013
items.description: Howard Rheingold (b.1947) is an author, teacher, and critic whose focus is primarily on technology and communication media. He was editor of Whole Earth Review and the Millennium Whole Earth Catalog (1994). The papers of writer and technologist Howard Rheingold include drafts, proposals, and other typescripts; notes; fliers; and many articles and videos by and about him. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Long Now Foundation records, circa 1900s-2000s
items.description: Collection consists of Stewart Brand's Long Now Archive: printed emails, press & ephemera; Rosetta Project Archive: papers, research, press & ephemera; Long Now Archive: press & ephemera. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: New Dimensions Media records, 1968-2024
items.description: The New Dimensions Foundation is an independent, listener supported, educational broadcasting group based in Ukiah, California. New Dimensions might be superficially described as about new age philosophy and self-help; as their website says, "Our purpose is to share knowledge that has the potential to deepen our connections to self, family, community, planet and the natural world. We encourage public awareness of various approaches towards creating a world that works for everyone." Recordings and files from long-running radio program New Dimensions Radio, along with recordings of related programming.

items.title: Stewart Brand papers, 1954-2000
items.description: He was loosely associated with the Merry Pranksters, USCO, and other countercultural groups, and spent much of the 1960s traveling and visiting communal experiments. Brand created the original Whole Earth Catalog in 1968 to provide practical information on tools that would be useful for people creating and living in communes. The Steward Brand papers contains correspondence, personal journals, manuscripts, photographs, project records, articles, and publications.

sectors.name: Ideas and intellectual history

items.title: Bucky Conversations: Conversations on the Life and Work of an Enigmatic Genius, 2002-2003
items.description: In 2002, to celebrate the acquisition of the Fuller archive, the Stanford University Libraries and the Stanford Humanities Laboratory launched a series of Conversations on R. Buckminster Fuller, alias "Bucky," inventor of the Dymaxion car, the Dymaxion Dwelling Unit, and the geodesic dome, author of Utopia or Oblivion, 4D Timelock, Synergetics, Tetrascroll and Critical Path. The series consists of filmed interviews with Fuller's key collaborators, interlocutors and contemporaries, and is designed to enhance critical understanding of Fuller and his work.

items.title: John Perry Barlow papers
items.description: Often called "the father of cyberlibertarianism," Barlow was a founding member of the Electronic Frontier Foundation and a lyricist for the Grateful Dead. The collection also contains Barlow's email account dating from 1996-2009. The email contains correspondence related to Barlow's life, work with the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and personal and family relationships. There are also series for Barlow's writing, as well as writing about him.

items.title: Kevin Kelly papers, circa 1981-2010
items.description: Scrapbooks, publications, articles, journal and VHS tapes. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Patrick McCray papers, circa 2006-2016
items.description: Research materials assembled during the writing of The Visioneers: How a Group of Elite Scientists Pursued Space Colonies, Nanotechnolosies, and a Limitless Future (2012); documentation and records of the Center for Nanotechnology in Society, University of California, Santa Barbara, circa 2006-2016. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Peter Schwartz papers
items.description: Collection consists of books, articles, speech drafts, and papers written by Schwartz. Also included are materials related to his research and time at SRI, Royal Dutch Shell, Global Business Network, Monitor, and Salesforce. [The subject placement of this collection was inferred and may not be correct.]

items.title: Clippings and articles about Paul Allen, 1993-1996
items.description: Primarily clippings, but includes two journal articles from Wired and Fortune, 1994.

items.title: Cortlandt Van Rensselaer papers, 1966-2013
items.description: Materials consist of Van Rensselaer's papers, including slides and some photographs.

items.title: Henry Lowood papers, 1980-2014
items.description: Includes teaching materials and project files.

items.title: Joaquin G. Avila papers, circa 20th-21st century
W. Conyers Herring lecture notes, 2003
items.description: The materials consist of notes prepared by Herring for a series of lectures.
